items.statement: Calibrated personal loan growth by increasing pricing, refining credit parameters and optimising sourcing costs, resulting in lower disbursements vs previous quarter
items.quote: The Bank calibrated its pace of growth in personal loans and it grew by 32.5% year-on-year in current quarter as compared to 37.3% in previous quarter. The Bank continued to work on increasing pricing, further refining credit parameters and optimising sourcing costs resulting in lower disbursements of personal loans during the quarter as compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth flat QoQ due to reset of loans by highly rated PSU NBFCs; expect to attract more private capex during the year
items.quote: a few highly rated PSU NBFCs, which sort of reset loans. Barring that, we have grown this book year -on-year on 10%. So, we will look at the overall portfolio. So, in terms of the growth, in terms of the areas that we really want to be focused on, we are quite happy with the growth. As you are aware, we follow a 360 -degree approach with the objective of catering to all banking needs. As far as ca

items.statement: Written back Rs 100 crore of the Rs 630 crore AIF provision made last quarter based on RBI guidelines relief; no current proposal to invest more in AIF
items.quote: No, I think the RBI guidelines did provide some relief. We made a provision for about Rs. 630 crore last quarter. Based on our current assessments we have written back about Rs. 100 crore.

items.statement: NII grew 8.1% YoY despite NIM compression from 4.9% to 4.4% due to peak margin in Q4 FY23; full year NIM 4.53% similar to FY23 4.48%
items.quote: On a YoY basis, if you look at it in the fourth quarter last year, we had our peak net interest margin of 4.9%, which is at 4.4% this quarter. So, that drop in margin has partly offset, as you rightly said, the underlying growth in the assets.

items.statement: NBFC and HFC outstanding reduced to Rs 77,000 crore (6.5% of total advances) in March 2024 from Rs 78,000 crore in Dec 2023 and Rs 82,000 crore a year ago
items.quote: Total outstanding to NBFCs and HFCs was about Rs. 77,000 crore in March 2024 compared to about Rs. 78,000 crore in December 2023. This constituted about 6.5% of our total advances. So, that is broadly the number. Last year this number was about Rs. 82,000 crore.

items.statement: Contingency provisions maintained at Rs 13,100 crore (1.1% of total loans) at March 2024
items.quote: The Bank continues to hold contingency provisions of Rs. 13,100 crore at March 31, 2024.

items.statement: Deposit growth healthy at 19.6% YoY and 6% sequentially; term deposits up 27.7% YoY; average deposits growing at 19.9%; not raising deposits at any cost
items.quote: Deposit growth for the banking system has increased about 12.9% year-on-year. As far as we are concerned, during the last quarter, we grew at about 19.6% and 6% sequentially. The term deposits have grown by about 27% year-on-year and about 1.6% sequentially. Even the average depo sit has been growing at a healthy rate of about 19.9%. We are not going to be raising deposits at any

items.statement: No specific loan growth guidance; focus on risk-calibrated growth, maintaining liquidity (LCR 123%), and service quality; difficult to forecast future growth
items.quote: It's very difficult to forecast what is going to happen in the future and we don't really kind of forecast. For us maintaining liquidity is important as we reported. The average LCR for the quarter was about 123%. We have been going at a healthy rate. We will see how it pans out during the course of the year. It's very difficult to change them. For us, it's important to focus on the service. For u

items.statement: Management does not provide specific loan growth outlook; will take opportunities that pass risk framework
items.quote: We don't really give an outlook, Mahrukh, in terms of growth. I think we have our risk framework, our distribution and our delivery system, whatever passes through that we'll be happy to take.

items.statement: NIM may see further moderation but expected to be range-bound for next few quarters until rate cut
items.quote: So I guess we could see some further moderation in the NIM, but I would expect it to be pretty range bound from here on for the next few quarters until a rate cut actually happens.

items.statement: Deposit costs increased 10 bps in February on retail side; some impact will flow through but not very large
items.quote: I mean, we did raise deposit rates by 10 bps in February on the retail side, which was not there at the time when we had our last call. So, some impact will be there, but I guess that will go through, it wouldn't be a very large impact.

items.statement: Operating expense growth pace has moderated and expected to remain moderate; technology expense growth rate to moderate given large base
items.quote: So I think in totality, as I said, we would expect the pace of growth of opex to be more moderate than we have seen in the last couple of years.

items.statement: No particular growth challenge seen in current environment; sufficient room to grow given market share in micro markets
items.quote: I don't see any particular growth challenge sitting here today in the environment.

items.statement: Corporate portfolio growth at 10-11% for some time; less competitive in some pockets due to profitability view but open to opportunities passing risk filters
items.quote: On the corporate side, actually, our growth has been 10% to low double-digit kind of for some time. See, we are very open. I mean, we have strong corporate relationships and a strong funnel for business.

items.statement: Credit costs at sub-40 bps this quarter; may normalize upwards slightly but nothing dramatic expected
items.quote: I guess, looking at it in terms of credit costs, we are still at sub-40 basis points for this quarter. I think, if you kind of adjust out one offs or if you take a more adjusted view, we would still be under 50 basis points.

items.statement: Employee headcount additions slowing from Q3; expect stability to moderate increase going forward
items.quote: I would expect stability to moderate increase from here on.

items.statement: FY25 presales guidance of Rs. 2,500 crores for residential plus Rs. 500 crores from IC&IC, totaling Rs. 3,000 crores combined
items.quote: Rs. 2,500 crores is the guidance that we had given for FY25 and then Rs. 500 crores. So, you can say we are already Rs. 2,700 crores or Rs. 2,800 crores on IC&IC plus Resi combined.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to reach Rs. 8,000-10,000 crores pre-sales by FY28
items.quote: Our aspiration to where we were in FY23 to 5X over which will mean we target a pre-sales scale of Rs. 8,000 crores to Rs. 10,000 crores.

items.statement: Estimated Rs. 7,000-7,500 crores capital needed to achieve 5X growth aspiration, half funded through internal accruals and IC&IC cash flows
items.quote: Our estimate is in order to achieve our aspiration, we will need something around Rs. 7,000 crores to Rs. 7,500 crores of capital. Half of that is available to us through our accruals, our IC business, our debt to equity.

items.statement: Actively discussing platform-level fundraise with parent Mahindra Group open to participate; open to QIP, products, or external partners
items.quote: We are in the process of doing some discussions, fundraise at a platform level where even our parent is quite open to participating given their desire to grow Mahindra Lifespaces into a growth gem and support our growth aspiration.

items.statement: Healthy business development pipeline of Rs. 5,000-6,000 crores GDV in addition to Rs. 4,400 crores acquired in FY24 and Thane project of Rs. 7,000-8,000 crores
items.quote: We continue to have a very healthy BD pipeline, anywhere from Rs. 5,000 crores to Rs. 6,000 crores. This is in addition to the Rs. 4,400 crores that we acquired last year. It is in addition to Thane which is around Rs. 8000 crores.

items.statement: Targeting project-level pre-tax IRR north of 20% across portfolio; not guiding on EBITDA margins due to accounting complexity
items.quote: Our goal is to be always north of 20% IRR and that's project IRR, pretax if you do equity IRR with the right debt to equity, capital structure, post-tax it'll come out to be a couple of percentage points higher.

items.statement: Residential demand remains buoyant driven by per capita income growth and home ownership desire across urban and non-urban centers
items.quote: The Resi segment will continue to have lot of buoyancy driven by per capita income, driven by the desire to own home across urban and non-urban centers.

items.statement: FY28 presales mix aspiration: Rs. 5,000-6,000 crores from Mumbai, couple thousand crores each from Pune and Bangalore
items.quote: Ideally it will be somewhere around Rs. 6,000 crores from Mumbai, let's say Rs. 5,000 crores to Rs. 6,000 crores and couple of thousand crores each from Pune and Bangalore.

items.statement: Acquiring land at peak cycle but pricing captures cost; maintaining deal discipline with IRR guardrails, walking away from deals below financial parameters
items.quote: Anytime we are acquiring a piece of land we are very diligent about the economic assessment related to that acquisition. We do lots and lots of market intelligence gathering to ensure that we are able to make our business case work.

items.statement: Kandivali land payment 50-55% done, balance 45% over next 1.5 years; Thane launch expected in another year after IITT approvals
items.quote: 50%, 55% is done and remaining 45% would be happening in the current financial year. Vimal Agarwal: Little more than half is done and balance will happen over the next 1.5 years. One and a half years

items.statement: IC&IC FY24 lease premium Rs. 370 crores (Jaipur 76 acres Rs. 234 crores, Chennai ~Rs. 135-140 crores); strong pipeline for FY25
items.quote: Overall, we finished IC&IC in FY24 with Rs. 370 crores. Jaipur gave us a very strong 76 acres of land which culminated with Rs. 234 crores and Origins Chennai & World City Chennai together roughly Rs. 135 crores to Rs. 140 crores.

items.statement: Unsold ready-to-move inventory minimal at Rs. 60-70 crores; total unsold inventory including land parcels upwards of Rs. 8,000 crores
items.quote: Our ready to move inventory you are asking? Meet Shah: Yes. Vimal Agarwal: Ready to move in very miniscule. Most of our properties and inventory is sold out. It’s a very small number of about Rs. 60 crores – Rs. 70 crores which will be

items.statement: Focus on procurement excellence and cost management to offset 5% annual labor cost inflation and commodity price spikes
items.quote: The biggest thrust area for me going forward is going to be project execution, especially cost of construction, the procurement, the design specs, the procurement excellence because that's where you will end up losing a couple of basis points, a couple of percentage points of margin.

items.statement: Organized players' market share in Mumbai only 20%; flight to quality benefiting organized developers like Mahindra Lifespaces
items.quote: All the organized players in Mumbai, if you count them together their market share is 20%. Given the cost of capital issue like GST and RERA and all those things we see what I mentioned earlier flight to quality, there is more momentum for the organized players.

items.statement: Murud land parcel (2 hours from Alibag) identified as hidden asset for second-home plotted/villa development; MoU signed, planning to monetize
items.quote: So, absolutely the whole leadership team went there a couple of months back. We think it's a hidden asset for us. It has huge potential, so absolutely we are thinking exactly the way you described.

items.statement: Origins Ahmedabad has IFC as partner; seeking 40-50+ acre anchor clients, rejecting smaller 1-3 acre demands; two large client discussions ongoing
items.quote: We get a lot of requests Shreyans for Ahmedabad which are small 1-2-3 acres kind of you know demand from them. But we want to get to anchor client which is at least 40 acres - 50 acres plus.

items.statement: Operating costs to reduce by INR200-300 per ton over next three years driven by controllable efficiency levers
items.quote: Over the next three years, as we grow, you will see the operating costs continue to come down, and we should be seeing a reduction of almost INR200 to INR300 per ton

items.statement: Capex of ~INR10,000-11,000 crores each year for FY26 and FY27 similar to FY25 spend
items.quote: So similar INR10,000 crore, INR11,000 crores capex will be there for '26, '27 also? Atul Daga: Yes.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton on a northbound journey; pricing environment expected stable or positive in FY25
items.quote: Profitability, it's going to improve. We will focus on EBITDA per ton, which will be on a northbound journey. And given again, Ashish I had already mentioned in my opening remarks that this year, it's too difficult to predict, but we expect the pricing environment to be stable or be positive only.

items.statement: Fuel cost at $150/ton currently, targeting $130/ton in next 3-4 quarters; substantial improvement from Jan-Mar 2025
items.quote: If you're referring to fuel costs, like this quarter also we had our fuel cost at $150 per ton. We have to reach a number of $130 when everything remaining same as of current times. This should be traveling to a number of $130 per ton given our mix that we consume. So that's the kind of improvement that you will definitely see in the next three quarters -- three, four quarters, yes.

items.statement: Industry volume growth 7-8% in Q4 FY24; FY25 industry growth expected at 7-9%
items.quote: For the full year for the industry, yes, it should be maybe 7% to 9%.

items.statement: Clinker factor improved to 1.44; composite cement penetration increasing rapidly to drive further improvement
items.quote: So if we're not at 1.4, we are at 1.44 because every penny matters. And from here onwards, we are seeing an increasing penetration of composite cement, which will help fast track that percentage growth

items.statement: Fuel prices remain unpredictable due to geopolitical factors; no concrete guidance on fuel prices
items.quote: Fuel costs, which are always a burning issue, remain at the same level, has stabilized, but we cannot have a concrete guidance on the fuel prices given the large dependence on the geopolitical factors.

items.statement: Hotgi grinding unit expansion (2.7 mt) put on hold due to Kesoram capacity in same market
items.quote: Keeping in mind the potential capacity that we will get from Kesoram in the same market, we have put on hold our Hotgi grinding unit expansion, which was a 2.7-million-ton ground clearance capacity.

items.statement: Acquired grinding unit in Southern Maharashtra; dispatches commenced last two days using surplus clinker
items.quote: Last week, we had concluded the acquisition of a grinding unit in Southern Maharashtra, which and with available surplus clinker in the state, it gives us a unique opportunity to increase our footprint in the fast-growing state of Maharashtra. Dispatches from this unit have already commenced since last two days for UltraTech.

items.statement: Target zero net cash on standalone balance sheet by end FY25; net debt including Kesoram at INR1,500-2,000 crores
items.quote: Our target is to inch towards zero net cash on the balance sheet by the end of '25, not taking into account the Kesoram debt. But yes, if I take that into account, so INR2,700 crores of debt -- net debt that we have today, we should be inching towards INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores of net debt, including Kesoram.

items.statement: Price improvements seen in April across Maharashtra, Eastern and Southern corridors; North and West flat
items.quote: Several markets. So we've seen in Maharashtra. So there have been positive movements only practically across all the markets, except North, we have not seen so much North and West. West is already a well -priced market. So we have seen improvements, margina l improvements in Eastern corridor, Southern Corridor

items.quote: Yes. So we have obtained a single-window clearance that is the license required. We will -- we have identified mines. Atul Daga: You will hear from us within this year, within this

items.statement: RIDF balances to reduce below 5% of total assets by end of FY27 from current 11%
items.quote: And that will start flowing int o the margins over the next two to three years. As I said, the total stock hit is about 70 basis points

items.statement: NIM improvement of 80-100 bps over next three years from RIDF reduction and retail mix shift
items.quote: All and the Retail Assets mix, both of these, we believe, will add to about 80 to 100 basis points of margins for the next three-year period.

items.statement: FY25 recoveries and upgrades expected to exceed INR 5,000 crores
items.quote: So, Jai, this year we have done the ecovery and upgradation to almost like 6 ,000 crores and we are quite confident that FY ‘25 also we will see a similar trend , but definitely more than INR 5,000 crores

items.statement: FY25 non-tax provisioning to remain below 50 bps of average assets
items.quote: we do believe that the non-tax provisioning that we will end up for Fiscal 25 should again be contained below 50 basis points.

items.statement: FY25 slippage ratio expected at lower end of 2%-2.5% range, trending to 2% or below by year-end
items.quote: We do believe that for next year the slippage ratio should be on the lower end of the 2% to 2.5%. I think that is really how we see it.

items.statement: Operating expenses to assets targeted below 2.6% over next two to three years
items.quote: we do believe that we should operate at sub-2.6%.

items.statement: Non-interest income fee-to-assets to accrete 8-10 bps annually over next two to three years
items.quote: We do believe that over the next two to three years, we will see about 8-10 basis points of accretion, let's say, typically every year.

items.statement: FY24 NIM at 2.4% vs 2.6% in FY23 due to RIDF drag; Q4 NIM flat at 2.4%
items.quote: Full-year FY 24 Net Interest Margin (NIM) came in at 2.4% against 2.6% in Fiscal 23 due to negative drag because of the RIDF deposit placed for the PSL shortfall.

items.statement: RIDF balances peaked at 11% of total assets, causing ~70 bps drag on NII-to-assets
items.quote: the current drag on the stock is about 70 basis points on NII to assets.

items.statement: SR carrying value reduced from INR 1,700 crores (Mar-23) to INR 1,250 crores (Mar-24); rating agencies estimate INR 5,000 crores recovery
items.quote: we had about INR 1,700 crores of face value, sorry, not face value, carrying value in our balance sheet as of March 31st, 2023. That's come down to about INR 1,250 crores.

items.statement: Retail + SME to Wholesale advances ratio to stay at 62:38 near-to-medium term; corporate advances to grow high single digits
items.quote: As guided earlier, we expect that within Advances, the Ratio of Retail + SME Segment Advances to Wholesale Segment Advances (Mid-Corporate and Large-Corporate) would remain at the similar level of 62:38 from here on over the near-to-medium term.

items.statement: Retail asset growth tapering from 35-40% to 20s, expected to move to teens
items.quote: you would have seen retail has been growing at about 35%-40% and has kind of now come into the 20s and we should possibly see the growth taper also to, let's say, the teens, right?

items.statement: Blended savings account rate not increased in FY24 despite tight liquidity; gained incremental market share
items.quote: if I look at, let's say, the blended savings account rate, over the last one year, we would actually not have increased our blended savings account rate despite the backdrop of a tight liquidity.

items.statement: Added 134 new branches since Jan-23 in CASA-rich clusters; branch expansion to continue
items.quote: We remained committed to judiciously expand our distribution and added 134 new branches since January 23 in CASA rich clusters.

items.statement: One mid-corporate road project slipped to NPA due to DCCO breach with nil financial overdues
items.quote: this was actually an account on the road. It's a road project, where because there is a date of commencement of commercial operations, if you don't meet that, then you slip into NPA.

items.statement: CA Basque warrant exercise in Apr-24 lifts proforma CET-1 to 12.7% from 12.2%
items.quote: including the effect of the warrants exercise by CA Basque in the month of April 24, the proforma CET-1, as on March 31, including the proceeds from warrants conversion, works out to 12.7%.

items.statement: Target to double gross sales in next financial year
items.quote: Our target is to double the gross sales in the next financial year, led by the strong traction that we are witnessing in our existing product as well as a slew of new products that we propose to launch in the next financial year.

items.statement: Target final close of Rs 2,000 crores for sixth series real estate fund in FY25
items.quote: We have launched the sixth series of real estate fund in FY24. We have already done the first close and we are looking at a final close of Rs. 2,000 crores during the course of FY25.

items.statement: Fifth series equity growth capital fund expected to launch in second half of FY25
items.quote: Our fifth series of equity growth capital fund is expected to be launched in the second half of FY25.

items.statement: Target to double disbursements in FY25 compared to FY24
items.quote: With a new and a strong leadership team in place, we believe that we are geared to double our disbursement in the FY25 compared to FY24.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio in Housing Finance to improve from FY26 onwards
items.quote: From FY26 onwards, we would see some respite to the cost-to-income ratio, which would start coming down.

items.statement: Plan to grow distribution team 3x in three years
items.quote: Our focus is on ramping up the distribution team's strength to improve our currently low cross-sell ratio of 6%. We are aiming to grow this distribution team 3x in three years' time.

items.statement: Doubled salesforce to 925 RMs in FY24, plan to double again in FY25
items.quote: We have doubled our salesforce during FY24 to 925 RMs and are looking to double this count once again in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Added 110 RMs in Q4FY24 and 177 RMs in FY24; future hiring more measured
items.quote: We added 110 RMs during Q4FY24 and a total of 177 RMs during FY24. Our incremental RM growth will be more measured and strategic.

items.statement: Asset Management AUM grew 57% YoY to Rs 71,810 crores
items.quote: Our Asset Management business AUM across Mutual Funds, PMS, AIF grew by 57% YoY to Rs. 71,810 crores.

items.statement: Mutual Fund AUM grew 65% to Rs 48,800 crores; Alternates AUM grew 41% to nearly Rs 23,000 crores
items.quote: Our Mutual Fund AUM grew 65% to Rs. 48,800 crores. Alternates AUM grew 41% to nearly Rs. 23,000 crores.

items.statement: AIF AUM surpassed Rs 10,000 crores mark
items.quote: AIF AUM surpassed the Rs. 10,000 crores mark.

items.statement: Private Equity fee-earning AUM over Rs 10,000 crores
items.quote: The Private Equity business fee-earning AUM stood at over Rs. 10,000 crores across our equity growth capital funds as well as real estate funds.

items.quote: We have grown from Rs. 450 crores in FY23 to Rs. 914 crores and we have invested hugely in that business in terms of manpower cost.

items.statement: Insurance premium collected Rs 100 crores in FY24 vs Rs 76 crores in FY23; expects FY25 to be good without giving estimates
items.quote: For ‘23- 24, we have totally collected Rs. 100 crores of premium, which is compared to Rs. 76 crores for the previous financial year which includes, of course , Rs. 4 crores of general and health insurance. There is still lot of growth left in this business and we are hoping that ‘25 also should be good for

items.statement: Majority of group cash (Rs 750 crores) deployed in margin trading book and working capital; limited free cash for acquisitions
items.quote: On the group basis, the cash available is Rs. 750 crores. But as MD said, the majority of that is used for MTF books, lending, MT F and another major portion is used for the working capital requirements on a regular basis

items.statement: Software income declined 16% in FY24; no aggressive business plan but will consider growth over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: At the moment we do not have an aggressive business plan on the software business, but over a period of next 1 year to 18 months, we will think about growing that business.

items.statement: Interest income increased to around Rs 110 crores in FY24
items.quote: But having said this, our interest income has gone up to around Rs. 110 crore last year.

items.statement: Inorganic acquisitions will be explored if opportunities align with culture and compliance standards
items.quote: Inorganic acquisition is an opportunity we will explore as and when we see opportunities that are aligning with our culture as well as the, you know, particularly on the compliance culture, etc.

items.statement: Targets 30% top-line growth in FY25 including Warner deal
items.quote: As committed earlier, this year for FY25 I feel 30% growth on top line is possible -- as you see in FY24 bottom line as compared to last year was up by 66%. But still we feel on 66% we will do another 30% this year i.e. in FY 25 as well.

items.statement: Targets 30% PAT growth in FY25 on FY24 base of INR127.2 cr
items.quote: FY 25 see now you can calculate whatever our entire year's bottom line you calculate 30% growth on that. Our target is to achieve that. So we will try and achieve that.

items.statement: Content investment budget of INR75-80 cr for FY25
items.quote: Yes, we have a budget of INR75 crores-INR80 crores. We have thought about it. Yes.

items.statement: Plans to acquire 8-10 films across languages (~50 songs) plus independent music in FY25
items.quote: I think our target is to at least acquire Hindi, Tamil, all languages put together, around eight to 10 films, yes. And average should be five songs per movie, so 50 songs we should get from film side. That's the idea.

items.statement: Will release ~150 songs in FY25 vs 733 in FY24, focusing on quality over quantity
items.quote: Maybe our target is, maybe we will reduce further, and maybe this year we will do only between 150, approximately 150 songs. So we are not going to reduce amount, but we are improving our quality and going for bigger numbers, bigger artists and bigger those things.

items.statement: Content cost target 25-30% of revenue; will invest up to 30% if quality content available
items.quote: Actually, still, if we get a good content, then we will do 30% also. We will go for 30%. 25%-30% is our target. We will invest that much money.

items.statement: Warner deal: fixed MG for 4 years with 85:15 overflow split; first-year advance higher
items.quote: MG is constant. MG is constant. It is fixed. We have taken it from them according to the projection of 4 years. And if we surpass that MG there will be an immediate kick-in of overflow.

items.statement: Paid streaming growing but will take 2-3 more years for meaningful numbers; Spotify targets 60-70% paid conversion in 5 years
items.quote: I think that's a good thing for the industry, but as mentioned earlier it will still take 2 years, 3 years more to have very good numbers to see.

items.statement: Client concentration risk with Warner mitigated by content ownership and upfront MG; Warner negotiation power stronger
items.quote: No, there won't be any revenue loss. I think Warner being an international big player, their negotiation power is better than us. It is not less than us. So, you can rest assured that we took this decision very carefully.

items.statement: Group company Tips Films to supply 30-35% of content acquisition budget in FY25
items.quote: I think maximum it can be 30%-35% from our own company. We acquire content. I think it will be that much. And that is the target we have kept for this year.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 75% digital streaming, 25% non-streaming; YouTube ~45-50% of total revenue
items.quote: That is same, 75%-25%. So 75% is digital and 25% is online.

items.statement: Content cost written off fully in quarter of release; expects investment recovery in 4-5 years
items.quote: We don't carry forward anything. We just write off everything in the quarter we release our content. So, we don't have any liability. So that way, we feel safe. It's our kind of business.

items.statement: Non-current liability >INR70 cr from Warner MG advance; current liability INR64 cr
items.quote: Yes. I think it will be more than INR70 crores.

items.statement: Short-term investments INR91 cr in liquid and short-term debt mutual funds
items.quote: Yes. So, primarily it's into mutual funds, debt mutual funds. And towards, let's say, it's liquid and short-term funds.

items.statement: Employee cost to rise nominally for new hires in brands/sync team; hiring nearly complete
items.quote: Little bit will be here and there, very nominal. It won't affect much. But it will go up because we need a few expensive people. And with these new businesses, we are getting more aggressive in that.

items.statement: Management aims for industry-leading revenue growth in FY25 but will not provide specific guidance due to market volatility
items.quote: We will, of course, aim to deliver industry-leading growth. Now what that number is, we can't guide. It is very, very hard to guide.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to stay in a narrow band for next 24-36 months while investing 1-1.5% of revenue in capabilities
items.quote: For the next 24 to 36 months we will be in an investment mode and we would love to keep the margin in a ramp narrow band. And if you realize that when we invest we will invest upwards of 1% or 1.5% of revenue in our business.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin at 16.3%, up 31 bps QoQ, exceeding the 16% exit target set at start of FY24
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for quarter 4 stands at 16.3%, which is a 31 basis points growth quarter-over-quarter. You may recall at the start of the financial year, we have indicated that we would like to exit the year with 1 6% EBITDA margin, and I'm happy to note that we've been able to deliver above that number

items.statement: Pipeline at all-time high of $1.8 billion, targeting $2.4-2.5 billion; TCV signings flat YoY at $240M in Q4 with 45% from new deals
items.quote: Our pipeline is currently growing. The one thing however I will tell you Shradha is the decision-making is getting pushed out because the discretionary spends are getting pushed out. So I can't really comment in terms of what that growth number will be.

items.statement: Pipeline at $1.8 billion, target to improve to $2.4-2.5 billion over next 6-8 months with focus on order booking
items.quote: We've got about $1.8 billion worth of pipeline and we want to improve it to about $2.4 billion to $2.5 billion. We are working on it. Are we there yet? We are not. But yes, a lot of effort over the next 6 to 8 months will be on order booking.

items.statement: Demand environment remains challenging with slower client decision-making and discretionary spend push-outs; no material change from past 4-5 quarters
items.quote: The past few quarters the demand environment has been quite challenging and marked with a lot of uncertainty. And the situation going forward is not going to change. We see the situation in the market nothing different from what we saw in the past 4 or 5 quarters.

items.statement: Will continue investing in capabilities for long-term growth including Gen AI platform Cogito, ROW expansion, and Optimus efficiency program
items.quote: we will continue to make investments that are required to create and scale up our capabi lities for long -term growth, we will also be driving multiple initiatives across the company to increase our operational

items.statement: Two whistleblower complaints received, both behavioral in nature with no financial impropriety found so far; investigations ongoing
items.quote: So first of all, we have had two complaints. Both complaints are behaviour in nature in terms of the way some of our leaders have conducted themselves and the way some of our leaders have used language, etcetera, etcetera. So we don't see any financial impropriety at this stage.

items.statement: Life Sciences vertical softness expected for Q1 and Q2 FY25 due to seasonality and client budget cycles; growth expected to return after
items.quote: I feel we will see two more quarters of pain in healthcare but the growth will be back. Fundamentally, I don't think there's anything wrong with the business. I think we are happy with where we are going.

items.statement: Client rationalization continues: active accounts reduced from 272 to 259 QoQ and 288 YoY to focus on high-potential accounts
items.quote: This quarter, we have further rationalized our tail accounts and now our active accounts stand at 259 from 272 from a quarter ago and 288 from a year ago, so that we can free up resources and our capabilities to focus on high potential accounts.

items.statement: $100M deal won in Q2 on track to start contributing revenue from April; 70% renewal, 30% net new
items.quote: The large deal that we won in Q2 is on track. But again, I must be careful of saying this because the large deal is on track. There is no problem. We will continue to start seeing revenues from them.

items.statement: Board proposed final dividend of INR 4/share plus interim INR 2.5/share; cash balance $209M, zero debt, operating cash flow 86% of EBITDA
items.quote: At their meeting today the Board of Directors have proposed a final dividend of INR 4 per share, subject to shareholders' approval. This is on top of an interim dividend of INR 2.5 per share that was paid out during the preceding quarter.

items.statement: Gen AI used internally via Optimus program to drive efficiency and protect margins while investing; client-facing Gen AI revenue not yet material but deals close
items.quote: We are using Gen AI to disrupt our own company. Under Selva's organization and Kamini has spoken about it, I've spoken about it in the past, we've embarked on a program called the Optimus program. Now the Optimus program is going to be a 2-3 year program where we will use AI and Gen AI technologies to not only disrupt our own processes but also automate our processes within the company.

items.statement: BFSI vertical grew 4.4% QoQ driven by account mining and new logos; management bullish on BFSI long-term despite small base
items.quote: From a BFSI perspective, clearly, account mining is working. We're creating larger and larger accounts. Now we have a very large account in BFSI which is doing well for us. We are also opening a couple of new logos, which has helped us bounce back in 4Q.

items.statement: Geographic concentration risk: 86% revenue from US; expanding in UK, Switzerland, Germany, and India via new ROW leadership
items.quote: Today, as you know, 86% of our revenues come in from the U.S. But that doesn't mean we will not focus on the U.S. The U.S. is a key market. It is a huge market. We are probably a very small player even in the U.S. So there is a lot of opportunity to do much more in the U.S. But equally to get a little bit more global, we want to expand our business outside the U.S.

items.statement: Expect higher growth in India in H2 CY24 as delayed EV and export orders ramp up
items.quote: We expect to show to the market higher growth in the next quarters. Probably by the third and the fourth quarter let's say, by the end of the year, we will see this jump happening finally.

items.statement: Expect tractor market in India to recover slightly in second half of CY24
items.quote: We also expect the tractor market to recover slightly in the second half of the year.

items.statement: European light vehicle production forecast 2% lower in CY24 vs CY23
items.quote: IHS forecasting European light vehicle production in 2024 to be 2% lower than in 2023.

items.statement: US construction equipment market slowdown expected to pick up towards end of CY24
items.quote: The slowdown in the U S construction equipment market continues and is expected to start picking up towards the end of the year.

items.statement: Capex target ~5% of sales for CY24; Q1 at 4.2-4.3%, growth capex concentrated in India
items.quote: The capex in our, let's say, you know that our guide is to have approximately 5% turnover, the sales -- 5% is the figure that we consider reasonable and very sound. In the first quarter, we had -- our capex, we spent was almost INR1 billion. This is a little bit less than 5%. We are at 4.2%, 4.3% over sales.

items.statement: New orders in India ~INR3 billion per year added in Q1 CY24
items.quote: Additionally, in this first quarter, we already got additional new orders of -- in India of about INR3 billion per year more for the next year.

items.statement: India recurrent EBITDA margin 17.2% in Q1 CY24, up from 16.5% in Q4 CY23 and 16.7% in Q1 CY23
items.quote: Without that subsidy, the recurrent EBITDA margin in the India business for Q1 C '24 is 17.2%, which is higher both year -on-year and sequentially versus 16.7% in Q1 C '23 and 16.5% in Q4 C '23.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margin 16% in Q1 CY24, expected to recover to last year levels in coming quarters
items.quote: We think that in the next quarters, despite the market will not be fantastic, and there will be no big growth, but we will recover, and we are in line to recover the margins that we had last year, okay?

items.statement: Bill Forge Mexico EBITDA margin expected between 10-15% due to high US steel prices
items.quote: So we can be between 10% to 15% of EBITDA margins on those businesses.

items.statement: India two-wheeler market showing good growth on recovering rural/suburban demand, expected to continue
items.quote: The two-wheeler market has shown good growth on the back of recovering rural and suburban demand, and we expect this trend to continue.

items.statement: Europe EV transition slowing; ~40% of new orders in Europe for EVs but programs delayed
items.quote: Regarding the new orders that we are getting in Europe approximately 40% of the new orders that we got are for electric vehicles. So the evolution and the, let's say, the transition from the internal combustion engine to the electric vehicle components will happen smoothly

items.statement: Metalcastello revenue run rate ~EUR50-60 million in CY24 vs EUR75-80 million previously
items.quote: And we will -- we are selling now at approximately EUR5 million per m onth. This is about between EUR50 million and EUR60 million this year , instead of the EUR75 million, EUR80 million we were at the beginning of last year.

items.statement: EV transition risk in India low (<INR500 cr value-at-risk over 3-4 years); Europe transition managed via EV order book
items.quote: So if you do value very at risk, it is not very high. you're talking about less than INR500 crores value-add risk, maybe 3, 4 years down the line.

items.statement: Euro VII norms delayed to mid-2027, slowing EV transition in Europe
items.quote: The new Euro VII norms that will be applied by the European Commission will -- or has been delayed until mid of 2027.

items.statement: Bill Forge Mexico now subsidiary of CIE Galfor post equity infusion; running at ~$3M/month, targeting ~$40M in CY24
items.quote: Bill Forge Mexico, that is BF Mexico, is now a subsidiary of CIE Galfor post the equity infusion in the BF Mexico done by CIE Galfor.

items.statement: Plan to take generation capacity to over 24 GW in coming years through organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: Taking the organic and inorganic growth opportunities together, we plan to take our generation capacity to over 24 GW in the coming years.

items.statement: Mahan Phase-II total capex is INR 13,500 crores
items.quote: Mahan Phase-II's total capex is INR13,500 crores.

items.statement: FGD orders placed for all capacities with completion timeline of December 2026
items.quote: the FGD order s for all capacities have been placed now and the timeline to complete this is December ’26

items.statement: Raigarh brownfield expansion of 1.6 GW thermal capacity in Chhattisgarh under evaluation for PPA tie-ups
items.quote: We have recently initiated the development process for expansion of Raigarh power plant, which we plan to set up 1600 megawatt thermal power capacity in Chhattisgarh.

items.statement: Expecting NCLT approvals soon for Coastal Energen and Lanco Amarkantak inorganic acquisitions
items.quote: We are also evaluating several inorganic growth opportunities, and we have announced progress in two of them. That is Coastal Energen and Lanco Amarkantak. We expect to receive NCLT approvals for these two companies soon.

items.statement: Continuing EBITDA grew 126% YoY to INR 5,273 crores in Q4 FY24; full year continuing EBITDA up 120% to INR 18,789 crores
items.quote: continuing EBITDA for Q4 FY '24 grew impressively by 126% to INR5,273 crores as compared to INR2,329 crores in FY '23. Similarly, the continuing EBITDA for full year FY '24 is higher by 120% at INR18,789 crores

items.statement: Imported coal prices expected to settle at $90-100 per ton; no significant further reduction expected; substantial coal cost pass-through in PPAs
items.quote: we believe that it will eventually settle at $90, $100 per ton. So, we don't expect any further significant reduction in this. And for a substantial part of our PPAs we have a coal cost pass-through.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from A to AA- family due to revenue visibility, fuel security, profitability improvement and deleveraging
items.quote: The company's creditworthiness has improved sharply as marked by credit rating upgrades from A to AA family i.e. AA -.

items.statement: FY25 residential bookings guidance of Rs 27,000 crores, targeting 20% growth over FY24
items.quote: For Financial Year '25 , we hope to grow residential bookings by 20% over a high base to Rs.27,000 crores through the launch of a large number of exciting new projects combined with strong substance sales.

items.statement: Medium-term aspiration of 20% booking growth per year, calibrated based on market conditions and business development
items.quote: I think we'd like to stick with our guidance of 20% growth over the medium-term. Of course, this might get calibrated upwards or downwards basis market conditions and how strong business development additions from here are.

items.statement: Added 10 new projects with estimated booking value of just over Rs 21,000 crores in FY24
items.quote: In all, we added four group housing projects with an estimated booking value of Rs.12,800 crores in the 4th Quarter of the financial year and a total of 10 new projects with an estimated booking value of just over Rs.21,000 crores in the full financial year.

items.statement: Business development guidance of Rs 20,000 crores for FY25, not an upper cap if opportunities arise
items.quote: Honestly, I think our BD guidance is probably the one we pay the least attention to if I am being totally honest, because BD really depend on what we have seen during the year and the specific opportunities. There is not going to be if we see great opportunities, the 20 is not going to form any kind of upper cap certainly.

items.statement: Imputed EBITDA margin of 27% in FY24, sustainable near-term with 25-30% reasonable expectation
items.quote: I think overall these kind of margins we are expecting to be I think 25% to 30% is a reasonable expectation. As Gaurav said, plotted development might be a little bit higher than that.

items.statement: Underwriting target imputed margin of ~25% for group housing, higher for plotted; price upside captured when market allows
items.quote: Yes, in plotted, of course it will be much higher, but yes, ballpark what you're saying is right.

items.statement: Strong customer response to new launches drove record Q4 bookings of Rs 9,519 crores, up 135% YoY
items.quote: Booking value for the quarter stood at Rs.9,519 crores, up by 135% year-on-year over what was the time our best ever quarter , and 66% quarter -on-quarter over what was also our best ever quarter at the time.

items.statement: FY25 guidance heavily launch-driven; launches to be bigger contributor than sustenance sales
items.quote: So, I think quarter-to-quarter it would shift, but fair to say it will be a very launch heavy year balance with some amount of sustenance, largely launches would be the bigger contributor.

items.statement: Construction cost contingency of up to 10% factored in pro forma; execution risk could marginally reduce returns
items.quote: we have intentionally, even shown you a scenario with 10% sort of a contingency exactly to help one get a perspective, but eventually in execution , our ability to manage costs will either improve the r eturns or could marginally reduce it

items.statement: No immediate plan to raise capital; comfortable with net debt gearing of 0.5-1.0x and net debt not exceeding Rs 10,000 crores
items.quote: Yes, I think we have no plan for the moment to raise capital. We would never kind of entirely rule that out, but certainly don't have any immediate plan for that.

items.statement: Entered Hyderabad market in Q4 FY24 with two land deals worth ~Rs 5,000 crores estimated booking value
items.quote: I am happy to announce that Godrej Properties entered the Hyderabad market in the 4th Quarter with two land deals with an estimated booking value potential of nearly Rs.5,000

items.statement: Vikhroli development management agreement continues indefinitely with 10% of top line fee; no time-bound exclusivity
items.quote: Yes, it's very clear that DM has already been in place for many years and will continue exactly as is and is applicable for the entire Vikhroli land. There is no time-bound period to which it is applicable.

items.statement: Collections guidance of Rs 15,000 crores for FY25, up from Rs 11,436 crores in FY24
items.quote: We understood that the kind of sales we have achieved in F Y'24 is very, very high quality which has given us the confidence to kind of step out and give a relatively much higher guidance, which is about 15,000 crores.

items.statement: Commercial portfolio rental potential of Rs 1,100 crores with full potential NOI of ~Rs 270 crores; outperforming internal estimates
items.quote: Total rental portfolio opportunities is about 1,100 crores and the full potential is about 270-odd crores. And of course, as and when we will hit OCs, this will continue to come, most of the OCs will hit in this year itself.

items.statement: Economic interest in projects at 85%, not expected to rise significantly; some JVs still being added
items.quote: No, I don't think it will keep going up. It's already at 85%. So, it's already at a very high level. So, I would not expect it to really grow up from here.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by over Rs 700 crores in Q4 FY24 despite strong business development; gearing at 0.62x
items.quote: The strong cash collections allowed for GPL to reduce net debt by over 700 crore s in the 4th Quarter despite strong business development in that piece

items.statement: Lakshya 2026 targets updated: Retailisation >95%, Retail book growth >25% CAGR, Consol GS3 <3%, NS3 <1%, Consol RoA 2.8%-3.0%
items.quote: Accordingly, the new targets for Lakshya 2026 are as follows: • Retailisation at >95%, against which we are at 94% in Q4FY24 • Retail book growth to be maintained at >25% CAGR. In Q4FY24, the growth stood at 31% YoY • While we have improved portfolio quality by sustaining the Retail GS3 & NS3 levels within the threshold levels, we have now tasked ourselves to converge Consol GS3 & NS3 below 3% & 1

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 at 2.25%-2.5% range
items.quote: The credit cost, in terms of trajectory, you are referring to 2.4% that we have. I think it will be somewhere in the range of about 2.25% to 2.5%. That's the internal plan.

items.statement: Q4FY24 Consol NIMs + Fees at 11.25%, FY24 at 10.67%
items.quote: Consol NIMs + Fees remained strong at 11.25% owing to change in portfolio mix to Retail and WAC remaining stable on a sequential basis on account of astute liability management

items.statement: Rural demand weakness likely to spill into H1FY25 due to uneven monsoon and FY24 crop output decline; urban consumption projected upbeat but uneven
items.quote: The ongoing weakness in rural demand is likel y to spill over into H1FY25 due to probability of uneven monsoonal rains and decline in crop output in FY24, as per ICRA. Urban consumption is projected to remain upbeat in FY25, though

items.statement: Two-Wheeler premium share increased from 41% to 50% in Q4FY24; Personal Loan cross-sell to existing customers rose from 47% to 60%
items.quote: If you see in slide 16 of our investor presentation, we have given the premium share of our Two-Wheeler originations have gone up by almost 9 percentage points this quarter from 41% to 50%.

items.statement: Investing in technology, people, new branches for SME and Personal Loans; cost-to-book target opex plus credit cost within 7%
items.quote: We have rolled out new branches for the new businesses that we started off last year in the SME. Personal Loans is also absolutely digitized product where lot of investments have gone into IT. So, all these -- whatever savings we get on the credit cost, the intent is to actually apply t hat money towards the investment in new technologies as well as manpower

items.statement: Additional prudential provision of Rs. 721 Cr created for SR portfolio sequencing risk; PCR on SR net EAD at ~55%
items.quote: To minimise the possibility of above variations on a quarter-on-quarter basis arising out of this 'sequence risk', the Company has created additional prudential provisions of Rs. 721 Cr comprising Rs. 546 Cr released on account of fair value changes in the Wholesale loan book and an incremental amount of Rs.175 Cr created through P&L.

items.statement: Wholesale book reduced from Rs. 38,058 Cr (Q2FY23) to Rs. 5,528 Cr (Q4FY24); further reduced to Rs. 4,400 Cr post March 31, 2024
items.quote: Apropos to the above, I am pleased to share that the Company was able to sell down/ reduce the on-book Wholesale portfolio successfully from Rs.38,058 Cr at the end of Q2FY23 to Rs.5,528 Cr by the end of Q4FY24.

items.statement: Beta version of next-gen digital credit engine expected to deploy in production by latter part of Q1FY25
items.quote: The work on the next generation digital credit engine has progressed at a satisfactory pace and we expect the Beta version to be deployed in production towards the latter part of Q1FY25.

items.statement: Management guides NIMs plus fees between 11% to 11.25% for FY25.
items.quote: So, we hope that we'll be able to keep our NIMs and fees between 11% to 11.25% sort of corridor in FY25.

items.statement: Management targets managing overall opex plus credit cost within 7% of cost to book over the next 15-18 months.
items.quote: So, I think the best barometer is to manage the overall opex plus credit cost within the range of 7% when it comes to cost to book.

items.statement: Board recommended 25% dividend for FY24, subject to AGM approval.
items.quote: And this year, Board has already recommended 25% dividend, which will have to be approved at the AGM.

items.statement: Investments in technology, people, and marketing will continue for the next 15-18 months.
items.quote: Moving forward, we should start at least over the next 15 to 18 months, investments would continue.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds expected at 8.15%-8.2% for the full year versus back book at 7.82%.
items.quote: Yes, yes. So that is based on the current situation. Naturally, if something dramatic happens, we will have to factor in. But as we speak, this is what our expectation is.

items.statement: Cost of funds may increase 35-40 bps during FY25 due to lagged transmission of past rate hikes and bank capital requirements.
items.quote: So, we are more or less sort of, given the certainty that sort of the cost of funds regime that we are in probably will trend towards a majority part of the year, which might see to a 35 to 40 basis points increase in our cost of funds during the course of the year.

items.statement: Rural demand weakness noted in Farm/Tractor segment due to uneven rainfall; MFI industry growing at 30-31%.
items.quote: Because of the unevenness in rainfall and because of the lowered water tables all across the coun try, tractor demand has been sluggish, OEM shipments have been sluggish and the entire industry has degrown

items.statement: Q1FY25 (April) started reasonably well for MFI; hopeful for improvement with normal monsoon.
items.quote: As of now, as I said in my call, Q1FY25 also, which is basically the month of April also looks to have started reasonably well.

items.statement: Wholesale book reduction largely complete at Rs 4,400 Cr; Retail book at Rs 80,000 Cr driving higher yields.
items.quote: And the Rs. 80,000 Cr Retail balance sheet will actually give me much better yields.

items.statement: Personal Loans growth tempered deliberately; will grow measuredly focusing on salaried and cross-sell segments.
items.quote: It will be measured and we will grow it measuredly. And you will see guidance from us and performance commentary from us in the next couple of quarters on this.

items.statement: Created Rs 721 Cr floating provision on SR portfolio to cover sequencing risk over 4-5 year resolution timeline.
items.quote: So, we have created a Rs. 721 Cr of floating provision to sort of protect us against and protect ou r quarter -to-quarter performance against variation that might come because of a sequence risk while we resolve those

items.statement: Retail portfolio credit metrics robust; Rural Group Loans delinquency 1/3rd of industry, Two-Wheeler at 80% of industry.
items.quote: If you look at our Rural Group Loans and our Micro Finance, our sort of delinquency levels on an apples-to-apples basis is 1/3 rd that of industry. If you look at our Two-Wheeler Finance, we are at about 80% of industry.

items.statement: New integrated underwriting engine beta version expected in production by latter part of Q1FY25.
items.quote: So, we are hopeful that the beta version will come into production in sometime around the latter part of Q1FY25.

items.statement: Received insurance corporate agency license; will enable insurance cross-sell through loan lifecycle for additional fee income.
items.quote: One additional point of information I'd like to give is that as an organization, we have received an insurance corporate agency license.

items.statement: Frontline attrition reduced by up to 30% in 2-3 months via salary corrections and welfare initiatives.
items.quote: we have done some salary corrections and made parity corrections over -- compared to some of our competitors, whi ch has seen our attrition levels in some of our front lines come down as high as 30% in a period of 2 to 3 months

items.statement: FY2025 expected to be a high rollout year with elevated capex continuing for next few quarters
items.quote: I think FY 2025 still remains a high rollout year for us in terms of towers.

items.statement: Hopes FY2025 tower additions stronger than FY2024 but remains uncertain
items.quote: I think Kunal we hope to be stronger, but I think it remains quite uncertain.

items.statement: High capex phase to continue for few more months and quarters due to strong rollout momentum
items.quote: I think the momentum has not slowed down so we do expect the momentum to continue for a few more months and quarters , so from that perspective I think there will be sort of a high capex phase for some more time.

items.statement: Order book looks very strong for remaining part of the year

items.statement: 85 km slurry pipeline 50% complete; DRI and pellet projects expected completion by FY25

items.statement: All mine expansion clearances (IBM plan, EC) expected by year-end 2024-25
items.quote: We expect this to, in various phases there are approvals such as the IBM plan approval and ultimately the EC. We expect all that to happen by the yearend 2024-25.

items.quote: So, in the first plant, around Rs. 700 to Rs. 800. In the second plant, around Rs. 1,100 to Rs. 1,200 rupees.

items.quote: Domestic demand is robust and is growing at 8% CAGR. Domestic production capacity is around 5 million tons. The new capacity addition in next 2 years will be 450,000 tons only.

items.quote: However, the only point to be made is that private consumption is down. The GDP numbers are looking good because of the gross fixed capital formation that's happening in the country. However, we are confident that as we go through this year, things will change on the private consumption side as well.

items.statement: Cheese factory at Ranjangaon commercialized; products just moving into trade
items.quote: also commercialized our cheese factory in Ranjangaon, and we've started to now make the products and supply to the market as well. Are they in the market yet? Vipin Kataria: Just moving into the trade

items.statement: Wheat outlook slightly inflationary due to low government holdings and government buying; sugar crop not as good as last year
items.quote: see while the crop seems to be fine as far as wheat is concerned, the government holding has been reasonably low. So there is going to be a government buying because of their programs. So I would think that the wheat outlook is slightly inflationary during the year, while until the elections, things will not move. But beyond the elections, I think it will be slightly inflationary. Similarly, sugar

items.statement: Volume growth 2x revenue growth in Q4; volume and revenue growth nearly at par for full year FY24
items.quote: So the situation on volume and revenue for the last year has been, they are almost at par, right? So volume and revenue are the same. However, if you look at it by quarter, it's a very different story. So the last quarter, the volume growth is 2x the revenue growth, right?

items.statement: Direct distribution expanded from 26.8 lakh to 27.9 lakh outlets; rural distributors increased from 28,000 to 30,000
items.quote: We've expanded direct distribution from March '23, we were at 26.8 lakh outlets. In March '24, we are at 27.9 lakh outlets. We've strengthened our rural distribution by going from 28,000 rural distributors to 30,000 rural distributors.

items.statement: Service levels in modern trade and e-commerce up 15% to north of 90%; some accounts exceed 93%
items.quote: So our service levels have gone up by 15%. We are at north of 90%, which is best-in-class, both in modern trade as well as e-commerce. In some of the accounts, we are at service level, which is in excess of 93%.

items.statement: International business performed well led by GCC and Americas; Nepal business consistent and seen as replicable model
items.quote: The international business has performed well this quarter as well as this year, and this is led by the GCC as well as Americas. Nepal has been a very consistent performance, albeit at a very small base. But the fact is that this is an experiment, which we feel very proud of.

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,332 crore via CCDs (Rs 275 crore) and warrants (Rs 1,057 crore) to fund growth for current year and next two years.
items.quote: This total capital raise of 1,332 crores, of which is 275 crores in form of CCD and 1,057 crores in form of warrant fulfils our capital need for the year, and also for the next 2 years.

items.statement: AUM growth of minimum Rs 3,000 crore per year; targeting 30-35% AUM growth with focus on higher-yielding segments.
items.quote: First and foremost, we were at Rs 3,000+ in AUM in FY22, at Rs 6,000+ in FY23, and at a Rs 9,000+ in FY24, which means this company sees minimum of Rs 3,000 crore of AUM growth.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of 40-45% over 6-8 quarters from current 54%.
items.quote: Cost to income ratio, as of now is closer to 54%, we'd like to take it to 45% which may be over 6 to 8 quarters from now, and ultimately we'll reach the desired ROA of 4%, which we believe may take around 8 quarters time.

items.statement: Micro-enterprise vertical expanding from 75 to 250 branches by year-end; micro loans at ~20% yield to drive yield expansion.
items.quote: We are going to increase that branch count to 150 now, and by end of the year it should be 250, and most of this portfolio of Rs 8 lakhs secured loans happens at around 20% yield.

items.statement: Intermediated channel share to reduce from ~50% to 40-35% over 8 quarters; direct channels (micro, machinery, retailer, digital) to increase.
items.quote: We see this going towards 40% or sub 40% in next 8 quarters.

items.statement: MyShubhLife acquisition expected to add Rs 1,500 crore AUM and Rs 100 crore incremental PAT over 3 years.
items.quote: This acquisition over the next 3 years potentially helps us acquire retailers as customers, and probably 1,500 cr in AUM at the end of 3rd year implementation, and roughly around 100 crore of incremental PAT.

items.statement: Rate reset on secured portfolio done on 25th January; full impact reflecting from March quarter.
items.quote: The reset was done on 25 th January. Since then, the entire book has been, almost the entire secured book has been reset so the numbers would continue to reflect the way they are in March.

items.statement: Expecting 50 bps cost of borrowing reduction from scale/vintage and 25-30 bps from rate cycle over 8-10 quarters.
items.quote: We are expecting that because of the increase in vintage and in scale and because of a very sizable capital raise nearly equal to our existing networth, a 50-basis point rate reduction would happen over 8 quarters, and hopefully, some bit of rate cycle change would give us additional 25 to 30 basis points decrease.

items.statement: Credit cost guided at 1.8-2% for FY25; Q4 blip due to one-off Rs 10 crore write-off on old unsecured loan.
items.quote: As per our plan and as per the way we have calibrated, we would be between for the next year we should be between 1.8% to 2% overall.

items.statement: On-book GNPA higher due to FLDG on co-origination; comfortable with on-book GNPA up to 5%.
items.quote: We are quite comfortable, and lot of our banks' covenants are basis that comfort, and we are quite comfortable to go up to 5%.

items.statement: No fresh capex needed; existing digital, physical infrastructure (105 branches to 400 in 2 years) and tech stack can support accelerated growth.
items.quote: Our existing physical infrastructure and digital infrastructure is sweating more multi products, our AUM is growing and our costs is not growing in proportion to AUM and that's the operating leverage of 50 basis point we are presuming.

items.statement: PAT growth to be significantly higher than AUM growth for next 3 years to achieve 4% ROA target.
items.quote: It's of course it is likely that our PAT growth will be higher than the AUM growth. Otherwise, this target of reaching 4% ROA cannot happen.

items.statement: Foreclosures higher than expected in Q4; quarterly AUM growth 8% vs 15% target; will correct with higher growth in high-yield segments.
items.quote: The foreclosure for us was a negative surprise, and higher than what we expected. Obviously, we'll correct that, and we will match that at higher growth rate. Quarterly growth coming at 8% rather than 15% was a function of that.

items.statement: Leverage capped at 4.5x for next 2-3 years; CRISIL upgraded rating to A/Stable in March; further upgrade expected post capital raise.
items.quote: Yeah, for next 2 to 3 years, we have not built ever more than 4 and a half times multiple leverage.

items.statement: Flares revenue expected to grow 2.5x to 3x FY24 level
items.quote: It should be anywhere in the ratio of 2.5x to 3x of what it was this year.

items.statement: Flares margin expected similar to prior expectation with slight dip due to cost overruns
items.quote: Very similar margin to what you had expected earlier. I'd say a slight dip because there are a few small cost overruns and stuff that they need to be looked at.

items.statement: Equipment margins target double-digit, can get close next year
items.quote: It will be a bit of a push, but we can get close to it. We can get close.

items.statement: Capex this year similar to last year at ~70% of prior plan, continuing for 18 months
items.quote: We have a little bit of capex, not a little bit we have. I would say 70% of the capex plan we did last year, we will have this year as well.

items.statement: Consumables volume growth ~10-12% in FY24, in line with market
items.quote: We've been seeing it in the region of 10%, 11%, 12% on the consumers front.

items.statement: Export revenue growth target 35-40% in FY25
items.quote: I do not think it is realistic to expect them to do 100% year-on-year throughout, but I definitely think that in the region of 35%, 40% is something that you can definitely put in.

items.statement: Equipment steady-state margin expected 7-9%
items.quote: So steady-state margin should be a little better than that. It should be closer to about 7%, 8%, 9%.

items.statement: Automation revenue share in equipment to rise to 25-30% in FY25 from ~12-13%
items.quote: it'll be approximately 25%, 30% of our revenue for this year on our welding equipment front.

items.statement: ONGC flare project delayed; ~INR 30-35 cr revenue pushed to FY25, execution to accelerate May-June
items.quote: what should have been approximately another INR 30 crores to INR35 crores of revenue that should have come in last year has got pushed in and will start ticking from now.

items.statement: Consumables gross margin gap vs peers 1-2% pricing, rest product mix
items.quote: It is slightly, maybe 2% -3%, 1%-2% would be pricing led, you are right. It is not a massive difference.

items.statement: Flares division strategic review after ONGC project execution in 6-8 months
items.quote: I think where we are right now is just to keep our head down and execute this project correctly as per our commitment and as per our prior achieved margins we had planned to. And I think at that time, which is another six, eight months from now, to reassess exactly the question you asked whether this makes sense as a long-term play in a large capacity or not.

items.statement: Domestic consumables volume growth ~7-8% in FY24
items.quote: On the volume basis, you are somewhere in the region of approximately, I would say 7% 8% or something like that about 7% on the consumer's part.

items.statement: Domestic consumables double-digit growth possible in FY25 barring elections
items.quote: I would assume -- elections apart and everything else apart, just regular movement of the economy the way it is, I would assume so that we would be in a position to do that, yes.

items.statement: Consumables revenue mix: stick electrodes ~58-65%, wires and flux balance
items.quote: Electrodes are probably be approximately 60%, 65% or something, 58.2% is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Project-based consumables gross margin ~100 bps lower than distributor model
items.quote: On the basis po ints difference that you see would be maybe about 100 basis points. That's fair enough

items.statement: Ador Fontech M&R products growth 8-12%, services exponential potential
items.quote: If you are looking at an e-waste, you can hit, depending on how high it is, you can hit between 8%, 10%, 12% growth on that. I think kind of well in the value mix of that going forward. On the services front, where you can take on more and more jobs and more and more competitive partner solutions, there is potential to do that exponentially if executed correctly.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 16-17% for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: This brownfield CapEx will enable us to grow by 16% to 17% in the current financial year as well as the next financial year.

items.statement: Long-term CAGR target of 15-16% for next 3-4 years

items.statement: EBITDA margin to increase by 1-1.5% by FY27-28
items.quote: As we have earlier guided, Bharatji, that after the implementation of the new projects and increase in the retail prices retail sales and exports, we will be adding another 1% to 1.5% EBITDA by financial year '27 and '28.

items.statement: FY25 capex of INR900-1,000 crore for Sanand greenfield project
items.quote: Close to INR900 crores plus CapEx will be for the Sanand project in the current year because we need to complete the Phase 1 for that project.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR500-600 crore to complete Sanand project
items.quote: Next year will be a remaining portion of INR500 crores to INR600 crores only.

items.statement: Additional INR65 crore at Chinchpada in 1-2 months; INR125 crore at Pathredi operational by June 2024

Another greenfield, brownfield expansion is going on at Pathredi with approximate cost of INR125 crores, which will increase the capacity for LT power cables approximately INR800 crores to INR900 crores per annum. items.statement: Order book of INR3,531 crore as of 30 April 2024
items.quote: The pending orders booked as on 30th A pril is approximately INR3,531 crores, out of which, EPC INR771 crores, EHV cables INR374 crores, cable from the domestic market, INR1,865 crores and export orders pending are INR521 crores

items.statement: EBITDA margin to be maintained near 11% in FY25
items.quote: Yes, margin is close to 11%, and we will be maintaining close to 11% margin in this year also.

items.statement: Copper price increases passed to customers via price variation clauses and new tenders
items.quote: And all the raw material increases, we are passing on to the customers in the new tendering. Many of the orders in our order book are already having inbuilt price variation clause.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook driven by solar, RDSS, transmission, thermal, pump storage, real estate, construction, infra

items.statement: EV charging cables added to portfolio in FY24 with commercial sales started
items.quote: We have added EV charging cables in our portfolio, and this is a factor addition in the last financial year. We have already started production and commercial sales of EV charging cables.

items.statement: EPC business to remain at 5-6% of total; focus on cable supply to EPC contractors
items.quote: EPC project, we have already reduced to the level of 5%, 6% of our total business, that we will be maintaining actually.

items.statement: Export growth driven by certifications, China+1, and sales network; major markets Australia, US, Europe, Middle East, Africa

items.statement: Volume growth of 24% in Q4 FY24 and 22% for full year FY24
items.quote: Actually, price was less. So the volume growth in the Q4 was 24%, but volume growth for the full year was 22%.

items.quote: Capacity utilized during financial year 23-24, 92% in the Cable division, 71% in the House Wire division, 90% in Stainless Steel Wire division.

items.statement: FY25 focus on increasing volume capacity utilization and improving margins

items.quote: So, I would say from those projects, so this year also we expect overall 30, 35 crores.

items.statement: Maintenance capex not more than Rs 20 crore for both plants
items.quote: The maintenance CAPEX is not more than, would not be more than 20 crores or so, for both plants.

items.quote: Export is now 30% of our overall sales.

items.quote: Look, if you would ask me on an annual basis this is really the lowest we have seen in four, five years 10, 11, four years, after four years . So, we think it is quite sustainable, we obviously endeavor is only to improve on it and yes, that's what I would say.

items.statement: Nitrile Latex EBITDA near breakeven; drag on overall margin by 2-3 percentage points
items.quote: EBITDA margin is just about breakeven if that so, that's of course being a drag.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin mid-teens when market turns and capacity utilization reaches healthy levels
items.quote: And when the market turns hopefully we will see EBITDA margins return back to sort of mid-teen levels as we expect.

items.statement: India demand good across industries; export volumes grew 71% YoY in Q4; overall volume growth 34% YoY in Q4, 28% YoY FY24

items.quote: So, synthetic latex we are 66% and rubber is 34%. Large chunk of the growth has come from the latex business this year given that both are expansion, major expansion projects or latex.

items.statement: Nitrile Latex plant at 30% avg utilization FY24; may repurpose part to SB/SA latex if margins don't improve in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: It would be one to two quarters max.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on NBR rejected by FinMin; court cases ongoing; may reapply later

Now we along with several other companies that are in the same boat had filed , or have filed cases in several courts, and those cases are ongoing So since it's sub-judice I would sort of not want to comment much on that.

items.statement: Net debt ~Rs 70 crore (term loan Rs 125 crore minus investments); long-term debt net of investments ~Rs 14 crore
items.quote: So on a net debt minus in the investments we will be around including the short term borrowing around 70 crore odd.

items.statement: Nitrile Latex revenue contribution sub-10% of total; peak revenue potential Rs 300-350 cr at 50k tpa, plus Rs 230-250 cr from 35k tpa expansion
items.quote: Revenue contribution from our Nitrile Latex segment probably around 10%, 12%, between 10% and 15%, lower digit 10%, 12%. Sachin do you have a exact data? Sachin Karwa: Yes, it’s sub 10

items.statement: Management hopes to grow top line around 20% in FY25
items.quote: We certainly hope to grow at 20% around in terms of top line.

items.statement: Building material revenue target of INR 170 crore by Q4 FY25 at peak utilization
items.quote: By Q4 in the current financial year, we should be inching towards optimum utilization of the whole capacity we have.

items.statement: Aspiring to touch double-digit EBITDA margins in building material segment at INR 160-170 crore revenue
items.quote: We are aspiring touch double digits in building material itself.

items.statement: Expect double-digit YoY growth in agriculture segment for Q1 FY25
items.quote: For agriculture, we would certainly be able to demonstrate a double-digit growth.

items.quote: So for a 20,000 around capacity plan, because it will have agriculture as well as building material pipes requirements. So there will be about CapEx of about INR 35 crores, INR 40 crores minimum to begin with.

items.statement: Agriculture segment has continuous daily order inflow through dealer network
items.quote: In agriculture, every day there is a continuous order inflow because we have dealers. So there is always continuous order inflow and supplies.

items.statement: Building material margins currently suppressed due to high marketing expenses per unit; will improve as volumes ramp up
items.quote: Once the volume of building products grows, our expenses will be distributed in a higher base. And that's where the margins will improve.

items.statement: Targeting 12% EBITDA margin in building material at INR 170-180 crore revenue scale
items.quote: We internally look at 12% margin once we reach that number on building material.

items.statement: Agriculture demand robust with affordable prices and good top-line traction
items.quote: The demand scenario looks to be fairly good because prices are affordable and we are seeing good traction on the top line.

items.statement: Building material showing 23% QoQ volume growth in Q4 FY24
items.quote: If you compare our sales in Q3 to Q4 in building materials, it is about 23% growth QoQ.

items.statement: Building material capacity of 9,000-10,000 tons can generate INR 170-180 crore revenue at peak utilization
items.quote: We can easily scale it up 1.5x times. So it will be about 9,000 tons to 10,000 tons.

items.statement: Agriculture growth constrained by single-location logistics; multilocation expansion needed for faster growth
items.quote: Unless you go multilocation, the volume growth will have to be within a range of what we are achieving.

items.statement: Raw material prices down 35-40% vs FY22 CapEx announcement, reducing revenue value per ton
items.quote: Prices of material if you see prevailing at that time and prices of material prevailing now, there is a reduction of about 35%, 40% in terms of the raw material base price.

items.statement: Management expects 100-150 bps consolidated EBITDA margin improvement from Q4 FY24 level
items.quote: I think consol level the margins which you see right now we are expecting at least 150 basis points improvement in overall margin at this level.

items.statement: Auto/non-auto mix target of 70-30 first then 60-40 over 4-5 years
items.quote: my auto and non-auto will be 70-30 is the first target, then 60-40 over a period of 4 to 5 years. So, we stick to that guidance.

items.statement: Net asset turnover target of 2.5-3x in next 2-3 years
items.quote: we have already given guidance that we will be somewhere around 2.5 to 3 on net asset turnover in the next two to three-year time.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated capex of INR 400+ crores including Mexico plant and brownfield expansion
items.quote: cumulatively, we are looking at almost INR 400 plus crores of capex this year. That includes standalone on the RKFL side in terms of addition of capacities in the Mexico venture as well as in the capacity in a brownfield activity in our current Plant.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of INR 40-50 crores annually
items.quote: So it should be around INR 40 Crores to INR 50 Crores every year on the maintenance side.

items.statement: USD 220 million contract over 10 years for light vehicle segment in North America
items.quote: The Company achieved a significant contract worth USD 220 Million, that will be executed over a period of 10 years, making our entry to a new vertical within forging sector, the strategic move focus on supplying Tier 1 customers in the light vehicle segment across North America

items.statement: Vande Bharat train set order worth INR 270 crores to be supplied by FY26

items.quote: right now, PV is close to 2% or 2.5% passenger vehicle. We expect a double-digit PV in next two years' time with the current order wins and the order wins, which we have had totally, I think going forward, we should look at a double-digit PV in next two years time.

items.quote: in next 3 to 5 years, we are looking at almost 60%, 40% i.e 60% automotive and 40% on non-automotive. That the Company aspires to and we are working very diligently to achieve this. And out of this railway is going to be biggest element of growth going into next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Domestic CV industry expected to grow 10-12% in coming year
items.quote: in the coming year, we could see at least 10% to 12% growth in the industry.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin around 50% with per tonne EBITDA similar to last quarter

items.statement: Export margins 100-200 bps higher than domestic margins

items.quote: this quarter, it is higher by INR 17 Crores from the previous quarter.

items.statement: Management does not provide formal revenue or margin guidance for FY25 or FY26
