items.quote: We see some price hike happening in the festival period. Generally, media pricing happened -- it's a supply and demand case. The pricing yield will depend on that. And we believe some bit of pricing hike happening in the second half of the year.

items.quote: Our radio contribution used to be 65% to 70%. We believe radio contribution will come down in this year and next year to about 50% to 55%. Digital ambition is today -- this Q4, our digital revenues are almost 25% of our radio revenues.

items.quote: We believe Gaana will become breakeven in 2 to 3 years' time. Until that time, it's going to be an investment. I don't see it as a loss, but it's an investment in a product, which we believe will deliver great results for us as a company.

items.statement: International markets turned EBITDA positive in FY24 at INR 7.4 crores
items.quote: Another heartening development is that our international market turned positive during FY '24 and reported an EBITDA of INR 7.4crores.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain margins around current 14% levels, with slight improvement possible through operating leverage and utilization gains.

items.statement: Optimistic on market sentiment improving in second half of calendar year 2024; seeing green shoots in deal sizes and decision-making duration.

items.statement: Focus on cloud, data, AI, and Salesforce driving higher quality revenue; new offerings in generative AI and smart manufacturing rolled out.
items.quote: Overall, the quality of revenue has improved with our focus on doing more with cloud, data and A I. Leading our value propositions with cloud data and AI has led to better quality of deals, which is reflected in the quality of revenue that we are reporting now

items.statement: Investing in sales, marketing, and leadership (Chief Customer Officer, Chief Marketing Officer); more middle-tier talent additions planned through the year.
items.quote: We will continue to invest in bringing some focused talent around sales and marketing because we had promised we will continue to invest in sales and marketing as we develop our go-to-market motion.

items.statement: Strong sales funnel at mid-to-late stage; deals above $1M ACV growing consistently quarter-on-quarter; working with double-digit Blackstone portfolio clients.
items.quote: Our deals which are above $1 million in ACV or above $2 million or $3 million in ACV or beyond, have continued to grow consistently quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Funding drought for US tech/startup clients persists; no immediate reversal expected; churn from R&D budget cuts elevated but hoped to stabilize.

items.statement: No explicit revenue guidance provided; aim to grow faster than industry average and at par with best performers.
items.quote: We don't provide guidance. But we have consistently mentioned that we are tracking ourselves closely with the industry and industry peers. And our ambition, our goal is to grow at least faster than the industry average and hopefully, at par with some of the best performing players in the industry.

items.statement: Velotio acquisition is growth and margin accretive; integrated business showing positive momentum and better margins in Pune center.
items.quote: Velotio has been both growth and margin accretive for us. So, that the business is integrated with ours, we have seen that bring positive growth momentum to our overall business and to the portion of business which we execute out of Pune.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with IIT Delhi for joint COE on applied AI and sustainable solutions signed in February 2024.
items.quote: We have also signed a strategic partnership with IIT Delhi. This is something we did in January or rather, February this year to create a joint COE for research towards applied AI and sustainable solutions.

items.statement: Organic growth flattened in Q1; expects positive organic growth in next two quarters with both QoQ and YoY improvement.
items.quote: Q1 trend has sort of flattened out, and we are seeing a positive impact coming towards the future. We are seeing positive organic growth. Hopefully in the next 2 quarters, we will start seeing both quarter-on-quarter, year-on-year positive organic growth impact as well.

items.statement: RSU expense of Rs 6.5 crore booked in Q1; future RSU grants for new hires will be minimal and spread over 7 years.

items.statement: Telecom sector resilient but not growing significantly; operators struggling to monetize 5G spend, causing some technology expense squeeze.
items.quote: If you look at in the last 4, 5 quarters after the 5G spectrum, a lot of operators have spent a lot of money on 5G spectrum. They are struggling to monetize. And that has resulted in some amount of expense squeeze of what these operators spend on technology or refreshing their technology, etc., which has some impact on us.

items.statement: No bonus issue planned; capital allocation via dividends continues; board decides on form of shareholder returns.
items.quote: We have never issued bonus in the past since the IPO. Currently, there is no such plan. Whenever there is any such thing, we will inform the stock exchanges.

items.statement: Expecting 35% EBITDA margin and 25% PAT margin in FY25

items.statement: Targeting ₹2,000 crores revenue by FY27 with 50% CAGR from FY25
items.quote: We have said that there will be a CAGR of 50% from next year, FY27 will be ₹ 2,000 crores that's right.

items.statement: Order book surpassing ₹1,400 crores as of 31st March 2024
items.quote: Our order book position is surpassing ₹ 1,400 crores as on 31 st March and this positioning as far as sustained growth for FY25.

items.quote: We expect it to be replenished between ₹ 1200 to 1300 crores so that next year we have set an internal target.

items.statement: R&D spend expected around ₹30 crores in FY25, may increase opportunistically
items.quote: FY25 R&D we are expecting to be in the tune of around 30 crores but again, you should not hold me to it because we are a very opportunistically our investment R&D company.

items.statement: Shareholder approval obtained for QIP up to ₹1,000 crores for inorganic acquisition; no target identified yet
items.quote: We have taken permission to raise up to, place up to the ₹ 1,000 crores. But, we have not yet identified any target and when and if the things become clear we may raise the bid of the, we may go for the QIP.

items.quote: Considering these three factors that we understand that this raw material cost will be around in the range of 35% to 40% we need to consider on that.

items.statement: Export order book ~₹400+ crores out of ₹1,400 crores; expecting ~35% export contribution in FY25

items.quote: We didn't do any exports in the Q4 actually, that's why we did not report anything. There were no exports in Q4, all the sales were domestic sales. But, in the forthcoming quarters you will see a significant export figures coming.

items.statement: Strong demand for anti-drone systems and simulators domestically and internationally; Middle East showing robust demand
items.quote: Exhibition we received very positive response and very robust demand was seen there and that is one of the reasons after visiting there, we had lot of request for collaboration and developing the product in, we went for this world differential in Saudi Arabia.

items.statement: New products to be announced in weeks/months; will enhance existing anti-drone and simulator lines or target adjacent markets
items.quote: We are going to announce in the next, few months, weeks and months some new product, very interesting range of products and that should the end users not only in India, but worldwide will find them very interesting.

items.statement: Working capital cycle sustainable at 140-160 days; Q4 FY24 at 148 days due to higher sales and inventory build for FY25 execution
items.quote: That we would say this is sustainable going forward also our working capital cycle will be in the range of 140 to 160 days, this is number one.

items.statement: Order book entirely from government (Indian or foreign); virtually no private orders

items.quote: For creation, onetime charge of INR20 is levied on the insurance company. So these are the 2 recurring charges which are charged to the insurance companies and not to the policyholders.

items.statement: Other income breakdown: ECAS charges INR9.37 crore, e-voting charges INR4.42 crore, plus miscellaneous user facility and account maintenance charges
items.quote: other income largely consists of ECAS charges of INR9.37 crores, e-voting charges of INR4.42 crores and miscellaneous income in terms of user facility charges, account maintenance charges and similar income heads.

items.statement: Impairment cost INR8 crore for full year FY24; Q4 saw reversal of INR1.11 crore
items.quote: impairment cost is INR8 crores for the full financial year on impairment. And for the quarter, we have a reversal of INR1.11 crores.

items.statement: Technology cost increased from INR38 crore to INR63.3 crore in FY24; includes infrastructure, applications, security, network and insurance repository tech
items.quote: from INR38 crores, it's Central Depository Services ( going to INR63 crores is a meaningful jump in the current year. So the INR63 crores also included, included repository tech, insurance repository tech costs because you wanted to scale it up given the regulations are coming

items.statement: Management transition process underway; shortlist submitted to SEBI, confidential, timeline dependent on SEBI
items.quote: So the process is on. It's a confidential list. And whenever there is a SEBI kind of a standard operating procedure at the time when it is required to be announced, CDSL would promptly announce that.

items.statement: Pricing risk exists but depository pricing approved by SEBI; future regulatory changes uncertain
items.quote: I think the cost, the pricing is approved by SEBI in case of depositories. So, it's taken on record and then it's taken forward from there. So, I think we'll see how it goes forward.

items.statement: Transaction charges comprise debit charges, pledge and margin pledge charges; not solely delivery-based
items.quote: the transaction charges consist of debit charges, pledge and margin pledge charges. So it's a combination of various other transactions which are happening.

items.statement: Technology capacity not linked to demat count alone; must support new products like T+0, AIF processing, multi-language eCAS
items.quote: It is not just folios and demat accounts. There are a lot of new products. For example, T+0 has come in. That will need new processes and new in AIF processing has come in. So it's not just a simplistic answer that how many folios you can do or etc.

items.statement: KYC records created and fetched grew substantially in FY24, driving KYC income growth
items.quote: both the number of records created and a number of records fetched have gone up substantially, which added to the overall KYC income.

items.statement: CDSL does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance; no forward-looking numbers given for folios, unlisted opportunity, insurance, or tech spend
items.quote: CDSL does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance. Anything said on this call, which reflects CDSL's outlook for the future or which could be constituted as forward-looking statements must be reviewed in conjunction with the risks that company faces.

items.statement: Single demat account aggregator model evolving; long-term proposition, framework uncertain
items.quote: I think the account aggregator model is in the process is getting picked up. So, we'll see how it goes forward, how that will get linked to a single demat. This is a very long-term kind of proposition.

items.statement: T+0 settlement in beta phase with 25 scrips; expansion dependent on SEBI review of participation and issues
items.quote: if you see the SEBI press release, it clearly talks about this is regular beta phase. And they will see how many people have participated. Has there been any issues, et cetera. And based on that, we said we will take that call whether it has to be increased in what framework to how many stocks, et cetera.

items.statement: EBIT margin guidance of 12% to 13% maintained for next 12-24 months
items.quote: we've been saying consistently. I think both Ashok and I and all of us have been saying that 12% to 13% is a reasonable expectation to have for the EBIT margin. And annually, I would still say we are staying with that point of view.

items.statement: Jewellery EBIT margin dropped 140 bps for full year and 110 bps in Q4 due to competitive intensity and gold price impact
items.quote: this year, yes, in the current quarter, there has been, let's say, a gross margin, which is lower than what we would usually deliver in a studded quarter, studded intensive quarter.

items.statement: Jewellery margin improvement expected from Q2 FY25 onwards as gold price impact corrects
items.quote: I'm hoping that from quarter 2 onwards, we'll start seeing some improvement because some of these efforts require -- take time.

items.statement: Watches margin decline due to wearables pricing pressure and higher advertising spend
items.quote: we did prioritize growth, and we have got 19% growth in sales and for doing that, I think we've invested a lot more in advertising, which is more than 40% growth.

items.statement: Watches margin expected to improve in FY25 as operating leverage flows through
items.quote: for this financial year, we continue to push the pedal on Revenue growth, but also put a lot of focus and attention on managing costs much better, so that the overall benefit and the operating leverage actually flows through to the profit line.

items.statement: Competitive intensity in jewellery to continue; consumer sentiment soft due to elevated gold prices
items.quote: competitive intensity will continue, and we will continue to invest in growth and respond accordingly in the marketplace to ensure that we continue to gain market share.

items.statement: Jewellery discounting driven more by gold price volatility than demand weakness
items.quote: I would say greater emphasis on the gold price increase because we didn't see it all the time, not the entire quarter. It is -- it became particular only when gold prices were jumping up significantly.

items.statement: Studded ratio stable at 33% in Q4 despite gold price inflation
items.quote: studded ratio being constant in spite of sharp inflation in gold prices. Because in Q3, there was a 200 bps drop. This time, it is stable at 33%.

items.statement: High value studded grew to 14% contribution in Q4 from 13% last year; targeting aggressive growth
items.quote: high value studded the way we've defined it has done well for us. The price bands that we look at consistently over the last several years, we have continued to gain. And even in the quarter, it was a 14% contribution compared to 13% last year in the same quarter.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds not yet significant in India; monitoring U.S. market stress and early adopters
items.quote: so far, we have not seen any significant traction, though there is some traction at the margin, but it is very small. In the 3 years period, how it will emerge is very difficult to conclude.

items.statement: Tanishq added 46-47 stores in FY24; sees opportunity to expand beyond 300 towns
items.quote: we have added in the current year several stores, in fact, 46 or 47 new stores in Tanishq. And of course, Mia, we've added 67 and CaratLane also has continued to add quite a few 50-odd stores.

items.statement: International jewellery targeting ~30 stores across North America and GCC from current 16
items.quote: from the 16 stores, we are looking to get to something like around 30 stores across both North America as well as the GCC region.

items.statement: Gold exchange contributed 31% of non-Tanishq gold sales in FY24; total exchange ~40-41% of sales
items.quote: Last year, gold exchange, excluding the -- this is the non-Tanishq gold, was 30% contributor to sales. This year, it was -- in FY24, it was 31%. So there was a 1% improvement. And Tanishq exchange also does pretty well. So at an overall level, exchange gold accounts were about 40% - 41% of our total sales.

items.statement: Long-term debt of INR 3,000 crores for CaratLane acquisition to be repaid in 18 and 24 months
items.quote: We have a long-term debt of about INR 3,000 crores, which is squarely linked to our acquisition of CaratLane balance stake. And if you would have noticed that the term for that NCD, which we took is 18 months and 24 months.

items.statement: Zoya MRP turnover just under INR 300 crores in FY24, up from INR 60-65 crores 4 years ago
items.quote: Zoya, we have ended the year with an MRP turnover, not NSV, MRP turnover of just under INR 300 crores. 4 years ago, it was around INR 60-65 crores.

items.statement: Demand growth in India for FY25 expected to be better than FY24's 2.7%
items.quote: We definitely see that next year '24-25 the demand growth will better as compared to '23-24.

items.statement: Greenfield soda ash project capex ~Rs 4,000 cr over next 3 years; vacuum salt ~Rs 150-170 cr and bromine ~Rs 115-120 cr
items.quote: If you look at the investment into the bromine project which is very hardly around 115-120 crores kind of a thing and in vacuum salt is roughly around 150 to 170 crores. So, put together both, we are talking about 300. So, the major growth investment which is coming into the greenfield project which is around 4,000 crores and that also will be happening in next 3 years of time.

items.statement: Maintenance and smaller expansion capex ~Rs 250 cr per year for FY25 and FY26 excluding greenfield
items.quote: Next year also '25-26 other than the greenfield project completion of vacuum salt and bromine and some maintenance. This will be in the range of around 250 crores kind of a situation every year kind of a situation.

items.statement: India soda ash demand projected to grow from ~4.3 mt to ~7 mt in next 5-7 years
items.quote: If you take that into account, there is a kind of a projection which we have is the demand which is around 4.3 million tons which is likely to be around 7 million tons in next 5 to 7 years of time.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 23.9% vs 20.3% in Q3 FY24; improvement due to higher volume and lower input cost
items.quote: For the quarter, the EBITDA margin came at 23.9% compared to 32.5% in the corresponding quarter of last year and 20.3% in Q3 of the current year.

items.statement: Realizations in Q4 FY24 lower than Q3 FY24; EBITDA per ton slightly better due to cost control
items.quote: In terms of the realization yes, the realization was lower as compared to the last quarter, Q3 of '24, it was lower. And EBITDA was slightly better because of the better cost control.

items.statement: Global soda ash demand ex-China fell 3.2% in CY23; CY24 likely similar growth ~2.5%; no major capacity additions in CY25-26
items.quote: Calendar Year 2024 is likely to be dull year, but I believe it should not be worse than Calendar Year 2023 and growth will be similar of Calendar Year 2023 at about 2.5%.

items.statement: Sodium bicarbonate capacity expanded; expect significant utilization growth in FY25 and possible further expansion
items.quote: You will see in '24-25, the demand expansion happening into the sodium bicarbonate. And probably '24-25 we will have a significant amount of growth into our utilization of '24-25 and hopefully the full utilization and probably maybe we will be looking at a few more expansion into the sodium bicarbonate in next year probably.

items.statement: Bromine project ~2,800 tpa capacity, ~Rs 120 cr capex, IRR 18-20%, revenue ~Rs 60-63 cr
items.quote: The preparation was going on in this and just to kind of give you like I said, approximately the investment is around 120 crores, and we will be producing something around 2,800 tons and our IRR will be roughly around 18% to 20% kind of IRR will be there.

items.statement: Turkey imports into India temporary; will redirect to Europe when European demand recovers
items.quote: Turkey supply which you are getting into the Indian market is a temporary phenomenon. Because for them the natural market is the Europe market. The moment the Europe recovers all the volume or majority of the volume of Turkey will go to that market.

items.statement: Prices have bottomed out; near-term range-bound realizations; upside possible if opportunity arises
items.quote: I think prices of that trajectory has bottomed out. This would be in the range bound kind of a situation on this pricing. This is a way we look at this point of time.

items.statement: Greenfield project timeline ~3 years from now; final approvals in last leg; physical activity to start in few months
items.quote: I think the projection at this point of a time is likely to take around 3 years of time from now onwards to complete this kind of a massive project.

items.statement: Net cash surplus ~Rs 701 cr at FY24 end; gross debt Rs 197 cr, cash Rs 898 cr; peak debt/equity <0.5x for greenfield
items.quote: We are a net debt-free Company and our gross debt stood at 197 crores with cash and cash equivalent of Rs. 898 crores resulting in a net cash surplus of around 701 crores at the year end.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend Rs 12/share (120% of face value, 20% of net profit)
items.quote: Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 12 per equity share of Rs. 10 each which is 120% of the paid capital and 20% of our net profit.

items.statement: Salt yield improvement benefits accruing gradually over 3-4 years; some benefit in FY24, more in FY25
items.quote: No, it started happening like last year also we got some improvement, this year we will get another improvement on that, and this will be journey like I said in the past also 3-4 years of time.

items.statement: Expects telecom equipment revenue of ~Rs 2,000 cr in FY25 vs Rs 150 cr in FY24
items.quote: We expect the revenue from this segment during FY 25 will reach to approximately Rs.2000 Crores from Rs.150 Crores of FY 24.

items.statement: Expects optical fiber cable revenue of >Rs 2,000 cr in FY25
items.quote: we expect a revenue again more than INR2,000 crores in the current financial year from optical fibe r cable business

items.statement: Expects turnkey project revenue of Rs 1,750-2,000 cr in FY25
items.quote: current year, we are looking at turnkey projects of about INR1,250 crores plus INR500 crores, about INR1,750 crores to INR2,000 crores

items.statement: Expects OFC demand recovery from Q2 FY25
items.quote: We are confident that OFC demand will be restored from Q2 FY 25 onwards in both India and key global markets.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 7,685 cr as of 31 Mar 2024
items.quote: Our order book now stands at INR 7685 crs as of 31st March 2024 as compared to INR 7010 crs last year.

items.statement: Incremental order book added in FY24 ~Rs 3,725 cr
items.quote: During FY24, the Company added an incremental order book of ~INR 3725 Crores comprising of products orders worth more than ~INR 1500 Crores and System Integration orders worth ~INR 2225 Crores.

items.statement: Has >Rs 1,700 cr orders in hand for telecom equipment
items.quote: Of the INR2,000 crores revenue I'm expecting, we have more than INR1,500 worth of order already in our hands, more than that, about INR1,700 crores.

items.statement: Has ~Rs 1,200 cr turnkey orders in hand
items.quote: On turnkey business, we already have orders worth of about INR1,200 crores in hand.

items.statement: Poland OFC plant investment up to Euro 15.9 mn (Rs 144 cr) for 3.25 mn fkm capacity
items.quote: HFCL has committed an initial investment of up to Euro 15.9 million (INR 144 crores) for its Poland optical fiber cable manufacturing plant with an initial capacity of 3.25 million fiber km

items.statement: Poland plant targets production start from April next financial year
items.quote: 3.25 million capacity, we are targeting to start manufacturing from April of next financial year.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin 15-17% in FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin would be something like, I would say, 15% or so. 15% to 17% depending upon order to order and the situation.

items.statement: BharatNet Phase III tender ~Rs 60,000 cr capex over 3 years + Rs 40,000 cr O&M over 10 years
items.quote: One of the most anticipated opportunitie s on the horizon is the government’s ambitious Bharat Net Phase III project under which BSNL has already floated approximately Rs.60,000 crore tender for capex to be incurred in next 3 years followed by additional O&M opportunity worth approximately Rs.40,000 crore over a period of 10 years

items.statement: Product revenue mix to shift to >2/3 of total revenue in FY25
items.quote: would mean that our revenue would consist of more than two third of the product driven and less than one third of project driven

items.statement: Debt-equity to stay 0.24-0.30; capex funded by internal accruals, equity raise done, and part debt
items.quote: debt equity ratio, which is currently 0.24, it will remain in the same range. I mean, 0.24 to maybe 0.27, and max it be will 0.30, not more than that.

items.statement: Expect 8-10% volume growth and 8-10% EBITDA per ton growth in FY25
items.quote: In terms of volume, we are expecting 8% to 10% growth. And in EBITDA per ton also, we are expecting an 8% to 10% growth next financial year.

items.statement: Mukutban volume target of 2.7 million tons for FY25
items.quote: In Mukutban, we are expecting to have a volume of about 2.7 million tons.

items.statement: Total incentives guided at INR 100-110 crores for FY25 including all plants
items.quote: Overall, incentives next year will be around INR100 crores -- INR110 crores, including the other plants.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 800 crores for FY25 split across sustenance, coal mines, and Kundanganj line 3
items.quote: See, out of the INR800 crores, we plan to spend about INR400 crores on sustenance capex, about INR200 crores on the development of coal mines and another INR 200 crores on Kundanganj line three.

items.statement: Net debt expected to close below INR 3,000 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: And as a result, net debt number, we expect to close that number below INR3,000 by the end of next year.

items.statement: Premium sales grew from 51% to 54% of total volumes in FY24
items.quote: And certainly, in our premium sales, which is really a function of the trade sales, we have had a growth from 51% to 54% in terms of percenta ge growth

items.statement: Q4 demand driven by infra and commercial segments; trade segment grew only 2%
items.quote: Actually, in the quarter 4, if you look at the entire industry, the demand mostly came from the Infra and Commercial segments.

items.statement: Competition in central markets depends on capacity additions and player behavior; too early to predict
items.quote: This year, it's too early to predict. It all depends on how the growth happens in the next 2 quarters, especially the capacities having come up.

items.statement: Pricing discipline maintained due to 100% capacity utilization in core markets and premium focus
items.quote: Our strategy is very clear. We do not have in these markets any anxiety for volumes, because we do not -- our capacity utilization is 100% in the key markets, which are our core markets of Central India.

items.statement: Freight cost optimization is market-specific; focus on net realization rather than absolute freight reduction
items.quote: We look at our net realization. So if you see a Mukutban situation, obviously, there, we will have to now spread ourselves further. So you may not get a freight cost reduction in Mukutban.

items.statement: Bikram coal mine expected in Q4 FY25; Marki Barka in FY26/27
items.quote: See, Bikram, we are expecting in Q4 of FY '25. And Marki Barka, we are expecting in FY '26/'27.

items.statement: Bikram coal mine savings to start from FY26 after ramp-up phase
items.quote: In this year, we don't envisage much savings, because it is in a ramp-up phase. The savings will start acquiring from next financial year.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 600 crores in FY24 to INR 3,003 crores
items.quote: About INR600 crores compared to last year.

items.statement: Fuel cost in Q4 was INR 1.56/Kcal, ahead of guidance
items.quote: And our fuel cost in Q4 was INR1.56/Kcal, of course, leading to your guidance.

items.statement: No clinker capacity expansion planned; only announced grinding unit expansion
items.quote: First of all, I would request you again to keep your questions to only one question because others don't get a chance. But since you have already asked it, we have stated that our clinker capacity expansion is not going to come just now. So there's no plan for clinker capacity.

items.statement: Price outlook uncertain due to elections, heat, and monsoon; last quarter saw unexpected price decline
items.quote: This quarter is affected by elections, extreme heat in most of the country. And once the elections and everything is over, it will probably take a little while for the economic condition to stabilize.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected in 16-17% range
items.quote: earlier were expecting it in the ran ge of 15, now we expect it will be in the range of —16- 17 because there are a lot of initiatives that is being taken on cost control, on cost reduction, on innovation, on improvement , productivity

items.statement: Volume growth expected at 10-15% for FY25
items.quote: It would be more modest; it will be more in the range of 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Capex budget for FY25 estimated at 500-600 crores
items.quote: We expect the CAPEX spends to be a modest 500-600 crores this year.

items.statement: Order book stands at $1.5 billion with 30% export and 70% domestic
items.quote: The order book is a robust $1.5 billion , out of which export is 30% , domestic 70%.

items.statement: ROCE improved to around 20%
items.quote: The ROCE has improved. The ROCE is now in the range of 20.

items.statement: Raw material prices expected to stay in current band: iron ore $100-120, coal around $250 for 6-8 months
items.quote: The raw material prices if you see we expect them to move in a current band, iron ore between 100 to 120 but we don't import any. Domestically we are able to source iron ore at $80, 5,000 to 6,000 which is a good thing for us and we expect we'll continue to do that. Coal will remain around 250 and that should continue at least for the next 6 to 8 months is what our understanding.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility for 3-5 years driven by water infra and industrial growth
items.quote: So next now 3 to 5 years we do have certain confidence, we have certain visibility of good performance moving forward.

items.statement: QIP of 1,000 crores unlikely; enabling resolution for 1,000 crores debt instrument approved
items.quote: I can let you know that now it looks like the QIP may not happen. On the contrary yesterday we have taken again an enabling resolution from the board and we are going to take it to the shareholders 1,000 crores of a debt instrument.

items.statement: Middle East conflict escalation could disrupt shipping and demand in the region
items.quote: Only point of concern is a Middle East conflict if it gets blown into a full-fledged war then there could be disruptions in the area.

items.statement: Successfully extruded 13 Chrome Inconel, only Indian company with this capability
items.quote: I am very happy to let you know that in our stainless , we have now successfully extruded 13 Chrome Inconel which are very exotic, and we would be the only one in the country who would be able to do that.

items.statement: Prepaying entire 1,000 crore acquisition loan for Sathavahana during calendar year 2024
items.quote: I am very happy to announce that this year , we are prepaying the entire loan of that 1,000 crores even though it was an acquisition funding long term. But now we have a strategy in place where we want to prepay, already the prepayment has started April onwards and during this calendar year we would prepay the entire 1,000 crores

items.statement: Consolidated ROC to incrementally keep growing and cross 20% mark in next 2 years
items.quote: I am confident that given the multiple growth engines, we should see strong growth for 25 and our ROC to incrementally keep growing and cross the 20% mark in the next 2 years.

items.statement: India operations CAPEX about Rs. 500 crores for FY25
items.quote: So, it would be about 500 crores.

items.statement: Overseas entities CAPEX about $65 million for FY25 mainly towards US Aluminum Phase 2 and maintenance CAPEX in Europe
items.quote: For the next year, the CAPEX for overseas entities would be about $65 million, which is mainly towards the US Aluminum Phase 2 and some maintenance CAPEX in Europe.

items.statement: Consolidated CAPEX for FY25 expected to be about Rs. 800 to 1,000 crores
items.quote: Yes, about I would say 800 to 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Defense order book Rs. 5,200 crores execution timeline 3 to 4 years
items.quote: Some of it is 3 years. Some of it is 4 years.

items.statement: New business secured worth almost Rs. 6,300 crores across all key businesses in FY24
items.quote: During the year, the company secured new business worth almost Rs. 6,300 crores across all key businesses including defense, traditional busine ss as well as the casting business

items.statement: European aluminum business will be profitable in 2025 at both EBITDA and PBT level
items.quote: So, I would say that the European aluminum business will be profitable in 2025, both at EBITDA and at PBT level.

items.statement: US operations to see positive EBITDA in Q4 FY25
items.quote: But I think we have a handle on that, and we should see even the US operations with the positive EBITDA in Quarter 4, healthy, profitable EBITDA in Quarter 4.

items.statement: Overseas subsidiaries to reach double-digit EBITDA margin by exit of FY25
items.quote: Definitely in a double digit. I would say definitely double digit at the EBITDA level, yes.

items.statement: US truck market outlook reasonably optimistic with stability expected
items.quote: And everybody is talking about a reasonably optimistic scenario, which does not mean necessarily growth, but stability. And that is what we are following. That is also what we are seeing in our order book.

items.statement: Domestic CV space expected to be flat compared to last year
items.quote: We are expecting it to be flat as compared to last year.

items.statement: JS Auto business to double over next 4 years with 30% YoY growth over last 2 years
items.quote: This business will double over the next four years, mo st probably double or more than double over the next 4 years

items.statement: Aerospace business expected to double in next 3-4 years from roughly Rs. 300 crores revenue
items.quote: So, I expect in the next 3-4 years or 3 years also to double this growth.

items.statement: Oil and gas contribution about Rs. 300 crores in FY24, expected to go up slightly in FY25 with new products
items.quote: It's about 300 crores right now. I think we expect this to go up a little bit this year because we have new products that we are developing which we haven't supplied before.

items.statement: Defense business moving entirely to 100% owned subsidiary KSSL in FY25 once new facilities commissioned and licenses transferred
items.quote: The defense business will move entirely into the 100% owned subsidiary K SSL in FY25 once the new facilities are fully commissioned and the licenses get transferred to those physical facilities

items.statement: Two new sunrise sectors identified, expected to ramp up from next year and become meaningful by FY27
items.quote: We have made initial breakthroughs in two new sunrise sectors, and we expect that these will become large growth sectors for us going forward and this will ramp up from next year, but we will become meaningful by about FY27.

items.statement: Target 10% top-line growth in FY25 despite 5-8% negative rate variance; aim to cross 14% EBITDA margin and reach 15% if stable
items.quote: So considering that negative rate variance, we would target to reach like 10% top line growth. We will target that in spite of negative rate variance. And as far as EBITDA is concerned, so we are now more and more confident that we should be crossing the 14% mark at the company level. And slowly, if the situation continues to be stable, then probably we'll try to reach the 15% mark.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin 15.5-16% at INR4,000 cr turnover; implies EBITDA doubling in three years
items.value: EBITDA margin 15.5-16% at INR4,000 cr revenue
items.quote: And the steady - state EBITDA, if everything goes wel l, should be in the range of 15.5% to 16% at a turnover of INR4,000 crores

items.statement: FY25 capex budget INR200-250 cr for two greenfield projects; FY26 onward mainly maintenance INR150-200 cr plus formulation oncology
items.quote: So that spill over c apex would be there for FY '25. And we are estimating, we have set the budget of around INR200 crores to INR250 crores for the coming financial year that is FY '24-'25

items.statement: Oncology formulation pipeline: 12-14 oral molecules filing over 6-18 months; target INR300-350 cr additional revenue in 24-36 months
items.quote: We are developing about 12 to 14 oral oncology molecules, which would all come into filing over the next 6 to 18 months. And many of them are kind of day one launches with patents expiring from '25 till '27, '28.

items.statement: Gross contribution expected to improve ~1% to at least 35% from current just below 34% with stable API selling prices
items.quote: So with the current selling prices of API, we expect that the gross contribution should go at least till the level of 35%. And right now, it is somewhere just below 34%. So we hope that around 1% more improvement should be there as far as gross contribution is concerned.

items.statement: API prices stabilized after December quarter; only risk is crude above USD100 pushing up solvent and KSM costs (65-70% RM crude-linked)
items.quote: Then from December to March quarter, the prices have almost stabilized now, so they are not falling further. However, recently, we saw some uptick in the crude prices. So if the crude goes beyond a certain point, then definitely that will start -- that uptick will start slipping into the prices of crude derivatives like solvents, which we use.

items.statement: Export volume declined ~10% in FY24; expect recovery on interest rate cuts, low stocks, government tenders; domestic volume grew 16-17%
items.quote: Because export market we saw a degrowth of almost around 15% for the last quarter, whereas for the domestic market, it was almost flat, means there was hardly 1% decline was there.

items.statement: Formulation margin improvement driven by shift from domestic CMO to higher-margin export business in LatAm, Africa, regulated markets; 20%+ margin sustainable
items.quote: So as a conscious decision, we are trying to replace our domestic CMO business to more of value-added export business in Latin America, Asia, Africa and now increasingly in the regulated markets. So as in every year, every quarter, our international markets contribution to sales is increasing. And majorly, that is what is leading to the higher margins.

items.statement: Geopolitical tension in Middle East could renew dollar shortages and disrupt export demand; FDA import alert on API plant unresolved, inspection hoped by Sep'24
items.quote: What we need to be watchful was -- is current geopolitical tension in the Middle East. More and more countries should not get involved in the conflict, otherwise, with total -- then the situation might be little dicey.

items.statement: Dermatology greenfield at Tarapur: final capacity 2,000 TPM, ramping through H1 FY25; Sayakha specialty chemicals greenfield to commence end Q1 FY25, scale up Q4 FY25

items.statement: CXM vertical mix: BFSI ~60-65%, healthcare growing; EXM top sectors IT/ITES and manufacturing; no significant logo losses
items.quote: As far as the new business acquisition in CXM, I think it's a mix of both. So, as I mentioned, BFSI and Healthcare are two of our key verticals in CXM of which BFSI is almost about 60%-65% as of now, but with the growth in healthcare which has happened this year, that number will come down.

items.statement: Q4 collections INR 131.4 cr, up INR 7.1 cr QoQ; cash position robust
items.quote: Our collections for Quarter 4 increased to 131.4 crores up by 7.1 crores quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR 22.9 cr (INR 15/share); FY24 total dividend INR 68.6 cr (INR 45/share), 2.25x prior year
items.quote: Further, the Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of Rs. 22.9 crores at the rate of Rs. 15 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM, which brings the total dividend payout for the full year at Rs. 68.6 crores, which would be Rs. 45 a share, 2.25 X (times) of the previous year.

items.statement: Platform upgrade costs (Smart Pay SP4, HRMS v2) already capitalized; no significant incremental capex expected in FY25
items.quote: On your question on platforms, as mentioned in one of our earlier calls, the cost relating to those are already in the balance sheet and those will be amortized over an appropriate period of time, again, as per the market practice and accounting standards. So, there are no incremental costs expected on those platforms, at least for this year other than small add-on investments if needed, but I don

items.statement: Average headcount grew ~12% YoY FY23-FY24; March-end headcount just under 6,000; headcount growth to remain in similar ballpark FY25
items.quote: So, the average headcount between FY '23 and FY '24 has grown by about 12%.

items.statement: EXM processes 1.32 million employee records (market leader, 20-30% above competitors); payslips per FTE improved 10% YoY
items.quote: We have added new employee records in excess of 4 lakhs in H2 and now process 1.32 million employee records at the end of March, remaining the clear market leader in the managed services space, being 20% to 30% higher than competitors' volume.

items.statement: CXM FTE grew 9.5% YoY, 1.7% QoQ; attrition maintained at 7.2% per month (near best-in-class)
items.quote: Our staff attrition was maintained at 7.2% per month for Q4, which continues to be near best-in-class in the domestic outsourcing industry.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by higher international mix, productivity (payslips/FTE), new logos, cost savings; absorbed salary and non-wage inflation
items.quote: A higher share of international and cost savings from operational efficiencies have enabled us to improve EBITDA margins by 200 basis points over FY '23 even after absorbing salary and other inflation.

items.statement: Evaluating niche capability acquisitions in healthcare/RCM; some targets acquired by others at higher valuations; organic build also an option but slower
items.quote: we continue to look at it, I mean, we will continue to balance the niche capability acquisition, the referenceability, the mar ket endorsement which an acquisition can get vis-a-vis what we have to pay for that acquisition. So, we were looking at some assets which have got concluded with other players at a much higher number, then what we were talking about

items.statement: CXM new US sales (hired sales leader March 1, account-based marketing for SME BFSI/Healthcare) expected to contribute only from Q2 FY25; quarterly mining visibility limited
items.quote: We believe that some of the revenues for the new business should only start getting in from Q2 and not prior to that as per our Annual plan.

items.statement: Local Level Compliance (LLC) business sold to Aparajitha Corporate Services; financial closure 30 April 2024; assets classified as held for sale
items.quote: And as far as the held for proceed (held for sale) number is concerned, that relates to our LLC transaction, which was the sale of our local level compliance business to Aparajitha C orporate Services. The formal financial closure of the transaction happened only on 30th April

items.statement: Management expects ~10% volume growth in coming years and targets value-added product mix >50% of revenue within 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So considering everything put together, we should be in a range of volumes. We should consider 10% around volumes for the coming up, coming years.

items.statement: Debt repayment of INR145 cr in FY25 and INR174 cr in FY26; no new loans planned for FY25
items.quote: Secondly, as far as going forward we are definitely tearing down some of our debt which is a normal repayment of debt of about INR150 crores in the next year. So that will definitely come down.

items.statement: Routine capex INR15-20 cr/year; major expansion capex not yet decided; INR840 cr invested over last 1.5 years (30% to fabric/knitting, rest to spinning)
items.value: INR15-20 cr routine; major capex TBD
items.quote: Normal capex, which is of the routine nature, is about INR15 crores to INR20 crores t hat is happening. That happens every year due to various requirements for debottlenecking and other things. Apart from that, major capex plan has not yet been decided

items.statement: Yarn capacity ~91k tons vs rated 110k tons (max 105k tons); fabric/weaving can improve 7-8%; knitting utilization lower with scope to improve; overall ~10% volume headroom
items.quote: Our rated capacity is around 1,10,000 tons per annum. And we can produce, after giving all efficiencies and others, about 1,05,000 tons. So, we are looking for that kind of capacity utilization which is about 10% more from the present last year's capacity.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 14.52%; management indicates maintaining ~14.5% would be substantial improvement over FY24 average 13%; long-term target 16-20% if export demand and FTAs materialize
items.quote: Basically, we do not give any projections for the margins. But just an indication is that our last quarter margin was 14.5. So, if you are able to maintain that also it should be substantial improvement from the existing levels, yearly levels.

items.statement: Cotton prices stable at INR57-58k/candy (±INR3k) for 6-8 months; expected to remain stable this calendar year; yarn realization FY24 INR274/kg vs FY23 INR338/kg (-19%); fabric realization FY24 INR160/m vs FY23 INR182/m
items.quote: Cotton prices have remained in the range of INR 57,000, INR58,000 plus minus INR3,000 a candy for good last 6 months, 7 months, 8 months which is going to continue going forward as well as we look forward.

items.statement: Export demand improving at normal pace; China re-importing cotton yarn (+35-40% YoY in March); Indian exports improved last 6-8 months, expected stable next 6 months; full demand recovery may take 5-6 more months
items.quote: Demand is definitely improving and it is not a very fast pace. It is a normal pace. If you see the data of imports by various of these countries we are seeing that China has started to re-import large quantities.

items.statement: Export mix targeted at 55-60% of revenue (down from 73% in FY22); domestic and export realizations similar; exports include both yarn and fabric
items.quote: As a strateg y, we would rather keep ourselves limited up to 50 -- in the band of 55 % to 60% on the export side. And that's what we're doing

items.statement: Total debt INR1,339 cr (INR811 cr long-term, INR383 cr WC, INR145 cr current maturities); term debt 5.5% net of subsidies (new loans at full rate pending sanction); WC ~7.5%; debt/equity 1.15-1.16; target interest cost 2.5-3% of revenue
items.quote: As of March 24, the company's debt profile stood at INR1,339 crores comprising INR811 crores in long-term debt, INR383 crores working capital and INR145 crores as current maturities of term loan.

items.statement: Solar capacity increased from 12-13 MW to 23 MW (+10 MW); adding 7-8 MW more in current year; solar generation ~2.7 cr units/yr at lower cost vs grid INR7-7.5/unit; renewables 7-8% of power mix; INR95-100 cr invested in solar over 3 years
items.quote: We have added substantial solar capacity -- solar power capacity. Now our capacity is about 23 megawatts. If you see at the end of the last year this capacity was about 12, 13 megawatts. So we have added more than 10 megawatts of capacity.

items.statement: Value-added products ~38-40% of revenue (fabric 25-26% + value-added yarn 14-15%); target >50% in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So that all put together, it is about 38 % to 40%, where we do a reasonable value addition in comparison to normal commodity yarns. So this proportion slowly is going up. We expect that total, we should be doing it more than 50%.

items.statement: Government schemes (textile parks, PLI, export incentives) delayed due to elections; expected implementation post-elections to aid long-term growth; FTA with EU could benefit >20% of sales (UK only 3-4%)
items.quote: The measures were in active consideration, however held up due to elections. I hope implementation of these schemes post -elections will h elp long-term growth of Indian textile industry

items.statement: Board recommended dividend 25% (INR2.5/share), same as last year
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of 25% i.e. INR2.5 per share, i.e. same as last year.

items.statement: Captive consumption 20% of yarn production; depreciation run-rate INR36 cr/quarter (INR145 cr/yr) on current asset base
items.quote: Yeah, this INR36 crores every quarter will be charged. So the average -- the depreciation next year is expected to be on the current set of fixed assets is about INR145 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Russia-Ukraine, Red Sea crisis) increasing freight costs and transit times; margin recovery dependent on export demand pickup and FTA implementation
items.quote: Despite ongoing geopolitical challenges such as Russia-Ukraine conflict, Red Sea crisis, which has resulted in a higher freight cost and extended transit times, our country's cotton textile exports have demonstrated a healthy rebound.

items.statement: Target to double AUM to $125 billion by 2030; could reach by 2029 if 15-20% growth sustained
items.quote: REC management and board have decided to have a clear-cut roadmap and we are targeting to double our asset under management to about $125 billion by the year 2030.

items.statement: Target renewable energy portfolio to grow 10x to $40 billion by 2030 from current $4 billion
items.quote: We are trying to increase our renewable energy portfolio by 10x to about $40 billion by the end 2030.

items.statement: Target non-power infrastructure logistics AUM to grow fourfold to $25 billion by 2030
items.quote: We are anticipating that our total asset under management from non-power infrastructure logistics will see fourfold growth to say about $25 billion by the end of 2030.

items.statement: Expect 30% AUM from renewables, 15-20% from non-power infra, 50-55% from conventional by 2030
items.quote: By the year 2030, we would like to double our asset under management to about $125 billion, 30% of it will come from renewable energy segment, 15% to 20% will come from non-power infrastructure logistics, and 50% to 55% of asset under management will come from conventional coal-based generation capacity, distribution and transmission sector.

items.statement: Sanctioned projects worth $43 billion in FY24, up 34% from $32.2 billion in FY23
items.quote: We sanctioned projects worth $43 billion in the last financial year, as compared to $32.2 billion which we had sanctioned in FY23.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 67% to $19.3 billion in FY24 from $11.6 billion in FY23
items.quote: The disbursements have also grown by 67% or total disbursement stood around $19.3 billion last financial year, as compared to $11.6 billion in FY23.

items.statement: Renewable energy sanctions pipeline of over INR175,000 crores for current financial year
items.quote: In the current financial year, we have a huge pipeline of projects amounted to more than INR175,000 crores.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 15 bps to 7.13% in FY24; spread improved 41 bps to 2.86%; NIM up 19 bps to 3.57%
items.quote: We were able to bring down our cost of funds by 15 bps from 7.28% in the last financial year to 7.13% in FY '24. The spread has already improved by 41 basis points from 2.45% to 2.86%. The net interest margin has seen an increase of 19 bps from 3.38% to 3.57%.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 29% to $2.12 billion (PBT); net profit up 27% to $1.68 billion in FY24
items.quote: Our total profit after tax at the end of the financial year was about $2.12 billion -- profit before tax, sorry, profit before tax. And our net profit has seen an increase of 27%. It was about $1.68 billion.

items.statement: Return on net worth at 22.17% in FY24
items.quote: Our return on net worth was about 22.17%.

items.statement: Power demand increased 8% in FY24 and 11% in April 2024
items.quote: Last year, power demand increased by 8%. And in the current financial in the last month in April, power demand has increased by 11%.

items.statement: RBI draft circular proposes phased additional provisioning for under-construction projects: 2% by Mar-25, 3.5% by Mar-26, 5% by Mar-27
items.quote: But it's to be effected in phased manner by 31st March, 2025, only 2% provision has to be done. By 31st March 2026, 3.5% provisioning has to be done. And by 31st March, 2027, 5% crossing has to be done.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines not applicable to loans backed by state government guarantees (~40% of loan book)
items.quote: This RBI guideline would not be applicable to these loans which have been supported by the state government guarantee. About 40% of our loan is supported by the state government guarantee.

items.statement: Distribution CapEx loans backed by state guarantees (65% of distribution portfolio) exempt from RBI provisioning
items.quote: the total book size under the distribution segment is close to 25.75 billion, out of which the CapEx which is supposed to attract provisioning requirement is only 9 billion, which is just 35% of total dis tribution portfolio

items.statement: Expect write-backs of INR1,500-2,000 crores in FY25; target net zero NPA by end FY25
items.quote: We are expecting a write-back to the tune of INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores in the financial year FY '25. And we hope that all this asset would get resolved in the current financial year itself and will become net zero NPA company by the end of FY '25.

items.statement: Gross NPA INR13,800 crores; INR2,222 crores (7 projects) fully provided heading to liquidation
items.quote: Our gross NPA is about INR13,800 crores. And out of that, about 7 projects are heading towards liquidation that is amounting to INR2,222 crores. For this, we already made 100% provisioning.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio 25.82% vs 15% minimum; Tier 1 capital 23.32% vs 10% minimum
items.quote: Our minimum capital ratio required is 15%, and we are having about 25.82%. For Tier 1 capital, the RBI statutory minimum requirement is 10%, and we are having to the tune of 23.32%.

items.statement: May pass on some RBI provisioning impact to borrowers via higher lending rates, but lower borrowing costs may offset
items.quote: We'll have to pass on some impact of this -- we'll be able to pass on to the borrower. But another -- the silver line of fact is that, our cost of borrowing is going to come down in after Q2, Q3. Once this cost of borrowing comes down, we'll pass on or perhaps balance out actually.

items.statement: Green bond funding provides 10-15 bps cost advantage for renewable projects, offsetting provisioning impact
items.quote: There are a number of lenders who are willing to lend at slightly lower rates as compared to the normal raising, which we are doing, both in domestic market as well as the international market. So there are enough funds which are available, and the differential is about 10 to 15 basis points as compared to the normal borrowing which we are doing for general purposes, for conventional generation al

items.statement: Additional 94 GW coal capacity identified by 2032; REC targets 30-40% share of capex financing
items.quote: About 94 gigawatt capacity has been identified to be brought in by year 2032, in the next 8 years, all the approvals for this additional coal-based capacity will happen next 2 to 3 years. There also, we see a huge potential or REC, we'll be able to share at 30% to 40% of the coal base capacity, addition capital would be coming in the next 8 years.

items.statement: Distribution infrastructure upgrade opportunity over next 10-12 years as assets are 40-50 years old
items.quote: After RDSS period is over and the modernization is over, in the next 4 to 5 years, country will still require a lot of CapEx for upgrading the infrastructure, because distribution infrastructure all the poles, wires, the distribution transformer is quite old, 40 to 50 years old.

items.statement: Renewable sanctions in FY24: large hydro INR32,450 Cr, pump storage INR28,304 Cr, solar INR21,000 Cr, module manufacturing INR21,565 Cr, green hydrogen INR8,000 Cr, e-mobility INR8,000 Cr
items.quote: Last year, we sanctioned project of INR136,515 crores. Out of this, large hydro projects constitute about INR32,450 crores, pump storage hydro project was about INR28,304 crores; followed by solar, about INR21,000 crores. Then model manufacturing was INR21,565 crores; followed by green hydrogen project, about INR8,000 crores we have sanctioned; electric mobility, about INR8,000 crores.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines may reduce Tier 1 capital by INR2,000-3,000 crores over 3 years but won't impact approval process
items.quote: Even if this Tier 1 capital gets reduced by say 2,000 to 3,000, it will not impact our approval process.

items.statement: Only ~20% of AUM (INR1 lakh crore) impacted by RBI draft guidelines; 80% of renewable book already commissioned
items.quote: Out of 5 lakh crores this asset under management, most of them are already commissioned. Only 1 lakh crore of projects are under construction, which will get impacted.

items.statement: Ramped up manpower and hired sector experts for infrastructure logistics appraisal since Oct 2022 diversification
items.quote: We have ramped up our manpower strength. We have got in experts from different fields, putting to infrastructure logistics.

items.statement: Government committed to 50 GW annual renewable capacity addition from FY25 vs 12-14 GW previously
items.quote: From this year onwards, they stepped up their ambitions and per annum, they are targeting installation of 50 gigawatt capacities.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines on project finance exposure norms will impact Tier 1 capital; state government guaranteed loans are kept out of exposure norms per common understanding with RBI.
items.quote: As for exposure is concerned, we are very clear that state government guaranteed loan are not counted. Yes, out of the purview.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines apply to all under-construction capex projects regardless of DCCO extension; company will request RBI to limit applicability to DCCO-funded projects only.
items.quote: It will be on all under-construction project -- all CapEx projects. So we have made it clear, it will be affecting all the under construction projects despite whether it is DCCO shift or not.

items.statement: Loan book grew 17% in current year; if sustained, INR 10 lakh crore target could be reached by FY29 instead of FY30.
items.quote: If we are able -- like this year, our asset grew by about 17%. If this 17% growth is continued, then we'll be able to reach this INR10 lakh crores by the year 2029 itself, in next 5 years, not 6 years.

items.statement: Targeting minimum INR 175,000 crore disbursements this year, up from INR 151,000 crore last year, with significant increase in capex disbursements.
items.quote: But this year, o ur CapEx disbursement are going to jump quite substantially. And we are targeting minimum INR175,000 crores

items.statement: Renewable energy share of total assets to grow from 7% to 30% in 5-6 years; conventional generation 29% growing 2-3% annually; distribution & transmission 40% stable; logistics 15-20% by 2030.
items.quote: Right now, share of renewable energy is only 7% of our total assets. It will gradually increase to 30% in the next 5 to 6 years. So every year, we see that incremental growth of 5% to 7% growth will be there as far as renewable energy is concerned.

items.statement: Spread expected to improve from 2.8% to 3% driven by higher-margin coal-based generation (94 GW pipeline, 40% share target), large hydro, pump storage, and non-power infra.
items.quote: So we do hope that our spread is going to improve further, not going to come down. It may go up to 3% actually, from 2.8% it may increase to 3% actually.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 15 bps from 7.28% to 7.13%; ECB share increased from 24% to 29%; all-in ECB cost 6.6-6.7% via innovative hedging; 54EC bonds target >INR 50,000 crore.
items.quote: You might have seen that our cost of funds has come down by 15 basis points from 7.28% to 7.13%. And the share of our external commercial borrowing has increased from 24% to 29%.

items.statement: 7 projects worth INR 2,222 crore heading for liquidation, fully provisioned; no new NPA added in last 9 quarters; targeting net NPA zero by FY25.
items.quote: Not 9, 7 projects are getting towards liquidation, total value of INR2,222 crores, for which we already made 100% provisioning.

items.statement: No impairment reserve currently as Ind AS provisioning already exceeds IRAC norms; standard asset provisioning ~0.5% overall, up to 1% on individual projects.
items.quote: Our provisioning is already higher than the IRAC norms, there is no impairment reserves at present.

items.statement: Power demand grew 8% last year and 11% in April; DISCOM AT&C losses fell from 22% to 15.5% over 2 years under RDSS; state gencos/transcos health improving.
items.quote: The AT&C loss, which was 22% 2 years back, came down to roughly 16.5% and then it has now further come down to 15.5%.

items.statement: 94 GW coal-based capacity pipeline; targeting minimum 40% business share; lending rates 10-11% for coal projects with ability to pass on incremental provisioning costs.
items.quote: You might have observed that our lending rate is the highest in respect of coal based capacity only. It varies from 10% to 11% actually. This 94 gigawatt capacity, some additional impact was because additional provisioning some impact would be there, that we'll be able to pass on actually.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines may impair bank lending capacity for private capex, creating opportunity for REC to capture high-quality assets with less competition.
items.quote: But then that gives us greater opportunity. In any case, we are a very active lender in the power sector space, and we started lending operations in the interest space as well.

items.statement: Tier 1 capital impact from RBI guidelines to be calculated after final norms; comments due by June; impact may reflect in Q1 or Q2 results depending on final guideline timing.
items.quote: So whatever impact will be there in any case, the comments are to be sent by June. So in case they come out with the final guidelines before the first quarterly results, then in any case, we'll be having the impact there in the first quarterly result itself.

items.statement: Collections increasing; 54EC capital gains tax saving bonds at INR 40,000 crore targeting >INR 50,000 crore; foreign currency borrowing with innovative hedging at 6.6-6.7% all-in cost.
items.quote: One is 54 EC bonds that is capital gains tax saving ins trument, that is about 40,000. That also will increase to more than INR50,000 crores. That's what we are targeting.Collections are going to increase

items.statement: Bridge financing and RBPF not covered under RBI project finance definition as DCCO required; only projects meeting specific definition fall under new norms.
items.quote: There is a definition of project which is given under these guidelines. So we have to go by that definition. So these type of bridge financing which they are doing or even if we are doing RBPF for this type of funding, so that won't be covered in -- because in any case, DCCO has to be there for these type of project.

items.statement: Banks largely absent from infra financing; private sector banks (ICICI, HDFC) not in infra; state banks lend to REC which on-lends to projects leveraging REC's evaluation capability.
items.quote: Actually, banks in any case are not lending for the infra. In case you see the private sector banks, ICICI, HDFC nowhere they are in case of the infra financing. It's only the state sector banks which are there.

items.statement: 70% of profits retained to grow net worth (ROE >20%), 30% paid as dividend; write-backs from stressed asset resolutions (KSK etc.) expected next year.
items.quote: So there'll be 70% in any case will be going towards the net worth itself, 30% we have to declare by way of dividend. Remaining will be incrementally going towards the net worth itself.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned in transcript.
items.quote: On behalf of REC, I would like to thank all the participants for asking inquisitive questions and hope that we have been able to answer your queries and on the various issues to your satisfaction.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected around INR 5,500-5,600 crore based on order book execution
items.quote: So, INR 1,700 crores of CV, about INR 3,600 crores of wagon. So that means INR 5,300 crores and maybe some amount of the current year order book executed. So, about INR 5,500 crores, INR 5,600 crores turnover is a reasonable possibility, right? For the current year?

items.statement: Order backlog at INR 7,10,166 lakh, highest ever, with 75% wagons executable over 18 months and balance CV business in FY25
items.quote: In terms of outlook, we are pleased to report an order backlog of INR 7,10,166 lakh our highest ever.

items.statement: Capex of INR 1,000-1,500 crore planned for Bonatrans wheel set backward integration over 18-24 months
items.quote: In terms of investments, I think our Capex in this business will be anything between INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores of Capex, which we are looking to invest in this business.

items.statement: Targeting 1,000 wagons/month run rate by Q2 FY25; Bonatrans wheel set capacity to expand from 15,000-20,000 to 100,000 sets/annum
items.quote: By I think quarter 2 is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Visible margin improvement expected in FY25 from wheel sets, brakes, and specialized wagons; brake business margins upward of 14-15%
items.quote: It will not be something marginal, but there'll be a visible improvement in margins.

items.statement: Shift to specialized wagons (steel, cement, auto), BESS/data center containers, and brake systems driving higher margins
items.quote: We are now working with a lot of marquee names global names, such as GE, Schneider, Toshiba, Tata Solar.

items.statement: Private wagon market share 60-70%; order wins from Ministry of Railways, Ministry of Defence, and leading auto manufacturer
items.quote: Jupiter continues to dominate the private segment. So if you look at the private order books, I think Jupiter share would be more than 60% to 70% in this segment.

items.statement: Acquired Bonatrans India for wheel set manufacturing; Stone India integration on track
items.quote: During the quarter, we acquired Bonatrans India Private Limited which further solidifies our integrated business model.

items.statement: Rail freight modal mix projected to rise from 29% (FY24) to 35% by FY31
items.quote: Projections indicate a rise in the rail freight modal mix from 29% in fiscal year 2024 to 35% by fiscal year 2031.

items.statement: Net debt near zero after QIP; long-term borrowings nil, sufficient cash available
items.quote: Net debt is around 0 because the long-term borrowing we don't have, and we have the sufficient cash available.

items.statement: Board approved INR 1,000 crore fundraise (mix of equity and debt) primarily for wheel business capex
items.quote: The Board, I think, has cleared fresh set of, I think, INR 1,000 crores of new capital fundraise the Board has cleared. So it will be a mix of both debt as well as equity.

items.statement: Bonatrans FY25 revenue target INR 300-400 crore (captive + external); 14,000-18,000 wheel sets production
items.quote: This year, we are looking to produce about close to 14,000-to-18,000-wheel sets in Bonatrans and we are looking at revenues of about INR400-odd crores.

items.statement: Brake systems (KOVIS/DAKO) FY25 revenue at least INR 300 crore combined
items.quote: We are looking at least about INR 300 crores of revenue at least in both the businesses.

items.statement: eLCV launch expected July 2024; FY25 target upward of 500 vehicles, margin positive from day 1
items.quote: We are expecting the approval to come any day, I think, in the next week or 10 days, I think we expect approvals to be there. And I've maintained that July, we are going to be launching a vehicle.

items.statement: Greenfield foundry in Jabalpur ~INR 200 crore for weldable crossings; 18-month timeline
items.quote: About close to INR 200 crores, if I am not wrong for...

items.statement: Weldable crossing market size INR 4,000-5,000 crore; railway to buy >100,000 crossings in 3-4 years
items.quote: So, it is about -- the market is about INR 4,000 crores to INR 5,000 crores is the market size.

items.statement: Working capital ~75 days in FY24, expected to remain same in FY25; debtor days stable at 49 days
items.quote: The working capital is around 75 days. And I think that will remain in FY '25 also.

items.statement: Final dividend INR 0.30/share recommended; combined with interim INR 0.30, total FY24 dividend INR 0.60/share
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR 0.30 per share, accompanied by the interim dividend of INR 0.30 per share, the combined dividend for financial year 2023-'24 amounts to INR 0.60 per share.

items.statement: Strong private wagon demand continues; BOXN wagon tender hold expected to lift post-elections; railway tender of ~6,000 wagons nearing finalization
items.quote: Already, there is one tender. I don't remember that I think it's close to about 6,000 wagons, which is going to be finalized very shortly.

items.statement: Vande Bharat tenders margin-negative; focusing on component supply (brakes, wheel sets, battery systems) where competition limited
items.quote: But definitely, we are not partnering with them to -- partnering with anybody to bid for the tenders because, again, which we feel that these are very margin negative right now, the pricing is very margin negative.

items.statement: Significant export potential for wheel sets to Tatravagonka (Europe) due to Russia-Ukraine conflict; Bonatrans certified for Europe and North America
items.quote: Further, I think there's a significant export potential because one of our significant partners and promoters in Jupiter Wagon, which is Tatravagonka, they are again, very keen to acquire wheel sets from India.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on consolidating new segments
items.quote: I think right now, we are looking to consolidate all the new segments which we have entered into.

items.statement: Foundry capacity constraint limiting CMS crossings and weldable crossings; dependent on capacity additions
items.quote: So, a lot of the capacity was towards wagons. And that's why there's a drop in the CMS numbers.

items.statement: eLCV regulatory approval expected within 1-2 weeks; weldable crossing RDSO final approval in couple of months
items.quote: We are expecting the approval to come any day, I think, in the next week or 10 days, I think we expect approvals to be there.

items.statement: Specialized private wagons command better pricing and margins vs railway wagons; passenger wheel sets higher margin than freight

items.statement: Expect strong double-digit growth in Elite and Premium segment; mid-single digit (5-6%) volume growth in economy segment; not guiding 15% overall volume growth, expect slightly below double-digit blended growth
