items.statement: Wine tourism revenue expected to grow at very strong double-digit in FY25 and decade beyond
items.quote: We continue to be extremely bullish about the growth prospects ahead and we see very strong double-digit growth ahead in FY'25 and in the decade beyond.

items.statement: Long-term elite and premium volume growth guidance of 15% remains intact
items.quote: Vinamra Hirawat: Okay. So I take that as the 15% long-term volume growth guidance is still intact, right? Karan Vasani: Yes.

items.statement: Packaging material cost per case expected to decline 3% in FY25 after 4-5% increase in FY24
items.quote: In FY25 we are expecting a 3% decline in packaging material cost per case which goes well for margins going forward. In FY24 with some of the geopolitical issues we have seen a 4% to 5% increase in packaging material costs and that is now moderating coming down by about 3%.

items.statement: Non-traditional markets (Telangana, Rajasthan) driving growth; CSD business grew >50% and is biggest growth segment; Mumbai and Goa challenging in FY24, expect softness to continue in FY25; Karnataka growing well
items.quote: The last 25 years have been tremendously fulfilling. And out of that, the last three or four years particularly have been, I would say, the most fulfilling and really have taken our company to a different level, including navigating the pandemic, completing our IPO, and now completing one year since our IPO.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 softness expected due to election restrictions on alcohol movement and heat wave
items.quote: We see some softness in Q1. However, we have some very strong hopes for the entire FY. In Q1, with the elections happening, the kind of restrictions that have been placed on AlcoBev, are much harder than anything that we've seen in the past.

items.statement: Capacity utilization ~85% at FY24 end; adding 1 million liters (6% increase) for 2025 harvest; first low-cost cellar at INR80/liter vs prior INR120/liter
items.quote: at the end of the financial year stood at around 85% and we will be expanding our capacity by about 1 million liters in time for the 2025 grape harvest which represents a 6% increase in capacity. Up until now, we have had only capacity really for one sort of capacity dedicated which can all make Elite and Premium wines. Now, for the first time we will be developing and putting in place a low-cost

items.statement: Sales team headcount growing 8-10%, 80% of increase in Tier 2/smaller cities; Maharashtra+Karnataka share of sales fell 300 bps to 60% in Q4; expanding distribution nationally
items.quote: The headcount of our sales team will be growing in the region of 8%-10% and I am happy to report that almost 80% of this increase is going to be coming from Tier 2 and smaller cities as we look to build a broad base for wine consumption.

items.statement: Trade receivables up to INR170 crores from INR115 crores due to slow payouts from Telangana corporation market and higher CSD sales (longer credit days); inventory up 10% to INR198 crores due to good harvest
items.quote: See, there is largely on account of the slowdown in payouts being made by certain corporation markets, particularly Telangana. So, that's where some of the collections are outstanding and it's kind of impacting our receivables balance as on 31st of March.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.54x, net debt/EBITDA 1.1x; average borrowing up INR45 crores YoY as WIPs payout received March 31
items.quote: Our prudent financial management is evident in our debt matrix with our debt-to-equity ratio of 0.54 times and our net debt to EBITDA ratio of 1.1 times, reflecting a healthy balance sheet.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR4.5/share, full-year INR8.50/share (same as last year); conserving cash for organic and inorganic expansion
items.quote: Considering the expansion potential in our wine tourism and other inorganic expansion opportunities, company's board has recommended final dividend of INR4.5 per share subject to shareholders' approval. This takes the full-year dividend to INR8.50 per share, almost at the same level as last year.

items.statement: Maharashtra WIPs scheme revived for 8 years (4 retrospective to FY24, 4 prospective to FY28); prospective cap INR20 crores/unit vs no cap earlier; impacts Sula with 3 qualifying units
items.quote: The scheme was revived for eight years, four years which are retrospective until FY24 and another four years after FY24 until the end of FY28. There is a little bit of a difference in the scheme for the prospective four years as a cap has been imposed of INR20 crores per unit as against no cap earlier.

items.statement: Economy segment driven by high discounting, race to bottom; Sula not competing there; gained market share in new institutions via elevated S&D spend in Q3-mid Q4, now moderating S&D
items.quote: On the economy side, yes, we do expect volume growth there to be in the range of 5% to 6% or mid-single digits. Mid-single digits, you can say. And we do see this as a segment that is sort of driven by high discounting and becoming a race to the bottom.

items.statement: Onboarded VFX Supervisor Dan Levitan with 30+ years experience and 85 feature films, and COO Zameer with 20+ years at ILM, MPC, DNEG
items.quote: We are excited to update you about the onboarding of two exceptional individuals who will enhance our creative and operational capabilities. VFX Supervisor, Mr. Dan Levitan. With over 30 years of experience, this esteemed VFX Supervisor brings a rich depth of knowledge to BFS.

items.statement: Launched upskilling program to convert 2D VFX artists into 3D concept artists with 100% employee participation
items.quote: Basilic Fly Studio proactively upskills its workforce through upskilling technical programs. This initiative focuses on equipping employees coming from 2D digital VFX background with cutting-edge proficiencies and nurturing their talent to grow as 3D concept artists.

items.statement: Expanding project portfolio into emerging markets Italy, Spain, France and seeing surge from North America post writers' strike resolution
items.quote: BFS is expanding its project portfolio with new ventures originating from emerging markets such as Italy, Spain, and France, as well as experiencing assertive projects from the established markets of North America post the resolution of the writers' strike.

items.statement: Visible pipeline before September 2024 includes previs for video game cinematics (INR25M, 10 months), blockbuster sequel (INR180M, 10-11 months), exclusive vendor project (INR340M, 8-10 months), June 24 project (INR200M, ~500 shots), produc
items.quote: Previs for video game cinematics commencing in the coming days, this project spans for 10 months. Coming from AAA level gaming company showcasing our commitment to long-term engagement and creative excellence this shall bring an expected revenue of INR25 million. A blockbuster sequel anticipated to generate significant revenue of INR180 million over the next 10 to 11 months.

items.statement: Confirmed order book visibility for H1 FY25 is roughly INR75 crores
items.quote: Total order book would be roughly around INR75 crores. This is the visibility of the first half.

items.statement: Expecting ~30% revenue growth each for FY25 and FY26, with surge from August/September 2024 based on confirmed movie release dates
items.quote: Currently, we are estimating a growth of around 30% each for FY25 and also from September onwards, from August, September onwards we do see a surge in the market based upon the confirmed release dates of the movie project that has been announced by the major production networks.

items.statement: Aim to maintain FY24 EBITDA margin (~50%) and PAT margin (~35%) in FY25
items.quote: Yes EBITDA margin is something that would be able to maintain what the EBITDA margin that we have maintained for the previous year.

items.statement: Currently balancing margins: ~75% of India work at discounted rates, ~25% overseas work at better margins
items.quote: If you look into maybe 75% of what we work in India is discounted, but 25% what it comes out of these overseas locations would add to our margin. So that is where we've been balancing out this current situation.

items.statement: Direct studio work increased from 30% to 35%; targeting 45-50% by Q1 FY25 (March 2025)
items.quote: In terms of direct production initially were around 30% and we have increased to 35% now. And from the studios it's around 65%.

items.statement: Revenue split by service: ~30% Roto, 20-25% Paint, ~45% Compositing and other
items.quote: Approximately, I think percentage 30% for Roto and 20%, 25% for Paint and rest are just Composting and other was 45% each.

items.statement: Standalone receivables INR63 crores: INR15 crores >180 days (on declining trend, installment arrangements), INR48 crores <180 days; net working capital cycle ~60 days normalized
items.quote: Net working capital I would say 60 days.

items.statement: Other current assets include WIP ~INR19 crores and GST refund ~INR5+ crores
items.quote: Work in progress is roughly INR19 crores, GST refund is INR5 crores plus.

items.statement: Timing recruitment for June-July 2024 ahead of expected August/September surge; also pursuing strategic partnerships in incentive locations and technology-driven companies
items.quote: We are timing our recruitment closer to that, that is by June, July. It's what we would not be recruiting around August, but by June, July is what we've been planning and apart from that we're also working towards strategic partnerships as well.

items.statement: Appointed advisor for inorganic opportunities; in close discussions with potential partners, may materialize soon
items.quote: Yes, very much, Pranav and we've been working on that as well and we also have appointed an advisor who's working on that and we are very much closer in terms of discussing with few potential partnerships.

items.statement: Government VFX incentive: 30% of minimum project expenditure (capped at INR300M/project) for foreign content; 5% bonus for Indian content; applying for fresh projects
items.quote: So one thing is, it is more promising and encouraging where the government has announced 30% of minimum project expenditure based off for the VFX studios that would be working on foreign content, international content. And likewise, the minimum cap at, sorry, not minimum cap, maximum cap at INR300 million for each project.

items.statement: FICCI EY report: India VFX industry revenue ~INR5,400 crores last year, expected to grow to INR6,300 crores this year; animation & VFX CAGR 17.5% to INR185B by 2026
items.quote: Overall media industry, for example, based on FICCI EY report of the revenue for the VFX industry it looks like it's around INR5,400 crores for the overall for India VFX industry, around INR5,400 crores for the last year, but it's expected to grow to INR6,300 crores for this year.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated: Revenue INR105.79 crores (+33.75%), EBITDA INR52.18 crores (+34.35%), PBT INR50.61 crores (+34.95%), EPS INR17.85 (+9.38%)
items.quote: Consolidated financial. Total revenue surged by 33.75% amounting to INR105.79 driven by strong operational efficiency, EBITDA and profit before tax increased by 34.35% and 34.95% respectively reaching INR 52.18 crores and INR50.61 crores.

items.statement: FY24 standalone: Revenue INR103.19 crores (+46.34%), EBITDA INR51.68 crores (+40.69%), PBT INR50.18 crores (+41.64%), PAT INR26.44 crores, EPS INR17.69
items.quote: In our standalone financials for fiscal year 24 total revenue impressively increased by 46.34% to INR103.19 crores underpinned by strong operational efficiency, EBITDA rose by 40.69% to INR51.68 crores And profit before tax increased by 41.64% to INR50.18 crores.

items.statement: Wrong consolidated financials uploaded to NSE on April 30, 2024 due to clerical error (UK subsidiary numbers); correct financials were board-approved; informed NSE May 1; added internal controls
items.quote: On behalf of BFS, I wish to apologize to the investors for unforeseen inconvenience caused due to typographical errors present in the uploaded documents of consolidated financial statements as of 31st March 2024, which we submitted on National Stock Exchange on April 30, 2024.

items.statement: Workforce ~500 as of March 2024 (up from 400+ post-IPO); operating from Chennai, Pune, London, Vancouver
items.quote: As of March 2024, we employ around 500 individuals. A robust team dedicated to driving success following our IPO, we've experienced significant growth expanding our employee count.

items.statement: Global footprint with HQ in Chennai and offices in Canada, UK; executives based overseas to capture direct international work
items.quote: Established in 2016, Basilic Fly has emerged as a leading force in VFX innovation with our headquarters based in Chennai and a global footprint extending to Canada and the UK.

items.statement: India cost advantage: ~USD150/day vs USD500-600/day in UK/US for high-end work; targeting streaming platforms (Netflix, Amazon) cutting costs but demanding quality
items.quote: For example, if you take USD500 to USD600 per day there, and if you take USD150 per day here is much better margin. So that is something we will be working towards and getting those kinds of projects.

items.statement: Diversifying into gaming cinematics (previs), corporate films, real-time 3D content creation (Unreal), advertising VFX (5-10% of revenue)
items.quote: We've been working on these kinds of projects and working on a short and real-time projects for corporate films and likewise for gaming cinematics and likewise diversified into other markets as well.

items.statement: Targeting INR300 crore+ EBITDA from Crop Protection and Specialty Nutrients by FY26-27
items.quote: We are on track to achieve our FY 26-27 numbers of INR300 crore + of EBITDA.

items.statement: Board approved additional energy efficiency projects worth INR120 crore for implementation during next annual turnaround
items.quote: As we speak, our Board has also approved further energy efficiency projects worth about INR 120 crore, and these will be implemented during next annual turnaround.

items.statement: Energy efficiency improvements in Gadepan I and II expected to add 8-9% to urea EBIT
items.quote: 2% to 3% increase is about $2 to $3, $3, $4. You are right. 8% to 9%.

items.statement: CPC and SN business EBIT margins of 19-20% sustainable for a couple of years due to MNC price positioning
items.quote: The margins are culminating from the price positioning of the products, which we started initially. So, we targeted the MNCs with regards to price positioning of the product. And that's why and these are sustainable at least for a couple of years.

items.statement: Launching 12 new Crop Protection products in FY25 with focus on weedicides; 4 already launched last month
items.quote: We have a strong pipeline of 12 new products of CPC for FY25, with focus on Weedicides. We have already launched four of these products in the last month.

items.statement: Launched biological nano phosphorus product Uttam Pranaam in collaboration with TERI; targeting 5 lakh acres in Kharif
items.quote: We're launching the product in a week's time and targeting around 5 lakh acres in Kharif.

items.statement: Ammonia profit declined from INR125 crore to less than INR50 crore in FY24 due to margin normalization
items.quote: So last year, we made around INR125 crore. This year, we have made less than INR50 crore.

items.statement: IMACID JV evaluating 55-60% phosphoric acid capacity expansion funded by internal accruals
items.quote: In our joint venture in IMACID we strongly evaluate expansion of the order of 55% to 60% of the existing capacity for phosphoric acid. And should that number on basis the evaluation come close to what the management thinks, definitely, there will be an investment in that particular business.

items.statement: Country urea inventory at 87 lakh tons, DAP at 22 lakh tons, NPK at 47 lakh tons, MOP at 9 lakh tons as of April 1, 2024
items.value: 87 lakh tons (urea), 22 lakh tons (DAP), 47 lakh tons (NPK), 9 lakh tons (MOP)
items.quote: The inventory of urea in the country as on 1st of April was around 87 lakh tons. And DAP was around 22 lakh tons. NPK is 47 lakh tons and MOP 9 lakh tons.

items.statement: Gas price for Q4 FY24 around $17 per mmBtu on NCV basis
items.quote: Gas prices for this quarter was around $17 per mmBtu on NCV basis.

items.statement: Concentrated Nitric Acid plant detailed cost estimation approved; to be ordered on major license
items.quote: Yes, we are going in for a detailed cost estimation on Concentrated Nitric Acid plant which will be ordered on one of the major licenses. That has been approved.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for FY25 expected in range of 24.5% to 25.5%
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the full year is expected to be up 200 basis points over last year, which should result in the range of about 24.5% to 25.5% to EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Plan to deploy INR1,500 crores in capital investments in FY25
items.quote: We aim to deploy INR1,500 crores in capital investments to enhance our manufacturing capability and improve sustainability.

items.statement: Chronic therapies share increased to 61% of One-India portfolio, up ~100 bps YoY
items.quote: Chronic therapies now have a share of 61% in the portfolio, higher by almost 100 basis points year-on-year and grew at 10% year-on-year versus IQVIA MAT March '24.

items.statement: One-India Branded Prescription grew 100 bps ahead of market per IQVIA Q4 FY24
items.quote: Our Branded Prescription business continued to outpace the market growth in this quarter with Cipla growing 100 basis points ahead of the market as per IQVIA Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: North America revenue reached $906 million in FY24, up 24% YoY
items.quote: In North America, we reported an all -time high annual revenue of $906 million, which was 24% growing over the previous year.

items.statement: South Africa prescription business grew 11.2% YoY vs market growth of 2.1% per IQVIA MAT March 24
items.quote: Here, again, we recorded 11.2% year-on-year growth in secondary versus a market growth of 2.1% as per IQVIA MAT March '24.

items.statement: Plan to launch 4 peptide assets in FY25
items.quote: As alluded earlier, we strive to launch 4 peptide assets in FY '25.

items.statement: Patalganga facility received six 483 observations, Kurkumbh received one; awaiting official classification
items.quote: Recently, 2 of us the Patalganga and Kurkumbh also underwent the U.S. FDA audit. The Patalganga facility was issued with six 483 observations and the Kurkumbh audit ended with 1 observation.

items.statement: Goa Unit 5 remediation complete, ready for US FDA re-inspection expected around July-August
items.quote: We think the Goa inspection from our last inspection, we will be completing roughly about 2 years in July, August of this time frame. So that would -- around that time or beyond that is probably the time to expect reinspection.

items.statement: Respiratory portfolio ~30% of global revenue; US key products are respules, Albuterol, Arformoterol
items.quote: See, overall, if you look at our Respiratory across global revenue, it should be somewhere around circa 30%. That's the kind of share that we have and in the U.S., it's the respules, it's Albuterol, these are the key products that we have, Arformoterol.

items.statement: R&D spend expected to remain in 6% to 7% of revenue range for FY25
items.quote: So it should be in the range of 6% to 7%. We continue with that range.

items.statement: Emerging markets Europe expected to show respectable double-digit growth going forward
items.quote: I think we should hopefully be able to see a respectable double-digit growth in this segment.

items.statement: China respules facility investment ~$40-50 million; approved for facility and product
items.quote: About $40 million to $50 million, somewhere around that ZIP code. And it's got its approval now and both for the facility as well as for the product.

items.statement: MDI inhalation line at Fall River approved by FDA; DPI line equipment qualification underway
items.quote: The first is in line for MDI, which -- where we have already taken reg batches for several assets, right? And the line has been approved by the FDA, and it's -- the plant has gone through an audit possibly 2 times already. The second is a new facility for DPI, which is summing up and where the -- equipment qualification is happening now, feasibility batches are being taken.

items.statement: Abraxane launch timing depends on Goa plant re-inspection; likely later part of FY25 if inspection occurs in H1
items.quote: So the timing of Abraxane is going to depend on Goa inspection. We've earlier -- Goa is the earliest path for a launch. I think so -- that can happen earlier part of the year. There's a good chance for Abraxane to visit this in the later part of the year, maybe not.

items.statement: Dividend increased from INR8.5 to ~INR13 per share; actively evaluating large M&A growth opportunities
items.quote: We have stepped up the dividend by -- from INR8.5 per share to almost INR13 per share. And beyond that as well, I think the whole idea is to focus on some large growth opportunities, not just smaller investments, but large M&A growth opportunities that we have.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth expected to be as good as or better than FY24
items.quote: I think it will be as good, if not better than FY '24.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20-24% range for FY25
items.quote: we will always be guiding you in the 20% to 24% now. How it plays out, what happens with the number , but we will be comfortably in the 20% to 24% range

items.statement: Gross margins improved 690 bps YoY in Q4 FY24 due to lower VAM costs
items.quote: Gross margins in the quarter were higher than the fourth quarter of last year by 690 basis points, largely led by softening in commodity costs.

items.statement: VAM consumption price at $925/ton in Q4 FY24, flat currently
items.quote: VAM consumption was at $925 a ton versus $1,300 in the fourth quarter last year.

items.statement: Overall prices reduced ~5% in FY24; no further reductions expected unless input inflation
items.quote: if you look at the difference between our value and volume growth, which is approximately 5%, at a yearly level, we would have reduced prices, overall, by 5%.

items.statement: Rural growth 1.5x urban for full year FY24; both grew double digits
items.quote: For the whole year, our rural has been 1.5x urban.

items.statement: Domestic projects order book strong; execution is key constraint
items.quote: domestic projects business is buoyant. It is growing at rapid rates that is strong. That will continue to be strong when we look at our order book.

items.statement: Ad spend increased 70% YoY in FY24 to ~3.8% of revenue; targeting 4-4.5%
items.quote: Our ad spend was 70% higher than the earlier year, so you can see that, Sonali, we put our money where our mouth is, and we said we will invest behind growth.

items.statement: Lending business pilot starting; 6-9 months before meaningful update
items.quote: I think it will be 6 to 9 months before we come back to you on that business.

items.statement: Paints business in 4 states for 6-9 months; meeting action standards; will assess success in 6 months
items.quote: I would frankly declare success or otherwise give us another 6 months. As of now, we have always said it's a range-completion exercise.

items.statement: Growth/pioneer categories now 45% of business vs 20% at start of journey
items.quote: We are now at 55% - 45%. 55% is core, and 45% is growth in pioneers.

items.statement: Domestic tractor industry expected to register lower mid-single-digit growth for full year FY25 led by near normal monsoon
items.quote: For the full year, however, we expect the domestic sector industry to do well and may register lower mid-single-digit growth, led by the near to our normal monsoon this year.

items.statement: Agri Machinery EBITDA margin expected to recover to 13-14% range for full year FY25
items.quote: If you look at the full year margins for tractor business also, which has been closer to 13%, so we expect -- I think the margin should be actually recovering slightly from this level. And we should be able to be in 13% to 14% range, which has been the range we've been guiding now for the full year basis.

items.statement: Normal capex for FY25 planned at INR300 crores excluding greenfield project
items.quote: See, next year, our initial plan is to do about INR300 crores of cash flow this year. Now this is obviously excluding the greenfield project, which will come up.

items.statement: Rajasthan greenfield plant land acquisition cost estimated at INR400-odd crores, project to double tractor capacity over 4-5 years
items.quote: Well, like I said, it's still being negotiated, but the ballpark number, what we are getting is close to INR400-odd crores.

items.statement: Railway Equipment division order book stood at approximately INR950 crores at end of March 2024
items.quote: At the end of March '24, the division order book stood at a robust level of approximately INR950 crores.

items.statement: Railway EBIT margin expected to stay within 100 bps of FY24's 18.9% in coming period
items.quote: EBIT margin, what we have achieved in financial year '24, we see that in the coming period, it will be within the range of 100 basis points, plus/minus, considering as we will be launching new products.

items.statement: Construction Equipment EBIT margin of 9.3% seen as sustainable for coming years
items.quote: On construction equipment, also, we see this 9.3% EBIT is sustainable, and we should be able to do similar numbers for the coming years.

items.statement: Minor price hike taken from 1st May to cover overhead cost increases, not due to significant commodity pressure
items.quote: So the end of the early inflation has been fully passed on to the market. And there's also a reaction which was visible in the market from the competiti on. So we have been following the competition on that front which is why we also take a minor

items.statement: Construction Equipment demand may see short-term pressure from elections and monsoon but expected to pick up post-monsoon due to government capex
items.quote: But after the monsoo ns, I think the demand will pi ck up. And so this year the growth may not look very, very attractive because the base already is very high last year. But nevertheless, it will still be -- there will be high demand as far as the end user is concerned because of the large number of projects which are announced and the capex investment of government is again 10% higher than last

items.statement: Railway division launched 3 new products in FY24 including electrical control panels, brake pads for Metro coach, and dampers for Vande Bharat Coach
items.quote: Division launched 3 new products in FY '24, which include electrical control panels and brake pad for Metro coach and damper for Vande Bharat Coach.

items.statement: First quarter FY25 expected to be subdued for tractor industry due to elections, low reservoir levels, reduced haulage activity and moderate rabi output
items.quote: In the first few months of the fi scal '25, we might expect a slight decrease in the domestic tractor industry due to the ongoing election, low reservoir water levels, reduced haulage activity and a moderate rabi output

items.statement: NBFC license application submitted to RBI in March, expecting approval within 6-8 months to start operations in FY25
items.quote: We made this application sometime in March. So we are still in touch with RBI. We got some queries back from them, and we responded to them. And typical time from RBI for giving a license is anywhere within six to eight months.

items.statement: JV merger with NCLT pending, expected to be effective in Q1 FY25, combined JV revenue ~INR2,000 crores, initially margin dilutive
items.quote: So overall, I think like we mentioned, it will be close to roughly about INR2,000 crores of top line, which we get added. And initially, it will be a margin dilutive merger. So we are still in the process and the thing is pending with NCLT.

items.statement: Export volumes expected to grow 25-30% in FY25 but major growth from FY26 as base corrected after 30% decline in FY24
items.quote: If you grow by 25%, 30% this year, we'll probably come back to the same level what we were in FY '23. So essentially, to your question, I think, yes, the major growth will actually start coming from FY '26 on export number.

items.statement: Component export potential significant under China+1 strategy, Kubota currently sources ~USD1 billion from China, intends to shift significant part to India
items.quote: because we also looking at a China plus one strategy in Ch ina, they are doing sourcing of close to USD1 billion currently for the production requirement in Japan and they intend to shift the significant part to India, I think as we're going along

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA grew 53% YoY to Rs. 232 crores with margins at 13%, up 325 bps; combined with Excel EBITDA is Rs. 309 crores at 15.2% margins.
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA for FY24 stood at Rs. 232 crores vis-a-vis Rs. 151 crores last year in the same period, a growth of 53% year-on-year. This has also been helped by extremely good margins at 13%, an improvement of 325 basis points compared to last year's 9.77%.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward guidance but notes consolidated EBITDA and operating PBT were positive in FY24 and they remain committed to the EV business.
items.quote: As you know Rahil, we do not get into forward guidance, but the CFO can add to that, if you want to give any additional input.

items.statement: Standalone cash of Rs. 500+ crores will be used for further expansion and investments going forward.
items.quote: In terms of balance sheet strength, the company continues to have an almost zero-debt and standalone cash of Rs.500 + crores, which will be used for further expansion and investments as we go forward.

items.statement: Board is discussing and deliberating various options for raising funds in Greaves Electric Mobility; more information to come.
items.quote: The Board of the company has been discussing and deliberating the various options for raising funds in green electric mobility. And we will come up with more information as and when it is available.

items.statement: Commodity cycle has been soft in FY24 with positive impact expected to continue; geopolitical situation being monitored.
items.quote: One area where we saw a lot of pressure in the early parts of the last year was the overall commodity cycle. I'm happy to note that the commodity cycle has been soft in this current financial year and had a very positive impact and will continue to do so going forward.

items.statement: Engineering business growing fuel-agnostic portfolio (CNG, biodiesel, ethanol), engine components, and exports (12.5% of revenue); Excel integration advancing with cross-selling and mechatronics.
items.quote: In FY24, exports accounted for about 12.5% of total revenue. Our exports are relatively evenly distributed across the USA, European Union, and the rest of the world.

items.statement: Retail revenue grew 10% YoY to Rs. 588 crores with 120 bps margin improvement; expanded into EV parts, construction equipment parts, railway gensets, and digital mechanic loyalty program (20,000 mechanics, 5,000 daily active).
items.quote: Full year revenue increased by 10% Y-on-Y. Revenue was Rs. 162 crores for Q4 and for the full year was Rs.588 crores, which is a growth of 10%. Highlight was also the overall almost 120 bps of margin improvement overall compared to last year.

items.statement: EV business sold 61,000 units in FY24 (8,448 2W + 2,579 3W in Q4); launched Nexus family scooter without subsidy; ELTRA electric 3W gaining traction; awaiting FAME/EMPS subsidy approvals.
items.quote: In total for Q4 we did 11,527 to be precise. And we closed the year at 61,000 total units of two-wheeler and three-wheeler together.

items.quote: We anticipate a 35% growth in revenue for FY '25 compared to FY '24 while maintaining an EBITDA metric ton of INR5,000 plus for the whole year.

items.statement: Expect volume of 4.5 lakh tons for FY25, to be upgraded as capex commissions
items.quote: The projection for this year was already mentioned; we'll be going close to 4.5 lakh tons of volume this year going forward, which will be further upgraded when our different CapEx missions come into the plants.

items.statement: Target minimum 30% revenue growth for next 3-4 years
items.quote: And if you talk about the guidance for the next year, which should be again doing a 30% growth minimum for the next 3, 4 years.

items.statement: Expect to deploy INR150-200 crores on capex in FY25
items.quote: This year, as well, we are expecting to deploy close to INR150 crores - INR200 crores on CapEx.

items.statement: Plan to spend INR500-600 crores over next 2-3 years on capacity expansion
items.quote: And if you compare the next 3, 4 years, we'll be spending close to INR500 crores plus, INR600 crores plus in the coming 2, 3 years.

items.statement: Expect demand to pick up enormously by H2 FY25; H1 should also be strong with new all-time highs each quarter
items.quote: So we're expecting our -- obviously, the demand should pick up enormously by H2, but our H1 should be strong as well. And we should try and give new all time high in every quarter.

items.statement: Nabha Steel acquisition to increase EBITDA per ton on black pipes by at least 30% once fully operational
items.quote: Having the acquisition of Nabha Steel will in-house makes the coil itself and it will be from scrap. So effectively, we should be -- like on a black pipe right now if you are making close to INR2,000, INR1,500 EBITDA per ton. So it should be at least 30% more saving on increasing the EBITDA per ton on the black pipe itself.

items.statement: VAP share was ~35% in FY24, target to cross 40% in FY25 with new GL line, color-coated line and DFT structures
items.quote: This year, our value-added product was around 35%, . And going down the line, this year, we expect to cross the 40% mark.

items.statement: DFT capacity of 2 lakh tons (1 lakh each at Mangaon and Raipur) to be added by early FY26; DFT products have EBITDA per ton of INR7,000-8,000
items.quote: By the end of this year, we are adding 1 lakh tons of capacity, DFT capacities in our Mangaon plant. And say, by the early next year, we'll be adding another 1 lakh tons to the DFT capacity in our Raipur plant.

items.statement: Industry growing at 13-14% CAGR; no structural oversupply risk as JTL adds differentiated SKUs (DFT, larger sizes) rather than commodity pipes
items.quote: Otherwise, the market has been growing at a rate of 12%—13%. And this is what we're expecting, or maybe higher than this is going to happen post-elections. So there is no tailwind that we are expecting in the market. It's a growing industry, and the use case scenarios are expanding as Dhruv mentioned. So the industry, for primary and secondary, both, is growing at a good 13%, 14%.

items.statement: DFT commissioning delayed by 1-2 months; expected to reach plant by end of Q1 FY25 and commissioned by end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: DFT technology is talking to you, right in the way right now, and is being imported from China. It should reach the plant by this quarter or maybe the beginning of next quarter and should be commissioned by the end of Darshil Pandya: So it's kind of delayed... Pranav Singla: Yes, it's been delayed by a month or 2

items.statement: Promoter warrants: INR675 crores total committed, INR170 crores received; balance expected by August 2025 (1.5 years from Feb 2024); promoters to infuse as needed
items.quote: Out of INR675 crores, the large date is supposed to be having the money that we receive around February. So the date for us to make the last payment is 1.5 years after February. So that's effectively August for next financial year.

items.statement: Management aims to beat FY24 revenue growth of 10.4% in FY25 without taking any price increase, driven by volume and test-per-patient growth.
items.quote: If we don't do that, I would say that we will probably better our growth slightly than what we have delivered i n FY24 without the price increase

items.statement: Management targets patient volume growth of 6%+ quarterly in FY25, up from 3.2% in FY24.
items.quote: We want to see definitely this number moving up. And should be about 6% quarterly was the better number, yes, you're right.

items.statement: Gross margin is around 80% with limited room for further improvement; sustainable range is 78-80%.
items.quote: I think it's pretty high. I mean 80% roughly is gross margin. I think what we can do is, in my view, we can sustain here. But beyond this, I don't think there is a room to improve further, especially on the gross margin. But I think we can sustain between this 78% to 80% kind of margin.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target is pre-COVID level of around 26%, with willingness to reinvest operating leverage into growth rather than expand margins.
items.quote: I think we are saying pre-COVID level margins, which is around 26% EBITDA margin, where we are confident that we can maintain.

items.statement: Annual capex of Rs 50-60 crore for IT, instruments, and labs; plans to add 20 new hub labs primarily in North India.
items.quote: See, our average capex for this normally is about Rs. 50-60 Crore, which is a combination of investments in IT, investments in instruments, investments in labs. So I would say that will continue.

items.statement: Industry growth expected to be better in FY25 than FY23/FY24 as COVID base effects are fully cleaned up.
items.quote: My personal view is our industry would see better growth in FY25 than what we have seen in FY23 or even FY24.

items.statement: No price increases planned for routine or specialized tests in FY25; pure price benefit was 3.5% for FY24 but only ~1% in Q4.
items.quote: No. as of now, we don't plan to take any price increase neither on specialized nor on routine.

items.statement: Competitive intensity remains stable; predatory pricing has reduced as some players have taken price increases.
items.quote: So the deep discounting or if I were to call, predatory pricing, I think that is now not there in the market. So overall, I would say it's a positive news as we go forward into FY25.

items.statement: M&A remains part of strategy with focus on South India market entry; open to tuck-in acquisitions; Rs 960 crore cash on balance sheet.
items.quote: That would also include M&A as well. So, it's not that, while it may be a bit of a time since we did last M&A, but that has not been our eyes are not on inorganic. We will also search for inorganic.

items.statement: Tier-3/4 expansion continues with franchisee-driven collection network; margins sustained despite mix shift.
items.quote: We have seen that and you would have seen that over the last 3 years to 4 years the contribution of the Tier-3, Tier-4 markets have increased or improved in our overall mix. However, we've been able to sustain our EBITDA profile.

items.statement: Revenue for FY25 expected to be similar to FY24 levels even with zero new order inflow
items.quote: Even if we had zero inflow coming in this financial year, the new financial year. Even if there is zero inflow of orders we would still be doing a revenue of almost what we have done in this year the same range we should be getting in FY '25 as well of the same '24 revenues.

items.statement: Order inflow target for FY25 is Rs 10,000-12,000 crores across all sectors
items.quote: Shravanji this year, the total order inflow that we're looking at is to INR 10,000 crores to 12,000 crores at least that is the kind of range that we're looking for.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target for FY25 maintained at 12-14%
items.quote: We are looking at that same 12% to 14% kind of EBITDA targets, that I mentioned earlier as well.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is Rs 50-70 crores
items.quote: In terms of capex, the same INR50 crores to INR70-odd crores of capex is what we will be looking at.

items.statement: Net debt reduction target for FY25 is at least Rs 500 crores
items.quote: In this financial year in FY '25, we are targeting to further reduce the net debt by at least INR 500 crores plus.

items.statement: Target to become net debt-free on standalone basis within next two years (FY25-FY26)
items.quote: Our aim is to become a net debt -free company on a stand alone basis within the next two years. So FY25-FY '26, we will be net debt free company.

items.statement: Finance cost target for FY25 is Rs 350 crores vs Rs 500+ crores in FY24
items.quote: For FY '24 -25 the targeted finance cost is INR 350 crores against the INR 500-plus crores finance costs.

items.statement: FY24 order inflow was Rs 3,602 crores (42% irrigation, 35% water supply, 15% roads, 8% urban development)
items.quote: In FY 23-24, the company won orders worth Rs.3,602 crores, which obviously was lower than expected for the reasons that I mentioned. Of this total orders, 42% of the projects are in irrigation, 35% in water supply, 15% in roads and 8% in urban development.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin increased 256 bps YoY to ~12.3% on better execution and lower material costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margin witnessed a significant increase by 256 basis points. The EBITDA margin increased on account of better execution of the projects and reduction in cost of construction material.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin increased 250 bps YoY on higher revenue and lower construction material costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margin witnessed a significant increase by 250 basis points. The EBITDA margin increased on account of higher revenue and reduction in construction material costs.

items.statement: Road sector exposure reduced from 65% in FY20 to 37% currently as part of diversification strategy
items.quote: In the pre -COVID year of FY '20, it was 65% and in the current year, it's at 37%.

items.statement: Equipment debt of ~Rs 170 crores, 80% to be repaid in FY25 as scheduled
items.quote: Currently, our equipment debt stands at about INR170-odd crores, like I said, somewhere in that range is where we are standing, almost 80% of which we will be paying down in this financial year anyways.

items.statement: Alpha Alternatives warrant subscription: Rs 133 crores received (25%), balance ~Rs 400 crores by June 2025
items.quote: Rs 133 crores you rightly said received already in December 2023, Rs 400 crores as per SEBI guidelines under warrants they can put within 18 months from the first tranche. So 18 months will be completed in June 2025, around 20th June 2025.

items.statement: Divestment of 26% in 5 HAM assets to Alpha expected to yield Rs 508 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: From the next 5 projects 26% will receive total INR 508 crores and out of INR 508 crores majority of money will be received in this quarter and around INR 60 crores, INR65 crores will be received in quarter 2.

items.statement: Expect significant ordering pickup in H2 FY25 post-elections; NHAI/MORTH alone have Rs 1.2 lakh crore orders floated
items.quote: Even at the NHAI level there is more than INR 1,00,000 crores of orders that have already been floated. So, INR 1,20,000 crores of orders purely on NHAI and MORTH levels that have been floated.

items.statement: Election year historically slow for ordering; expect sharp recovery post-elections with 100-day government plan
items.quote: Election year is always a slow order ing year. And if you look at this detailing from back from a Vajpayeeji's era to now every election year is a slow year. But the year after it is usually or ordering increases significantly.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth slightly better than FY24's 12% and EBITDA margin expansion of ~100 bps annually for next couple of years
items.quote: More generally, my expectation is that we should be able to grow at a level slightly better than what we grew this year from the previous year. Margin expansion in terms of EBITDA should reflect our endeavor which I have outlined a couple of years ago, to have our EBITDA margin increase by 100 basis points every year for the next couple of years and I think that should hold.

items.statement: Expect 3-5% ARPU expansion in test-prep for current fiscal year
items.quote: going forward we are reasonably confident of a 3-5% ARPU expansion in the current fiscal year

items.statement: Intangible investments ~Rs.13 crore in FY24, amortized over 5-10 years; future investment rate to reduce 15-20% vs FY24
items.quote: They would be in the Rs.13 crore odd range for this year and we see that those kinds of investments are typically amortized anywhere between 5 to 10 years, on an average of 7 years and we will continue to make such investments over the years ahead but probably at a reducing rate of about 15 to 20 % compared to what we did this year.

items.statement: Test-prep enrollment grew ~10% in FY24; CUET student growth ~50%; Law test-takers down ~30% due to calendar shift
items.quote: FY24 we saw our volume expansion by about 10 % in terms of enrollment and the billing also has increased by 10% that would basically mean m ore or less consistent or constant average realization per

items.statement: International revenues grew ~32% in FY24; MarTech international +34%, EdTech international +28%; Indonesia and US drove 50% of MarTech international growth
items.quote: if you look at our international revenues, they have grown by about 32% in the year gone by, the MarTech revenue increase internationally has been 34% and in the EdTech segment that revenue expansion has been about 28%.

items.statement: Middle East premium admission consultancy grew 58%; Middle East volume +20%, billing +16%; 6 locations operational, plan to double in 12 months
items.quote: Our premium admission consultancy business grew by about 58% over the previous year and business in the Middle East has been growing steadily with a 20% volume expansion and a 16% billing expansion. We currently have 6 locations operational there and we are looking to double that number in the next 12 months.

items.statement: MarTech margin expansion driven by shift to higher-margin revenue mix and higher-margin international revenue (Singapore, Indonesia, US)
items.quote: MarTech showed a highly divergent trend, with revenue expanding by about 6% but margin expanding by a healthy 29% which was predominantly driven by two parameters - one being the pivoting of the revenue mix to higher margin business thereby effectively increaseing our gross margin and hence the follow-through into the business EBITDA.

items.statement: Publishing margin expanded due to paper prices cooling ~25% in last 6-9 months; expect stability and further margin improvement from selective price hikes
items.quote: As I shared about 12 months ago paper prices had hit the r oof but they have now cooled down by about 25% in the last 6 - 9 months, have been pretty stable in the last quarter and we expect that the price stability will hold and the enhanced margin should only get better in the new season because of price hike s which we will go through with in certain select title

items.statement: Platform business (Common Application Form) onboarded 40 institutions in first 4 months, sold 3,000+ forms; expect multiple-fold revenue increase
items.quote: We are extremely positive about the direction this new initiative will take in the coming years and we are expecting a multiple fold increase in the revenues through form sales through the platform.

items.statement: MarTech added 56 new clients in FY24; expect new clients to contribute 10-15% of revenue in coming year
items.quote: We continue to add new customers and we expect going forward the customers which were added last year will contribute about 10 to 15% of the revenue in the coming year and will continue to expand customer base in the current year.

items.statement: Law exam calendar shift (May to December) caused ~30% test-taker decline; recovery expected over couple of years; currently Rs.8-10 crore short of pre-COVID law revenue
items.quote: keeping that possibility aside we expect that the number of test takers will go backwards to the original numbers in a couple of years and CL being a market leader a large chunk of that increased test taker segment will proportio nately come to us

items.statement: MarTech Q4 muted due to Chinese New Year shutdown (4 weeks), Indonesia elections hiatus; best quarters typically Q2/Q3
items.quote: However, the opening for the current fiscal year has been reasonably strong usually because different multinationals in different geographies have different year endings. At the start of the new fiscal, their budgets get released at different points of time. Usually our best quarters are Q2 and Q3 with Q1 and Q4 being slightly muted.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic M&A opportunities in EdTech and MarTech; active discussions ongoing; hopeful of decision in next 2-4 quarters; cash held in FDs meantime
items.quote: There are active opportunities both in EdTech as well as MarTech space being evaluated and we are hopeful that something would come through in the next 2 to 4 quarters.

items.statement: Added 25 new test-prep centers in FY24; expect 30-40 new centers in FY25; centers on 3-year franchise contracts with renewals/exits
items.quote: Just to add the new centers which were added was the number was 25 and we expect somewhere between 30 to 40 new centers to go live in the current

items.statement: MarTech virtual revenue 6-7% of total; expect to increase 1-2pp annually, targeting 20% in 3-5 years; 20% from tech-enabled, 80% physical events/services
items.quote: the total virtual revenue to both the virtual events platform and some bits of meta commerce of transformations into 3d environment would be in the currently the range of 6 to 7% of the total revenue, going forward we see this percentage increasing marginally every year by 1-2% points of the total revenue and we are hoping to hit that in 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: MarTech EBITDA margin target ~10.5-11% for coming year; Q4 had one-time adjustments from older project closures
items.quote: Broadly there were some one-time adjustments of older projects etc. older costs which we closed which flowed in from Q3 and into Q4 and hence there was slight mutation of profitability in Q4 but overall I think we are on track to maintain a 10½ - 11%, a bit on that business going forward at least in the coming year.

items.statement: Animal feed FY25 EBIT per ton expected to be better than FY24 average of Rs 1,531/ton
items.quote: Our average last year was about Rs. 1,531 and I can definitely F.Y. 2024 was Rs. 1,531. The only thing I can say is that F.Y. 2025 will better than that.

items.statement: Cattle feed and fish feed expected to sustain double-digit volume growth for foreseeable future
items.quote: Cattle Feed and Fish Feed the game is wide open. There is no integration likely to happen because Cattle Feed market is huge. Category conversion is at 20% level, and we believe Cattle Feed and Fish Feed can both grow in double digits for the next at least foreseeable future.

items.statement: Dairy VAP salience targeted to grow another 4-5% in FY25 from current 36%
items.quote: we hope that this year we will grow the salience by another 4%-5%.

items.statement: Astec CDMO revenue expected to maintain ~67% growth run-rate in FY25 with base now over Rs 250 Cr
items.quote: This year we have grown by almost 67% from last year and we have a very good confidence that we'll continue to maintain that run rate as we get into F .Y. 2025. Now our base for the CDMO new products have also crossed 250 Crore.

items.statement: Astec new product revenues expected to start contributing from July-August FY25
items.quote: as we move forward in F.Y. 2025 from July-August onward we will start seeing the financial performance kicked in from some of these new products which we have been working on.

items.statement: Consolidated capex run-rate of Rs 250-300 Cr to be maintained in FY25; oil palm refinery expansion decision by end of Q2
items.quote: On an average we keep on investing about Rs. 250 to 300 Crore. I think, we will maintain that run rate but the investment will come. We just have added some capacities in our dairy business. We have to invest in distribution in our chicken and dairy business. I will tell you how we invest in distribution because wherever we go , we require freezers and chillers which we invest in and a big chunk o

items.statement: Astec capex cycle to be discussed in Q3-Q4 FY25 depending on CDMO pickup
items.quote: Astec, we have commissioned one herbicide plant and capitalized it in Q 1, so we are in a situation where we have capacity to fill. But I am very sure that Astec CAPEX cycle will come under discussion in Q3 and Q4 because in case contract manufacturing or CDMO business picks up , we will require specialized capacity for specialized product for specialized customers.

items.statement: Animal feed Q4 EBIT margin Rs 1,874/ton; management expects to maintain close to Q4 levels in current quarter
items.quote: Q4 we have gone to Rs. 1,874. So, my sense is that the upward trend will continue and I am very sure whatever on the year-on-year basis I am saying, and we will be able to maintain close to Q4 numbers in this quarter also.

items.statement: Oil palm value addition reduced profit impact of 20% CPO price drop from expected 40% to actual 20%
items.quote: we had a target of Rs. 184 Crore PBT and there was a significant drop in CPO prices. There was almost a 12% - 13% drop in crude palm oil price, 20% drop. So, if we were only in crude palm oil and palm kernel oil , our profits should have fallen by 40%. But because of these profits came down only by about 20%.

items.statement: Astec enterprise business seeing no green shoots; focus on CDMO and new products to de-lever from enterprise profits
items.quote: On the enterprise side , we haven't seen any green shoots in the market. But internally I would hate to give any forecast on when the market should revive back. In turn what we are focusing on are the things which are in our hand which are the CDMO, and the new product development and our entire goal and ambition is that as we get into F.Y. 2025, we completely de -lever ourselves from enterprise p

items.statement: Fish meal prices softening; company well-placed with low inventory in India and Bangladesh
items.quote: what we are seeing now is some kind of softening has started happening and good thing is that we don't have too much of stock either in Bangladesh or India. So , my sense is that we are reasonably well placed in case the price falls.

items.statement: DDGS availability from ethanol program offsetting higher corn prices in animal feed
items.quote: if the energy prices because of corn have gone up , the protein prices because of DDGS have come down which has helped utilize the cost increase in our feed segment.

items.statement: Palm oil prices stabilizing but could rise; import duty may increase post-elections due to bumper mustard crop
items.quote: Palm oil prices have dropped somewhat but they seem to be stabilizing now and of course they could rise a little bit. We don't expect that palm oil prices will go very high but Indian prices also depend on the import duty and since we have bumper red seed crops and farmers have to be kept satisfied it is likely that after the elections import duties on imported oil could be raised.

items.statement: No equity raise planned for Astec; debt-equity ~1.3x, short-term needs to be met internally
items.quote: No, we are not looking at any raise because we strongly believe that we have industry has bottomed out and now the journey will be upwards and in this business, I am saying that debt equity is still about 1.3 or something. So, it's not a very big concern. We can tide over whatever is the short-term requirement by supporting internally.

items.statement: Branded poultry volumes grew ~15% in FY24 (Yummy's 13%, Real Good Chicken 15.6%); live bird declining
items.quote: Yummy's grew about 13% and Real Good Chicken grew about 15.6% and if we take the blended number, then the branded volumes grew by about 15% in F .Y. 2024 over F.Y. 2023 and that is the focus for this year also.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 30-40 bps
items.quote: We continue to maintain our credit cost guidance of 30 to 40bps.

items.statement: Ex-CL spread guidance of 5.0-5.25% for medium term
items.quote: Our ex-CL Spread guidance of 5.0-5.25% stands for the medium term.

items.statement: Opex to assets guidance of around 3.0% going ahead
items.quote: We continue to maintain the guidance of around 3.0% going ahead; as we focus on expansion and get deeper into new markets.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing may increase another 10-20 bps at best
items.quote: Net-net, coming to cost of borrowing another 10-20 bps increase at best is what we're looking at.

items.statement: Co-lending to contribute around 10% of disbursements in near future
items.quote: Co-lending business is growing and expect this to contribute around 10% of disbursements in the near future.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25 branch additions per year and 60-70 touchpoints per year
items.quote: Branch expansion, we are targeting 20 to 25 branches every year. And along with that, say, about 60 to 70 touchpoints per year.

items.statement: AUM growth target of 30%
items.quote: Overall, we are targeting 30% growth.

items.statement: LAP portfolio target of 20% by March 2027 from current 13%
items.quote: Our 3-year plan is to take it to 20%. So, it will be gradual, it will not be very sharp but March'27 is 20%.

items.statement: ROA expected around 3.5% (3.4-3.6%) next year with ROE 16%+
items.quote: So that range can be 3.4% to 3.6%. But let's say you anchor around 3.5% plus/minus which essentially leaves you with a 16% plus ROE.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target of 5x (asset-to-equity 6x) with 2-2.5 years runway
items.quote: At our planned expansion, debt-to-equity of 5x or asset-to-equity of 6x is what we have in mind.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of close to 30% in 3-5 years, 34-35% for next 1-2 years
items.quote: Our aim in the medium term is to get that down to around close to 30% levels. In maybe 3- to 5-year timeframe, we should be able to get it down to 30% levels. Otherwise, next 1 to 2 years, we are looking at 34%, 35% level.

items.statement: Insurance agency license obtained in Feb 2024, expect INR 5-6 Cr quarterly income from Q3
items.quote: Once we sign with at least 2 to 3 companies and cover the entire book that we onboard today, my expectation is that should add close to INR5 crores to INR6 crores of additional income into the P&L, on a quarterly basis. So, let's say Q3 onwards is when you should be able to see the full income.

items.statement: NIM expected to stabilize at 5.3-5.5% with spread at 5.0-5.25%
items.quote: Our NIM should be in a similar range where we are today like 5.3% - 5.5% is what we have thought.

items.statement: Will absorb COB increase up to 20 bps, not pass on to customers; will pass on 25-50 bps if rates rise sharply
items.quote: As we mentioned earlier, up to small increases like 10, 20 basis points, we are looking to absorb it, and we are not looking to pass it on to the customer.

items.statement: No stress seen in customer incomes; incomes growing 10-15% annually extrapolated from ticket size growth
items.quote: Ticket size growth as you can see annually, we are seeing about a 10% kind of ticket size growth. So, I would say incomes are also broadly moving up maybe 10% to 15% income growth is what we can kind of extrapolate.

items.statement: BT Out elevated due to repricing (3 PLR hikes in 2 years), but total erosion stable at 16-18%; will do cohort-based repricing
items.quote: BT Out rates are higher largely because of rates being higher because we have repriced the large part of our book and that is creating some tension with customers. That's primarily the reason.

items.statement: NHB refinance at ~20% of borrowings; drew Rs 250 Cr in Apr'24; NHB rate ~50 bps below marginal bank rate
items.quote: NHB refinance as a percentage of the overall book my sense it will be 20% on an average basis.

items.statement: Loan book growth guidance of 30%-35% for FY25
items.quote: in terms of loan book, we are talking about a 30%-35% of growth

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance of 40%-45% for FY25
items.quote: in terms of deposits we intend to have somewhere around a 40%-45% kind of a growth

items.statement: Secured book mix target of 45% by end of FY25
items.quote: by the end of next year we would want to be around 45%

items.statement: ROA guidance range of 2.3%-2.5% for medium term
items.quote: we would want to be range bound to 2.3 to 2.5

items.statement: ROE guidance of 14%-16% for next 2 years
items.quote: our aim will be to have a guidance for ROE for 14% to 16%

items.statement: Cost to income including CGFMU target of 57% for FY25
items.quote: our ambition is that for the next year, our cost to income including CGFMU will be in the region of 57%

items.statement: Credit cost outlook of 1.5%-1.8% for FY25
items.quote: I would want to be at the same stage where we are today for this financial year which has been somewhere in the range of 1.5% to 1.8%

items.statement: CGFMU expense estimate of 70-80 crores for FY25
items.quote: our expense on CGFMU will be somewhere in the range of 70 to 80 crores

items.statement: Capital raise expected in 15-18 months as CRAR approaches 20%
items.quote: We should be able to raise capital when we are inching towards that 20% number

items.statement: No slowdown or stress observed due to elections
items.quote: We haven't. We haven't to an extent not heard anything from the market or from our peers

items.statement: Vikas Loans AUM surpassed Rs. 2,600 crores, contributing over 53% of inclusive finance portfolio
items.quote: Vikas Loans, the individual loan portfolio offered to Bank's graduating JLG customers has surpassed Rs. 2,600 crores of AUM and now contributes over 53% of the inclusive finance portfolio

items.statement: NIM increased to 9.8% in FY24 from 9.5% in FY23
items.quote: NIM has increased from 9.5% in FY23 to 9.8% in FY24

items.statement: Plan to reduce Vikas Loan pricing from 28% to around 24% over next year
items.quote: our intent was really going on the pricing path in terms of reducing it from current 28% to around closer to around 24% over the next 1 year

items.statement: CGFMU claim target of 45-50 crores gross claims for FY25
items.quote: for this financial year we would look to make claims, gross claims somewhere in the region of 45 to 50 crores

items.statement: Universal bank license eligibility expected in about a year
items.quote: we will take about a year to be eligible to fulfill all the criteria for being eligible to apply for being a universal Bank

items.statement: Management expects demand improvement from Q2 FY25 and significant improvement in H2 FY25 across both segments.
items.quote: We anticipate that the overall scenario will start normalizing from second half of FY25 and we have all the enablers to regain our normal double-digit growth trajectory which we had demonstrated throughout all these years.

items.statement: Prices have bottomed out in both pigment and agro segments; prices will go up with demand improvement.
items.quote: Yes, definitely we can say that not only in the pigment segment but even in the agro segment. Prices have bottomed out completely and with the improvement in demand, we see the prices will also go up and there will be increase in volume as well as value.

items.statement: ECL provision estimate was ₹30,000 crores over 5 years (₹6,000 crores/year), now lower due to improved book quality
items.quote: At a point of time, we have made on assessment for the ECL, the provision requirement was about 30,000 odd crores, which is required to be in about 5 years' time, which works out to be about 6,000 crore a year. With the balance sheet profit of about 60,000 crores, this does not really worry us at all. But, I must also mention that, then and now, the quality of book has even improved. So, my assess

items.statement: JLR expects EBIT margin around FY24 level (8.5%) for FY25, investment spend ~GBP 3.5bn, targets net debt zero by end FY25, Q1 cash flow broadly breakeven
items.quote: we expect EBIT margin for this year to be around the level of FY 2024. We do expect to have to spend a little bit more in terms of demand generation, and we will oﬀset that operationally with cost reduction. We expect investment spend to be around GBP 3.5 billion, and we are holding our target to be net debt zero by the end of this ﬁnancial year

items.statement: Tata Motors consolidated capex for next year broadly similar to FY24 at ~Rs 8,300 Cr, JLR capex ~GBP 3.5bn
items.quote: is well funded by the operating cash, and nothing abnormal there. And the investment spending, we ended the year at Rs. 8,300 Cr. There are some sure questions, I already see what is likely to be JLR's investment and what is ours - about GBP 3.5 billion in JLR and broadly similar lines for Tata Motors

items.statement: CV business achieved double-digit EBITDA for FY24, Q4 EBITDA ~12%, PBT ~Rs 6,000 Cr, $1bn EBITDA new high
items.quote: Overall numbers, it's been again a very strong year, there's a highest ever revenues, highest ever proﬁts as far as this business is concerned as well. And we ended at Rs. 78,800 Cr revenue with a double -digit EBITDA that we had co mmitted. And for the quarter the EBITDA came in stronger at about 12

items.statement: PV industry growth expected <5% in FY25 due to high base, channel inventory, elections, heatwave; secular growth 6-8%
items.quote: after triangulating the projections from multiple places, we clearly see that the industry will moderate and grow less than 5%, given that the pent -up demand has got exhausted, the channel inventory is high a nd in the ﬁrst quarter, we will face certain factors like that of elections, heat wave which might dampen the demand temporarily for quarter one

items.statement: JLR order book 133k units (excl. 33k Range Rover BEV waitlist), above normalized 110k; Europe/UK soft, NA/Overseas/China strong
items.quote: We did end the year with an order book of 133,000 units, that includes orders for SV vehicles that does not include the 33,000 people I mentioned to have signed up to the waiting list on Range Rover BEV. Pre-COVID, our order bank sort of averaged a normalized level, of around 110,000 units.

items.statement: JLR Range Rover/RR Sport production capacity ramped up; Solihull plant at record 201k Range Rover sales, Defender 115k record
items.quote: Range Rover is up 27%, that's driven by progressive improvements in both our production system and those of our suppliers, allowing us to move up capacity levels in our Solihull plant. That level of 201,000 units is a record sales for the Range Rover brand.

items.statement: PV Sanand EV facility ramp: Jan <1k, last month 6,500, targeting 10k soon, then 15-16k/month
items.quote: Sanand facility, we started in Jan, we did about less than 1,000 production in Jan, but we have progressively ramped up. And last month we crossed 6,000, to be speciﬁc, 6,500. And soon the production ramp-up is going to attain a level of 10,000. And going forward then, you know, further improvement up to 15,000 to 16,000 numbers

items.statement: JLR VME increased from 0.5% to 3% YoY, offset by material cost improvements (GBP 267m, half raw materials, half non-repeat of semi/supplier costs)
items.quote: price is now a negative in this walk, whereas historically for the last few quarters, it's been positive. That is due to slow increases in our VME rates from 0.5% a year ago to 3%, that 3% is still very light in comparison to many others in the market. Those increases in VME have however been more than oﬀset by material cost improvements versus a year ago

items.statement: CV commodities: ferrous metals softened, aluminum up, other non-ferrous stable; Q1 seeing increases in castings, forgings, aluminum, tires, forex; will pass through price increases
items.quote: In Q1 itself, we are seeing some increase in casting , forgings, aluminum, tires. Fore x will also have some impact. So, yes, Balaji, I think we will have some impact due to commodities, which we will pass through appropriate price increases at the right time

items.statement: PV battery costs still declining, secured best costs from supplier; further reduction expected but nearing floor; better realizations from this quarter
items.quote: So far, you know, we have been seeing the battery prices still coming down. We have secured the best possible battery costs from our supplier. Going forward, I think this is going to still go down to some extent, but I think this would be more or less reaching the level of what we can think as the best possible reduction of sale prices.

items.statement: PV multi-powertrain mix: petrol 58%, diesel 13%, EV 13%, CNG 16%; CAFE headroom substantial, prepared for CAFE III/IV
items.quote: With petrol at 58%, diesel at 13%, 13% EVs, and 16% CNGs, so we are playing all the powertrains and it's coming through very nicely. And that has ensured those green emissions friendly vehicles also mean that our CAFE headroom that we have is substantial at this point in time.

items.statement: Tata Motors Finance GNPA 5.6%, NNPA 3.2%, collection efficiency improving, early delinquency healthy, capital adequacy and liquidity adequate
items.quote: Collection eﬃciency continues to improve and that's why GNPA has now reduced to 5.6% and NNPA is 3.2%. So from that perspective, the portfolio is back under control

items.statement: Consolidated automotive debt Rs 16,000 Cr (Rs 7,300 Cr external, Rs 8,700 Cr finance leases); India business Rs 1,000 Cr net cash; JLR net debt GBP 732m (from GBP 3bn), repaid >GBP 1.8bn from operating cash flow
items.quote: automotive debt is now Rs. 16,000 Cr, of it Rs. 7,300 Cr is the external debt a nd Rs. 8,700 Cr is ﬁnancial leases. And split diﬀerently, the India business is now Rs. 1,000 Cr positive cash. JLR and Singapore are the two places where we have the debt to be knocked out, and the plan is to ensure this year we take that out completely

items.statement: JLR no immediate plans to access bond markets; will fund in due course
items.quote: At the moment there are no plans to access the bond markets, but in due course, we will of course do funding again, but no direct, no immediate plans.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend: Rs 3 ordinary + Rs 3 special = Rs 6/share; DVR Rs 3.1 + Rs 3.1 = Rs 6.2/share; total payout ~Rs 2,300 Cr (highest ever)
items.quote: the Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 3 for the ordinary shareholders, Rs. 3.1 for the DVR shareholders, which is the normal dividend and there is also a special dividend in lieu of the successful TTL IPO of Rs. 3 per share for Ordinary and Rs. 3.1 for the DVR holders . So together is about Rs. 6 and Rs. 6.2 resulting in a cash ﬂow of almost Rs. 2,300 Cr, the highest ever dividend that Tata

items.quote: PLI, so far we have got the cer tiﬁcate for Tiago EV. And right now the SOP for disbursement is being ﬁnalized. And we are hoping that in the second half of this ﬁnancial year, we may start getting the disbursement. We are also going to apply for additi onal two products in Q1 and for the additional one product in Q2 also

items.statement: Management expects FY25 volume growth of around 10% and EBITDA margin of 20-22%
items.quote: we have always been optimistic, and we always feel that 10% to 15% growth rate has been our norm. There have been a few years like last year where we have dropped below that. But otherwise, 10% is, I think, what we expect.

items.statement: FY24 capex was INR120 crores; FY25 capex planned at INR60-80 crores plus potential INR75-200 crores for new products over 2 years
items.quote: this year, our total capital expenditure is about INR120 crores. In that INR120 crores is also some expenditure for routine maintenance capex and the solar plant to supply electricity to our Dahej facility.

items.statement: Ethylamine plant (100 TPD, INR375 cr capitalized) commissioned and running well; utilization ~60% in H2 FY24
items.quote: the ethylamines plant, which we had been constructing over the last 2, 2.5 years has been commissioned and has been running very well much better than our expectations. And it is now probably the largest ethylamine plant in the world.

items.statement: Acetonitrile plant utilization ~55-60% in H2 FY24 due to Chinese competition
items.quote: The second half was not as good as the first half because the Chinese pressure continued in terms of price and aggressive selling in the Indian market. So -- we were at about half our capacity 55%, a little better than half.

items.statement: Pharma demand stable and growing; agrochemical destocking ending but Chinese competition increasing
items.quote: the market demand for pharma is quite stable now and growing. And we have managed to increase our sales in terms of tonnage.

items.statement: Ethylamine margins improved in last 3-4 months due to lower ethanol prices and stable selling prices; methylamine margins stable; MIPA margins pressured after anti-dumping duty expiry
items.quote: But as far as pricing is concerned, yes, it has improved on both the selling side as well as the raw material side, the ethyl alcohol has softened. compared to what it was, say, 6 months, | year ago.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20-22%; FY24 average selling price dropped ~20%, top line down ~14%
items.quote: I would say that 20% EBITDA margin is what we hope to achieve between 20% and 22%.

items.statement: FY24 volume growth under 10% (just short of 1 lakh tons); H2 weaker due to acetonitrile and MIPA pressure
items.quote: Yes, total volume growth for the whole year is under 10%. Second half was much -- I mean, it was disappointing largely under pressure from Acetonitrile, as I said earlier, to Nilesh.

items.statement: Acetonitrile prices stabilized around INR145-160/kg; ethylamine prices INR150-160/kg; raw materials: ammonia INR50-52/kg, acetic acid <INR40/kg, methanol <INR30/kg
items.quote: About INR150 or so. For the larger people INR145, for the smaller people INR160 that kind.

items.statement: Chinese competition across products (acetonitrile, MIPA, methylamine); Balaji adding 40k ton methylamine plant; Chinese methylamine capacity announcement noted
items.quote: it's not just acetonitrile, it's across the board, they have too much capacity in most of their chemical industry. And in fact, we recently saw an announcement by one of their companies for a huge methylamines plant.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty investigation on acetonitrile initiated March 2024; interim relief possible Q4 FY25; injury estimated 15-20%
items.quote: we have filed antidumping in December and in March '24, the investigation has been initiated, hearings are going on right now and we are planning for filing interim relief also in that. But it will take time. Maybe in Q4 of '24-'25, we expect that to come, if it is favorable on our side. Injury is in the range of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: FY24 sales mix: ~40-50% amines, ~25% derivatives, ~20-25% specialty (mainly acetonitrile)
items.quote: It's still, I think, in the region of 40% to 50% is the main Amines about 25% is derivatives and about 20% to 25% is specialty, which is the main one being Acetonitrile.

items.quote: So mainly CSR expenses, which we could not spend, we had to make provision for that, and there was one asset at Patalganga, which was not being used, so we had to impair that. and since there is increase in production, the power and fuel expenses have increased.

items.statement: Solar capacity 8.5 MW total (3.5 MW added in Jan FY24); saves INR3-4 crores/year vs grid; power cost lower in FY24 due to lower coal prices
items.quote: Yes, about -- my estimate would be these 8 megawatts would be giving you about INR3 crores to INR4 crores of savings in view of if you were buying from the grid, right?

items.statement: Old ethylamine plant at Patalganga (15k tons) to be converted to methylamine over ~2 years; Dahej methylamine plant at 80-85% utilization (45k tons/yr)
items.quote: No, we are having plans to convert it into methylamines. The engineering has just started. It would take a little time to convert it but_we are preparing for 2 years down the line when the demand has grown to a level where we will need it.

items.statement: Acetonitrile market size 30-35k tons; 50-55% imported in FY24
items.quote: Market size would be in the range of 30,000 to 35,000 tons. And I would say about 50% of that estimated is imported last year. 50% to 55% was imported.

items.quote: In all of these projects, launches and the expansions, we are looking at a guidance of about 33% to 35% growth in our pre-sales figure from what we did this year, where we are aiming between Rs.1,350 plus crores in this FY25.

items.quote: And our target is to bring this to 0.8x by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Estimated net cash flow of Rs.750 crores from OC received and ongoing portfolio
items.quote: The 5 estimated net cash flow from OC received and ongoing portfolio is estimated to be Rs.750 crores

items.statement: Business development pipeline targeting Rs.3,000-3,500 crores of new projects in FY25
items.quote: We also have further guided that we are also looking at our portfolio expansions wherein we are under advanced talks to a lot of projects, and hopefully that should materialize during this financial year, the coming financial year. items.statement: Manhattan new phase targeting launch in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our estimate is that towards the last quarter of FY25 we should be able to launch this.

items.statement: Existing land bank of ~12 million sq ft carpet area (Wadala, Kanjurmarg, others) to be launched over next 2-4 years
items.quote: With our existing portfolio and existing land banks, that is Wadala, Kanjurmarg and other places, we have about 12-odd million square feet of carpet area to be launched.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 30%, PAT margin 15%; Q4 FY24 EBITDA Rs.69 crores, PAT Rs.29 crores
