items.quote: Whenever it is a slum, it is usually around 18% to 22%. If it is society, it is about 25% to 35%. MHADA redevelopment is about 30%, 35%. So, that's where we range. And if it is our own land, then it is about 40%, 50%.

items.statement: Debt stable at Rs.780 crores, debt-to-equity 0.9x, weighted average cost of debt below 12%
items.quote: I am pleased to inform that despite aggressive business development activities, our debt remained stable at Rs.780 crores, improving the debt equity ratio below 1x benchmark and precisely at 0.9x to equity. The weighted average cost of the debt remains stable and below 12%.

items.statement: FY24 collections Rs.570 crores; Q4 FY24 collections Rs.197 crores (91% YoY growth)
items.quote: The collections stood at Rs.570 crores.

items.statement: Strong demand across segments: high-end (Juhu 38% sold pre-completion), mid-affordable (Bangalore), mass (Manhattan 76% sold at podium stage)

items.statement: Portfolio average realization ~Rs.19,000/sq ft (Rs.1,000+ crores sales / 4+ lakh sq ft); Bangalore Rs.6,000-9,000/sq ft, Mumbai varies by micro-market

items.quote: In Mumbai market, we are spending on a very different micro market right from our own land at Wadala to Juhu or to the Pantnagar Eden Project, Greenfinity which is another affordable product at Wadala kind of a thing.

items.quote: It's about 4,000 square meters of land.

items.statement: Residential market at 10-year high in CY2023; Mumbai highest sales volume and YoY growth; demand fueled by need for larger spaces and upgraded lifestyle
items.quote: Sales volume in primary markets have grown at an extremely healthy rate since 2020 and it has culminated into a 10 year high in the calendar year 2023. The last quarter, Mumbai has witnessed the highest sales volume and year on year growth all across the Indian metros.

items.statement: Redevelopment deals preferred by societies/slum dwellers due to brand trust, quality, and timeline confidence
items.quote: Now society, slum dwellers, even the cluster people, all of them prefer to have larger branded developers coming and doing their development because, A, they are convinced with the kind of project quality; B, they are convinced with the kind of timeline.

items.statement: Targets FY26 revenue of about 4,000 crores with steady EBITDA margin around 12.5%
items.quote: we aim to achieve a top line of about 4,000 crores while maintaining a steady EBITDA margins at around Sangam (India) Limited 13 th May 2024 12.5% for FY26

items.quote: During this quarter, there has been an improvement in capacity utilization under all the segments of the company

items.quote: EBITDA margin is at 10%, which is expanded about 1.7% quarter on quarter again

items.quote: Currently, 53% of our product mix comprises of value-added products, and going forward, we are committed to increase this further

items.quote: As the sector headwinds have reduced a little, we are witnessing a slight uptake in demand, reflected in improved price relations across all our product segments

items.quote: And it is around 57 to 58,000 rupees is the prices per candy. So it is in the reasonable market

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity comfortable; at 85-90% of peak debt levels; undrawn long-term debt Rs 150-200 cr; peak interest cost in Q4 FY24, expected to decline
items.quote: We can safely say that we are at least about 85-90% at the peak debt levels

items.statement: Working capital borrowing cost blended at around 8%
items.quote: Working capital is between around 8%. Blended

items.statement: Maintained 20% dividend for continuity; will work on codified dividend policy
items.quote: So we just tried to maintain continuity. Last year, it could have been a higher number, but since we could see that, you know, margins are going to be under pressure in the future. So we tried to be conservative last year and this year we try to maintain some continuity there

items.statement: FTA talks with UK and Australia advanced; expected to progress after new government forms in a couple of months
items.quote: the very advanced talk with the UK and Australia, but it will take some time with the new government will come into power, right? Probably it will happen in a couple of months time

items.quote: For example dyes and chemicals used in processing. When our fabric turnover increases the raw material on the processing division is dyes and chemicals but that is classified in other expenses

items.quote: Currently, Garment consists of about 3% of the total business

items.quote: we are at the peak of the interest rates across the globe. So now that is beyond our control. So whatever easing will happen there, that can contribute

items.statement: 30-40 major clients across segments; details in investor presentation
items.quote: there are about 30-40 big clients that we put on the presentation

items.quote: we are better placed in terms of the varied product ranges and when we are entering some markets where you know we're dealing with brands so we are able to supply various products versus just doing one product there

items.statement: ESOP/Sweat equity issued 2 years ago amortized over 5 years; exceptional item relates to this non-cash cost
items.quote: this is with regards to the the ESOPs and SWEAT equities that that were issued to various company, company officials, I think 2 years back. So that is that that is going to be amortised over 5 years

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target upwards of 20%
items.quote: We continue to be bullish in terms of our outlook for '25 and expect revenue growth to be upwards of 20%.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin target high-teens
items.quote: In terms of margins, we are looking at high-teen margins on a consolidated basis.

items.quote: We have also broken ground in our Surat greenfield project and have committed INR75 crores for Phase 1 expansion.

items.quote: So overall, between Surat, Nadiad, Nashik, we are looking at about INR100 crores CAPEX.

items.statement: Truly Indian brand 3-4% of standalone revenue, targeting Ashoka size in 3-5 years
items.quote: We are looking at anywhere between 3 to 5 years for the Truly Indian brand to get to that.

items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 20.2%, expanding by 230 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 22.3%.

items.statement: Standalone FY24 EBITDA margin 24.6%, up 290 bps YoY
items.quote: We managed to expand EBITDA margin by 290 basis points, reaching 24.6%.

items.statement: Strong demand across all brands; volume and revenue growth near equal in FY24

items.statement: Negotiated orders Rs.31 crores and under negotiation Rs.33 crores as of 1st May (excl. large tickets)

items.statement: FY24 consolidated gross margin 59.7%, EBITDA margin 20.2% (up from 18.6%), PAT margin 12.8% (up from 12.5%)

items.statement: Water reuse market in India expected to become significant by 2027-29; Invent product line targets Rs.75-125 crores in India
items.quote: I would say, i f we do everything right, we are looking at anywhere between Rs.75-125 crores

items.statement: Southeast Asia order book >Rs.100 crores; entering Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Indonesia; Thailand revenue projection $2-3M
items.quote: The orderbook is still great. We have more than Rs.100 crores of orders for Southeast Asia.

items.quote: So, 10-15% new products will contribute once they get stabilize. For new product to launch is very easy , for ne w products to capture the market and become a dominant player takes time, 4-5 years

items.statement: FY24 ex-India revenue ~60%; UK Waterfront targeting 5-6x growth to Rs.200 crores in 4 years
items.quote: We are planning 18-20 million pounds like Rs.200 crores in four year time. So, from Rs.35 crores today.

items.statement: Three large international orders (Hong Kong, Canada, USA) totalling $50-60M with >75% win probability

items.statement: Government approved Jash technology for all hydropower plants under new small hydro policy
items.quote: on those interactions the government has now in their new small hydro policy approved our technology for all the hydropower plants

items.statement: Working capital cycle ~100-110 days when averaged across quarters
items.quote: If you average it out through all the four quarters, then will realise our working capital cycle is not more than 100-110 days.

items.statement: Tax rate currently 20-22% (100% SEZ exemption), rising to 24-25% after 50% exemption; US losses fully absorbed
items.quote: This year we only got 100% exemption in SEZ unit IV after that we will have 50%. So, at present our tax level will be 20-22% but later on its around 24-25%. In US we have already absorbed all losses.

items.statement: Waterfront UK acquisition completed; 80% owned; share issuance done April 2024; Scottish Enterprise grant 75,000 GBP received
items.quote: Its was done in April 2024.

items.statement: Employee retention initiatives: ESOP, sports turf, restaurant, campus investments to attract talent
items.quote: ESOP, turf cricket, restaurant, employee engagement activities, good campuses are all part of that.

items.statement: Rodney Hunt order book $43M; FY25 revenue target $35M (up from $26.5M)
items.quote: We already have order book of $43 million in Rodney Hunt. So, it means that next year also Rodney Hunt would grow by more than 30%.

items.statement: India addressable market Rs.800-900 crores currently; 30% of wastewater capacity built, 70% pending
items.quote: So, Rs.800-900 crores was our addressable market in India. Now this can increase if t he government increase the spending on water and wastewater

items.quote: Most of the time we are dependent on EPC contract or, we may produce an email not a delivery. So, in spite of having orders, we may not achieve the desired targeted revenue.

items.statement: >70% market share in gates in India; competitors are small; detailed competitor list in website FAQ
items.quote: For gates, by the way gates we have more than 70% market share in India. So, there are very small companies turnover wise who are our competitors.

items.statement: Discrete manufacturing model: capacity utilisation skewed to H2 (Q4 40% of revenue); adding shifts/people can increase throughput
items.quote: in the first quarter revenue is 10%, in the first half the revenue is 30% , in the third quarter the revenue is 60% and the last quarter the revenue is 100

items.statement: Tata Motors capex for next year broadly similar to FY24 at Rs 8,300 Cr, JLR capex ~GBP 3.5bn

items.statement: JLR Q4 revenue GBP 7.86bn (+11% YoY), EBIT 9.2%, full-year EBIT 8.5%, free cash flow GBP 2.27bn record, net debt GBP 732m from GBP 3bn
items.quote: Record revenue in the quarter of GBP 7.86 billion, that's up 11% year-on-year. Full-year revenue also a record. And free cash ﬂow, GBP 892 million (Q4) or GBP 2.27 billion for the full year that's a record for JLR and a record by a large margin

items.statement: CV business FY24 revenue Rs 78,800 Cr, double-digit EBITDA, Q4 EBITDA ~12%, PBT ~Rs 6,000 Cr, $1bn EBITDA

items.statement: JLR order book 133,000 units (excl. 33,000 Range Rover BEV waitlist), above pre-COVID normalized 110,000
items.quote: So we did end the year with an order book of 133,000 units, that includes orders for SV vehicles that does not include the 33,000 people I mentioned to have signed up to the waiting list on Range Rover BEV. items.statement: PV industry FY25 growth expected <5% due to high base, channel inventory, elections, heat wave; secular trend 6-8%
items.quote: after triangulating the projections from multiple places, we clearly see that the industry will moderate and grow less than 5%, given that the pent -up demand has got exhausted, the channel inventory is high a nd in the ﬁrst quarter, we will face certain factors like that of elections, heat wave which might dampen the demand temporarily for quarter one, I would say

items.statement: CV FY25 volumes expected flat to slight decline; Q1 panned well, demand pickup from H2
items.quote: we expect, I think, the same way to continue. But I think overall, for the whole year, as we had said earlier, we remain cautiously optimistic. I think we will see a ﬂat to maybe a slight decline in the overall volumes for the year. That's what we see

items.statement: EV industry grew 70% YoY in FY24, Q4 growth 40% vs PV industry 8.5%; barriers reducing with 14 models, 12,000+ chargers, prices from Rs 8 lakh
items.quote: You know, we just saw, in the charts that I presented, that while the P V industry just grew by 8.5%, the EV industry grew by a whopping 70%. items.statement: JLR VME increased from 0.5% to 3% YoY, offset by material cost improvements (half raw materials, half non-repeat of semiconductor/supplier costs)

items.statement: CV commodities: ferrous metals softened, aluminum up, other non-ferrous stable; Q1 seeing increases in castings, forgings, aluminum, tires, forex
items.quote: In Q1 itself, we are seeing some increase in casting , forgings, aluminum, tires. Fore x will also have some impact. So, yes, Balaji, I think we will have some impact due to commodities, which we will pass through appropriate price increases at the right time

items.statement: PV powertrain mix: petrol 58%, diesel 13%, EV 13%, CNG 16%; CAFE headroom substantial
items.quote: With petrol at 58%, diesel at 13%, 13% EVs, and 16% CNGs, so we are playing all the powertrains and it's coming through very nicely. And that has ensured those green emissions friendly vehicles also mean that our CAFE headroom that we have is substantial at this point in time.

items.statement: JLR Range Rover up 27% to 201k units (record), Defender up 32% to 115k units (record 76-year history)

items.statement: Sanand EV facility ramped from <1,000 in Jan to 6,500 in Apr, targeting 10,000 then 15,000-16,000/month

items.statement: JLR Solihull capacity improvements drove Range Rover production to record 201k units
items.quote: Range Rover is up 27%, that's driven by progressive improvements in both our production system and those of our suppliers, allowing us to move up capacity levels in our Solihull plant.

items.statement: Consolidated auto debt Rs 16,000 Cr (Rs 7,300 Cr external, Rs 8,700 Cr finance leases); India business Rs 1,000 Cr net cash; target net cash overall
items.quote: automotive debt is now Rs. 16,000 Cr, of it Rs. 7,300 Cr is the external debt a nd Rs. 8,700 Cr is ﬁnancial leases. JLR and Singapore are the two places where we have the debt to be knocked out, and the plan is to ensure this year we take that out completely

items.statement: JLR repaid >GBP 1.8bn debt from operating cash flows in FY24; net debt GBP 732m from GBP 3bn
items.quote: And of course, the products continue to do exceedingly well. And with the kind of cash that got generated, more than GBP 1.8 billion of debt has been repaid out of operating cash ﬂows in JLR

items.statement: Board recommended dividend Rs 3 (ordinary) + Rs 3 special = Rs 6; DVR Rs 3.1 + Rs 3.1 = Rs 6.2; total payout ~Rs 2,300 Cr highest ever
items.quote: the Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 3 for the ordinary shareholders, Rs. 3.1 for the DVR shareholders, which is the normal dividend and there is also a special dividend in lieu of the successful TTL IPO of Rs. 3 per share for Ordinary and Rs. 3.1 for the DVR holders . items.statement: PLI: certificate for Tiago EV received, SOP finalization underway, disbursement expected H2 FY25; applying for 2 more products Q1, 1 more Q2
items.quote: PLI, so far we have got the cer tiﬁcate for Tiago EV. And right now the SOP for disbursement is being ﬁnalized. items.statement: Tata Motors Finance GNPA 5.6%, NNPA 3.2%; collection efficiency improving; early delinquency rates healthy; capital adequacy and liquidity adequate
items.quote: Collection eﬃciency continues to improve and that's why GNPA has now reduced to 5.6% and NNPA is 3.2%. So from that perspective, the portfolio is back under control

items.statement: JLR wholesales 110,000 in Q4; FY24 Range Rover 201k (+27%), Defender 115k (+32%); all regions up YoY
items.quote: In each quarter and you'll see at the top, each of our brands is improving, allowing us to get to 110,000 wholesales in the quarter. items.statement: PV FY24 wholesales 573,000 (highest ever), Vahan market share 14.3% in H2 (rank #2); EV volumes +48% to 73,800; cumulative EV production 1.5 lakh

items.statement: CV electric buses: 2,600+ deployed, 140M km, 95%+ uptime; 1,200 buses in hand for FY25; payment security addressed, asset-light model near resolution
items.quote: As I said earlier in the presentation, we have now more than 2,600 buses deployed, more than 140 million kilometers experience. As far as the tender orders in hand, we have around 1,200 more buses to be supplied this year.

items.statement: JLR sees some markets struggling (Europe, UK issues), but diversified across 5 regions provides resilience; China import business strong (+17% YoY, +27% vs FY22)
items.quote: we do see that some of the ma rkets are struggling a little bit, probably Europe, and we have some issues in the UK that we are very much on top of resolving. items.statement: Management will provide revenue and margin guidance for FY25 along with Q1 results

items.statement: Long-term target of INR 500 crore revenue requires new verticals beyond current nominal growth
items.quote: Yes. So, I've also told that from the things which we have been doing, they will not let us reach to INR 500 crores, they will give us nominal growth. We have to do something new to get to that number.

items.quote: The companies who are providing in building coverage like Indus or Crest or IBUS, they have forecasted a big growth and undertaken big targets for themselves in this year which are multi-fold of what they did last year.

items.quote: we have developed solution for that. So, this is what we have mentioned, smart meters. Smart repeater for smart meters. So yes, there is one big segment where we are seeing, expecting decent growth in this year.

items.quote: One more thing which we are now going to do pretty soon over the next few months is investing in SMT line which will get into our manufacturing as a service business. So, it's a PCB assembly line.

items.quote: So, building part is completed. So, the Phase II building is already constructed and it's done. So that part is completed.

items.quote: Now currently we are using manpower mostly in the single shift and in case there is a surge in requirements where we increase… Yogansh Jeswani We can increase the shift. Okay. Konark Trivedi Yeah. We go to two shifts. But in case it is required, we can run

items.statement: Jio, Tejas, ITI Limited, Indus and Crest Digital added as new customers in Q4 FY24
items.quote: we are happy to share that we have successfully welcomed Jio, Tejas, ITI Limited, Indus and Crest Digital as our valued customer.

items.statement: 70%+ of revenue comes from mobile operators
items.quote: primarily our 70% plus revenues do come from mobile operators. So, this is just to give you an idea.

items.quote: our competitors include companies like PROSE Technologies. Then there is HUBER & SUHNER, which is there. Then there is RV Telecom which is there.

items.quote: So the employee cost of R&D, I think that's about INR 1.7 crore or INR 1.8 crore which has been capitalized.

items.quote: there is some investment commitment that we have to meet to qualify for a PLI incentive. So usually, you know, that number gets done only till in that last quarter.

items.statement: PLI benefit of INR 2.7 crore booked in FY24 under income from operations
items.quote: We have about INR 2.7 crore.

items.statement: CEO Pankaj Gandhi departed; MD Konark Trivedi reassumed CEO role until new hire
items.quote: So yes, it's unfortunate that Pankaj has left us in a short time. So now I have taken over back as CEO position as well.

items.quote: Our industry share from that should be typically from the products that we made should be around 10%.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 18-20% for next 3-4 years reiterated, but near-term visibility shortened to 4-5 months due to high coffee prices
items.quote: we have been expecting more of an 18%, 20% going forward

items.statement: Domestic branded business targeting 30-40% revenue growth year-on-year
items.quote: we are looking to drive that aggressively in the range of anything around 30% to 40%

items.statement: Vietnam freeze-dried capacity on schedule for commercial operations by September-October 2024, completing expansion to ~77,000 MT

items.quote: our per kg EBITDA hasn't come down much there, maybe INR2, INR3 or INR5 here or there

items.quote: we work on a pass-on model, which is a cost-plus model that whatever the price is, we keep a certain amount of per kilo margin, and that's the price we quote

items.quote: there has been no reduction in the consumption for coffee. So that's a very heartening sight. People aren't drinking less of coffee because of higher prices

items.statement: Order visibility shortened to 4-5 months from 9-12 months previously due to client tentativeness at high coffee prices
items.quote: the visibilities have shortened to maybe 4 to 5 months

items.statement: Working capital debt likely to increase further due to volume growth and coffee prices; INR200 cr more term loans to be drawn for F&B and FD projects
items.quote: another INR200 crores on account of term loan is likely to increase somewhere

items.statement: Small pack volumes increasing in both domestic and export business, driving higher secondary packaging costs
items.quote: our proportion of small packs has increased. So that led to higher other costs where secondary packaging is included as the cost

items.statement: Order backlog grew 25% to Rs. 8,900+ crores

items.statement: Service revenues carry EBITDA margins north of 25%
items.quote: I think we deal at northwards of plus 25%. I mean, any service business revenues will go beyond 25% of the EBITDA margins level.

items.statement: Data center opportunity accelerating with larger sizes and players doubling investments
items.quote: It is accelerating. It's increasing in the size, the size of the data centers and also the players are doubling up the investment in this area. And this is something we will see continue having the same trend, yes

items.statement: Private capex in data centers, automation, metals & mining, PLI-led capex at starting point not peaking
items.quote: And private CAPEX, yes, we see a significant private investments in areas like data center, automation, industrial automation, metals and mining and PLI-led CAPEX. And this is something which has a starting point. I think many people say that they have peaked, but from our point of view, all these areas are just starting. They are just taking off. They are not peaking.

items.statement: Elections had no major impact on Q1 portfolio and growth
items.quote: You can see as such, we have not seen such a big impact in the 1st Quarter. And I really do believe that this time around, elections have had no real impact, but we are cautiously optimistic about it.

items.statement: Exports grew 23% but remain 10% of portfolio due to stronger domestic growth
items.quote: Our export expansion took place by 23% though exports remain by percentage 10% of our portfolio, but net-net there is a high growth. Why is the percentage of export looks 10%? Because the domestic growth is much, much stronger.

items.statement: Investing in incremental capacity expansion across Electrification, Motion, Process Automation
items.quote: We continue to invest in the incremental expansion of our capacities, both in the people resources as well as the physical resources are concerned. So, that's always an ongoing process.

items.statement: Added 450 people in Q1 CY2024 vs prior year
items.quote: And we added some 450 people during the quarter compared to last year to this year.

items.statement: Data centers, Railways, Metro, Electronics, Automotive EV driving product portfolio growth
items.quote: In material terms and the size terms, data centers definitely is one. Railways is another one and the Metro. These are the ones which are playing out plus the Electronic sector and the Automotive side, but on the EV side, there's an expansion for us.

items.statement: Tier-2/3/4 city penetration journey in early stages with long runway ahead
items.quote: If you ask me how much we have covered, we have a long way to go. So, we would do that in the course of the years to come and ensure that our customers get the best material, I would say the least possible time which is possible to be delivered to them.

items.statement: Market premiumization post-COVID shifting customers toward reliable, well-supported products benefiting ABB
items.quote: post -COVID, we talked about before, there is a huge shift of the customers who used to be very price sensitive earlier in terms of whatever products and the solution they bought towards the products which are more reliable and more availab le and also are better supported

items.statement: Buildings & Infrastructure segment contributes 8-10% of revenue mix
items.quote: I believe around the building and infrastructure, it's about 10% of our mix. T.K. Sridhar: 8% to 10% it will come.

items.statement: Service revenue share: Process Automation 40%, Motion 32%, Electrification 22%, Robotics 6%
items.quote: I would say in process automation or industrial automation, service contribution is 40%, electrification is 22%, robotics is 6% and motion is 32%.

items.statement: Standard Motion products facing price pressure as system stabilizes
items.quote: On standard products, there is a certain price pressure, what we see, and that's something which we have to navigate as the system stabilizes.

items.statement: Advocating government to raise minimum motor efficiency from IE2 to IE3/IE4
items.quote: So, as we learn more about motors, we should raise our bar to I3, I4 as the minimum efficiency level, which should prevail in the country in case we need to really cope up with what Europe of the world or US of the world are actually going to.

items.statement: Cash position robust at Rs. 5,036 crores
items.quote: We stand at robust cash position at Rs. 5,036 crores.

items.statement: Backlog margin sustainability uncertain as 40% is long-term projects priced at higher commodity costs; future book-and-bill orders will adjust to current lower prices
items.quote: So, these particular orders, whatever you have, so are something which has come from the periods where the material costs were high in which we had priced it to the customers. But whereas subsequently the material costs have softened. So, now the question is, the future prices what we give for the book and bill revenues which we give in the next 2 to 4 quarters for this particular year, shall have

items.statement: Cash earmarked for inorganic and organic expansion options
items.quote: And the balance would be required for we have earmarked some of the cash for inorganic and organic options, right? So, that's something which you already declared.

items.statement: Operating at 4,600 people in organization
items.quote: We are operating at 4,600 people in the organization.

items.statement: Zero debt on balance sheet; interest cost primarily from lease accounting and warranty discounting
items.quote: interest cost, primarily, I think this could be a bit of a question as to when we have zero debt on the balance sheet, so why do we have interest cost? I just want to tell you this, because that major el ement of this, almost 95% of it is basically one, what we need to do on account of accounting positions on lease equipments, what we buy, and the premises what we hold on lease, and also the warra

items.statement: Consumer products faced weak demand in kitchen appliances and general trade; rural and non-premium exposure higher than peers
items.quote: our consumer products business has faced the impact of weak demand, particularly in kitchen appliances , appliances have pulled us down as well as general trade we witnessed weakness in demand

items.statement: April saw top-line growth in both consumer and lighting businesses; Q1 looks much better than Q4
items.quote: April has turned out much better, we witnessed top line growth in April, both for our consumer business as well as lighting business. Fingers crossed, but clearly Q1 looks much better than Q4 has been

items.statement: CP margins dragged by industry-wide discounting and phasing out old products; logistics remains a drag
items.quote: One is the discounting that both competition in the industry and we had to resort to particularly in a weak demand situation. And this is partly accentuated in our case because as you know we have been churning out our product portfolio from phasing out old products into new products

items.statement: Discounting impact as high as 5-6% across categories; price hike effective 16th May to claw back some
items.quote: the discounting is as high as 5 % to 6% across different product categories that is happening. How much of that can be pulled back? When? That part I wouldn't want to hazard a guess. But some of that is what we're pulling back. The 16th may that we have spoken about is I think 6% is very high

items.statement: No price hike in Q4; price increase rolled out effective 16th May
items.quote: we have not had a price increase in Q4, but we have taken a price increase effective 16th May. So, that comes into play later this week

items.statement: Fans ~40% of CP revenue; non-premium fans grew faster, now ~70% of fan mix; Morphy Richards high single-digit growth
items.quote: Fans for us is in the 40% contribution range. So, we remain largely an appliance-driven company. In terms of volume growth premium, non-premium, both have been in the single-digits. That said, our non-premium has grown faster this quarter, so our share of non-premium, which is everything excluding premium is about 70%

items.statement: Consumer lighting 35%, professional lighting 65% of lighting revenue; CL volumes flat, revenue decline due to LED price erosion
items.quote: consumer lighting is about 35%, professional lighting is about 65%. We have not had a volume growth in CL. So, the decline that you are seeing in revenues pretty much approximates the price erosion. The volume is being relatively flat here

items.statement: LED price erosion in consumer lighting expected to bottom out in Q1 (May/June); volumes and normal growth to return
items.quote: my sense is sometime in Q1 as soon as May or June, you should see the price bottom out because a lot of the price erosion was coming because of DOB technology that is already now stabilized. So, I don't see any further price erosion because of that. So, prices should flatten out and going forward volumes and normal growth should come back into consumer lighting also both for us and for industry

items.statement: In-house manufacturing 20% in FY24, expected to rise to 22-23% in FY25; focus on quality and control over contract manufacturing
items.quote: In the last two years it has grown from 17% to 19% to 20%. I think this year should go up to 22 %, 23%. So, that's a kind of incremental that is continuing to happen

items.statement: Logistics cost drag ~2-2.5 percentage points; may bring external consultant to accelerate improvement
items.quote: I think there's at least 2-2.5 percentage sitting just in logistics. So, to me the three leve rs of performance that should drive improvement in the coming year ; one is consumer lighting , secondly, logistics, once we start getting that right

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to Rs.500 crores via NCDs for potential inorganic opportunities; nothing planned yet
items.quote: that's an enabling resolution that we have taken so that if some opportunities comes up for an inorganic sort of a deal, then we will have the money in place. So, nothing planned as of now, but that's just an enabling resolution

items.statement: Kitchen appliances likely to remain subdued for next couple of quarters; fans, coolers, water heaters to drive growth; festive season expected to revive kitchen appliances
items.quote: I would think fans, coolers, water heaters will be my growth drivers more than kitchen appliances would be, at least for the next couple of quarters. That said, this festive is what I'm banking on. Kitchen appliances has been subdued for a while, so by festive, hopefully, kitchen appliances should also come up and pick up pace

items.statement: Distributor count increased from 660 (Mar'23) to 749 (Mar'24)
items.quote: last year in March '23, it was 660, this year March '24, we exited at 749

items.statement: Employee cost run-rate between Q4 FY23 and Q4 FY24 levels; annual hike in July; other expenses fixed, providing operating leverage as sales grow
items.quote: I think from a future extrapolation, it will be somewhere between these two figures. We will remain optimal on employee cost. Our annual salary hike comes into play in July. That's when you'll see a normalized inflation impact on employee cost. But we're coming to focus with our digitalization, etc., remaining a lean company, lean team. On other expenses. I think both ways we are kind of fixed. So

items.statement: EPR cost Rs.9 crores in FY24, expected Rs.12 crores in FY25
items.quote: Cost for the current y ear was about Rs.9 crores and we expect it to be about Rs.12 crores next year

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs.6 per equity share (face value Rs.2) for FY24
items.quote: I am pleased to inform you that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend for the year of Rs.6 per equity share of face value Rs.2 which is about 300% of face value.

items.statement: Expect double-digit revenue growth in FY25 vs FY24 in domestic business
items.quote: We expect to achieve double -digit revenue growth in FY '25 compared to FY '24 in our domestic business.

items.statement: Standalone pending orders at Rs.1,826 crores as of March 2024
items.quote: As of March '24, the value of our standalone pending orders stands at Rs.1,826 crores.

items.statement: Expect international business to show respectable growth in FY25 vs FY24
items.quote: We expect international business to show respectable growth in Fiscal Year '25 compared to Fiscal Year '24.

items.statement: No one-time impact on margins; improvement from operational efficiency and product mix
items.quote: No, there is no one -time impact because when we have one -time impact like we did, I think in the third quarter of last year we had reported it and there is no exceptional item I think throughout the year there is no exceptional item.

items.statement: Expect to maintain or improve margins in FY25 if commodity prices stay stable
items.quote: My belief is if commodity prices stay stable and with the orders that are coming in, we believe that we will be able to maintain these kind of margins and hopefully improve on them as well.

items.statement: Debottlenecking and balancing machine capacities at Kirloskarvadi; may add shifts or machines per CAPEX plan
items.quote: look at each and every line in Kirloskarvadi and ensure that all the machines have a balanced capacity at the highest number . It might in some cases involve getting a machine, but in other cases it might be ensuring that some operations from one machine are moved to the other or things like that or showing that each machine is operational all the time

items.statement: Megastore and high-pressure molding line commissioned; operating two shifts, may run three shifts on some machines
items.quote: Similarly, last year as you are aware we also put up the high-pressure molding line for the sma ll pumps. So, over a period of time, we are slowly but surely increasing the capability of our factories to produce in greater numbers, but at the same time looking at how much we put in CAPEX year-on-year

items.statement: APOEM model converting made-to-order to made-to-stock; five APOEMs doing well, improving margins and lowering inventory
items.quote: what was a made -to-order product becomes a made -to-stock product. And so there's better balancing in the plant for this kind of industrial business. Cash comes upfront. So, these were the positives.

items.statement: Enquiry levels unchanged despite elections; no near-term demand fall seen
items.quote: How do I see the demand? Well, quite a large portion of our customers have already factored in what is going to happen. We don't see any fall or anything like that. Harshal: So, our enquiries are the same

items.statement: International order book stronger YoY; inquiries reasonably strong; oil & gas opportunities rising
items.quote: I think the order book position like you said is already visible. I think the order book is stronger this year same time compared to last year same time. We expect obviously the number of inquiries also seems reasonably strong.

items.statement: Products comply with US Build America Buy America Act and EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism
items.quote: has put in something called Build America, Buy America Act (BABA) which is a new thing that they've introduced . And if companies want to take advantage of the Inflation Reduction Act, which they've instituted, that give all kinds of benefits to companies, then they have to buy products that are complying to BABA. So, obviously our products are made in America and we have the Made in USA Stamp on

items.statement: Framework contracts at ~2x gross margins of product business; base contract with predictable revenue and efficiency upgrade upside
items.quote: So, on average, our framework contract tend to be about two times the gross margins of our product business for the international business and they don't start off low and go high.

items.statement: Acquisitions focused on route-to-market (e.g., SyncroFlo); not for products as portfolio already strong
items.quote: we do look at sometimes acquisition, but mainly look at route-to-market because we already have a lot of the products between SPP and KBL and so there's not any real need to buy a company for products.

items.statement: Other income boosted by forex gain from international entities and investment income
items.quote: So, in terms of other income, we have some income from our current investments and also there is a FOREX gain, i t was not there in the last year. So, we have a FOREX gain from our international entities and the investment income that these are the two

items.statement: Engine supplier delay of 1,360L 5,000HP engines ~1 year late affecting operations
items.quote: there's a unique issue of an engine supplier not supplying, but that's not to do with us, we need to do with a large engine supplier who's not supplied 1,360 liter 5,000 horsepower engines and many of them are close to a year late.

items.statement: APOEM model reduces WIP and inventory; cash-and-carry on industrial side
items.quote: The effect of this is that lot of the traded items like the motor, the base plate, the coupling, that are normally fitted on the pump and supplied by us and which are normally a bought-out for us and usually sit in inventory for us, would basically be done by the APOEM, so that would reduce the amount of WIP on our books, reduce the inventory in our books, and the APOEM would hold that and he woul

items.statement: Kolhapur steel foundry capacity ~200 tons/month; profitable with all stainless steel
items.quote: And there also I think it was about 200 tons per month is the capacity maximum. Chittaranjan Mate: But that is done with all stainless steel, it's profitable

items.statement: Digital initiatives (AR, VR, AI, IoT, 3D printing) sharpening tech edge and enhancing service revenue
items.quote: KBL has strategically invested in ground-breaking digital ventures such as AR, VR, AI, Internet of Things and 3D printing over the past decade. These investments not only sharpen our technological edge but also enhance revenue streams within our services.

items.statement: Soliqua launched in April 2024 entering the premix insulin segment worth INR1,000 crores where Sanofi previously had zero presence
items.quote: Now, since this month, we brought to market Soliqua, our best in class therapy for patients that today are treated with pre-mixed insulins in India. A segment of the market in which we didn't compete.

items.statement: Strategic partnerships signed with Emcure for cardiovascular portfolio and Cipla for CNS portfolio to expand reach of established brands
items.quote: You've seen in the last weeks the announcement of two strategic partnerships, Emcure and Cipla. Emcure for the cardiovascular portfolio and Cipla for the CNS portfolio.

items.statement: Domestic retained sales grew 3% YoY to INR566 crores; excluding NLEM impact growth was 8%
items.quote: So if we focus in th e first graph in the left side, so we see -- if we exclude the total domestic retaining sales, it's around INR548 crores. And in Q1 '24 we are moving to INR566 crores

items.statement: Profit before exceptional items and tax was INR215 crores at 31% margin, remaining among highest quarterly levels
items.quote: And for this year, we are at INR215 crores and remain one of the highest profit before tax and exceptional items for the rest of the quarter as well, Q2, Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Severance package of INR27 crores paid in Q1 FY25 due to team downsizing from Emcure and Cipla partnerships
items.quote: And finally, the strategic partnership with Emcure and Cipla in Q1, which is value-added for the shareholders and bringing an important volume increase for the business, is leading as well and downsizing of the team, and at the same time payment of severance package around INR27 crores.

items.statement: Lantus volume growth observed post NLEM price reduction with expectation of sustained acceleration
items.quote: We have done good progress on all fronts. Particularly, we now see with extended reach, also a growth in the volume of Lantus post the price reduction in NIM.

items.statement: Consumer Healthcare business contributes ~30% of sales and 37-39% of operating profit based on unaudited data
items.quote: So just to give an idea, in Q1 sales, the sales should be around 30% of the total sales of the company. And in terms of operating profit, we are giving a range and so the contribution from CHC is around 37% to 39%.

items.statement: New OTC regulations still in draft stage; modernization could unlock distribution and consumer engagement growth
items.quote: So the regulations are still in the draft stage and all OTC companies are partnering with the government to have the right regulations come into field.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward guidance or brand-level financial projections
items.quote: We also do not provide any future guidance. As mentioned in the registration, we will be taking questions from you in the sequence of your registration.

items.statement: TZIELD (first-in-class type 1 diabetes therapy) planned for India launch following Sanofi's global acquisition of Prevention Bio
items.quote: You may have read, you may have seen that the Sanofi Group has acquired a company called Prevention Bio, which has developed a product called TZIL. TZIL is a first-in-class product for diabetes type one. Now, we are also bringing that product to the Indian market as well.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 10-15% for FY25 driven by agri high single digits and non-agri near 20%
items.quote: Our expectation is that the growth will be anywhere between 10% and 15%. And that is -- that will be in line with what is expected for the industry over the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: EBIT per kg guidance maintained at INR10-12 for near term, targeting INR14+ in 2-3 years
items.quote: We have always said we used to be INR6 to INR8, and now we're co mfortable in the INR10, INR12 range and that the target is in the next 2 to 3 years, we should reach the INR14 plus mark

items.statement: Planned capex of INR150 crores for FY25 for incremental capacity and maintenance
items.quote: So the planned capex for FY '25 is INR150 crores. And we are also exploring opportunities for expansion. So that will happen as and when it certifies.

items.statement: New capacity additions expected only by FY27, evaluating locations for organic expansion
items.quote: Correct. That is accurate. And it will take -- but we do have headroom in our existing, and we can add additional capacity in our existing locations as well.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 pipe EBIT per kg improved to INR11.9 from INR5.09 in FY23 due to scale and mix
items.quote: If you actually look a t it from an EBIT per kg perspective, we did see a significant improvement, INR11.9 per kg versus INR5.09 per kg in FY '23

items.statement: Non-agri mix target of 50% in 3-4 years from 31% in FY24
items.quote: Our aim is to move this to almost 50-50 in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Agri demand expected high single digits, Building & Construction high teens in Q1 FY25 with stable PVC prices
items.quote: Yes, you're right with stable PVC prices, our expectation is that the agri demand will be in the high single digits. And you also look at it from the Building & Construction segment, you are seeing a robust growth in that segment as well, and we expect that to be in the high teens.

items.statement: PVC-EDC spread improved to $480 currently from $427 in Q4, EDC at $320, PVC at $800
items.quote: Today, as we speak, there is a slight improvement in PVC. PVC has been trending around $800. EDC, on the other hand, has reduced. It has gone to $320. And VCM has more or less remained stable at $660. In terms of delta, the most recent delta that I can tell you, PVC-EDC is $480 and PVC-VCM is $140.

items.statement: PVC price outlook uncertain due to Middle East volatility and anti-dumping duty talks
items.quote: We have to wait and watch. It's not just anti-dumping duty. It's also going to be dependent upon the Middle East situation, which has been quite volatile. So we are constantly watching -- very closely watching this situation. And let us see how this situation emerges.

items.statement: Net cash surplus of INR1,820 crores as of March 31, 2024; land sale gain of INR416.99 crores in April 2024 not in FY24 profits
items.quote: The company continues to have a strong balance sheet with a net cash surplus of roughly INR1,820 crores as on 31st of March '24. It is to be noted that the subsequent to 31st March 2024, that is in April 2024, the company has transfe rred leasehold rights of 25.27 acres of land in Chinchwad, Pune and recorded a net gain of INR416.99 crores on such transfer. This figure is not included in FY '24 pr

items.statement: Modular capacity additions during FY25 can enable 110,000-120,000 tons per quarter
items.quote: So this year, we will be adding some modular capacity in couple of our plants, especially in the mother plant. So that -- see, we can easily make 110,000 and 120,000 tons in a quarter, okay?

items.statement: FY24 agri volumes higher single digits, non-agri higher teens; Q3 agri drop recovered in Q4 and Q1
items.quote: So yes, it will be -- agri will be in the higher single digits. And very similarly, in non-agri, it will be in the higher teens, yes. Both will be in those range itself. We did see a drop in agri volumes especially in Q3 and which has picked up quite robustly in Q4 and continues to be in Q1.

items.statement: No material inventory gain/loss in Q4 FY24; Q3 FY24 had loss due to INR11 price drop post-September
items.quote: No, there has not been any material gain or loss this quarter at least. In September, in the third quarter, there was some inventory loss because if you remember, prices went down by INR11 right after the end of September.

items.statement: PVC resin external sales halved to ~14,000-15,000 tons in FY24 from ~27,000 tons in FY23; Q4 external ~6,000 tons
items.quote: So this year, we have sold roughly 14,000, 15,000 tons of PVC externally, balance all we have consumed in-house. So last year, if you remember, we had sold roughly 27,000 tons outside. This year, it is half. We just sold about 14,000 tons outside, balance 180,000-odd tons we have used ourselves.

items.statement: No PVC capacity expansion planned; all incremental capacity in Pipes & Fittings
items.quote: No, not in PVC segment. Most of the incremental capacity expansion will be coming in the Pipes and Fittings segment and also maintenance budget.

items.statement: Fittings plant at near-full utilization (900-1,000 tons/month); fittings revenue contribution expected to grow with non-agri
items.quote: the plant is close to near-end capacity utilization. Capacity was set up for almost 1,000 -- 900 to 1,000 metric tons per month. And we are hitting close to that. And with the improvement in Non-agri segment, we expect that the fittings' contribution to the overall revenue would grow.

items.statement: Management targets INR 300 crore+ per quarter revenue in FY25 and aims for double-digit EBITDA margin.
items.quote: But more or less, our strive is that to get into the INR 300 crores and INR 300 crores plus for the quarter in the coming year.

items.statement: Management expects to achieve INR 2,000 crore turnover without significant capex.
items.quote: And we expect that with increased market access, achieving a turnover up to INR 2,000 crores, as I have said in many of my investment calls is possible without significant capex or modernization.

items.statement: Simone Frederico & Figli brand expected to generate minimum INR 25 crore turnover in FY25, doubling annually.
items.quote: Simone itself, we expect about INR25 crores minimum turnover to happen in FY '25. And then we hope that this will continue to double every year.

items.statement: Gradual industry recovery expected in FY25 driven by domestic demand revival, export recovery, and lower raw material prices.
items.quote: A gradual recovery at an industry level is expected in the next financial year '25, and on the back of improvements in sales realizations and stabilized raw material costs.

items.statement: USA market showing strong interest and new customers joining; expects to recover close to prior year levels.
items.quote: U.S.A. is showing a lot of interest now. We lost 56% compared to last year in the U.S.A. market. And we expect now to recover and get pretty close to where we were last year in the U.S.A. market again.

items.statement: EBITDA margin lower in FY24 due to subdued demand and inventory correction after COVID over-ordering; aims for double-digit margin in FY25.
items.quote: The reason is that everybody in the financial year '24 had the subdued demand and the latent demand after COVID and had ordered more than they thought.

items.statement: Endeavors to reach double-digit EBITDA margin in FY25, subject to market dynamics.
items.quote: Aditya, yes, endeavors are there to really get into the double digit for surely. Also, it has external effect and the constraints from the market also.

items.statement: Order cycles: Fabric ~60 days, Garment ~90 days, Yarn ~30 days; uniform orders have longer projections.
items.quote: Otherwise, generally, the order cycling for fabric is around 60 days. 60 days before they need it, they tell you that this is a fabric order. For Garment, it's is usually 90 days and for Yarn, it's usually 30 days.

items.statement: No significant capex needed to reach INR 2,000 crore turnover; considering third automotive textile unit in Madhya Pradesh.
items.quote: We have one in Banswara, and we are considering a third in Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: Raw material costs stabilized; cotton prices falling but pricing under pressure; linen and wool prices rising.
items.quote: With the cotton prices falling, I think that will continue to remain good. The only problem is the pricing is now under pressure in the cotton and the natural fibers.

items.statement: Focus on high-value yarn products, synthetic/wool blends, technical synthetics, flame retardant curtains, tent fabric, automotive textiles, sportswear.
items.quote: We will continue to focus on high-value yarn products that will lead to enhancing value growth along with the overall top line.

items.statement: Bangladesh and Vietnam compete only in garments; FTAs needed to compete; Banswara's strength in yarn/fabric and sustainability compliance gives edge.
items.quote: So when you speak of Bangladesh and Vietnam, they're only doing garments, right? our bigger business is yarn and fabric. The garment part, you are correct that because unless we get FTAs, there's no way to compete.

items.statement: Hopeful for UK FTA to significantly enhance garment business outlook.
items.quote: On the regulatory front, we are hopeful that the U.K. free trade agreement happens, and that would significantly enhance the company's business outlook on Garment.

items.statement: Exports declined to 42% of revenue in FY24 from 48% in FY23; sequential recovery of 31% in Q4 FY24 driven by UAE and European uniform orders.
items.quote: The exports have declined to42% of the overall revenues in FY '24 as compared with the 48% in last year for the same period, mainly due to decline in export of more than 50% in key markets of Europe, Turkey, U.S. and the U.K.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 185 to ~175 days; debtor days cyclical; working capital borrowings lowered.
items.quote: Working capital cycle on the inventory side, if you look at, there is a reduction of a number of days coming from the previous year to this year. So now the inventory cycle goes like, okay, it's 175 days kind of average, which we were at 185.

items.statement: Working capital borrowings reduced due to improved working capital cycle.
items.quote: And that's the reason like our borrowings have also, on the working capital side, was lowered.

items.statement: Tesca JV (automotive textiles) turned profitable, paid tax first time; sales INR 80-100 crore range, 20% drop in FY24 but strong profitability.
items.quote: Tesca actually has the sales in the ranging from INR80 crores to INR100 crores. Like in FY '23, they did touch near to INR100 crores, like INR99.8 crores, so they were near to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Synthetic fiber consumption growing faster than cotton globally; technical synthetics (moisture management, performance fabrics) driving future demand.
items.quote: Synthetics is growing now faster than cotton. And the wool part is more ceremonial and for weddings and is more aimed at the upper end of the market.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, inflation impacting discretionary spending, inventory overhang, and lack of FTAs for garment exports remain key risks.
items.quote: The global economic climate remains challenging with geopolitical uncertainties dampening consumer confidence and impacting global trade.

items.statement: Enhanced travel budgets, larger marketing team, digital marketing tools adopted to explore new geographies.
items.quote: Travel budgets have been enhanced. We have a larger team available, and we are using all sorts of tools of digital marketing in terms of digitizing the product.

items.statement: Middleweight segment expected to grow in double digits; premiumisation theme continuing in India; motorcycle industry slowly returning to pre-COVID levels month-on-month
items.quote: What we can say is the two-wheeler market is poised for a growth, and especially the middleweight. We anticipate the middleweight growth will be in double-digit.

items.statement: Himalayan 450 currently clocking 200-plus motorcycles a day; preparing for higher numbers given global potential; supply ramp-up ongoing for domestic and international markets
items.quote: As far as the Himalayan is concerned, we launched and it has been a super hit for us and happy to share with you, it's beyond the expectation of the numbers, which we are talking about.

items.statement: New products lined up on 450cc Sherpa Platform and 650cc platform; platforms grouped to address different consumer segments with differentiated experiences
items.quote: We have currently three platforms. We have our super refined J-platform. Then we have our 450cc platform, which is the Sherpa Platform and the 650cc platform.

items.statement: Focus on absolute EBITDA increase rather than percentages; international market share recovery and non-motorcycle business growth accretive; monitoring commodity prices but no significant pressure currently
items.quote: First of all, revenue growth itself is something that we are actually focused on. We're looking at absolute increase as far as EBITDA is concerned. We're not necessarily so focused on percentages, as you know.

items.statement: No recent price hike for Royal Enfield; VECV focusing on discount reduction rather than MRP increases to improve transaction prices
items.quote: Royal Enfield side, we haven't taken the price hike very recently. VECV, Vinod? Vinod Aggarwal: In VECV, we are focusing more and more on the discount reduction

items.statement: Commodity prices stable currently; not a headwind or tailwind; tracking PGMs and working on value engineering to offset costs; pricing decisions based on price-value proposition for consumer
items.quote: Commodities, it is not a headwind as of now. Is it a tailwind? May not be. So to that extent, there is some amount of stability, which is there.

items.statement: Export retail sales strong across all markets globally; wholesale picking up slowly; long-term strategy focused on brand building, community, own subsidiaries and CKD plants in key markets
items.quote: international market, Jinesh? Jinesh Gandhi: Yes. B. Govindarajan: No. In the last quarter also I was just telling, we don't track the wholesale. Wholesale is only a transaction number for us. We always look at retail

items.statement: Export strategy divided into richer Western markets (strong profitability, salience) and high-potential LatAm/Southeast Asia markets aiming to create 'mini Indias' with deep penetration over 5-15 years
items.quote: We divided in our export markets into two. One is the richer countries, such as U.S., Europe, Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Korea, where the markets are there, they're not growing, maybe even declining, but affordability is very strong.

items.statement: CV industry has good growth potential driven by 7%+ GDP growth, strong infrastructure programme, and pent-up replacement demand for new technology trucks enhancing productivity
items.quote: As far as the demand for commercial vehicle market is concerned, I think it has got a very good potential for growth. Fundamentally, because our economy is continuing to do well, and of course, we are expecting on the back of around 6% to 8% of last year, we are expecting that this year also the economy should grow by 7% plus.

items.statement: E-bus products ready (9m, 12m, 13.5m intercity); electric truck traction good with 75 sold last year; small commercial EV on pilot with 10 customers, commercial launch from January next year followed by diesel/CNG variants
items.quote: As far as the trucks are concerned, we were the first one to introduce electric truck in 5.5 tonne category. And last year, we have sold 75 electric trucks. And this year, of course, the traction is good.

items.statement: VECV Q4 margin decline YoY due to one-off fiscal incentives accrued last year in Madhya Pradesh; no other reasons for margin decline QoQ despite volume growth
items.quote: Basically, last year in Q4, there were some fiscal incentives, which we had accrued based on the very old, which were pending in Madhya Pradesh. So due to that, there was one-off in last year Q4.

items.statement: Royal Enfield finance penetration at 61% and steadily growing; digital finance marketplace integrated; REOWN upgrade programme piloted in few cities, slowly gaining traction with dealership ecosystem
items.quote: Our finance penetration, as of now is about 61%. It's steadily growing over the period of time. I mean because when the demography is coming down, it also is quite natural that the finance penetration will be there.

items.statement: Replacement cycle for Royal Enfield yet to kick in but preparing with REOWN platform for 6 million vehicle park; focus on frictionless upgrade experience rather than pushing new motorcycles
items.quote: You touched upon the topic of the replacement cycle. In the last call, also I mentioned, it is yet to kick in. But we have to be prepared. So what we have done is to give a very frictionless experience for those consumers almost about 6 million motorcycles, which are there in the market as a vehicle park.

items.statement: Royal Enfield sold 912,000 motorcycles in FY24 (highest ever), up from 834,700 in FY23; 30% market share in 125cc+ category; 7.2% overall motorcycle market share
items.quote: For the financial year, as Siddhartha mentioned, we sold about 912,000 motorcycles, which is compared to last year, which was only about 8,34,700 motorcycles. This is our highest ever volumes in the country, India.

items.statement: VECV sold 85,560 units in FY24 (7.5% growth vs industry 4%); heavy-duty truck market share 9.2% (up from 4% industry growth); light/medium-duty market share 34.7% (market dropped 5.9%)
items.quote: For the full-year, we had 85,560 units as against last full-year of 79,623 units. So with a growth of 7.5% for the full-year. If you look at the industry, industry had grown by 4%.

items.statement: Oragadam plant awarded future-ready factory by Frost & Sullivan; plants creating benchmarks in efficiency, automation and manufacturing excellence; produced 9.2 lakh motorcycles (highest ever)
items.quote: On manufacturing, just to add, we have produced 9.2 lakh motorcycle this year, which is, once again, highest ever production with high quality fit and finish motorcycles for the globe.

items.statement: All VECV vehicles comply with BS-VI OBD2 standards; working on H2ICE technology, hydrogen fuel cells, CNG and LNG trucks; aiming to reduce water usage per vehicle by 5%
items.quote: And all our existing digital vehicles, they comply with all the strict current BS-VI, OBD2 standards. And then, of course, we are committed to increase the use of renewable energy and energy efficiency at our plants and operations.

items.statement: Achieved zero liquid discharge in all operations; all plants and warehouses net water positive (Oragadam index 3.23, Vallam 2.02); 35% renewable energy consumption; on track for 20% carbon emission reduction vs last year; motorcycle reusabi
items.quote: We have achieved zero liquid discharge in all our operations and all our plants and our warehouses are all net water positive, with an index of almost 3.23 in Oragadam and 2.02 in Vallam. We have been constantly working on improving the renewable energy usage. And during this year, further, we enhanced that, and we have 35% of total consumption onto the renewable energy.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated normalized EBITDA margin improved to 28%

items.statement: FY24 radiology EBITDA margin declined to 9% due to operational costs and revenue mix

items.statement: FY24 core business sample volume growth of 8% YoY, 10% QoQ

items.statement: FY24 franchise business revenue growth of 14% YoY, 13% in Q4

items.statement: FY24 pathology revenue (excluding materials) grew 10% YoY, 16% in Q4

items.statement: FY24 radiology revenue grew 18% YoY

items.statement: Targets 50-100 bps margin improvement in FY25; 20% EBITDA margin achievable in 3 years with 15% volume CAGR
items.quote: And on margin side yes, once we come back with higher volume certainly our margins will further improve by 50 basis points to 100 basis points.

items.statement: Plans 1.5-2% price hike in FY25 after minimal hike in FY24
items.quote: In this year, again we will be surely to take the price hikes in the range of 1.5% to 2%.

items.quote: We have achieved a total income of Rs. 320 crores, EBITDA is Rs. 47 crores which is EBITDA percentage margins is around 15%.

items.statement: Pricing linked to diesel; passes increases to ~85% of customers; retains benefit when diesel falls (only 2-5% customers get reduction)
items.quote: Basically if you see we have the only price hike clause we don't have any clause which is supposed to be reduced. So, wherever price is increasing or decreasing is a positive arbitrage for us.

items.statement: Customer mix maintained at 50:50 large vs SME; 97% revenue from B2B, 3% from B2C

items.quote: So, basically it is hovering around 17.5 to 18% continuously last year. For the full year also it is like 17.5 to 18%.

items.statement: Market share ~7% by volume; not losing share - industry-wide volume decline; premium margins from pan-India network and high utilization
items.quote: These are the industry numbers where we have a market share by volume transported by us is around 7% which is almost 7% market share.

items.statement: Re-certified as Great Place to Work; 3,000 workforce, 970 branches

items.quote: You know, really we will not be going into that sector, we're very clear about that and we will not be going that sector at all. We will keep stick to our express industry only.

items.quote: On the billing and revenue outlook for quarter 1, matchmaking and wedding service revenue will be at a similar level of quarter 4.

items.quote: EBITDA margin for the matchmaking business in Q4 is at 19.1 %, as compared to 18.9 % in quarter 3 and 21.1 % a year ago.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14.2% in Q4 FY24 vs 14.3% in Q3 FY24 and 15% a year ago
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our EBITDA margins in Q4 are at 14.2%, as compared to 14.3% in quarter 3 and 15% a year ago.

items.statement: Full year FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin 15.2% vs 16.2% in FY23
items.quote: For the full year, EBITDA is at INR73.5 crores, which is 15.2 % margins, as compared to INR75 crores, which is 16.2% margins in FY '23, a decline of 2%.

items.statement: Excluding marketing, matchmaking margins stable at 60% in FY24 vs 61% in FY23
items.quote: Excluding marketing expenses, our margins in matchmaking are stable at 60 % in FY '24, as compared to 61% in FY '23.

items.statement: Marketing expenses elevated due to competitor intensity; no reduction expected currently

At this point in time, we see that the marketing is going to get similar levels. We don 't see any reduction in marketing because the marketing spend or competitor intensity is still at a higher level.

items.statement: Google Play Store removal caused one-week disruption; apps restored after government intervention

So, we are providing additional services, and additional offerings to our customers. Yes, those are the changes.

items.statement: Provision made for disputed Google service fee based on developer agreement; PAT margin would be 300 bps higher without it
items.quote: If not for the disputed Google service fee, which we have provided, our PAT margins would have been better by about 300 basis points.

items.statement: Added 2.7 lakh paid subscriptions in Q4 FY24 (2.1% QoQ, 2.9% YoY); 10.74 lakh for full year (8% YoY)
items.quote: We added 2.7 lakhs paid subscriptions during the quarter, a growth of 2.1 percentage, quarter-over-quarter, and 2.9 percent year-on-year. We added 10 , 74,000 paid subscriptions during the year, which was a growth of 8 percent.

items.statement: Launched Jodi for non-degree holders in Tier 2/3 cities; free for females, vernacular support

Now we have Jodi which is a very simple product free for females and targeting diploma, plus 2 and below non -degree holders.

items.statement: Hyderabad plant commissioned May 6 with capacity to more than double current fan sales
items.quote: The fact of the matter is that the capacity that we've built at Hyderabad plant can more than double our sales as we stand.

items.quote: In this quarter, I'm happy to report that we've also done façade lighting at -- in Dwarka, the Sudarshan Setu that our honorable Prime Minister had inaugurated just a few weeks ago.

items.statement: Direct-to-market states grew 46% in Q4 and 65% for full year; now 30% of sales

items.statement: McKinsey engagement ending; variable pay component to be paid in Q1 FY25, then cost savings
items.quote: The last component of the variable pay will get paid out in the month of -- sorry, in this very quarter, in the very first quarter itself. So by -- so that will be accounted for in Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: CEO search nearing completion; announcement to follow decision
items.quote: I think we're getting close to the end of the search. And soon, once the decision has been made, obviously, we'll need to make a public announcement, we will make it.

items.quote: we know that 20 %-22% has always been our sustainable EBITDA margin, which we have always achieved, except that FY23

items.quote: the raw material prices are quite stable and demands are also almost more or less similar like last quarter, as at least in April-May I am seeing that

items.quote: EBITDA margin has increased because the raw material prices didn't go up . Normally, the raw material prices go up, but the prices don't go up, and the raw material prices are much better than we expected

items.quote: Right now, there are challenges, especially one is the global slowdown. Now the world is coming back to normal, except Europe. Everything else is getting slowly , it i s getting normal. That is number one. That is the one challenge. Second is this Red Sea crisis and all that

items.quote: Globally, as I told you earlier with our customers, they are ranging from 3 months to 6 months to 1 year and for raw materials also for some products, some raw materials, it is 3 months, 6 months and for some raw materials it is 1 year

items.quote: Our margins, which are at 18%, the thing will, we are, it's not that we are not, wanting an expansion in margins, but we are, I would say that our number one priority is to drive growth.

items.quote: Nature's Basket delivered healthy 12% growth, basis of reinvigoration of certain categories like fresh, but more importantly, the launch of three new stores and a dramatic expansion in margins, which were about 120 ba sis point improved

items.quote: But if you look at it netting off the impact of the closed stores and dispensers' part of the business, it is a 3% LFL like-for-like growth on a year-on-year basis, along with a slight expansion in gross margins.

items.quote: Today our non-food mix is 20% roughly. If you look at some of our stores I think in the past, I'll be honest, in a quest to increase that, we have probably given a far higher allocation to non-food.

items.quote: Our overall e-commerce orders in Calcutta have gone up by 30%, and of course you do see the surges, last couple of weeks we had an extreme, heat wave in Calcutta, and we saw that the number of orders, do spike up.

items.statement: Equity infusion up to INR300 crore approved for growth capex, capability building, and near-term debt repayment; modality/timing TBD
items.quote: The fundraise will not be just utilized for a specific purpose. It will be for managing all three.

items.statement: Seven to eight new stores in pipeline for FY25 in Eastern UP and East clusters; expansion judicious and concentric
items.quote: We have seven, eight in the pipeline already for the year which are in Eastern UP as well as in the East.

items.statement: Building capabilities in precision marketing/CRM, supply chain forecasting/inventory management, and e-commerce technology
items.quote: Three areas which I would like to kind of call out are the ones where we need to beef up our capabilities is one is in this whole area of precision marketing what I spoke about in customers.

items.quote: we've had just in the last si x months, I would say, we brought in a new chief me rchandising officer, we had a new head of operations, we had a marketing head

items.statement: Capex plan of around INR15 billion for next 2 years for announced projects, largely funded through internal accruals.

items.quote: On capex, we'll be spending around INR1,500 crores for next 2 years. Out of that, around INR700 crores for commercial tower INR650 crores, INR700 crores at the new commercial tower, which we are adding in Powai.

items.statement: Hospitality EBITDA margin of 47.8% in Q4 FY24, up 30 bps YoY; same-store margin at 48.4% with 80 bps expansion for the quarter and 300 bps for the year.
items.quote: The quarter also delivered one of the highest EBITDA margin of 47.8%, with an expansion of 30 bps despite the new inventory, which is getting stabilized and some inventory is under renovation.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA surpassed INR6 billion mark with 42% margin for full year FY24.
items.quote: I'm pleased to announce that on a consolidated level, the company's EBITDA surpassed the INR6 billion mark with an EBITDA margin of 42%.

items.statement: ADR grew 5% YoY to INR11,862 in Q4 FY24; same-store ADR growth was 8% YoY; full year ADR growth was 17% at INR10,718.
items.quote: Q4 record ed new highs in average room rates at INR 11,862, which is up 5% over the previous year. It is up by 8% on a same-store basis

items.statement: Industry has upside of double-digit rate growth going forward; Chalet delivered 17% rate growth in FY24 and will continue to work at industry rate growths.
items.quote: We believe the industry has an upside of double-digit rate growth going forward. And to reiterate, we have delivered 17% rate growth this year.

items.statement: Robust demand pickup in Q3 FY24 continued into Q4, led by corporate travel, MICE, weddings and social events; occupancies improved 2% YoY to 76%.
items.quote: For Chalet, the robust pickup of demand seen in Q3 FY '24 continued into the next quarter in Q4, largely led by corporate travel, MICE, weddings and social events.

items.statement: Supply and demand expected to outstrip supply for at least next 2-4 years; ADR growth will moderate after some time on higher base.
items.quote: I think we've got at least for the visible future, which is the next 2 to 3, 4 years, supply and demand is expected to outstrip supply. Beyond that, it's very difficult to predict now.

items.statement: Pipeline: 125-room addition at Marriott Whitefield by end FY25 (520 total); Dukes Lonavala upgrade to ~145 keys by end CY24; Taj Delhi Airport ~390 keys opening FY26; Hyatt Regency Airoli ~280 keys opening FY27; CIGNUS 2 commercial tower co

The Dukes Retreat in Lonavala is undergoing a major upgradation and repositioning. The res ort will have a final inventory of approximately 145 keys, and we look forward to welcoming guests to that hotel by end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Election impact limited to election days in respective cities; no significant government business in portfolio; travel may slow on election days in base and destination cities.
items.quote: So if I am in Delhi and I got my election happening in Delhi that day, I'd like to vote, I'd probably not travel out of Delhi. Similarly, if I have to travel to Mumbai and Mumbai elections are happening on that particular day, I may not want to travel to Mu mbai because we know the city will largely be slow on that day

items.statement: Utilities cost at all-time low of 4.1% of revenue through green power sourcing and energy-efficient equipment upgrades.

items.statement: Revenue target of ₹200 Bn by FY26 under Project LEAP; new mid-term goal plan to be unveiled during current financial year

items.statement: Capex of ₹8.6 Bn in FY24; ₹10-11 Bn each year for next 2-3 years to expand capacities

items.statement: EPC open order book of ~₹48-50 Bn to be executed over next 3-4 years, largely from RDSS scheme

items.quote: Rs. 30 crores is the CAPEX for Pharma Intermediate which will start in Q3, an additional Rs. 150 crores CAPEX is based on the pilot runs which we are running as soon as we are successful the additional Rs. 150 crores CAPEX will be made and announcement will also be made for the same.

items.statement: Next leg of capex being firmed up based on trial run outcomes for new performance products; will announce capital commitment in due course
items.quote: we are progressively positive on our trial runs for our new products u nder performance segment and we are in process of f irming up next leg of CAPEX as we analyze more outcomes of these trial runs. items.statement: No long-term contracts; business runs on monthly/quarterly basis for UV stabilizers targeting Indian market first

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin steady at 43% despite 16% revenue decline; Q4 margin 44%

items.statement: Subsidiary HALS margins targeted at ~15% in FY25 due to unabsorbed overheads; medium-term target ~25% at full utilization
items.quote: on blended basis for this year we a re not targeting more than 15% for the subsidiary, for the new products in the subsidiary which is namely HALS

items.statement: Pharma Intermediate margins expected to be better than HALS 25% medium-term target
items.quote: I think that would be better, much better.

items.statement: HALS 770 sold at 2.5-3% discount to imported pricing in India with just-in-time supply advantage; global discount ~5% max
items.quote: Typically, this product discount of 2.5% to 3% because we give that advantage of not letting them stock the material. We can do just-in-time supplies which our competitors cannot.

items.statement: HALS 701 discount <5% globally as first non-Chinese producer; blended HALS realization now $7-8/kg vs earlier $9 guidance
items.quote: 7 to 8 now on blended basis , so 770 cheap, 944 is expensive, 119 is expensive , so on blended basis it is $8 you can assume.

items.statement: Volume recovery across all segments in H2 FY24; Q4 volumes surpassed pre-destocking levels; FY25 volume growth from new plants and Pharma Intermediate from Q3
items.quote: Quarter 4, we have seen a lot of volume growth coming back. Now next volume growth for FY25 will all be from the newer plants and the new Pharma Intermediate which will start in quarter 3.

items.statement: New products contribution rose to 23% in FY24 from 18.5%; HALS 770/701 showing sequential 40% volume growth; 770 at ~50% India market share targeting 70-80%
items.quote: Further new product contribution increased to 23% from 18.5%.

items.statement: Export market ramp-up slower due to approval processes and distributor appointments; US market may take longer; targeting 200 tpm by March 2025

items.statement: Tax rate: Clean Science standalone 25%, subsidiary 15% for FY25 calculations

items.statement: Plan to double Blinkit store count in next 12 months, mostly in top 7-8 cities
items.quote: Broadly what we are saying is that the store count will double from here over the next 12 months and most of those stores will come in the top 7-8 cities.

items.statement: Food delivery GOV growth guided at 20%+
items.quote: We expect that as the business GOV continues to grow 20%+ (which we have guided on), that will likely be a combination of some AOV increase and order volume increase and majority of the order volume increase would come from transacting customers growing.

items.statement: Blinkit to remain at least EBITDA neutral during aggressive expansion
items.quote: Our attempt is to keep reinvesting back into the business to grow as fast as possible while maintaining neutrality on the EBITDA side - that's our strategy.

items.statement: Store expansion guidance includes element of hope, not all 500 stores tied up

items.statement: Each top metro can eventually support 500 stores, runway beyond 12 months

items.statement: Hyperpure EBITDA margin improved from -9% to -2% YoY, improvement to continue but focus on growth
