items.statement: Pakhajan capex increased to INR470 cr from INR350 cr; added 5,000 MT capacity and full automation
items.quote: From 350 that, see, the original project was conceived at INR350 crores with a 15,000 capacity. Anupam Agarwal: Yes. Parag Jhaveri: And we did it, made it to those, revised it to 17,000. So, that's the cost estimation. And again, from 17,000 it is going to 20,000. So, from 350 to 470, INR120 crores. But from there, we added an additional capacity of 5,000 metric tons

items.statement: Sharp customer commitments for new plant; revalidation underway; some approvals 1-2 months, others longer
items.quote: Well, for a new project, we already have some sharp commitments from many of our customers. It's a question of new location. Even though you are supplying from one plant, when you go to another plant, they need to revalidate their order. So, that work has to continue now. We already started the work.

items.statement: Pakhajan EBITDA margin better than Vapi due to volume, automation, coal fuel, lower manpower
items.quote: What we are just saying that the product which has moved to Pakhajan has a better EBITDA margin compared that is mainly due to the sheer capacity, volume and then automation what we have deployed. So, that is going to reduce a lot of our cost there.

items.statement: Selling prices under pressure; raw material prices also down; expect both to stay flat for next 6 months
items.quote: So despite having a higher turnover this the selling price is both under pressure, so the revenue growth has declined you have seen that we have grown on an early basis by 13% volume but still we have the degrowth of 11% in the top line so that clearly shows that the selling prices are under pressure and so does the raw material prices. And we expect that to continue at least for next six months w

items.statement: Peak debt INR550 cr in FY25; no further borrowing; repayment starts Apr 2025; target EBITDA/debt <3x
items.quote: I think this is a peak debt in FY25. We don't intend to borrow any further money. Our repayment is only starting from April 25 only not before that and we intend to bring down this EBITDA to debt ratio of 5.2 today to below 3 somewhere in that range in FY25.

items.statement: Working capital days 95-98; target max 105 days; no extra WC needed for Pakhajan scale-up
items.quote: Maybe right now we are running at an overall working capital number of days is about 95 to 98. Can we maximum stay to 105. Not beyond that. That's why we don't project any additional working capital requirement.

items.statement: Freight costs fell sharply FY24; power/fuel savings from process changes; gas cost down but not guaranteed
items.quote: Freight cost has reduced drastically. Number two, there was a saving on cost of power and fuel, where we did some changes in our process. So, we saved some power, but also cost of the gas has come down in the last six months. So, that also helped us to reduce the cost.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 guided at around INR200 crores, similar level for FY26, significantly below depreciation of ~INR380 crores
items.quote: we continue to keep capex in the range of about close to INR200 crores this year, most probably maybe around this level next year also or maybe slightly up, depending upon the requirement. But directionally, if you really see against our depreciation will up close to INR380 crores thereabouts. The capex spend going forward for the next two years also is going to be significantly lower only.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR983 crores (INR9,826 million) in FY24; net debt-to-equity improved to 0.63 from 1.27; net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.29 from 2.14
items.quote: The net debt came down below INR1,000 crores now at INR983 crores, which actually improved the net-debt-to-equity ratio to 0.63 from 1.27 that it was last year. Net debt to EBITDA also improved to 1.29 now compared to more than 2 that we had last year.

items.statement: Aim to reduce net debt to half of EBITDA by next year through free cash flow generation
items.quote: Directionally, that should come down because we hope to generate a good amount of free cash flow this year and next year also, which should obviously go to repay the debt only. So our idea is to bring it significantly down to half of EBITDA, maybe by next year.

items.statement: Lifetime new business wins of INR87 billion in FY24; 40%+ from EV category; expected to generate INR8.5 billion additional revenue in FY25
items.quote: In FY'24, our lifetime new business wins has been over INR87 billion. The annual peak value is around INR15 billion. These wins are likely to generate additional revenue of INR8.5 billion in FY'25.

items.statement: Order book revenue buildup: INR850 crores in FY25, INR1,450-1,750 crores over next two years from INR87 billion order intake
items.quote: from this existing INR87 billion of order intake, which we took, nearly 8,500 million of revenue comes in FY'25 itself, about INR850 crores of revenue for this year, which will add up to INR1,450 crores INR1,750 crores in the next two years.

items.statement: Full year EBITDA margin 10.1% in FY24 vs 8.7% in FY23; Q4 EBITDA 11.1% vs 9.4% YoY; ~1% sustainable improvement from contribution margin gains
items.quote: EBITDA also with regard to double-digit EBITDA, 10.1% for full year compared to 8.7% we had last year. Q4 PBT was 5.3% versus 2.4% we had same time last year. The EBITDA also was much stronger at 11.1% compared to 9.4% last year.

items.statement: Targeting ~1% per annum contribution margin improvement for next couple of years through cost reduction initiatives
items.quote: our effort is always to improve contribution margin steadily over a period of time, close to about 1% per annum is what we are targeting.

items.statement: India auto production grew strongly in FY24: 2W 10.3%, 3W 16%, PV 6.9%, CV 3%; Q4 FY24: 2W 26.5%, 3W 8.4%, PV 9.7%, CV -0.5%
items.quote: The automobile production in India during FY'24 grew on a year-on-year basis for all the segments. Passenger vehicles grew by 6.9%. The commercial vehicles gr ew by 3% . Three- wheeler and two-wheeler registered a strong growth at 16% and 10.3%, respectively

items.statement: Expect good monsoon and rural economy strength to boost 2W industry; inflation easing and interest rate cuts later in year to help
items.quote: going forward, we are hoping that the good monsoon and the strength in rural economy will further give that kind of a boost to the 2-wheeler industry and which in turn reflects in strong business growth. And then maybe later part of the year, we'll also see inflation easing out further at global level and also the interest rates coming down in the later part of the year.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 37.8% electrical/electronics/lighting, 32% polymer (~70% combined); 2W/3W ~75% of revenue; 87% domestic, 13% overseas
items.quote: The important point to be noted here is, of course, the large 2 segments, 37.8% coming from electrical and electronics lighting, plus the 32% comes from polymer. So these 2 add up to close to almost 70% of the total revenue. And in terms of geographical distribution, 87% comes from within India, 13% coming from outside. Segment-wise, product segment-wise, 2- and 3-wheelers added to close to 75%.

items.statement: Renewable energy projects nearing completion; benefits expected soon
items.quote: the renewable energy projects, which we talked about in the previous quarter communications, they are now nearing completion. So most probably, very soon, we'll be seeing the benefits of these projects also.

items.statement: Average receivables discounting ~INR600 crores, stable
items.quote: See, on the average, you can say close to about INR600 crores of receivable discounting we have. It varies from week to week or month to month. But on the average, you can say it's about INR600 crores.

items.statement: Board approved merger of 100% subsidiary VPL with VEL for operational ease
items.quote: our Board also approved the major of the 100% subsidiary, VPL with VEL. This is expected to give us significant ease of operations.

items.statement: Provision of INR16 crores for doubtful receivables from a prominent EV customer; conservative approach after waiting over a year
items.quote: we also went ahead and create a provision for close to INR16 crores for provision for doubtful debts against one of the prominent EV customers we have to be on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: China JV arbitration verdict expected by end of H1 FY25; Q4 impacted by Chinese New Year holidays
items.quote: the arbitration proceedings on the final verdict is likely to come out maybe by end of H1. So that's when around that time, we'll have something to communicate on this.

items.statement: Employee costs to grow in line with top line; Q1 may see merit increase impact
items.quote: There may be some increase because Q1 anyway tests this merit increase impact and all. But otherwise, this should grow more or less in line with the top line.

items.statement: Backward integration initiatives like SMT lines in place for margin improvement; cost reduction efforts ongoing in overseas markets
items.quote: The margin improvement efforts through backward integration initiatives like SMT lines are already in place. With these actions, we expect to see a revival of overseas business in the coming 1 to 2 years. We will also continue to strengthen our engineering capabilities and also focus on further cost reduction and working capital optimization for all our operations.

items.statement: EV engagement remains strong despite market slowdown and subsidy reduction; OEM optimization creates opportunities
items.quote: I don't think there is a drop in engagement or a drop in interest from an EV product line perspective, of course, maybe market is a little bit slower, and I think we know subsidy is also reducing. But OEMs look to continue to optimize also, right, which definitely creates opportunity -- which definitely creates opportunities for us.

items.statement: Return on capital employed annualized improved to ~29% in FY24
items.quote: the retur n on capital employed annualized, it also goes up to close to 29% now

items.statement: India operations outperformed industry with >14.5% growth in FY24; company clocked ~10% overall growth
items.quote: For the full financial year '24, our India operations continued to outperform the industry growth with a growth of over 14.5%. The India operation helped the company to clock closer to a 10% growth in FY'24.

items.statement: Target 700 restaurants by FY27
items.quote: Our guidance for FY '24 for restaurants was 450. We've beaten that guidance. We have 455 as of March 31, and our outlook for FY '27 continues to remain the same. We are targeting to open 700 restaurants.

items.statement: Gross margin target 69% over next 3 years from 67% base
items.quote: For gross profit, we had given a guidance of 67%. We've achieved that for the full year. For FY '24, our gross profit is 67%. And over the next 3 years, we want to take this up by 2 percentage points to 69% approximately.

items.statement: India FY24 EBITDA 9.7%, doubled from prior year
items.quote: If you look at it from the perspective of EBITDA, our EBITDA for the full year was closer to 10%, 9.7%, to be pre cise for the year

items.statement: India FY24 gross margin 67%, Q4 67.7% with small one-off
items.quote: For the full year, now we reported 67% gross margins. Quarter 4 was marginally higher at 67.7%. It had a one-off, but we should be able to improve for the coming years.

items.statement: Indonesia gross margin dropped due to value strategy and delivery focus
items.quote: Our focus, again, like in India, is going to be value strategy, drive more traffic, focus on delivery, and that is also one of the reasons why we've seen a drop in gross margins as far as Indonesia is concerned.

items.statement: India positive SSSG 2.9% FY24 driven by traffic growth every quarter
items.quote: In this environment, I think our work in India at least continued to deliver positive same-store sales, every single quarter. Every single quarter, we delivered positive sales, and we ended up being 2.9% positive.

items.statement: India traffic positive all year and into current year, no dent seen since April
items.quote: We continue to -- on top of building new restaurants in existing markets, in many cases, we have continued to drive positive traffic into our restaurant. More people coming to our restaurant. More people coming through our delivery system, right? That we haven't seen a dent since we started into April, May and going into June next month.

items.statement: Indonesia Q1 up 10%, Q2 up 13%, Q3 hit by geopolitical crisis, Q4 bounced back 11% ADS growth
items.quote: We started the year on a great note. The first 2 quarters, we delivered double-digit growth. In quarter 1, we were 10% higher. Quarter 2, we were 13% higher. But the third quarter actually has been quite challenging for us. Even in the month of October, as Sumit and Raj was mentioning, we were 17% higher in sales compared to same period last year, which is unfortunately, when the entire industry w

items.statement: India net restaurant growth 64 in FY24 (75 opened, 11 closed)
items.quote: We've built 75 restaurants last year with 11 closures. That's about 64 NRG, net resta urant growth

items.statement: Indonesia closed 26 non-performing BK restaurants, ADS improved from 18.5M to 19.3M IDR
items.quote: During the year, as Raj was also mentioning, we took some calls and closed some of the underperforming stores and as a result of which, our ADS also improved further by another 0.8 million. So the average has gone up from 18.5 million to 19.3 million.

items.statement: India growth funded by internal accruals and balance sheet cash, open to short-term debt if needed
items.quote: As far as India is concerned, we will continue to grow using the cash that we have on balance sheet plus internal accruals. As we've said in the past as well, that if there is a need to raise some short-term debt to fund any part of the growth, then we would be open to do that.

items.statement: Indonesia pausing new store openings for both BK and Popeyes in current financial year to focus on stabilization
items.quote: At the moment, as we've been saying that we are focused as far as Indonesia is concerned is goi ng to be really stabilizing the entire portfolio of -- both the portfolio as far as business is concerned. So the capital allocation on both the brands is going to be literally close to nothing. We are not going to put any capital allocation on expansion at least in the current financial year as far as

items.statement: India digital experience rolled out to ~100 stores, table service at ~250 stores
items.quote: As of today, we have almost 100 stores that offer 100% digital experience. So you can order on the kiosk or on the app or on the table, and your food will get served on the table. And we're expanding this as we speak, the table service is available at across almost 250 stores, which are all our dine-in locations now offer table service to our customers.

items.statement: India took price hikes on delivery offerings in line with industry while maintaining value
items.quote: Number two, we have recently taken some price hikes on our delivery offerings. These are keeping in line with where the industry is. And we are making sure that there are still value for money for our consumers.

items.statement: India launched India-specific nuggets, wraps, puffs, premium menu focus, Whopper recipe change, BK Cafe at 351 stores
items.quote: We launched the chicken snacking favorite nuggets. Now it's a crunchy nugget. It's got a twist on a typical nugget that we've seen in QSR. We also relaunched the BK chicken burger with 50% more chicken. So it's not just about new products, we go back and improve our existing products also based on customer feedback, right? And that's now available at 50% more chicken at the same price, so even bet

items.statement: India delivery traffic highest in industry, optimizing mix and entry pricing for profitability
items.quote: First of all, it drives the highest number of traffic numbers in delivery in India, right? We already shared that with you every single meeting that we get on the call. we are optimizing that, right? We are trying to make sure that, that is traffic that we are driving with profitable kind of margin numbers. So that optimization through product mix through entry-level pricing and through offers tha

items.statement: India non-current and other financial liabilities up ~INR100 cr due to late-year store openings, current in nature
items.quote: these are largely on account of the stores that we opened during -- towards the later part of the year. So those would kind of get pa id as they do, due to curren t in nature there. But that's something which is more like -- as you know, we are negative for the capital business. So we will always have business and expansion -related negative working capital cycles that we will continue to have

items.statement: India company EBITDA loss reduced from INR95 cr to INR55 cr, targeting breakeven in current financial year
items.quote: Last year, we were -- we had a loss of almost around INR95 crores. We brought that down by INR40 crores to INR54 crores or INR55 crores. Our endeavor is to make sure that if this improvement of journey that we are taking, we do believe that we should be able to achieve what we plan to achieve this year, in the coming financial year or the ongoing financial year.

items.statement: Prashant Desai stepping down as Head of Strategy and IR, Gaurav Ajjan appointed as replacement
items.quote: I have been moving on from Burger King or RBA, and in my absence, Gaurav Ajjan has now joined as the new Head of Strategy and Investor Relations.

items.statement: Indonesia geopolitical headwinds caused anti-US brand sentiment, dine-in dropped >30%, recovery expected over couple of quarters
items.quote: But what does that do is, it gave us a lot of headwinds in both Q3 and Q4. And instead of kind of gaining momentum, which we had reached ADS level in October as per plan to go over 20 million IDRs per restaurant, 20 million IDR per restaurant per day. But that got reverse d in the Q3 and Q4. It's not coming back, and we feel good about it moving forward. It might take another couple of quarters to

items.statement: India ADS fell from INR126k in Sep to INR105k in Mar due to seasonality, expected to improve in Q1
items.quote: There is seasonality. Quarter 4 Jan, Feb, March typically does have low seasonality. And we do see improvements coming through in April, May, June as seasonality kicks in, school holidays, malls -- mall events, all of that

items.statement: Indonesia ADS reached 19.5M IDR in Oct before geopolitical hit, Q4 bounced back to 11% YoY growth
items.quote: But right up to October, we got to an A DS of 19.5 million. And then with further investments that we had planned on chicken and all, we felt positive that we would have got to what we had been talking about to cash breakeven towards quarter 3, quarter 4 in Indonesia, but external factors really kind of pulled us back. We are back on track as far as Indonesia is concerned and we've started at leas

items.statement: FY25 store expansion target of 275-300 stores across core brands in India
items.quote: Overall, we are looking at a similar number, which is 275 to 300 stores.

items.statement: Opened 256 new stores in FY24 including 47 in Q4; total store count 1,782 as of March 31 including 283 KFC Thailand stores
items.quote: We opened 256 new stores, including 47 in the fourth quarter. As of March 31, our total store count has reached 1,782, including the 283 KFC stores we acquired in Thailand on January 18, 2024.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 70.3% for FY24 (+30 bps YoY); Q4 gross margin lower due to Thailand consolidation and Nigeria currency impact
items.quote: The gross margin for the consolidated business including Thailand was 70.3% for the full year versus 70% for the previous year an improvement of 30 basis points on a full year basis.

items.statement: KFC India Q4 gross margin 69.9% (+50 bps QoQ); brand contribution 19%
items.quote: Gross margins for KFC during the quarter was 69.9% thereby reflecting an improvement of 50 basis points over the previous quarter. Brand contribution remained healthy at 19% for the current quarter.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Q4 gross margin 77.3% (+150 bps QoQ); brand contribution 4.4% (lower QoQ due to ADS deleverage)
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter came in at 77.3% versus 75.8% in the previous quarter. Brand contribution was INR 7 Crore for the quarter with margins at 4.4% which was slightly lower on a quarter-on-quarter basis mainly due to the ADS deleverage impact.

items.statement: Costa Coffee Q4 gross margin 76.7%; brand contribution 17.9% (+300 bps QoQ)
items.quote: The gross margin was 76.7% in quarter 4. Brand contribution in quarter 4 stood at 17.9% an improvement of 3% versus the previous quarter.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment weak throughout FY24 due to weak disposable income, tight liquidity, geopolitical issues; expect improvement post elections and West Asia stability
items.quote: Consumer sentiment continues to be weak throughout the year , w eak disposable income, tight liquidity position, local consumption, geopolitical situation were the major drivers for the weak consumer demand

items.statement: Seeing some green shoots on ground; Q1 seasonally better than Q4
items.quote: we are seeing some green shoots and we hope that they are kind of lived long.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement sustainable due to supply chain negotiations, menu optimization, and promotion refinement; not from dramatic cost reductions
items.quote: It is a sustainable trend, Devanshu. Since the hyperinflation we experienced, things have stabilized, they have not come down dramatically. However, with our negotiations, we are seeing good results. We've also done menu optimization.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Fun Flavour value pizza damaged premium positioning; KFC value layers (rolls/wraps) successful as side dishes; Pizza Hut recovery initiatives underway
items.quote: During the period of hyperinflation, we tried to experiment with Fun Flavour pizza, which lowered the overall pricing structure. In hindsight we can call ourselves wiser, but this move impacted the brand positioning.

items.statement: Food courts strategy targets travel, tourism, shopping channels; partnership with PVR INOX for mall food courts; existing food courts at highways, railways, airports
items.quote: DIL has entered into a strategic partnership with PVR INOX to develop and operate the business of food courts at shopping malls across the country to co-promote movies and food.

items.statement: Costa Coffee-PVR JV performing well with ~80 outlets; expanding collaboration
items.quote: We have already opened close to 80 Costa Coffees in the PVR, and it will be expanded and adding great value to our business.

items.statement: Entire QSR market facing negative SSSG including burger segment leader; competitive intensity exists but partly inflated by cloud kitchen multiplicities
items.quote: We've seen the market leader in the burger segment reporting a negative SSSG , as well as our peer competitor s were in similar situation . We are in similar situation and the entire market is facing these challenges

items.statement: Nigerian Naira depreciated ~200% vs USD in FY24; INR 236 crore forex loss on USD liabilities (INR 90 crore exceptional, INR 147 crore OCI); full impairment of INR 116 crore investment in Nigeria
items.quote: During the financial year Nigerian Naira has got depreciated by almost 200% versus the USD. As a result of this, the Nigeria business has recorded an impact of INR 236 crore forex loss on account of USD denominated liabilities.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR 910 crore (INR 470 crore international, INR 365 crore India); gearing below 1x; debt/EBITDA 1.28x
items.quote: The total debt in the books at a consolidated level is INR 910 crore as of March 31, 2024. Out of this, INR 835 crore in the bank debt consisting of INR 470 crore at international and INR 365 crore in India.

items.statement: Senior management exits (Rajat moving South for family); no disruption expected as strategy unchanged and Virag Joshi continues leadership
items.quote: Rajat has been with the Company for almost 13-14 years, and he wanted to move to South to be closer to his family. He gave his best to the Company in any case. So we don't expect any disruption or significant changes because the strategy remains the same.

items.statement: Nigeria business fully impaired; Thailand geopolitical impact on few southern stores; Pizza Hut brand recovery uncertain
items.quote: In view of the above, DIL has also taken a full impairment of its investment of INR 116 crore in Nigerian business through its subsidiary, RV Enterprises Pte. Ltd.

items.statement: Thailand KFC purchase price allocation provisional under IND AS for up to 12 months from acquisition date
items.quote: As per the IND AS, DIL has a measurement period of up to 12 months from the date of acquisition and hence to that extent, this is subject to final adjustments.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth >60% YoY and operational EBITDA margin improvement >100 bps
items.value: >60% revenue growth; >100 bps EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: For the year 2025, we expect to clock a similar rate of growth in revenue greater than 60% and an improvement in operational EBITDA margin of more than 100 basis points.

items.statement: FY25 guidance excludes OSAT/PCB revenue; those will start in 1-2 years and reach full form in 3-5 years
items.quote: This year guidance OF 60% up is just on EMS and not based on activities in the OSAT and PCB. OSAT and PCB will take one to two years’ time to start the initial capac ity utilization and you can see them in full form maybe in a span of about three to five

items.statement: Medium-term aspiration of $1 billion revenue by FY28 (75% EMS, 25% other) remains on track
items.quote: We are very confident that we will be achieving this number in year 2028 because the tailwinds are very good and then entire globe is looking at India.

items.statement: Order book rose to Rs 41,152 million at end of Q4 FY24 from Rs 37,890 million at end of Q3 FY24; average monthly inflow increased to Rs 3,212 million in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The order book surged from Rs.37,890 million at the end of Q3 FY'2024 to 41,152 million at the en d of Q4 FY'24. The average order inflow per month increased from 2,788 million per month in Q3 FY'24 to 3,212 million during Q4 FY'2023

items.statement: Smart meter orders (concluded April-May) not yet in Q4 order book; will add next quarter; CDAC server order already included
items.quote: So these smart meter orders are actually not part of your 4,152 crores. Smart meter orders have been concluded, especially the large orders been concluded in April and May. So in the next quarter we will add these orders and show you.

items.statement: Strong demand across all verticals, notably Industrial & EV, Aerospace/Outer Space/Strategic Electronics, Railways
items.quote: Our growth was led by strong demand across all the verticals, more notably. Industrial and EV Aerospace, Outer Space and Strategic Electronics and Railways vertical.

items.statement: 100 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY25 driven by operating leverage, not gross margin expansion; further operating leverage possible
items.quote: So the numbers are clear. Obviously, the gross margins have come a tad down. So we have done operating leverage. And like I said, we still have fair amount of ope rating leverage possibility because we still have middle line which can be leveraged better

items.statement: FY25 capex funded from internal accruals; expect ~Rs 200-250 crore from operating cash flow (EBITDA >50-60% growth + 100 bps margin) at 7-8x asset turnover
items.quote: So it will give about 200 to 250 crores of money which can be invested into CAPEX and that will be sufficient taking a seven or eight times asset turnover eventually.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of Rs 1,400 crore earmarked only for OSAT and HDI PCB projects; no deleveraging
items.quote: We raise the funds for specific two p rojects, one is OSAT and the other is high density interconnection PCB and they will be used for only that

items.statement: Chamarajanagar facility becoming truly integrated; Pune facility now operational; preliminary construction started in Telangana; new regions in India and overseas planned
items.quote: continue to make serious progress in our expansion and con tinuously adding newer lines across various facilities, especially Chamarajanagar which is in line to become truly integrated facility. Our Pune facility which was acquired recently also now is opera tional. Also, we have plan to expand the new regions in India and outside India as well

items.statement: Bare board (PCB) manufacturing approval received; supplier orders being finalised, recruitment and construction starting; expect shipments in FY25
items.quote: We have got approval for that already. We are in the advanc ed stages of finalizing the orders with all the suppliers, recruitments are going on, and construction is also just starting. Indrajit Agarwal: So we can see some shipments this year

items.statement: OSAT/PCB government approvals expected soon after model code of conduct ends; 2-3 month delay absorbed in plan; preparatory work underway
items.quote: We are in the final stages of obtaining government approvals for ou r new investments and expected the approval soon after the model code of conduct is concluded. We feel even there is a delay of 2-3 months, we will be well within the expected plan a nd we will catch up with the timelines for these projects implementation through preparatory steps, wh ich are already underway

items.statement: EMS exports currently ~10% of revenue; expected to rise modestly in aerospace/defence/railways; OSAT/PCB will be export-driven and significantly increase export share in 4 years
items.quote: However, when we come to something like semiconductor assembly that is OSAT or PC board, HDI PC board, they are all export-driven and so another four years’ time you will see significant increase in the exports th rough the new businesses

items.statement: Portfolio rebalancing toward 50:50 high-volume (auto/industrial/EV) vs high-margin (aerospace/defence/medical/railways) by FY25
items.quote: this year, we have seen the orders of the financial year FY'25 and we find that the portfolio balance is coming back to our original expectation, which is like 60:40 and may be eventually it will be 5 0:50, so 50 of high volume and 50 of high profit making the products will be there in our portfolio

items.statement: OSAT/PCB subsidies pending government approval; model code of conduct delay of 2-3 months; approvals expected soon after elections
items.quote: We are in the final stages of obtaining government approvals for ou r new investments and expected the approval soon after the model code of conduct is concluded

items.statement: OSAT partner Globetronics facing issues (Apple contract cancelled); Kaynes says agreements intact, backup partners lined up, no impact on timeline
items.quote: The issue is once we get the government approval, we have severa l partnerships lined up and there are several backup also available. One of these can be consumm ated till we get the government's approval for the subsidy scheme, correct. So there is nothing cancelled, etc., We are in touch with

items.statement: Medical segment revenue expected to reach triple digits (Rs 100+ crore) in FY25 after long qualification cycles
items.quote: So this year you will see at least medical segment will go to triple digits, at least 100 crores plus will be there in the medical sector in FY'525 for sure.

items.statement: Management targets fee-based income to grow to 75% of EBITDA from current 55% over coming years
items.quote: I see that to continue or even grow slightly every year to become a 75% fee based earning business.

items.statement: AUM grew from Rs 1,665 cr to Rs 2,500 cr in FY24 driven by global arbitrage fund, AIFs and SATCO PMS acquisition
items.quote: The highlight of the results is the assets under management, which have increased from Rs. 1,665 crores in March'23 to approximately Rs. 2,500 crores in March'24 primarily due to our remarkable performance in our global arbitrage fund housed in Mauritius, our alternative investment funds and the acquisition of a renowned PMS called SATCO Growth & Momentum portfolio during this year.

items.statement: Global arbitrage fund AUM grew ~80% from $455M to ~$800M in FY24; similar trajectory expected in FY25 absent geopolitical issues
items.quote: So from a trajectory point of view, we have grown from 455 to approximately 800 this year. That in terms of percentages, I think we've grown almost 80%, and the way the inflows are coming in this year, I think the same trajectory should continue as long as there are no new geopolitical issues happening

items.statement: Received SEBI approval to operate as Investment Manager for AIFs in India, transforming Abans Holdings into an operational entity
items.quote: We have received approval from SEBI to operate as an Investment Manager for our alternative investment funds in India. This approval enables us to transform from a holding entity at Abans Holdings Limited level into an Operational Entity.

items.statement: Applied for US commodity pool operator license to access US investors for global arbitrage fund; approvals awaited

items.statement: Applied for mutual fund license to launch own commodity ETF; approval timeline uncertain
items.quote: As soon as the approvals are in place, we will initiate that business. items.statement: Focus shifting to fee-based income (subscription, performance, advisory fees) targeting 75% of EBITDA vs 55% currently
items.quote: Finally, the focus is always going to be on fee based income, either through inorganic growth, through strategic alliances, keep focusing on fee based income and keep building the lending book.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin ~11% in FY24, up 3.5% YoY; agency business EBIT grew from Rs 21 cr to Rs 59 cr YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins are at approximately 11% with the growth 3.5% increase year-on -year.

items.statement: Employee cost rose from Rs 14 cr to Rs 40 cr due to global hiring and ESOPs/performance incentives; future increases only inflation-linked

items.statement: Strategic tie-up with SMC Global Taurus Wealth for distribution; Abans manufactures products, partners provide sales reach

items.statement: Remittance business in UK subsidiary (FCA regulated) generated Rs 5 cr income in FY24; plans to replicate license in other countries
items.quote: if you've seen that about 5 crores of income this year has come from that entity and that is new income that we found in the group, and I think that can continue if we keep looking at different industries across the globe and try to understand the regulatory requirements of different regions, so that we can replicate this license in different countries.

items.statement: Lending focus remains on agri-commodities; gold lending not planned for current year pending RBI approvals
items.quote: Not as of now. Our understanding of Agri-commodities lending has grown over the years. items.statement: Global arbitrage fund growth dependent on no new geopolitical issues; US fund registration approvals uncertain
items.quote: I think the same trajectory should continue as long as there are no new geopolitical issues happening

items.statement: Wireless capex to moderate meaningfully in FY2025; transport, enterprise, data center, and homes capex to continue
items.quote: wireless capex which accounts by the way for a large part of the capex so to that extent we do see moderation going ahead into next year.

items.statement: B2B capex lumpy due to fiber purchase, data center build, and submarine cable milestones; otherwise steady state
items.quote: our B2B business had a bit of one -off this quarter which is primarily related to fiberi zation so we bought some fibers and some spends o n the data center business

items.statement: Rolled out ~43,100 network sites and ~55,982 km of fiber in FY2024; 5G available across the country

items.statement: Plan to rollout over 25,000 sites in next couple of quarters, lower than last year, focused on rural coverage gaps

items.quote: 70% to 80% of the shipments that are happening on smart phones are now 5G enabled so to that extent as people upgrade their devices they will naturally move to 5G.

items.statement: Pithampur plant capacities backed by awarded customer business; expects plant to get booked up soon
items.quote: All the capacities that have been put up is backed by forward-looking customer businesses that have been awarded already to us. So we expect that plant to get booked up very soon.

items.statement: Customer delivery delays (domestic and export) are recurring but secured by LCs; election outcome not expected to impact FY25 target
items.quote: I would say it is the part of the business, because those orders even though they delayed, but those were sure shot orders and we are not worried about whether we will get the payment on time because, all those orders were against LC.

items.statement: Chairman Prakash Lade highlights design capability as core differentiator; MD Rohan Lade leads growth strategy
items.quote: We are basically a design based manufacturing company it is very, very important. We are basically a design manufacturing company; we know ins and outs of this drying and the filtration system very well.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of 400 crores with EPC 250, Samruddhi 130, lease 20 crores
items.quote: As of now our projection is 250 from EPC , 130 from the project the Samruddhi project and 20 from our lease revenue because we construct and lease it out.

items.statement: FY26 revenue possibility of 1,000 crores based on existing projects
items.quote: Anticipating even better growth ahead Kore Digital Limited envisions an estimated 1,000 crores from similar ventures in 2026.

items.statement: Pipeline of projects totaling 400 crores for FY25 and 1,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: Kore Digital is poised for significant expansion and development in coming years with an impressive pipeline of projects totaling 400 crores for '24-25

items.statement: Navayuga Engineering work order worth 21 crores to be completed by June 2024
items.quote: Kore Digital has been awarded substantial work orders and extension value d 21 crores by N avayuga Engineering Limited. We anticipate completing this work by June '24.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 16.25%, Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 20.16%
items.quote: Financial Year '24 EBITDA surged to 17.07 crores showcasing notable year-on-year growth of 259.84% alongside a commendable EBITDA margin of 16.25%.

items.statement: Monsoon impacts Q2 revenue; Q1 moderate, Q2 low, Q3 and Q4 major revenue quarters
items.quote: Q1 is moderate, whatever you see last year that will be in similar line, higher. Q2 is always low. Because of monsoon Q2 is always low.

items.statement: Lease revenue rates fixed by MSRDC at Rs 14 per meter per month with yearly escalation
items.quote: Right now, I think, I am not 100% sure. Right now , it is Rs. 14 per meter per month. I can confirm and get you this thing back.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative due to trade receivables and advances; expected to turn positive next quarter
items.quote: The operating cash flow is negative 6.83 Cr and for investing we have just purchase of 7.52 and our financing activity cash flow is positive 156 and cash is available 40 crore s and operating cash flow is negative to high investing purchase stock and also trade receivable which sir explained

items.statement: Company is largely debt-free after using preferential issue proceeds to repay borrowings
items.quote: It is debt free. 20-30-40 lakhs for this big company is nothing.

items.statement: Preferential issue of 41 crores; 36 crores remaining after debt repayment for project funding
items.quote: I will tell you, 36. I am a very loaded company anyway. The bank debts also I am also very low. I don't like to pay interest.

items.statement: Preferential funds used for capital asset building in concession projects generating 25-year rental revenue
items.quote: Basically, these projects are concessions granted by government to us. And once we do the construction, the asset belongs to us for 25 years. So, that will go in financial terms capital or asset building which will bring me revenue for 25 years, rent.

items.statement: Technical qualification allows bidding up to 3x turnover (300 crores); no size limitation with partners like RailTel
items.quote: Normally we can go to tenders 3x of turnover. So, it is 105, I can go up to 300 crores. Even if when we are not qualifying, we have the partners like RailTel. So, there is no size limitation.

items.statement: Existing relationships with Vodafone, BSNL, Reliance, Tata Teleservices; deployment expected on Mumbai-Nagpur Expressway
items.quote: All, we have already explored and were earlier we were told that the funds are not there. Now funds are there. So, deployment will be there on Mumbai-Nagpur, so our margin will increase.

items.statement: Election code of conduct delayed project start; board approvals pending until officers return from election duty
items.quote: Unfortunately, the moment we got the award after 3 or 4 days this election code of conduct started. So, the board official who is having the signing authority has been deputed to election duty, expected to come back and join on 21st.

items.statement: Revenue recognition milestone-based every 100 km for Samruddhi concession project
items.quote: See, this is milestone based. So, it is not that we have to complete entire 700 km into 2. Once we complete 100 , we get our revenue starting. Every 100 km we are handing over to the telecom company and we are getting paid.

items.statement: Revenue fluctuates quarterly due to certification delays and monsoon; management avoids projections without clear visibility
items.quote: I never give a projection which I cannot complete. Unless I have a very clear vision, I will not give the guidance.

items.statement: Management commits to quarterly earnings calls going forward
items.quote: I would love to do that but then this work and then load and this project, it's massive and at times it is very difficult for me to prepare and then sit here for hours and answer. But I will try. It's my promise. I will give it a sincere try to do it every quarter.

items.statement: Management declined to provide revenue estimates for FY25 and FY26 due to potential tenant move-out and re-leasing variables.
items.quote: We don't normally comment on potential growth or what we estimate might be for next year. That's especially relevant in this year. As you know, there are some potential long standing discussions on one of our old, very valued licensees moving out and other new people potentially moving in, in their place.

items.statement: FY24 capex was Rs. 55 crores, down from Rs. 85 crores in FY23 due to Phase-5 completion; sustainable maintenance capex fluctuates yearly.
items.quote: The previous year's Rs. 85 crores included significant amounts of CAPEX for Phase-5. The numbers have obviously reduced significantly in the year under review just now.

items.statement: NKP is 100% occupied; Deutsche Bank agreed to take additional space for 200-250 seats.
items.quote: Deutsche has agreed to take up additional space at NKP, accommodating approximately 200 to 250 seats.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin was 79.47%; full year FY24 EBITDA margin was 79.26%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 79.26%.

items.statement: Management sees potentially good demand and is having good discussions for potential vacancy from a long-standing licensee.
items.quote: we see p otentially good demand and we're having good discussions for this potential vacancy, but since we don't have any vacancy not ices yet, there are no specific t ransactions that one can actually i nclude our contracts

items.statement: Restructuring discussions ongoing with no decision on delisting or REIT; no timeline provided; small REIT regulations under review but prima facie for unlisted companies.
items.quote: There is no decision at all on which option we are going to take. We've never put forward any information that says that we've agreed on delisting or on something other than a delisting.

items.statement: Company will stay in old tax regime due to MAT credit (~Rs. 25 crores remaining, to run down in ~2 years); moving to new regime offers nominal benefit vs restructuring benefits under old regime.
items.quote: The company has decided to stay with the old tax regime for the present. This is primarily due to the accumulated MAT credit available for set-offs in the old tax regime.

items.statement: Debt has 3 years remaining of interest-only moratorium (linked to T-bills), then 25% repayment over years 6-10, then 75% bullet at year 10.
items.quote: We have a 5-year moratorium on our debt where we pay interest only. Out of that, two years is over so far, so we have three more years of interest only. Then we have a situation where we pay 25% of the debt between years 6 and 10.

items.statement: Nirlon House restructuring complex due to 9-10 owners; no advanced stage discussions; Nirlon's share mostly licensed out; will update when significant progress.
items.quote: We have not really said at any point in time that any discussions are at an advanced stage. So what I said earlier on the call, is because of the profile of the asset, which is owned by multiple owners, these discussions and what we would like to do is definitely going to take some time.

items.statement: Nirlon Management Services contract renewed on similar terms; no development fees as no significant development envisaged.
items.quote: the new terms are very s imilar to the existing contract, of course, because there is no significant development envisaged in NL at this point in time. There are no development fees as part of the new contract

items.statement: Fair value of property per INDAS is Rs. 4,500 crores as of March 31, 2024; management does not publish market valuation.
items.quote: The valuation of the company as on 31st March is approximately Rs. 4,500 crores. Kunal Sagar: It is not a market value. This is the fair value in our annual report, as we are required to present it

items.statement: Maintain 15-20% EPS growth and 18% ROE targets
items.quote: At this time, we will stay with 15% to 20% EPS growth, and 18% ROE.

items.statement: Auto segment Rs 27,000 crore capex over next 5 years, self-funded
items.quote: For auto, it will take a bulk of that which is Rs. 27,000 crores. EV is 12,000 but w e are not giving up on ICE. ICE is still very important and ICE is going to continue to be a mainstay for the next few years and therefore ICE will continue to get Rs. 14,000 crores of CAPEX in this time period

items.statement: Farm segment Rs 5,000 crore investment over next 3 years
items.quote: For farm, we've got Rs. 5,000 crores that we've outlined right now, again, driving some of the growth in the farm business.

items.statement: Services segment Rs 5,000 crore investment over next 3 years
items.quote: And services again we've outlined 5000 crores right now. As Mahindra finance grows, it will need capital to fund its growth but beyond that our growth gems are doing well and we will put more capital there.

items.statement: Auto capacity expansion from 49,000 to 64,000/month by end FY25, then to 72,000
items.quote: We exited March at 49,000 capacity. By end of F25, we should be at 64. The breakup of 64 increase, which is the 15,000 number, is 5,000 between Thar 5 -door an d XUV 3XO and 10,000 which is the first lot of the born electric capacity

items.statement: SUV booking backlog at 220,000 including 50,000 XUV 3XO first-hour bookings
items.quote: The booking number at this point of time stands at 220,000, this is now upgraded or updated to only add the first hour of XUV 3XO bookings which is 50,000.

items.statement: Target mid to high teen growth in FY25 for auto
items.quote: We are very confident on mid to high teen growth rate in F25. We stay with that.

items.statement: Farm sector expected to grow at plus 5% in FY25
items.quote: On a balance we think the year will grow at plus 5%.

items.statement: Core tractor margin at 17.7% for FY24, 17.6% in Q4 despite volume reduction
items.quote: The core tractor margin has gone up to 17.7 for the year. But interestingly when you see the quarter trend, in the quarter the core tractor margin is 17.6.

items.statement: Auto margin balancing growth and margin, new launches start with lower margins
items.quote: For every new launch, there will be lower margins. So, the 3X0 also at the start will have lower margins and what it will go up, the Thar 5 door will be coming in will have the same thing.

items.statement: EV percentage margins lower than ICE due to lower GST
items.quote: The percentage for electric will be lower because GST is far lower. So, while the same if you let's say you have the same margin on an ICE vehicle and an electric vehicle, the percentage margin will be lower on electric because the GST is lower.

items.statement: CAFE III norms may require 15-25% EV penetration by 2027-28
items.quote: Our guess is 15% to 25%.

items.statement: BII and Temasek committed Rs 2,700 crore for EV business, additional Rs 725 crore from BII under review
items.quote: BII has already put in 1200 crores, Temasek has put in 300 and they will put in their additional 900 to hit 1200. But beyond that, we had an additional Rs. 725 crore transfer from BII.

items.statement: Mahindra Finance AUM reached Rs 1 lakh crore, grew 24%, GS3 at 3.4%
items.quote: It has reached one lakh crore of assets under management. Assets under management grew at 24%. In a year that has seen interest rates go up, in a year where we cut back on certain segments and did not lend to them because we wanted to improve asset quality and therefore even more importantly asset quality is up significantly and you see the GS3 numbers having come down to 3.4% now.

items.statement: Tech Mahindra turnaround expected over 2-3 years after 52% profit decline
items.quote: It will take a 2-to-3 year time period for the full turnaround, but there's a clear part that has been outlined. The impact for this year was negative where profit was down 52% from the prior year, but that's something that we see recovering very well over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Tractor industry growth expectation for FY25 is 5% with potential upside
items.quote: So, right now I think 5% will be a good starting point. But hopefully there will be more upside triggers to that than what we are taking on board.

items.statement: EV capex for FY25-27 estimated at Rs 12,000 crores in addition to Rs 4,000 crores already spent
items.quote: And now, having gone through that in detail, the estimate for the next 3 years is 12,000 in addition to the 4000 that we had.

items.statement: XUV 3XO capacity is 9,000 per month, scalable to 10,500 with minimal investment
items.quote: We did say that the capacity we have is 9000 a month, which is higher than the XUV300 capacity. That was part of that 49,000 to 55,000 that you saw on that slide. So, we said we have 9000 and with the very short lead time and a very minimal investment, it can go up to 10,500.

items.statement: XUV 3XO received 50,000 bookings with gasoline 65-70%, diesel ~30%, automatic ~20%
items.quote: I think early numbers are gasoline is 65%-70% and diesel is about 30%. I don't know the automatic you have. I don't ha ve that number yet. So, this is the only one I have right now, automatic about 20

items.statement: Tractor demand optimism for H2 FY25 driven by positive farmer terms of trade and monsoon
items.quote: There is a lot of optimism about how second half can bounce back very strongly. So, it's too early to call, but April was better than what we thought and hopefully we will see a better than 5% growth as we go along.

items.statement: XUV 3XO attracting new customers: 25% first-time buyers, 25% hatchback upgraders, 15% existing Mahindra owners
items.quote: So, the one data that we have not out of the 50,000 but the first lot of inquiries and test drives that were going on is 25% no vehicle ownership out of the first lot of people 25% hatch. So, it's a very different and only 15% Mahindra ownership out of the first lot of customers coming in.

items.statement: TREM 5 implementation in 2026 very unlikely; if implemented would cause significant FY25 volume upswing
items.quote: TREM 5, it is 26 . That's the current level of postponement. I mean, our sense is it's very unlikely to happen in 2026, very unlikely. So, of course if it were to happen in 26 , there would be a huge upswing in 2025 volumes but I would not count on the 2026 im plementation date certainly not the way it's envisaged with all models going into TREM 5 at the same time and all horsepower

items.statement: BEV portfolio targeting psychographic segment wanting latest tech and wow factor, not just existing Mahindra customers
items.quote: I would rather put it as attitude or a psychographic definition which is around people who want to stand out, do things differently, experience new things and definitely are hungry for experiencing the latest tech and this product is going to come with tech which is unseen in vehicles of way higher price points.

items.statement: Last mile mobility raised Rs 1,000 crores; investing in Zaheerabad plant for electric 3-wheeler capacity
items.quote: We've raised money as you know we have 600 from one investor and 400 now from the other, so Rs. 1000 crores. We have aggressive growth plans, so there is work happening on new gen platform and new completely new products for the future. We are also investing in capacity at Zaheerabad plant.

items.statement: Electric 3-wheeler penetration expected to rise from 11% to 40-50% in foreseeable future
items.quote: Over the next few years without defining what that is but in the foreseeable future we think that category penetration should go to 40% to 50% which would mean a very significant increase now.

items.statement: Core tractor margins supported by benign commodity prices in Q4 and cost management during downcycle
items.quote: I think quarter 4 comm odity prices on the tractor side have been benign. That has helped. Rubber went up now which will see some effect of that in quarter one, but overall commodity prices for tractors were pretty benign as well in quarter 4, which helped the margin

items.statement: Growth Gems portfolio targeting collective market cap of $17 billion by FY30 from $3.4 billion in FY23
items.quote: We want that 3.4 to go to 17 billion by the time we get to fiscal 30. So, we are looking at a significant growth in the growth gems overall and we are on path for that.

items.statement: M&A strategy to continue in core businesses and growth gems; may explore one new area beyond current footprint if it makes sense
items.quote: We will look at potentially one new area of growth. We have been looking at that frankly for the last two years but we haven't been able to get something that we say this really makes sense. So, if we don't get something we can say it really makes sense, we won't do anything. If we do, then we will look at one potential new area where we can leverage the Mahindra brand, where we feel we can delive

items.statement: Holidays business has high demand and occupancy; allocated Rs 5,000 crores investment from services capex
items.quote: The 5,000-crore investment we saw in services, that is a good amount that's allocated for Holidays because occupancy rates are high. The demand from customers is very high. We can deliver very well in this space. So, that's one that we see with a clear 5x growth path.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is INR 1,000 crores
items.quote: And our Capex guidance for the coming year, which is FY25, is in the region of INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: FY24 actual Capex spend was INR 700 crores against guidance of INR 1,100 crores
items.quote: The actual Capex cash flow for FY24 was significantly lower than the guidance as we curtailed Capex. Against a guidance of INR 1,100 crores, the spend was only around INR 700 crores.

items.statement: Expect demand in India to pick up post elections; April 2024 saw double-digit growth in CV and PV volumes
items.quote: We expect the demand in India to pick up post elections. We have already registered a double-digit growth in our commercial vehicle and passenger car volumes for the month of April 2024.

items.statement: Expect Europe demand momentum to be better in FY25 vs last year; April 2024 volumes grew double-digit
items.quote: Coming to Europe, we expect the demand momentum to be better in FY25 compared to last year. In Europe also, markets registered a double-digit growth in volumes in the month of April 2024.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin for Q4 FY24 was 16.4%; excluding EPR liability would be 17.8%
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter at INR 10.3 billion, was a margin of 16.4% compared to 16% in the same period last year. This included the EPR liability on the India Operations which Neeraj talked about. Excluding that, the consolidated EBITDA would have been at 17.8%.

items.statement: India Operations EBITDA margin for Q4 FY24 was 15.6%; excluding EPR liability would be 17.2%
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 6.8 billion, a margin of 15.6% compared to 15.9% in the same period last year. Again, if we exclude the EPR liability of INR 685 million, the margin for India Operations would have been at 17.2%.

items.statement: Europe Operations Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin was 19.1%, best-ever Q4 performance
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at EUR 35 million, with a robust EBITDA margin performance of 19.1% compared to 18.1% for the same period last year. This has been our best-ever Q4 performance for the European Operations.

items.statement: Raw material costs expected to rise mid-single digits in Q1 FY25; 3% price hike taken in May, may need another 2-2.5% increase
items.quote: In terms of raw material outlook, we expect the raw material cost to go up by mid-single digits in the current quarter. We will seek to negate that through price increases.

items.statement: May price increase of ~3% negates EPR and partially covers raw material; another small increase may be needed for Q1
items.quote: In May, we have taken about 3%. That negates the entire EPR and maybe to a certain extent, raw material. We may need another small increase to completely cover the entire raw material and the EPR cost increase for Q1.

items.statement: Europe UHP/UUHP proportion improved to 47% in Q4 FY24 from steady-state average of 43%
items.quote: The large part of this in the last quarter was a better mix. As Neeraj talked about, the UHP proportion was significantly higher at 47% against our more steady-state average of 43%.

items.statement: EPR liability of INR 68 crores charged in FY24; certificates in shortfall but availability improving
items.quote: Please note that this is despite additional charge of INR 68 crores on account of EPR liability.

items.statement: Dividend policy payout range 20-35%; Board declared INR 6 dividend, an all-time high
items.quote: We have a very clear, clearly listed dividend policy, which has been cleared by the Board, which is to say that the payout has to be between 20% to 35%. You also have to look at future spends as we go along. And therefore, the Board yesterday only has declared a INR 6 dividend, which is an all-time high.

items.statement: Expect Europe Operations to deliver 16-17% EBITDA margin consistently in FY25
items.quote: A 16% to 17% EBITDA margin for our European Operations with their current mix profile is something we are looking to deliver on a consistent basis.

items.statement: PCR capacity utilisation in 80s; small capacity expansion may start in H2 FY25 for FY27 needs
items.quote: If the current expectations on demand hold up, and we will be carefully watching that, maybe in the second half we will start a small capacity expansion on passenger car, nothing has been committed yet.

items.statement: Expect high single-digit CV growth and double-digit PCR growth in India for FY25
items.quote: My expectations would be a high single-digit for CV and a double-digit for PCR.

items.statement: Europe plans 1-2% price increase in Q2 FY25 due to cost push
items.quote: And in addition to this we are also planning, Amyn, to take a price increase of around 1% to 2% in quarter two, given the cost push that we are having so we will be taking -- we planned it, let's see how it goes.

items.statement: Three-to-five-year CAGR for like-to-like consumption growth estimated at 11-12%
items.quote: I would estimate anywhere between 11 % to 12% kind of growth.

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 400 crore residential sales in FY25 from ready inventory in Bangalore
items.quote: This would be our guidance for FY 25 that we are targeting to get about aim to sell about Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Trading occupancy expected to reach 95-96% by end of FY25
items.quote: we should be in 95% - 96% range for sure.

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 1,670 crore deployed in FY24 across assets under development and one land acquisition
items.quote: We have reinvested a considerable amount of this cash flow through capital expenditure acro ss assets under development and one land acquisition during the year in total aggregating about Rs. 1,670

items.statement: FY24 gross leasing over 500,000 sq ft with 360,000 sq ft new leasing and 170,000 sq ft renewals
items.quote: FY24 gross leasing has been over half a million square feet out of which approximately 3.6 lakh square feet is new leasing and 1.7 lakh square feet is renewal.

items.statement: New mall EBITDA margins to converge with existing mall margins as they stabilize in FY25
items.quote: going forward in FY25, EBITDA margins from new malls should start moving towards the margins we see for our existing operational malls as these malls stabilize

items.statement: Residential prices at Rs. 24,000+ per sq ft vs Rs. 15,000+ in 2019; Kolkata micro-market rates at Rs. 18,000-20,000 per sq ft
items.quote: We have taken some price hikes and the market has also accepted that well. And we are selling at about Rs. 24,000 per square foot plus plus, compared to Rs. 15,000 per square foot plus plus in 2019.

items.statement: Strong residential demand in Kolkata micro-market with rates exceeding Rs. 18,000-20,000 per sq ft
items.quote: micro market there seems to be very, very strong and stable. Our primary research is showing rates in that micro market to be in excess of about Rs. 18,000 – Rs.20,000

items.statement: F&B and entertainment allocation increased to 30% of GLA in new malls from 15% historically
items.quote: We have significantly increased the percentage of gross leasable area occupied by F&B in the new malls we maybe in about 15 %- 16% range for F&B alone. And then you add that, entertainment centers, multiplex and entertainment options, you are inching closer to about 30%.

items.statement: Retail sweet spot moved to 1.4-1.5 million sq ft due to demand from global brands
items.quote: No, absolutely the sweet spot has moved up simply because of the demand from retail brands. So many new global brands entering into the country its becoming, the sweet spot now is closer to about 1.4 -1.5 million square feet.

items.statement: Not actively pursuing new residential projects; selective on land in mature markets with consistent absorption
items.quote: So currently, we don't have any active plans on expanding on Residential. We are not in any race to become a larger Residential developer.

items.statement: Two more land transactions under pursuit to close in calendar year 2024 adding 2-2.5 million sq ft over 4-5 years
items.quote: There are probably two more real transactions that we are currently pursuing, and we should be able to conclude them in this calendar year. So that would add maybe another 2 - 2.5 million to our portfolio in the next four years or four to five years.

items.statement: Office assets: Asia Towers Bangalore near completion awaiting OC; Pune and Chennai Phase 1 (~1M sq ft) ready by end of CY2024; Mumbai offices by 2027; Bangalore offices by CY2026
items.quote: Asia Towers, Bangalore is nearly complete, we are waiting for the OC, and we should be able to commence operations immediately thereafter. Phoenix Millennium Towers at Pune, Wakad - these will be ready by the end of this calendar year and Chennai as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 BOPP margins expected steady at March 2024 level
items.quote: Q1' FY25 outlook for BOPP margins remain steady in line with the March 2024 month level.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals subsidiary to achieve double-digit EBITDA and over 20% ROCE in FY25
items.quote: What we feel now is that speciality chemical subsidiary is all set to make double digit EBITDA next year i.e. in FY'25 with more than 20% ROCE.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 300-350 crore planned for next year, mainly on BOPP production line
items.quote: We are looking for close to Rs. 300 to 350 crore CAPEX in next one year which will be largely on BOPP production line.

items.statement: BOPP film margin improved to Rs 12 per kg in Q4 FY24 from Rs 9 per kg in Q3 FY24
items.quote: BOPP film margin has been running at Rs. 12 per kg during March 2024 quarter versus Rs. 9 per kg in December 2023 quarter.

items.statement: Specialty sales increased to 66% of total volume in Q4 FY24 from 61% in Q3 FY24
items.quote: The specialty sales have increased to 66% of total volume in Quarter 4 compared to 64% for the full year FY24 and 61% in December 2023 quarter.

items.statement: Specialty mix target of 68-70% for FY25
items.quote: this year, we are hoping that we will be somewhere close to 68 to 70%.

items.statement: BOPP and CPP lines to increase production capacity by close to 50% over 12-15 months
items.quote: Both the lines will be the world's largest production capacity lines and will increase the company's production capacity by close to 50% in a phased manner over next 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: High-speed BOPP and CPP lines expected to rationalize production cost by 3-5%
items.quote: With these high-speed lines, it should rationalize cost of production between 3% to 5% depending on the product.

items.statement: Renewable power cost rationalization to add Rs 25 crore annually from April 2024
items.quote: Cost rationalization on renewable power should add to the bottom line starting from April 2024. We expect annual impact to be close to Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: North Korea plant relocation to India to rationalize cost by ~$1 million, operations to start Q2 FY25
items.quote: Post relocation to India, this production line should rationalize the cost by close to U.S. $ 1 million with improved capacity utilization of the line. We expect this line to start commencement of operation in India from Q2'FY5.

items.statement: Rigid packaging expected to reach 80% capacity utilization by H2 FY25
items.quote: we expect from the second half of FY25 we should be close to 80% capacity utilization.

items.statement: BOPET film margins remain negative; company to rationalize volume and focus on specialty and high shrink films
items.quote: The margin for the BOPET film, which is close to 8% of our top line, continues to remain negative. For BOPET films what we are going to focus on now is to be selective in terms of the volume. So, we will rationalize the volume to reduce the loss-making sales and focus more and more on specialty films and high shrink films sales.

items.statement: Net debt reduction expected to start from FY26; FY25 net debt may increase by Rs 20-50 crore from current Rs 561 crore
items.quote: Currently we are at Rs. 550 crores of net debt. We do not expect much change in the net debt level except that there maybe it may increase by Rs. 20, 30, or 50 crores. That will be clear at the end of March 2025, from there on, as we indicated earlier on the call, you may expect some reduction coming in.

items.statement: FY25 EXIM growth 15%, Domestic 25%, overall 18-20%
items.quote: I would like to give guidance for FY '25 EXIM, we are hoping 15% growth. Domestic, we are hoping 25% growth. That makes overall 18% to 20% growth in FY '25.

items.statement: FY25 capex budget Rs 610 crore, subject to mid-year review
items.quote: As far as Capex budget is concerned, now we have finalized the Capex budget of Rs. 610 crores, primarily centered at wagons, containers and rolling stock, etc., development of terminals, land procurement for terminals and IT.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 25% for FY25
items.quote: And our margins, EBITDA, which is in the range of 25%, we are very confident that we will be able to maintain the 25% EBITDA in this financial year also.

items.statement: 100% pass-through of rail haulage hike in EXIM, strategic in domestic
items.quote: In the EXIM segment, we have passed through the entire amount. In domestic segment, we have passed strategically. We have not passed everywhere, depending on the stream, depending on the capability of the customers to absorb that part, that hike.

items.statement: Drivers: bulk cement in tank containers, double-stack to Varnama near Nhava Sheva, new terminals, DPD movement
items.quote: The drivers for growth in this financial year will be bulk cement in tank containers, which is a new product that we are going to launch, then we will get -- we will be running double-stack trains to Varnama near Nhava Sheva very soon. And we are expecting sizable additional business at our new terminals.

items.statement: First/last mile 25% of volume, target 50% FY25, 80-85% FY26
items.quote: First mile, last mile, 25% of our entire volume, we are now providing first mile, last mile service to our customers. which has been very well appreciated by them. And our target this year is 50%. And by next year, that is FY '26, we are confident of reaching this number to 80% to 85% of our total volume, we will be providing first mile, last mile.

items.statement: LLF provision FY25 Rs 400-420 crore; Gati Shakti could reduce TKD cost 60-65%
items.quote: So, for the current FY, if you missed the discussion, we had a long discussion on LLF going forward. So, the one answer to your question is this year, our provisions will be hovering around Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 420 crores.

items.statement: Record double-stack trains 5,440 in FY24 (+33%), 14 new rakes, 7,653 containers, 90 LNG trucks, 200 more LNG trucks authorized
items.quote: Then we have run record number of double-stacked trains in the FY. That is 5,440, which is a growth of 33%. In the FY '23, we could run only 4,097 double-stack trains.

items.statement: JNPT DFC connection expected by March 2025 per DFC officers
items.quote: Yes, as per the Dedicated Freight Corridor officers, JNPT will be commissioned on DFC by March 2025. That is a projection they have given.

items.statement: Reiterated FY25 EBITDA per ton guidance of INR 18,000-20,000 and 20% volume growth
items.quote: Absolutely. We are quite confident of achieving that and we are reiterating our guidance.

items.statement: Reiterated full year FY25 guidance of 20% volume growth with EBITDA margin of INR 18,000 to INR 20,000 per ton
items.quote: But concerning all this thing I think if you look at a full year basis we are reiterating our guidance of 20% volume growth with an EBITDA margin of INR18,00 0 to INR20,000.

items.statement: Announced total expansion capex of INR 5,400 crores including Indonesia JV, Chromeni acquisition, Jajpur downstream, and infrastructure
items.quote: We have announced a total expansion capex of around INR5,400 crores. With these acquisitions and investments, we have orchestrated a plan to become one of the largest stainless steel producers in the world.

items.statement: FY25 total capex outlook of INR 4,700-4,800 crores including spillover from FY24, plus INR 500 crores maintenance capex
items.quote: With this, the total capex outlook of FY '25 is expected to be around INR4,700 crores to INR4,800 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at INR 1,200-1,300 crores for Odisha HR/CR capacity, Indonesia SMS, Jajpur infrastructure, and ESG renewables
items.quote: So overall, we are expecting that what capex we have outline right now close to around INR1,200 crores to say INR1,300 crores of the capex next year in FY '26.

items.statement: Export order book impacted by Red Sea crisis; stopped booking new export orders due to high freight costs
items.quote: So we actually stopped booking those kind of orders in our books which are reflected in Q4.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA per ton impacted by INR 250-300 crores due to nickel price fall, Red Sea freight costs, and lower exports
items.quote: So all put together they all have close to INR250 crores impact on these mul tiple events which has happened INR250 crores to INR300 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 expected to be better than Q4 FY24 as Red Sea impact stabilizes and nickel prices recover
items.quote: No Q1 is expected to be better than Q4.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand across all major segments including railway, auto, pipe & tube, lift elevator, and special grades
items.quote: In the domestic market, we experienced strong demand across all major segments. The railway sector in particular, saw unprecedented growth, achieving its highest ever sales in the wagon segment, while demand for passenger coaches and Metro remains robust.

items.statement: Export markets remain muted with geopolitical issues including Red Sea crisis impacting export performance
items.quote: On the export front, our key markets continued to see muted demand along with geopolitical issues such as the one on going in the Red Sea. These challenges have had an impact on our export performance and prevented us on optimizing our sales mix.

items.quote: So the dialogue is always on, and we always expect that something positive should come out, but immediately, in the short term, I don't see anything, maybe in the medium term, some relief could come, but nothing to really mention at the moment.

items.statement: Indonesia NPI project expected to commission in early Q2 FY25, with commercial sales starting then and 90% utilization by FY26

items.quote: And on Rabirun, we have just started now producing our tubes. We have just started it, so it will also gradually pick up. And we expect it to go to the level of 1,000 to 1,500 in the next couple of quarters.

items.quote: If we are able to grow our revenue, grow our billing by 15-16% year on year, we should be able to maintain margin. If we are able to grow at 20%, that will help us improve our margins. And if we grow at 9-10%, then our margins might take a dip in the short term.

items.quote: We are expanding our sales team, so we're hiring more sales people. Now, some of them have been hired, but some are yet to be hired. So, Naukri headcount will grow next year over last year.

items.quote: If we are able to grow the 99acres business by 25-30% again this year, then we should be able to make some, generate some cash this year. But fingers crossed, I mean, see, we've had a good 4-5-6-7 quarters in 99acres.
