items.quote: First, magnetite is very new. We are yet to start on the exploration. Once we get to the reserves, that time we'll be able to envisage what's going to be the investment on the magnetite mining site, etc.

items.statement: African expansions structured under separate subsidiaries: Maamba Collieries for power (Phase 2 under same), agri business in separate 100% subsidiary.
items.quote: There are different subsidiaries. Whereas Maamba Collieries is a different subsidiary under which we have the Phase 1 power plant, and the Phase 2 could be under that. And agri business is anyway 100% in a different subsidiary.

items.statement: Zambia Phase 2 equity to be funded by Nava Bharat Singapore using dividends and shareholder loan repayments from MCL.
items.quote: Yes. So with regards to the Phase 2 , the equity would need to be financed by NBS. But at the end of the day, MCL will declare dividends and repay the shareholder loan to NBS. So NBS will be utilizing some of that cash flow to fund its equity.

items.statement: ZESCO arrears collection uncertain; management doing best but cannot guarantee 100% recovery by calendar 2024.
items.quote: Yes. So I don't think we can be 100% sure of anything in life. So what we can assure you is we are doing our level best to discuss with ZESCO. ZESCO has been honouring a lot of its commitments. We are working with ZESCO times are tough in Zambia, and we definitely wish and hope to recoup the entire amount, but it will all depend on discussions that we have with ZESCO as we move forward.

items.statement: Aspirational target of $100 million revenue by FY26 maintained, dependent on execution and hiring
items.quote: We believe we have an amazing opportunity. We've always said $100 million was the dream, was aspirational target. And we still believe that these opportunities exist.

items.statement: No formal projections given for FY25; goal is to beat previous quarter and improve EBITDA margin
items.quote: We don't give projections. But as I said, my simple goal that I work with since the day I got this job and I think as long as I will be here is to beat the previous quarter and that's what we aspire to do.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 11%+, first time double-digit; Q4 EBITDA 8.2% due to one-off expenses; target 35% gross margin vs current ~29%
items.quote: We have delivered strong double digit EBDITA of 11%+ for the first time with phenomenal performance from entire team.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 8.2% lower than expected due to several one-time expenses; expect bounce back to double-digit
items.quote: And our EBITDA margin was at 8.2%, it was a bit lower than we expected because of several onetime expenses that we had in the quarter.

items.statement: Strong demand across all three verticals; pipeline better than ever; re-signed three lost customers; old customers returning
items.quote: So, V.P, our whole world has changed from April 1 because we all are fresh. There's nothing for us to move away from anymore. It's better and bigger than we've ever seen, I continue to maintain that.

items.statement: Active client roster reduced to 84 from 250; exited bottom 10-15 customers; target 75 clients for INR 800 cr revenue
items.quote: And while we added a lot of new customers, we also exited the bottom 10 - 15 customers. And now, our active client roster is down to a healthy 84.

items.statement: Just signed a Fortune 50 company as new healthcare customer; healthcare domestic and Europe revenue to go to zero, US/Canada to grow
items.quote: And as we speak, we have just signed a Fortune 50 company as a new customer. I'll get to that later.

items.statement: DSO improved from 86 days to 72 days; further improvement opportunity exists
items.quote: In terms of DSO, which I already touch base upon, we had a huge improvement from 86 days to 72 days, and we still see a lot of opportunity for us to improve.

items.statement: New office opening in Bangalore Whitefield in July; upgrading to A-grade tech parks for data security and amenities
items.quote: In addition to this, we strengthened our offshore infrastructure, whether it is Pune, Chennai and then very soon coming in July, we have a new office in Bangalore in Whitefield opening up

items.statement: Global headcount 2,529, down ~200 YoY due to exit of domestic volume business; target 2,700-2,800 with majority outside India
items.quote: I want to acknowledge my entire team, which is now at 2,529 employees globally. So, if you see this compared from a year ago, we've gone down by about 200-odd people.

items.statement: Key managers moved to USA and UK for global roles; hiring local talent and transferring employees from India; trend to continue 3 years
items.quote: Now, under each of these leaders, we are hiring local people and in parallel, we are transferring many more employees from our various India offices. I expect this trend to continue for next 3 years as we build our global presence and account management capabilities.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 5 per equity share, highest ever, 9th consecutive year, subject to AGM approval in July
items.quote: Based on the performance, our Board has recommended this morning a dividend of INR 5 per equity share, the highest ever in our history and marking the ninth consecutive year of dividend payout, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming 33rd Annual General Meeting in July.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Industrial Equipment 52%, Transportation & Mobility 37%, Healthcare 8%; 98% from three verticals, 2% ITS to go away
items.quote: Industrial Equipment & Heavy Machinery continues to be our largest vertical and growing very well, and we see amazing potential is at 52%; Transportation & Mobility, which is where automotive is predominantly the largest vertical and now rail is where we are investing, contributed 37% of our revenues; and Healthcare, which is our new vertical, contributed about 8% of our revenue.

items.statement: Pivoted from pure-play mechanical to software (embedded, digital, AI, ML, cybersecurity, data analytics); largest RFPs and deals in software
items.quote: The other side of the story, which is a real ga me changer for us for the last three years, has been when we pivoted from just a pure -play mechanical and engineering services company to software, both on the embedded side and digital side.

items.statement: Sales team fully relocated to US (Michigan) and Europe (London); no sales team in India from April 1; lead gen and presales remain offshore
items.quote: Our entire sales team led by Vignesh, who's Executive Vice President and part of my global management team, he has moved to Michigan. He's building a team around there. Pramod Patil, who's again Executive Vice President, part of the management team; has moved to London. He's building a whole team in Europe.

items.statement: US immigration opened up; Canada visa processing down to 3-4 months from 6-12; Germany 3-6 months, targeting 1 month
items.quote: US was shut for us till about last year. And now, US is open. So, we have people going to US. Canada, which was taking 6, 9 months, 12 months is now taking 3 to 4 months only. Germany is still 3 to 6 months, and we hope it goes down to 1 month.

items.statement: No active M&A discussions; open to acquisitions with cash and PE partner Convergent; priority is finding company supporting existing clients
items.quote: Shriram, on the M&A side, nothing concrete as of today. We haven't , there is nothing that we are actively discussing. But as I always said, we are very open. We have the cash. We have very strong PE partner in Convergent.

items.statement: Exited large Indian healthcare customer end of April (~130 engineers at USD 4.5-5/hr); domestic healthcare revenue to become zero
items.quote: So, for example, we exited a large Indian customer end of April where about 120 engineers moved away, and we transitioned them to some other pay roll the customer chose. So that significant number of headcounts will come down.

items.statement: Revenue grew from INR 440 cr to INR 470+ cr (7%+ YoY); PAT grew 194% (3x) from INR 11+ cr to INR 34+ cr; cash from INR 48 cr to INR 93 cr
items.quote: In terms of revenue, we have grown from INR 440 crores to INR 470 + crores, which is a 7%+ growth. I think we could have done much better if it wasn't for all the clients that we were exiting during our transition phase.

items.statement: Revenue grew from INR 307 cr to INR 472 cr over last 8 quarters; Q4 revenue INR 118 cr after Q3 dip from furloughs/holidays
items.quote: And the exact number from INR 307 crores in the last 8 quarters we have gone to INR 472 crores in quarters. So huge growth for a company of our size and I'm very excited and very happy where we are.

items.statement: Moving engineers from India billing (USD 5-10/hr) to onsite global billing (USD 18-75/hr) drives margin improvement; not headcount-driven growth
items.quote: Let us say we are invoicing at USD 5, USD 6, USD 7, USD 8, USD 10 an hour. And they are moving to my international business where we are invoicing from USD 18 an hour to USD 75 an hour if they are on site.

items.statement: Not competing with GCCs; focus on 80% of global companies in three verticals without India GCC; target customers wanting flexibility, agility, speed
items.quote: Less than 20% of the global companies in my 3 verticals that Onward is playing today, has a GCC in India. My focus is other 80%.

items.statement: Target 10 customers at USD 10 million/year each; currently have 3-5 customers at USD 3-4 million; sweet spot is scaling engagements
items.quote: We have 75 customers. We just need 10 customers to win, 10 customers which can get to USD10 million a year, right? So, for us, it's that.

items.statement: Expects AHP revenue to grow 20% in FY25 from Rs 310 crore base
items.quote: We are looking forward for the overall improvement in the volumes of animal health division from 310 crores to plus-20% for this financial year.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 estimated at Rs 40-50 crore with no major projects
items.quote: As such, there is no major capitalization during '24-25. Only the existing capital of all the units will be there, that's not much, maybe to the extent of 40 to 50 crores in all put together of all the existing unit of poultry, AHP, oil segment and all, but there's no any major project in hand.

items.statement: New AHP plant at 35-40% utilisation; old plant at 75-80%; full utilisation in 4-5 years
items.quote: New plant initially they will be utilizing around 35% to 40% of the capacity and the old plant is almost running at 75% to 80% of the capacity, yes, and in the subsequent year, it will definitely improve further.

items.statement: Summer mortality 10-11% vs 5-6% in winter; body weight drops to 2.1-2.2 kg from 2.4-2.5 kg
items.quote: So in terms of productivity or body weight, there is a decrease of 10% body weight and in terms of mortality, mortality goes to 4% to 5%. So put together close to 12% to 15% less yield is achieved during the period of summer.

items.statement: April broiler realization Rs 108-116/kg across India; expected to continue till monsoon
items.quote: Usually, if you see the year -on-year and month-on-month, this particular April month has gone and average realization has closed 108 to 116 all over India, same is the trend expected for the month of May also and it is likely to continue till the monsoon reaches until the heat is I mean the currently the temperature is on higher side.

items.statement: FY24 avg maize Rs 22.80/kg, soya Rs 47.60/kg vs FY23 Rs 23.90/kg and Rs 52.80/kg; April maize Rs 23.50, soya Rs 44.60
items.quote: As far as average price of maize is concerned for FY'23 it was Rs.23.90 per Kg. Soya price was Rs.52.80 paisa per Kg for FY'23. For FY'24 the same was Rs.22.80 paisa for maize price and Rs.47.60 paisa was for soya price.

items.statement: Expects maize and soya prices to remain stable at FY24 levels if monsoon is normal
items.value: similar line what it was in FY'24
items.quote: However, monsoon can have a greater impact either on positive side or negative side. But considering overall situation, we expect that the maize price and soya price looks to be on a similar line what it was in FY'24 as of now.

items.statement: Poultry margin was ~3% in FY24; expects good margin if input prices stay stable
items.quote: Financial year '24 also has recorded close to 3% in terms of turnover overall profitability. So, I'm not sure about percentage, but definitely there will be a relief in terms of ingredient prices and whenever there is a relief on ingredient prices front, the profitability in terms of poultry and poultry segment is very good.

items.statement: Oil seed margin 1.23% in FY24 vs 2.5% in FY23; 4-5% margins were extraordinary and unlikely
items.quote: This number what you are saying 4% to 5%, it was also not there in the '22 -23 also, that was not there, it was 2.5 only and this year it is 1.23. So 4% to 5% is when the market is so much bullish or uptrend is like Rs.1,25,000 per ton of soya and now it is reeling between Rs.45,000 per ton, so that was the extraordinary percentage in the top line and bottom line which may not be achievable since

items.statement: Oil seed segment revenue fell to ~Rs 1,800 crore in FY24 from Rs 2,600 crore in FY22; expects improvement from Q2 FY25
items.quote: As far as this segment performance is concerned, the first quarter is not that much lucrative since the consumption will be in the lower side. Poultry being the temperature through and through is not in a favorable conditions, but then the subsequent quarter hopefully there will be improvement.

items.statement: 42% revenue from group companies, 58% from outside; expects outside share to improve with better poultry realization
items.quote: 42% is the revenue from the group companies and 58% is the revenue from the outside business.

items.statement: Grown-up broiler segment revenue improved most among poultry sub-segments
items.quote: Yes, grown up broiler segment has improved the revenue. If we compare with broiler chicks and layer checks in general, even in the last quarter also as well as in the coming quarters also.

items.statement: Receivables expected to improve sharply in Q1 FY25 as poultry prices recover from April
items.quote: Because the indicators are shown in the month of April also, because of these, I mean, poultry as such is improving, industry as such is improving throughout the country, so hopefully in the first quarter ending as well as the subsequent quarter, this area of receivable will also be improved to the greater extent.

items.statement: Maize diversion to ethanol unlikely at current Rs 23-24/kg prices; feasible only below Rs 21/kg
items.quote: As of now, as per the policy, whatever has been directed, it shows that some of the maize is expected to divert towards ethanol. However, if we go on a price -wise basis, I mean the present maize price, which right now is being recorded is close to Rs.23 -24. We are also clueless that at this price diverting this maize to ethanol and then having the ethanol production at that particular cost of pr

items.statement: No development on US broiler import WTO dispute; only turkey import duty reduced
items.quote: There is no development on that front. It is settled on the prices or the import duty on the Turkey, where the Turkey prices for import of Turkey from USA to India, the import duty was reduced. However, the import duty for chicken still continues and presently the preference of Indians towards the purchase of a chicken is on the smaller side of the birds.

items.statement: Venky's Xpress: 13 company-owned outlets, 52 franchise outlets; added 1 company and 14 franchise outlets since Q2
items.quote: So presently we have about a Company owned outlets are 13 and we have 52 outlets which are for chicken experience, that is the franchisee outlets.

items.statement: FY24 broiler chick realization Rs 30.38 vs Rs 27.57; layer chick Rs 38.51 vs Rs 36.38; broiler bird Rs 84.16 vs Rs 89.36
items.value: broiler chick Rs 30.38, layer chick Rs 38.51, broiler bird Rs 84.16
items.quote: For broiler chicks, the realization in '23 -24 was Rs.30.38 paisa against corresponding broiler chicks realization was Rs.27.57. In terms of layer commercial chicks, the realization in '23 -24 is Rs.38.51 paisa against corresponding '22 -23 is Rs.36.38 paisa. In terms of broiler bird, the realization has gone down in '23-24; it is Rs.84.16 paisa per Kg which was in '22-23 it was Rs.89.36 paisa.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 realization for broiler chicks, layer chicks and birds better than Q4 FY24
items.quote: The trend in broiler chicks, layer chicks and birds prices in the first quarter seems to be better than the last quarter of '23-24.

items.statement: Biological asset loss of Rs 12 crore in cash flow is notional, not actual
items.quote: Biological notional loss was there and it was not an actual loss, but it was a notional loss, because at the time of closing of the financial, you will have to have a cost basis or NRB basis, so it is a notional loss which is not there.

items.statement: Other financial assets jumped to Rs 110 crore from Rs 17 crore due to Rs 96.07 crore bank deposit
items.quote: It is a bank deposit to the extent of Rs.96.07 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 area booked surged to ~4.6 lakh sq ft from ~50,000 sq ft in Q4 FY23, driven by sale of 275 units in Imperia Phase 2
items.quote: It is the area book ed which has experienced a remarkable surge, rising from approximately 50,000 square feet in Q4 FY23 to an all-time high of 4.6 lakh square feet approximately in Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 booking value reached all-time high of ~INR250 crores vs INR25 crores in Q4 FY23, driven by Imperia Phase 2 launch
items.quote: The booking value for the quarter was also at an all-time high at about INR250 crores, compared to INR25 crores in Q4 FY'23.

items.statement: FY24 area booked was ~7.8 lakh sq ft with value of INR388 crores, both highest in company history
items.quote: The area booked for the year was 7.8 lakh square feet approximately with a value of INR388 crores. Both the numbers are the highest in the company's history.

items.statement: Acquired ~61 acres across 3 sites in Lucknow in FY24; anticipate launching at least 2 projects in FY25
items.quote: We acquired approximately 61 acres of land across 3 different sites in Lucknow, where we continue to aggregate more land. We anticipate launching at least two of these projects in the fiscal year '24 -25.

items.statement: Aim to meet or surpass FY24's historic sales figures (INR388 crores booking value) in FY25; hope to launch at least 2 of 3 new acquisitions plus Trinity and Latitude 27
items.quote: For these upcoming projects, we aim to meet or surpass the historic sales figures set in FY'24.

items.statement: INR388 crores booking value is high watermark; do not want to go below that and should only increase from here
items.quote: So INR388 crores is the highest ever number. Earlier, our highest was INR250 crores. So I don't want to go below what we have already achieved. This is a high watermark and we should only increase from here.

items.statement: Luxury project Eldeco Trinity (5 lakh sq ft) to launch in Q1 FY25; also have Twin Tower (10-12 story), Latitude 27 (4.5 lakh sq ft), and GH-4 group housing in pipeline
items.quote: We are preparing for the debut of our luxury development, Eldeco Trinity, which will be launched in the first quarter of FY'25.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 per sq ft realization hit all-time high of INR5,500, up from historical INR3,200 and recent INR4,500 levels
items.quote: But this last quarter, it has been the highest in terms of per square foot realization. I think it was INR5,500 per square foot. So, that's another metric on which is the highest ever.

items.statement: INR5,500 per sq ft realization appears to be the new normal; weighted average may increase annually if market supports
items.quote: So, on a weighted average basis, I think this seems to be the new normal. And I think that if the market keeps supporting us, then it may increase on an annual basis also.

items.statement: Trinity is a much higher-priced luxury product with higher per sq ft realization than Imperia Phase 2
items.quote: Trinity is definitely a much higher-priced product. I would not say we'll probably get sold at the same pace at which the lower -priced products were sold. But it is definitely a product which gives us good margin.

items.statement: Historically margins ~40%; expect 30% as more sustainable level; do not see margins falling below 30%; range 30-40% depending on product mix
items.quote: Historically, our margins have been in the region of 40%. That does look like a very abnormally high margin to sustain. I always said that I do expect it to come down a little bit. I think 30% would be more like it. And of late, it has come down to 30%. But definitely, I don't see it falling below 30%.

items.statement: Should be able to hold or improve margins (30% EBITDA, 23% PAT) in coming years despite new launches
items.quote: Yes, these margins, definitely, you should be able to hold on to, if not improving them.

items.statement: Demand in Lucknow is strong and latent; whatever supply is brought to market gets lapped up quickly; not worried about demand-supply mismatch
items.quote: So at the moment, whatever you supply, because the supply is so constrained, whatever you supply is getting lapped up.

items.statement: Lucknow market sold ~3,000-4,000 units/year but can absorb much more; city poised for explosive growth over next 10-15 years like Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Hyderabad
items.quote: I would know that what the demand is once we supply the market with enough stuff. I don't think the market is getting supplied enough stuff. So it's not selling, I think in a year about 3,000 to 4,000 units were sold in Lucknow. But I think the market can take much more if there was enough supply for that.

items.statement: New land acquisitions add ~INR1,000 crores to gross developable value over next 3-4 years; more deals in pipeline
items.quote: With these acquisitions, I think it will approximately add about INR1,000 crores to our gross developable value in the next 3 -4 years. And we are looking for more, there are some m ore deals in the pipeline.

items.statement: Have 5-6 more land deals in pipeline for FY25; could surpass FY24 business development if they pass due diligence
items.quote: There are at least 5-6 more deals that are still in the pipeline. I don't know how many of those will actually get inked, and we will actually take them all because I will not like to do projects just for the sake of our market pressure to do projects.

items.statement: Expect national and regional players to enter Lucknow, intensifying competition for land; but market maturation favors larger branded players gaining market share
items.quote: I do. I do. If our location is going to do so well, why would the national players or even other regional players not look at that location with more keenness. They will. I have no doubt about it, and it's only going to become the competition for land.

items.statement: Key risk is unforeseen legal/statutory trouble on projects; mitigate via tight risk filters, compliance focus, careful title and approval due diligence
items.quote: There can always be an unforeseen legal or statutory trouble in one of the projects. So that's why we've been so conservative and careful in our project acquisition.

items.statement: Land supply remains difficult; entry barrier is availability of developable land at reasonable prices; but well-placed in Lucknow with 4-5 potential projects in pipeline
items.quote: It is going to be difficult. But as I said, we have been able to, with the hard work in the last 3, 4 years, we've been able to deve lop another potential supply of another 4 or 5 projects, out of which 1 or 2 will see the light of day because of the risk filters that we tend to put in.

items.statement: First time took loans in FY24 to fund new land acquisitions; deployed for the 61 acres acquired
items.quote: For the first time we have taken some loan last year, and we've deployed it for the new land acquisitions, which we have disclosed.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR8 per equity share for FY24, same as last year; no current plans for bonus issue
items.quote: Additionally, for the FY24, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR8 per equity share, which is the same as last year.

items.statement: No plans for bonus issue currently; free float unchanged regardless of share count; INR1,000 share price not prohibitive
items.quote: Right now, there's no plans about bonus.

items.statement: Ticket size INR1-1.5 crores is reasonable with strong demand; not making INR20 crore products in Lucknow
items.quote: Our ticket size is only INR1 crores, INR1.5 crores, which is quite reasonable, and it has a lot of demand there.

items.statement: Received preliminary approvals for one of three new Lucknow land parcels; applying for approval on another in couple of days; Trinity received RERA approval
items.quote: We have, in fact, received preliminary approvals in one of them already. And another one, we are applying for approval, I think, in a couple of days.

items.statement: Eldeco Housing (listed) operates only in Lucknow; sister company EIPL (unlisted) operates rest of India; no conflict of interest by agreement; will only expand outside Lucknow if necessitated and with arrangement with sister company
items.quote: Eldeco Group has 2 companies. One is the listed company, Eldeco Housing, which works in Lucknow. And the other is an unlisted company, EIPL, Eldeco Infrastructure, which works in the rest of the country is not the parent company of Eldeco Housing. They are entirely separate companies.

items.statement: Company listed in 1985 raising INR50 lakh; never skipped dividend in 40 years; market cap grown from INR1 crore to INR1,000 crores; no compelling reason to delist
items.quote: Well, I have a confession to make. There was hardly any strategic intent when it went public in 1985. So I don't think anybody saw 40 years into the future. And the company went public in 1985 and it raised a grand total of INR50 lakh.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue growth expected at high teens, all businesses double-digit, assuming Asacol competition
items.quote: At the aggregate level, we expect high teens growth. This is obviously after assuming competition in Asacol in FY25.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at FY24 level of 27.5% with Asacol competition, efforts to improve further
items.quote: On the EBITDA margins front, I think, assuming we have competition in Asacol, we expect to comfortably maintain FY24 margins of 27.5% in the coming year and we will make our best efforts to continue to improve those margins.

items.statement: FY25 R&D spend guided at 7-8% of revenue
items.quote: I think with revenue growth that we expect and also there w ill be growth on R&D, I think we are still giving guidance of around 7-8% for

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by consumer wellness, better efficiencies, easing inflation, and favorable product mix
items.quote: yes, one part of the reason s for the gross margins is we saw an improvement on the gross margins for the cons umer business. But, overall also, we have seen improvement in gross margins with better efficiencies and inflationary pressures reducing. So , I think both of them have aided and, obviously, it's also to do with product mix

items.statement: Gross margin without special products is sustainable; cost rationalization and price increases offset input inflation
items.quote: So, gross margin without special products is sustainable . A nd with continuous efforts in terms of cost rationalization, normal price increases that we can take in cons umer business, we are able to ta ke care of inflation in terms of input cost

items.statement: Other expenses increased by ~50 crore one-off items and consumer wellness seasonality in Q4
items.quote: So far as other expenses are concerned, for the quarter, the increase is partly because of one-off expenses to the extent of about 50 cr ores and largely because of the seasonality of Consumer Wellness

items.statement: US base business achieved sequential growth every quarter in FY24 on volume expansion and new product introductions
items.quote: The base business achieved sequential growth every quarter through the year on the back of vol ume expansion and new product

items.statement: US formulations revenue crossed $1 billion for first time in FY24 with strong double-digit growth
items.quote: Revenues of the business crossed US$ 1 billion for the first time on the back of strong, double digit growth.

items.statement: India branded formulations grew 8% YoY in Q4, faster than market, gained share in derma and anti-infective therapies
items.quote: branded formulations business in India grew faster than the market during the quarter as well with 8% year -on-year growth . Portfolio of key pillar brands and innovation products were the key growth drivers. During the quarter, we gained market share in derma and the anti -infective

items.statement: Consumer wellness revenue Rs 7.8 billion, up 10% YoY in Q4; personal care strong, food and nutrition mid-single digit growth
items.quote: The consumer wellness business recorded revenues of 7.8 billion rupees, up 10% on a year-on-year basis. The personal care segment, which comprises of Nycil and Everyuth brands, registered yet another quarter of strong growth. Performance of food and nutrition segment improved with mid-single digit growth during the quarter.

items.statement: International markets revenue Rs 5 billion, up 13% YoY in Q4 with healthy demand across key markets
items.quote: Overall, the business posted revenues of 5 billion rupees, up 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: Chronic portfolio contribution increased to 41.2% per IQVIA MAT March'24, up 360 bps over three years
items.quote: of chronic 4 of 23 portfolio has increased consistently over the years and stood at 41.2% as per IQVIA MAT March’24, an improvement of 360 basis points over the last three years

items.statement: Mirabegron launched in US with exclusivity on higher strength, one competitor on lower strength
items.quote: From our best knowledge, right now, on one strength, we have one more competitor and on the larger strength, we are exclusive for now.

items.statement: Zokinvy acquired for Progeria, approved in US, EU, UK, Japan; early access program in place
items.quote: Recently, Sentynl Therapeutics Inc. acquired world-wide proprietary rights to Zokinvy from Eiger Biopharmaceuticals for the treatment of Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome, an ultra-rare, fatal, genetic premature aging disease that accelerate mortality in young patients. Zokinvy is the first and only treatment approved by the USFDA for Progeria. The product is also approved in EU, Great Britain

items.statement: NULIBRY approved by UK MHRA for MoCD Type A; first and only treatment in Great Britain
items.quote: Sentynl Therapeutics, our wholly owned subsid iary, received marketing authorization from the UK MHRA for NULIBRY for the treatment of patients in Great Britain with Molybdenum C ofactor Deficiency (MoCD) Type A ; an ultra -rare life -threatening genetic disorder. It is the first and only treatment in Great Britain for patients with genetic disorder

items.statement: Zituvimet and Zituvimet IR launched in US (Januvia 505(b)(2)); good traction, meaningful over 5 years
items.quote: Yes, we have launched Zituvimet and Zituvimet IR will be the next one which has also got approval. We have had good success. It's a tough launch in terms of making a branded launch in the US market, but we are seeing a good traction on it and we see, over the next five years it being a meaningful product for Zydus.

items.statement: Vascepa launched recently but scale manufacturing capacity not yet available; third-party manufacturing used, need 2 more quarters for own capacity
items.quote: We have launched Vascepa, I think recently, but w e don't have scale manufacturing capacity yet, which we do to third party. So, once we are able to scale up our manufacturing which will require at least two more quarters, then we would see more capability of ours to take any meaningful business, but right now we don't have capacity

items.statement: Efficiency initiatives improved profitability by 50-70 bps in past; expect similar improvement going forward

items.quote: Syngene successfully concluded the acquisition of the s trategic biologics manufacturing facility from Stelis Biopharma, which will add 20,000 liters of manufacturing capacity, trebling Syngene's biomanufacturing capacity and providing the basis for future growth opportunity. The completion of the facility modifications and qualification remain on track and are expected in the second half of fisca

items.statement: Biocon Immunosuppressant facility in Vizag received CEP from EDQM; expects inspection and qualification for commercial supplies by other major regulators during FY25
items.quote: Our Immunosuppressant facility in Vizag received a Certificate of Suitability or CEP, from the European regulator EDQM. We expect the facility to be inspected and subsequently qualified for commercial supplies by other major regulators during this fiscal.

items.statement: Biocon Peptide facility in Bengaluru completed process validation activities, important step for future product launches
items.quote: Our Peptide facility in Bengaluru also successfully completed process validation activities, an important step in preparation for future product launches.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics crossed USD 1 billion revenue mark in FY24 with revenue from operations at INR 8,824 crores, 58% year-on-year growth
items.quote: On a full year basis, Biocon Biologics crossed the USD 1 billion revenue mark with revenue from operations at INR 8,824 crores representing a 58% year-on-year growth driven by the step-up from the acquisition, along with robust underlying growth in the core businesses.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics posted highest ever quarterly revenue in Emerging Markets in Q4 FY24 driven by consolidation of self-led and partner-led models and 7 product launches
items.quote: On the Emerging Markets front, Biocon Biologics posted its highest ever quarter revenue led by strong growth across its major regions in Latin America, Africa, the Middle East and Turkey and the Asia Pacific regions. Revenues were driven by the consolidation of the self-led and the partner-led business models and supported by 7 product launches during the quarter.

items.statement: Group core EBITDA margin for Q4 FY24 was 30%; full year FY24 core EBITDA margin was 29%
items.quote: Group core EBITDA was up 10% to INR 4,195 crores, representing a core operating margin of 29%.

items.statement: Syngene full year FY24 EBITDA margin stable at 31%
items.quote: reported EBITDA growing 10% to INR 1,105 crores, with stable EBITDA margins at 31%.

items.statement: Biocon Generics faced pricing pressures in API business resulting in contraction over FY24, balanced by formulations growth
items.quote: Momentum in our formulations business balanced the challenges we faced in pricing pressures on our API business, which witnessed a contraction over the year, resulting in Generics delivering a modest 1% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics sees pricing pressures in U.S. biosimilar market but sustained volume demand across private and government sectors
items.quote: we're seeing some very robust market share increases. These are, of course, driven by volume demand for our products, and they are c oming along with some pressures on pricing, but we see sustained demand in volume for our products, I think, both in the private and the government sectors

items.statement: Biocon Generics formulation share of product sales increased to approximately 35% from 25% in FY23, expected to overtake APIs in coming years
items.quote: During the fiscal, formulation share of product sales increased to approximately 35% from 25% last year, and it is expected to increase and overtake APIs as a share of our business mix in the coming years.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics secured 4 new commercial formulary agreements in U.S. including United Healthcare Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy effective May 1, 2024 as preferred oncology product
items.quote: We have also secured 4 new commercial formulary agreements, including United Healthcare's Commercial Medical Benefit Drug Policy effective 1st of May this year as a United Healthcare preferred oncology product.

items.statement: U.S. FDA accepted Biologics License Application for Biosimilar Ustekinumab for review under 351(k) pathway; settlement and license agreement signed with Janssen Biotech Inc. and Johnson & Johnson for U.S. commercialization no later than Feb
items.quote: We are pleased to share that the U.S. FDA has accepted our Biologics License Application for Biosimilar Ustekinumab for review under the 351(k) pathway and we have signed a settlement and license agreement with Janssen Biotech Inc., and Johnson & Johnson that clears the way to commercialize the product in the U.S., subject to regulatory approval, no later than February 22, 2025.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics signed settlement agreement with Bayer and Regeneron for YESAFILI (biosimilar Aflibercept) introduction in Canadian market no later than July 2025; product already approved by Health Canada
items.quote: Biocon Biologics has also signed a settlement agreement with Bayer and Regeneron that paves the way for the introduction of YESAFILI, our biosimilar Aflibercept into the Canadian market no later than July'25. The product has already been approved by Health Canada.

items.statement: FDA unable to inspect Bengaluru Bevacizumab facility within goal date timeline, issued supplementary CRL with no outstanding scientific issues; documentation submitted
items.quote: the FDA was unable to undertake an inspection of our Bengaluru facility that manufactures our Biosimilar Bevacizumab within the initially proposed goal date timeline and therefore, issued a supplementary CRL. The CRL did not identify any outstanding scientific i ssues and we have submitted all required documentation to the agency

items.statement: Malaysia site completed all corrective and preventative actions (CAPA) per committed timelines; provided comprehensive update to U.S. FDA; anticipating agency inspection of both Bengaluru and Malaysia sites
items.quote: Here, we have completed the implementation of all the corrective and preventative actions (CAPA), as per the committed timelines and have provided the U.S. FDA with a comprehensive update. As a next step, we are now anticipating the agency to visit and to inspect both the Bengaluru and Malaysia sites, which subject to outcome, would pave the way for approval of our biosimilar A spart from the Mala

items.statement: Biocon Generics appointed Vishal Nayyar as Head of Supply Chain Management and Amit Kaptain as Head of Commercial for global API business and Generic Formulations in select emerging markets
items.quote: I am very pleased to announce the appointment of Vishal Nayyar as Head of Supply Chain Management and Amit Kaptain as Head of Commercial for our global API business as well as for Generic Formulations in select emer ging markets

items.statement: Biocon Biologics appointed Dwight Hanshew as new Chief Quality Officer with over 30 years global leadership experience across Operations, Quality and R&D; most recently Head of Quality for Cipla in United States
items.quote: delighted to announce the appointment of Dwight Hanshew as its new Chief Quality Officer this quarter. Dwight brings with him over 30 years of global leadership, experience and expertise across Operations, Quality and R&D. And most recently, he was the Head of Quality for Cipla in the United States.

items.statement: Targets 30-40% revenue growth over FY24 and mid-teens EBITDA margin in FY25
items.quote: So we are looking at something like 30 % to 40% increase on the FY23 -24 sales numbers, but there's going to be a substantial increase on the profitability primarily because we've improved on a lot of parameters which includes manpower utilization, which includes revision of our contractual rates with our customers, which includes a little reduction in the overall raw material prices, giving us th

items.statement: Firm order book of INR110 crore for FY25, execution starting Q1
items.quote: So, we have an order book of about INR110 crores for the current financial year.

items.statement: Current utilization 30-35%, targeting 70-80% in next 2 years with minimal capex except moulds
items.quote: All in all, we are working to improving our capacity utilization, which is at about 30 %-35% overall. And some new clients are being added, as I mentioned, and our target is to have maximum capacity utilization, at least 70% to 80% of it in the next 2 years. And this would not involve much of a capex, except certain moulds that we might have to make specific to the requirement of our customers.

items.statement: New product categories beyond oral care will require capex for packaging lines; toothbrush capacity expansion needs only 5-8% mould cost
items.quote: Yes, that will require some capex. In terms of packaging lines, because it's going to be unique to each one of the products that we get. Some of the brands sell in pouches, some brands sell in bottles, some sell in pumps. So, each one of them have different packaging styles. So, that's probably we'll need to invest in.

items.statement: Expects healthy double-digit EBITDA margin in FY25 driven by price increases, cost reductions, operational efficiencies and volume leverage
items.quote: So considering all this added with the increased sales, I think we should be in a healthy double digit number on the EBITDA margins in the current financial year.

items.statement: Added Reliance (toothbrush, toothpaste, mouthwash), Unilever (Close-up toothpaste), Amway, Nycil (Zydus); CSD/CPC sales up 40%; no customer >25% of revenue
items.quote: We've got some new clients added. Reliance is one of the clients with whom we've started domestic sales to their retail stores and also the GT, the general trade division that they've opened is something that we'll be supplying to subsequen tly because the same products are being approved for the GT sales

items.statement: Exports recovering from 1-2% of sales; shifted payment terms from 180-day credit to documents through bank on fixed tenure; targeting global private label shows
items.quote: Apart from this, we've also renewed our focus back on exports, which during the COVID times had taken a major hit and from almost 25% of our sales to 1 or 2% of our sales, the export sales had dropped, which has started looking up again with a decent profit margin.

items.statement: Average credit period reduced from ~100 days to ~60 days; export credit cut from 180 to 45 days; some domestic from 90 to 60 days; supplier credit extended from 30 to 45 days
items.quote: So, earlier in exports, we were giving about 180 days credit, which is down to 45. There were a lot of our customers, which were at 90 days, we brought them down to 60 days. So, our average credit period is now down to, I would say, from a high of 100 days to about 60 days on an average.

items.statement: 50% contracts have price pass-through, 50% fixed annual; secured price increases by justifying input cost inflation (labour, electricity)
items.quote: 50% I would say are price pass-on contracts and 50% are full year fixed contracts.

items.statement: FY24 revenue mix: 60% toothbrush, 30% toothpaste, 10% talcum/mouthwash/tongue cleaners; toothbrush share up from 57% toothpaste previously
items.quote: So, in current financial year '24, 60% of our revenues are driven from the toothbrush segment, while 30% coming in from the toothpaste segment. Rest of the revenues are from the new segment, which is the talcum powder coupled with mouthwash and tongue cleaners.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions in broader personal care (creams, lotions, soaps, shampoos) using cash and stock; no more mergers
items.quote: We are now looking at acquisitions very actively and we are very confident that in the current financial year, we will be able to do a substantial acquisition with whatever cash that the company holds currently and maybe some stock.

items.statement: Added senior team members and new marketing team; hiring young talent for unconventional sales channels
items.quote: We've also added a few senior team members in our company, which has seen a change in the overall outlook in terms of the deliveries, in terms of capacity utilization, in terms of order book.

items.statement: Oral care market INR15,000 crore dominated by 5 players (85% share); JHS now supplies to 3 of top 5 (Colgate, P&G historically, now Unilever, Reliance)
items.quote: So as you would know that oral care as a category is about INR15,000 crores in India, and it is predominantly dominated by four big companies, which is Colgate number one, Oral-B number two, Dar bar number three, Unilever number four. So four of these companies and fifth Sensodyne, which is GSK now, Haleon, together five of these own about 85% of the market.

items.statement: CSD (canteen stores) sales up 40%; now among top 7 brands sold in CSD
items.quote: There also, the sales have improved. We've increased the sales and profitability specific to that section by about 40%.

items.statement: Past over-dependence on P&G (70% revenue) led to plant stranding; now consciously limiting each customer to <25% of sales
items.quote: We've consciously kept all our customers less than 25% of our sales. None of them wou ld be now more than 25%, like P& G at one point in 2012 -2013 and INR180 crores revenue was close to 70

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20-22% for next 3 years
items.quote: We expect to maintain the momentum of revenue growth of 20% – 22% going forward as well for the next 3 years.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of 12-13%
items.quote: We are confident of maintaining long-term EBITDA margin at 12% to 13% from the operations, which we have guided historically.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to reduce by Rs 5-6 Crores
items.quote: We expect the interest cost to further go down as I said because the arbitration money was only used in the February and March months to repay the banks. So we expect the interest cost to be further reduced by Rs 5 Crores to Rs 6 Crores going forward as well.

items.statement: Interest cost guidance of Rs 25-26 Crores for FY25
items.quote: We expect the interest cost in this year to be almost Rs 25 Crores – Rs 26 Crores.

items.statement: Net unexecuted order book of Rs 3,099 Crores as of April 1, 2024
items.quote: As of April 1, 2024, we have a net unexecuted order book of almost Rs 3,099 Crores, with order inflow for the year being Rs 1,841 Crores amounting to almost 3.02x our FY'24 revenues, thus providing strong visibility to the management.

items.statement: L1 in Rs 700 Crores of new orders expected post elections
items.quote: we are L1 in almost Rs 700 Crores of new orders, which we expect to be finalized post the Code of Conduct of the general GPT Infraprojects Limited M ay 21, 2024 elections being over

items.statement: Long-term book-to-bill ratio target of 3x
items.quote: Going forward, we expect to maintain long-term book-to-bill ratio of almost 3x.

items.statement: Concrete sleeper order book of Rs 222 Crores executable over 1.5 years
items.quote: So the concrete sleeper segment has an outstanding order book of Rs 222 Crores that is to be executed over the next 1.5 years.

items.statement: Concrete sleeper segment peak revenue capacity of Rs 250 Crores
items.quote: At the peak this segment can generate revenues of close to Rs 250 Crores.

items.statement: Ghana factory technical approval received, revenue booking expected from Q2 FY25
items.quote: We expect the company, the subsidiary to start booking revenue in the second quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin threshold of 13% maintained for bidding discipline
items.quote: We have a very strict discipline in terms of maintaining our EBITDA margin. Our EBITDA margin is in the range of 12.5% - 13%, and we will be able to maintain that threshold.

items.statement: Both infrastructure and sleeper segments have comparable EBITDA margins of ~13%
items.quote: It's almost comparable at 13%.

items.statement: Debt reduced to Rs 186 Crores, further reduction expected from strong cash flows
items.quote: In terms of the debt position, you're right, it is at almost Rs 186 Crores. Like I said in my opening remarks, we expect to further reduce the debt from the strong cash flow that the management has.

items.statement: CRISIL credit rating upgraded from BBB+ to A- in February 2024
items.quote: As you are aware, we have already informed the stock exchanges earlier that the external rating agency, CRISIL, has upgraded the external rating -- or credit rating of the company in February 2024 from BBB+ to A-.

items.statement: Contract assets reduced by ~30% despite revenue growth
items.quote: The management has been able to reduce the contract assets by almost 30% despite the increase in volume of business, thus evidencing more optimized balance sheet, which is reflecting in the return ratios.

items.statement: Target working capital days in double digits
items.quote: We have been able to keep the working capital days also closer to double digits, which will be the long-term target as well.

items.statement: Trade payables decreased by Rs 10 Crores vs Rs 61 Crores increase last year
items.quote: If you see last year, as a number, trade payables on a stand-alone basis increased by Rs 61 Crores. This year, it has decreased by almost Rs 10 Crores. So that Rs 70 Crores delta is coming from the trade payable number only.

items.statement: Target payable days of ~2 months for better supplier pricing
items.quote: So the idea is to maintain a reasonable payable day of almost 2 months so that we get better pricing from the suppliers as well as better -- they also want to work with us.

items.statement: Bonus issue 1:1 and total dividend of Rs 3 per share (30%) for FY24
items.quote: The Board has recommended has already announced a bonus issue of equity shares in the proportion of 1:1 by capitalizing the reserves of the company. items.statement: International revenue ~2% (Rs 20 Crores) in FY24, targeting 7-8% in FY25
items.quote: It's only 2%-odd percent currently, about Rs 20-odd Crores last year. We expect this year to be much stronger to be almost 7% – 8%.

items.statement: No EPC business outside India, only product exports
items.quote: Yes, we don't -- no, we don't do EPC outside the country.

items.statement: Competition not affecting order inflow; Rs 1,840 Crores new orders in FY24
items.quote: Given the increase in the volume of business and the opportunities available even if more people do enter the field, there is no challenge in terms of new contracts that can be procured. So, that is not affecting our inflow of orders. Like I said, we are at an all-time high in terms of new orders that we procured last year of Rs 1,840 Crores.

items.statement: Key risk is government infrastructure focus deviation
items.quote: Obviously, this is subject to government having a focus on the infrastructure sector which we don't think that the focus will be different. So that is one of the major risks that always will be there. If the government's focus on infrastructure deviates, then obviously the pipeline will shrink.

items.statement: Cash flow to EBITDA conversion at 103%
items.quote: Our cash flow from operations to EBITDA conversion continues to be strong and stands at an industry-leading 103% conversion.

items.statement: ROE and ROCE north of 20%
items.quote: This has led to both ROE and ROCE being north of 20% for the year, and we expect to maintain the same going forward as well.

items.statement: Currently bidding for projects up to Rs 900-1000 Crores, largest won Rs 740 Crores
items.quote: So we are already bidding for projects upto Rs 900 Crores – Rs 1000 Crores. And for the largest contract that we got last year was Rs 740 Crores from NHAI.

items.statement: Insurance surety bonds used as alternative to bank BGs for bidding
items.quote: In terms of bidding opportunities, we have the flexibility of also using these insurance surety bonds as well. The government has allowed most of the government departments nowadays except these surety bonds, like NHAI, MORTH, etc.

items.statement: Management expects 12-15% volume growth for FY25
items.quote: And at the end of the -- on a full year basis, yes, definitely, you can expect around 12% to 15% volume growth.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is around INR300 crores, predominantly for vehicles
items.quote: Yes, since to grow at around again, 12% to 15% growth in tonnage, definitely we n eed to have a capex in the range of around INR300 crores

items.statement: Branch addition target for FY25 is around 100-plus branches, with most in Q1
items.quote: Yes. More branches is in Q1 and in subsequent period, there will be lesser additions. And on a full year basis, definitely it will be in the range of around 100-plus branches.

items.statement: South zone tonnage grew only 2% in FY24 due to poor monsoon; north 15%, east 20%, northeast 25%
items.quote: On an origination basis, actually, south zone contributed around -- growth is around 2% and the north is around 15% and east is around 20%, nort heast is around 25% and the rest is around 10

items.statement: Textile segment grew 6% in FY24, expected 14-15% in FY25; agro grew 4-5%, expected double digits in FY25
items.quote: we are expecting that the textile which was impacted in the last year, again, the growth in textile we are expecting at least around 14% to 15% in the current year. That's one. So since most of the reports are giving positive outlook on the monsoon in the current year, we are expecting that defin

items.quote: The key changes in the operational costs, which are reasons to decrease in EBITDA margins are: the major impact i s on account of increase in employee cost. The employee cost as a percentage to the total revenue increased by around from 15.4% to 16.6

items.quote: The EBITDA margin has increased from 13% to 14% and the improvements in EBITDA margin is on account of the decrease in fuel costs, which is a major cost in our operations.

items.statement: Management targets return to 16-17% EBITDA margin (post Ind AS) if tonnage grows 12-15%
items.quote: Even if the tonnage growth, say, at least around 12%, 15%, then again, our EBITDA margin is around 16%, 17%.

items.statement: Freight rates linked to fuel rates; no rate hike taken as fuel rates stable; fuel cost benefit retained, not passed to customers
items.quote: No, basically, the thought process is very clear because the freight rates are directly linked with the fuel rates. So it all depends on the movement in the fuel rates. And if a substantial increase in the fuel rate, then definitely, we look forward to increase the freight rates along with to take care of increase in other expenses.

items.statement: Customer base grew from 8 lakh to 9 lakh in FY24 due to shift from unorganized to organized transport and GST compliance
items.quote: Further, our customer base has increased from 8 lakh customers at the beginning of the financial year to 9 lakh customers by end of the year due to shift from dependency on the unorga nized transport service providers to organized transport service providers on account of better service level and also increase in GST compliances

items.statement: Own vehicle capacity reached 86,405 tons as of March 31, 2024; added 83 branches in FY24, 184 in FY23
items.quote: With this, our own vehicle capacity has reached to around 86,405 tons capacity as at 31st March 2024.

items.quote: So that's the reason, instead of calculating based on the number of trailers, I can say that at least around in the near future, we may reach around 10% of overall carrying capacity what we are having, it will be through trailers.

items.statement: Net debt rose from INR167 crores to INR262 crores YoY; fell sequentially from INR271 crores to INR262 crores; FY25 debt not expected to rise above current level due to strong cash flows (INR350-400 crores free cash flow)
items.quote: See, even with capital expenditure of INR300 crores, our debt level will not increase from the current level. The reason is we are having good cash flows. items.statement: Employee count up 1,132 YoY due to branch expansion and more drivers for own vehicles; employee cost rose from INR108 crores to INR128 crores
items.quote: The number of employees also increased by around 1,132 numbers as compared to the last year and mainly in -- on account of expansion in branch network and also due to increase in number of drivers because the number of own vehicles are increased.

items.statement: Competition increasing from express players offering non-time-sensitive rates and local operators; VRL responding with aggressive branch expansion in untapped markets
items.quote: And aggressively in the current year, actually, most of the branches we are planning to open in quarter 1 only because we identified those places and those are very potential areas where actually we can enhance our business in those locations.

items.statement: Realization per ton up 1% YoY to INR6,724 due to route mix change; freight rates unchanged as fuel rates stable
items.quote: During the quarter, there was an increase in total realization per ton by around 1% from INR6,650 to INR6,724. The increase is mainly on account of change in route mix in our overall operations.

items.statement: Fuel procurement cost fell from INR89 to INR87 per liter YoY; bulk purchase share rose from 28% to 31%
items.quote: The reduction in fuel cost is mainly on account of decrease in average fuel procurement cost from INR89 it was there in Q4 FY '23 now it has been reduced to INR87 in Q4 of FY '24. And also the bulk purchase of the fuel from the refineries a t a discounted price is increased from 28% to 31% in the current quarter

items.statement: April-May operations impacted by driver and labor shortage due to general elections; issue resolving as elections complete
items.quote: However, in quarter 1 of the current year, in April and May period, we faced some performance impact because of some disturbances in our operations on account of short in attendance by the drivers and loading and unloading labors, especially in the metro cities like Chennai, Bangalore, Pune, Ahmedabad, et cetera.

items.statement: Operating under 5% GST reverse charge mechanism; evaluated 12% forward charge but found 5% reverse charge more beneficial after customer survey and government consultation
items.quote: We examined this option. In fact, we are closely working with the government ministry also. And the thing here that we analyze, we made a survey of our customers and everything. And based on that outcome, what rate we are already practicing, at 5% on a reverse charge, that is beneficial to us compared to the 12%.

items.statement: Focusing on trailer additions (25-30 ton capacity) to reduce hub waiting time, improve driver utilization and turnaround; planning larger trailers for long routes like Delhi-Bangalore
items.quote: As mentioned in the presentation, we are concentrating more on addition of trailers in our fleet that will result into increase in turnaround time of the vehicles and the increase in the utilization of drivers, etcetera.

items.statement: Free cash flow estimated at INR350-400 crores annually, supporting capex without increasing debt
items.quote: Since we are having the cash flows of almost close to around INR350 crores to INR400 crores as our free cash flows, so that will support to add this capex.

items.statement: Capex plan for next two years is roughly Rs 80-100 crore, focused on manufacturing capability improvement and product development/innovation.
items.quote: Roughly, we are looking about 80 to 100 crores. This will be largely towards manufacturing capability improvement, also behind product development and product innovation.

items.statement: ECD EBIT margin improved from 12.7% in Q1 FY24 to 17.2% in Q4 FY24 (excluding EPR impact of Rs 14.1 crore).
items.quote: ECD EBIT margins have consistently increased during the year from 12.7% in Q1 FY24 to 17.2% in Q4. Again, the Q4 number excludes the EPR impact because obviously that is the entire impact of EPR has been taken in one quarter.

items.statement: Lighting EBIT margin is at 11.1% excluding EPR impact.
items.quote: Lighting EBIT even as we are coming back to a stable lighting business in the face of declining prices in the market , has remained very strong. So, lighting EBIT margin is at 11.1% , again, excluding the EPR impact.

items.statement: Fans gross margins improved from about 23% in Q1 to about 25% in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: this is of course, also enabled us to improve our gross margins in fans and they have gone up order of magnitude from about 23% to about 25% this quarter - 23% in Q1 to about 25% in this quarter.

items.statement: Butterfly long-term target is double-digit EBIT margin; near-term focus is to restore growth and return to category EBIT margins of 1-2 years ago.
items.quote: In the long run we should look at a double digit margin for this business, Renu, but in the near term we want to get this back on growth, get into a category EBIT margin that the business used to operate say 1-2 years back and then expand from there.

items.statement: Demand outlook for summer is reasonably good and robust, despite some recent rains.

items.quote: During the quarter, we secured fresh orders of 87 crores making our total empanelment for the year of about 122 crores. Needless to say, we have therefore a strong pipeline going forward.

items.statement: Butterfly revenue was Rs 166 crore in Q4 with EBITDA loss of Rs 20 crore, impacted by transition and one-offs.
items.quote: This quarter the revenue of Butterfly came in at 166 crores. The EBITDA was -20 crores and you can tell that the transition is having an impact , and one off s are having an impact on the EBITDA there.

items.statement: Premium saliency improved YoY by 300 bps overall; ceiling fans +380 bps, lighting +410 bps in large domestic appliances; premium fans mix improved from 1 in 5 to >1 in 4.
items.quote: We witnessed an improvement in premium saliency YoY of 3 percentage points, that is 300 basis points . In ceiling fans, 380 basis points in lighting, and 410 basis points in large domestic appliances .To put our premiumization journey in fans in perspective, a year ago we were selling one out of five premium fans. Now, we are probably selling more than one out of every four fans.

items.statement: Fans volume grew strong double-digit in Q4 and full year FY24; premium fans growing at ~2x overall category growth; non-ceiling fans (TPW, exhaust, DOMEX) also strong double-digit growth.
items.quote: we do see from a category perspective, premium fans are growing at almost a 2x of the overall category growth for fans has been growing in. In terms of mass premium or the value segment is concerned, if I look at our overall fans performance on the market share also, it's reflecting that we are moving in the right direction. Equally important to look at non-ceiling as a category. So today we see t

items.statement: Took measured price increases in fans (Sept, Nov, Feb, and another upcoming), pumps, LDA and SDA; cost savings via Unnati program contributing to margin improvement.
items.quote: We are continuing to take both measured price increases sometimes or even frequently, not the approach that the rest of the industry is taking, but we are taking them and we are working on costs. So, yes, I remain quite positive about the way margins will evolve going forward.

items.statement: A&P spend increased 49% YoY to Rs 217 crore (3.14% of revenue vs 2.5% last year); R&D spend Rs 71 crore with 85 design registrations, 17 patent applications, 10 patents granted.
