items.statement: Apollo standalone mix 55% housing/plumbing, 45% agri; Kisan 30% building material, 70% agri
items.quote: So for Apollo Pipes, I have told earlier as well, 55% is non -agri, 45% is agri. And for Kisan, it will be 30% building materials and 70% agri.

items.statement: Target Apollo 70% building material, 30% agri; Kisan 45% non-agri, 55% agri in 3 years
items.quote: Apollo on stand -alone basis will be 70% building material and 30% agri in next three years when we achieve this INR3,000 crores top line.

items.statement: Conscious decision to avoid low-margin government projects to protect working capital and ROC
items.quote: we don't want to deploy too much capital for the government-based projects, right? And in their low margin, so we just took a back seat there, okay?

items.statement: Balance sheet remains debt-free; capex funded via equity infusion and operating cash flow
items.quote: I am glad to share that our balance sheet remains debt-free despite such commitments. Our finance and sales team have worked wonders to improve working capital cycle to 23 days.

items.statement: Working capital target for Kisan: NWC less than 60 days by FY26
items.quote: Yes, so look going forward, by FY'26 and I think we should be -- the working -- NWC should be less than 60 days.

items.statement: Group EBITDA target of INR400 crores in 3-4 years from INR100 crores in FY24
items.quote: So if you see, I have -- I mean as a management we have formulated th e strategy to take this EBITDA from INR100 crores to INR400 crores at a group level

items.statement: Guiding for 22% to 24% revenue growth in current financial year
items.quote: The gui dance for the current financial year is to grow at the same pace as last year. So again, we are guiding for revenue increase of around 22% to 24% in the current financial year

items.statement: Guiding for EBITDA margin improvement of 100 to 150 bps in current financial year
items.quote: And also as we see more operative leveraging or leverage coming our way, we are also guiding for a better EBITDA margin in the coming financial year, improving by around 100 to 150 bps.

items.statement: Guiding for 50% growth in renal business this year
items.quote: And this year, definitely, we are guiding for almost 50% increase in renal business.

items.statement: Guiding for $15 million U.S. revenue over next 3 years
items.quote: Our U.S. business, of course, I've spoken about it a little bit. So we co ntinue to guide for $15 million of revenue over the next 3 years or so

items.statement: Guiding for 22% to 25% export growth in current financial year
items.quote: Export business continues to be -- has a good momentum. We're planning at 22% to 25% overall growth in exports.

items.statement: Targeting 25% domestic business growth this year versus 18% last year
items.quote: We are very confident of now achieving a better growth in domestic business from last year's 18% to around close to 25% this year.

items.statement: Capex of INR250+ crores in FY24; similar significant amount planned for current year
items.quote: Capex, we have done last year of around INR250-plus crores. And because of that, those more 4 new plants are operational with increased capacity in each segment. So -- and we'll continue to invest a similar significant amount in the current financial year also to augment more capacity in newer transformative businesses.

items.statement: Board approved fund raise of INR800 crores in March 2024 for accelerated expansion and acquisitions
items.quote: To fast track this, the company is looking at new fund raise of around INR800 crores, which was already approved by our Board of Directors in March 2024. And these funds will be basically utilized for rapid expansion of Cardio and Critical Care business and also setting up 3 new facilities.

items.statement: Firm order book enabled accurate forecasting and guidance
items.quote: And when we look at now the full year financial results and then in comparison from FY '23-FY '24, the stand-alone growth is around 22.5%, and the consolidated growth is around 23.36%. So again, the guidance was between 22% and 24%. So, we have -- in the guidance, what we had projected in the beginning of the year and that's very important that we have firm business plan, we have firm order book.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 operating EBITDA margin close to 27%, at higher end of 25-27% guidance
items.quote: And we have now reached the higher side of the guidance we have given. So the guidance was for between 25% and 27%. So operating EBITDA was close to around 27% quarter 4 of the last financial year.

items.statement: Standalone operating EBITDA margin close to 26%+ for FY24
items.quote: Also, the total EBITDA also increased from INR300 crores to INR407 crores on a stand-alone basis, including operating EBITDA, which was cl ose to around 26-plus percent for the stand- alone

items.statement: Focus shifting to transformative businesses: Cardiology, Oncology, Renal Care, Critical Care
items.quote: There will be more focus on the transforma tive businesses like Cardiology, Oncology, Re nal Care and Critical Care because these are basically transformative businesses where these are through non- communicable

items.statement: Renal business grew 35% in Q4 FY24 due to regulatory changes; expect 50% growth in FY25
items.quote: And this year, definitely, we are guiding for almost 50% increase in renal business. And also, I think in coming years, we will see a similar growth coming from renal side of our business.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation remains choppy; mitigating supply chain and manufacturing risks
items.quote: Of course, the geopolitical situation continues to be very choppy. But I think with the ki nd of new product additions we have done, as we've ventured into more Critical Care products which have higher margin compared to our current conventional products, I think that will also help us to improve our margin

items.statement: Italian subsidiary grew 40% to 16-17% EBITDA; expect 30-35% growth this year and revenue doubling in 3 years
items.quote: subsidiary has done well, has grown by over 40% in the past year. So from let's say, we have done almost from a negative margin a few years ago to almost 16%, 17% EBITDA last year. So the company continues to now be self- sufficient and in terms of its own cash requirements and is again poised to go by another 30% to 35% this year

items.statement: Plan to sell 500+ dialysis machines in FY25 vs 200 in FY24; first BIS certification for dialysis machine in India
items.quote: Last year, we sold close to around 200 machines, dialysis machines. This year, we plan to sell over 500 dialysis machines. Also, we are the first company to receive a BIS certification for the dialysis machine.

items.statement: Expect slippages of INR700-800 crores for FY25 and year-end net NPA of 1-1.25%
items.quote: We expect the similar reduction in the slippage maybe about INR700 crores to INR800 crores slippage we could be having for the current financial year. Going by this trend, our current expectations on our closing year net NPA -- towards the end of the current year, we should be having between maybe around 1 to 1.25 % plus or minus.

items.statement: NIM expected to remain stable at current level with 5-10 bps variation
items.quote: Our net interest margin continued to be stable and on current level, maybe at the best 5 to 10 basis points this way or that way.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio for FY25 expected between 47% and 51%
items.quote: So the financial '24-25 we should be finishing somewhere in between the final quarter figure of 51% and the full year figure of 47 %.

items.statement: ROA to improve from current 1.52% despite higher cost-to-income ratio
items.quote: Our endeavour is to improve the annual ROA. Our best efforts are to ensure and see that the improvement in the ROA is seen as we progress even though we have higher level of cost-to-income ratio compared at about 50 %, 51 % compared to whatever we had last year.

items.statement: Technology capex and opex around INR200 crores annually, ~20% of PAT
items.quote: Capital investment and revenue investment close to INR200 crores expenditure every year happens at an average for the last 2 years, 3 years on the technology thing which works out to about 20 % of your PAT.

items.statement: Digital lending for MSME up to INR7.5 crores by mid-June; secured retail (housing, LAP, micro LAP) digital launch by end of Q1
items.quote: The digital lending implementation for MSME is reaching the last leg and should be through before the mid-June. Along with the MSME, digital lending model is being expanded to secured retail lending such as housing, LAP, micro LAPl. Currently, we are doing that, and they should be completed before the end of Q1.

items.statement: New retail secured products (home loans, LAP, micro LAP) to start booking from Q2 FY25 (September)
items.quote: So we will start our booking from Q2. Our policies are getting up, and we are also getting our systems in place. We have a couple of more things to cover in terms of legal and technical processes, and we wanted to do it digital for LAP and home loans so that we go back to the best at in the market. So eventually, we are looking at end of Q2 for launching.

items.statement: Plan to open 50-75 branches in FY25
items.quote: We are planning to open about 50 to 75 branches during the current financial year.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 saw substantial sequential credit growth (6% Q-o-Q); Q1 FY25 expected better than previous years but still lull
items.quote: If you look into sequentially in Q1, Q2, Q3 the growth that has happened in Q4 is substantially more than previous quarters which given us sufficient confidence to take things forward. Q1 probably will be having a lull as in the past, but this year we hope it would not be as lull as we had it in the earlier years.

items.statement: Treasury income headwinds due to interest rate environment and regulatory changes on HTM treatment
items.quote: Now there is a headwind in the treasury income because of the interest rate at the moment and also changes in the regulatory policies on treating the HTM, how you vouch the treatment of treasury itself has changed, that will have some amount of headwind.

items.statement: Long-term NIM average 3.4-3.7%; current 3.65% is at long-term average
items.quote: See if you had a chance to look into our last 50 quarters or so, at least, for about 35 quarters to 40 quarters it used to settle between 3.4% and 3.7%. It was above 4 % for a handful of -- maybe about 8 quarters to 10 quarters or so, but our long-term average had been between 3.4% and 3.7% only.

items.statement: KCC loan rundown complete; incremental growth now visible on daily basis
items.quote: Yes, it has come down to the bottom. And the incremental growth rates started we have started seeing in a small way on a daily basis now.

items.statement: LCR at 200%+; divergent practices across banks on calculation
items.quote: See, we are at about 200 % plus and will be published shortly in that Pillar 3 disclosures.

items.statement: Insurance income doubled to INR55 crores in FY24; expect significant growth in FY25
items.quote: As we have on boarded 6 insurance companies covering life, general and nonlife insurance companies during the financial year 2023, our insurance income contribution has also doubled and stood at INR55 crores in the financial year '24, compared to about INR27 crores in the financial year '23. We expect a significant growth in the current financial year also.

items.statement: MSME 45-day payment rule caused reduction in working capital utilization; now stabilized
items.quote: Definitely, the thing is we could see in the mixed way, the smaller entities returned the money and that utilization was coming down. Under the larger industries their utilization improved because they had to make payment to the smaller entities. I think, largely, we settled and on a holistic basis, we had a reduction of utilization because of this.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 180 billion via FPO, Rs. 14.4 billion via ATC OCD conversion, and Rs. 20.75 billion via promoter preferential issue; total equity raised ~Rs. 215 billion in last 3 months.
items.quote: Considering all above, we have successfully raised equity of ~Rs. 215 billion during last 3 months.

items.statement: In discussions with banks to raise Rs. 250 billion debt and Rs. 100 billion non-fund based facilities.
items.quote: Additionally, we are in discussio ns with consortium of banks to raise debt of Rs. 250 billion and additional non-fund based facilities of Rs. 100 billion

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs. 500-550 billion over next 3 years, funded by equity and debt raise.
items.quote: This Equity funding and proposed bank facilities are to be utilised p rimarily towards capex over next 3 years which is expected to be in range of Rs. 500 to 550 billion

items.statement: Capex spend was Rs. 5.5 billion in Q4 FY24 and Rs. 18.5 billion for FY24.
items.quote: Capex spend for the quarter stood at Rs. 5.5 billion, and capex for the year at Rs. 18.5 billion.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS EBITDA margin improved to 20.6% in Q4 FY24; quarterly EBITDA Rs. 21.8 billion, highest post-merger.
items.quote: Quarterly EBITDA excluding IndAS116 im pact, improved by 5.4% on YoY basis to Rs. 21.8 billion recording the highest EBITDA post merger and EBITDA margin has improved to 20.6

items.statement: Tariff rationalization on higher usage plans and pay-more-for-using-more pricing structure critical for reasonable returns.
items.quote: That said, tariff rationalization on the higher usage plans and moving to a pricing structure of paying more for using more remains critical to ensure that the operators make reasonable returns on their large network and spectrum investments.

items.statement: 4G subscriber base grew for 11th successive quarter to 126.3 million; overall subscriber base 212.6 million.
items.quote: On operations front, the 4G subscriber base has continued to grow for the eleventh successive quarter and stood at 126.3 million as on March 31, 2024 vs 122.6 million as on March 31, 2023.

items.statement: ARPU grew for 11th consecutive quarter to Rs. 146 in Q4 FY24; 2-year ARPU CAGR 8.4%, highest in industry.
items.quote: We have seen ARPU growth for eleven consecutive quarters now. Q4FY24 ARPU stands at Rs. 146 compared to Rs. 145 in Q3FY2 4 despite one day less during the

items.statement: 5G rollout to start in ~6 months, focusing on key cities with high 5G device concentration; 5G investment iterative based on market evolution.
items.quote: On the 5G front, we should be able to start rolling out 5G on a from about 6 months from now. 5G market as you see has been evolving, we will have to see as to how the market is evolving.

items.statement: 3G shutdown completed in 6 circles (Kerala added); refarming 3G spectrum to 4G continues in other circles.
items.quote: We continue to work towards refarming the 3G spectrum towards 4G considering the overall ecosystem and have shut down 3G completely in 6 circles with Kerala getting added to the list of 5 other circles where it was done earlier.

items.statement: AGR curative petition seeks ~Rs. 6,000 crore base correction implying ~Rs. 24,000 crore total correction as of Oct 2019 plus interest; also seeks penalty waiver.
items.quote: We have asked for corrections on the base amount which is about 6,000 crores roughly. Now as you know as far as the AGRs demand is concerned it had built up of interest, penalty and interest on penalty.

items.statement: Post-moratorium government liabilities in FY26-FY27 expected to be addressed via conversion per reforms package; non-convertible portion from internal accruals.
items.quote: In FY26 and FY27, we will probably be looking at the conversion of the installments which are convertible as per the reforms package. That is what we are currently looking at.

items.statement: Capacity to double from March 2024 to March 2026; largest part of capex guidance allocated to 5G, 4G coverage skewed over capacity.
items.quote: As given in our investor presentation, as we go from March '24 to March '26, the capacity increases about 2X.

items.statement: Deferred payment obligations to Government at Rs. 2,034.3 billion as of March 31, 2024 (spectrum Rs. 1,331.1 billion, AGR Rs. 703.2 billion).
items.quote: The deferred payment obligations to the Government were at Rs. 2,034.3 billion as of March 31, 2024 as compared to Rs. 1,888.6 billion as of March 31,2023.

items.statement: Bank debt reduced by Rs. 70.9 billion YoY to Rs. 40.4 billion; cash balance Rs. 1.7 billion.
items.quote: The total debt from banks and financial institutions stood at Rs. 40.4 billion and Optionally Convertible Debentures at Rs. 1.6 billion as of March 31, 2024. The debt from banks and financial institutions reduced by Rs. 70.9 billion during the last one year.

items.statement: Revenue grew 0.5% QoQ to Rs. 106.1 billion in Q4 FY24; FY24 revenue Rs. 426.5 billion, Pre-IndAS EBITDA Rs. 84 billion.
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter stood at Rs. 106.1 billion and the QoQ average daily revenue grew by 0.5%.

items.statement: Revised full-year EBITDA margin guidance to 24%-28% for FY25 due to investments in sales and delivery capabilities
items.quote: These investments will result in a n impact of about 400 bps to EBITDA. So , we are revising the range for full year EBITDA to 24% to 28%.

items.statement: Aspiration for double-digit revenue growth in FY25
items.quote: Absolutely, aspiration. Why wouldn't we aspire for double-digit. Our aspirations are higher, so.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 expected to be lowest margin quarter due to wage hikes and full impact of Q4 investments
items.quote: So, you would expect that Q1 will be the quarter of the lowest margin, predominantly because of wage hikes and the full impact of the investments that we have made in Q4 that will hit Q1, and any additional investment that we might do.

items.statement: Subcontracting costs expected to remain in 2%-2.5% range depending on project volumes
items.quote: So sub-contracting cost should remain in the same range , between 2 -2.5 specifically in every quarter depends on what kind of search volume that we get, what kind of projects we get that we have to ramp up in a very short period of time.

items.statement: Digital business soft in Q4 due to slow 2024 budget allocations; expect some momentum pickup in Q1 but environment remains cautious
items.quote: It was a soft quarter for Digital with clients starting slowly with their 2024 budget allocations and renewals. We expect momentum to make up a little bit in Q1, but overall environment continues to be cautious for the digital business.

items.statement: Strong demand in Financial Markets for compliance offerings and client life cycle management; increased transaction volumes
items.quote: We saw strong demand around our compliance offerings, client life cycle management f rom several clients. We also saw an increase in transaction volumes.

items.statement: New deal ACV for FY24 was USD 91 million, up 10% from FY23; pipeline healthy across all three businesses entering FY25
items.quote: New deal ACV for the year was USD 91 million, up 10% from FY '23, which was USD 82 million. Our pipeline is healthy across all 3 businesses as we get into FY '24/'25.

items.statement: Revenue concentration in volatile industries (retail, financial markets) but balanced portfolio helps manage risk; pricing pressure expected when gaining market share
items.quote: As you know that there is a revenue concentration across volatile industry because the re tail, financial markets have higher volatility than some of the evergreen industries. But our portfolio and balanced portfolio allows us to manage their risk. And obviously, we want to gain market share. So, there will be some pricing pressure on the deals.

items.statement: Announced buyback of INR 385 crores and dividend of INR 1 per share, subject to shareholder approvals
items.quote: We have about INR 1100 crores of cash on our books and in line with the usual practice of returning excess cash to shareholders, we have announced a buyback of INR 385 crores and a dividend of INR 1, subject to shareholder approvals.

items.statement: M&A strategy continues focusing on complementary capabilities and capability access; dedicated person handling outbound and inbound targets
items.quote: On the M&A, yes, that continues to be our strategy. We would be looking at areas where we bring in complementary and that also helps us on our capability access. So that's what we will continue, and we have a dedicated person who is looking at outbound as well as inbound M&A targets.

items.statement: Expect absolute EBITDA and EPS growth in FY25 despite margin guidance range
items.quote: Yes, that's correct. See, the split between what we are investing in sales, capability, infrastructure and other things. I think it's difficult to give a line by line which I've been saying. You asked that will report the increase of the bottom-line profit despite the margin guidance we have given. And I said, yes, it's a real time business.

items.statement: Sales investments typically take 6-9 months to yield results; H2 FY25 expected to see results from current investments
items.quote: So, I think typically, we see in sales that there is a 6 to 9 months of lag from the investments made. So, you are right, H2 should start seeing results.

items.statement: Management targets consolidated EBITDA margin of 10% to 10.5%
items.quote: We are evaluating pricing actions in some products, which combined with some further initiatives should aid us in bringing EBITDA margins back to the range of 10% to 10.5% that we have indicated earlier.

items.statement: Capex guidance unchanged at approximately INR 100 crores for FY25
items.quote: Capex, there's no change in the guidance, whatever we said last time. We probably see about INR100 crores of capex in the coming year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 310 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Gross margins continue to improve. In this quarter, we have reported an improvement of 310 basis points Y-o-Y and 40 basis points Q-on-Q.

items.statement: Pricing actions initiated in April for fans and pumps; further action planned in May
items.quote: Maybe about 2% has flown through in maybe fan. And maybe in May, we expect in pump.

items.statement: Commodity inflation impact estimated at 1-2% margin hit; copper up, aluminium stable
items.quote: But definitely, I think, as of now, maybe a 1% or 2% impact is there. But having said that, we have already taken some pricing increases in categories like fan and pumps because of this.

items.statement: Strong summer demand in South and East drove Q4 and April growth; non-summer categories flat
items.quote: The fourth quarter witnessed a good start to the summer season with revival in demand.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing at 65%, targeting ~75% in next 12-18 months as new battery and kitchen factories scale
items.quote: On the current manufacturing status, in-house is about 65%. With all the new factories that are coming online, we probably expect it to go to about 75-odd-percent in the next 18 months or so.

items.statement: Battery and kitchen appliance factories commenced commercial production; benefits expected in FY25
items.quote: The battery and kitchen appliances factories, which recently commenced commercial production are expected to deliver benefits during the coming year.

items.statement: Sunflame revenue grew 28.3% YoY in Q4; integration design complete, execution over 12-15 months
items.quote: Sunflame also delivered robust growth in top line of 28.3% on a Y-o-Y basis in Q4 leveraging on our various strategic initiatives implemented over the last year.

items.statement: Electronics margin impacted by product mix (AC stabilizers vs refrigerator stabilizers) and EPR charge of INR 70 lakhs on batteries
items.quote: Yes, Achal. It's not major. It's only about INR70 lakhs for battery. So that's not a big factor. The major factor is the product mix, which Mithun spoke about.

items.statement: Non-summer categories (wires, switches, pumps) showing no significant demand change; wires uptick due to copper price rise
items.quote: So far, we are not seeing much of a change in demand for non-summer categories. It's probably a situation as usual as it was in the earlier quarter.

items.statement: Consumer Durables EBITDA margin ~3% in Q4 (EBIT ~1.5%), target pre-COVID levels of 6-7% over 2-3 years
items.quote: I think we are at about 1.5-odd-percent in Q4 as far as EBIT in Consumer Durables margin is concerned. Sudarshan Kasturi: EBITDA was 3%.

items.statement: Electronics margin expected to stabilize around current 13-14% range as battery cost competitiveness improves
items.quote: Mithun K Chittilappilly: Yes. Correct.

items.statement: Distribution reach now ~100,000 outlets (up from ~50,000 estimated); 3,500 direct partners
items.quote: So we have now in the last 1 year have completed scan of the number of outlets we are present in, and I think it's now touching almost 1 lakh as we speak.

items.statement: Switches and switchgear business to grow faster than company average; Simon manufacturing insourced
items.quote: I think these businesses will obviously grow faster than the company growth rate.

items.statement: Gegadyne battery technology investment; meaningful revenue expected in 24-30 months
items.quote: I think maybe it's at least another 24 to 30 months away before we can be able to derive meaningful revenue out of the technology.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 10%-15%
items.quote: this FY25, is guided for 10% -15%

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain in 13%-15% range
items.quote: the entire range from 13%-15% is the standard industry range where we continue to be a part of. And this will continue to be the same within this particular span of EBITDA margins that we are discussing

items.statement: CapEx planned in FY25 for capacity expansion to benefit FY26
items.quote: we plan to do cert ain amount of CapEx, also for the subsequent financial year, that is the next financial year where we will start building up on certain capacities for certain products within this financial year so that we can get benefits out of it in the next financial year

items.statement: Dividend of 25% announced; no immediate equity raise planned
items.quote: we have already announced a dividend of 25% in the last board meeting last week for the shareholders

items.statement: EV battery and semiconductor products under development; commercialization expected by end of FY25
items.quote: we are expecting it to happen sometime towards the end of this financial year

items.statement: 50% of kaolin raw material sourced from captive mines; balance procured externally
items.quote: we are currently using about 50% of our mining material in -house and 50% we are procuring from outside

items.statement: No immediate plans for equity raise; CapEx to be funded from internal accruals
items.quote: we will not need to borrow, but through our internal accruals only, we will be doing the CapEx in the next couple of years

items.statement: FY25 footfall growth expected at max 5% for existing parks; ARPU growth 10-12%
items.quote: But having said that, I think at a company level we are not expecting more than 5% footfall growth for FY'25. But the footfall growth and ARPU growth will be about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Odisha park targeting 4 lakh footfalls at ARPU Rs 800-1,000 in first year
items.quote: We are expecting about 4 lakh visitors at an ARPU of roughly Rs.800-1,000. So that's the way we are looking at it. This is our conservative estimate.

items.statement: Existing parks ARPU growth ~10% in FY25; marginal footfall growth
items.quote: We are expecting an ARPU growth in our existing parks of around double digits, 10% this year because we've had huge ARPU growth in the last two years.

items.statement: Odisha park EBITDA positive from year 1; PAT positive from year 2-3
items.quote: We are expecting it will be EBITDA positive from first year itself, and at the PAT level, it should be positive from year two or three.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin may shrink 3-4 percentage points due to Bhubaneswar park
items.quote: In the next FY , Bhubaneswar Park into our k itty, there could be some little shrinkage in the margin percentage of about some three to four percentage.

items.statement: Chennai park revised budget Rs 515 crore including land; Rs 194 crore committed/paid by Mar 2024
items.quote: In Chennai Park, we had a revised budget expense of somewhere close to 515 crore s and including the orders what we committed, we have about 194 crores has been committed or paid till 31st of March 2024.

items.statement: Odisha park budget ~Rs 190 crore; nearly complete
items.quote: And then in Odisha Park, we had a budget of about 189 crores and we are at the last leg of completing it. So probably , we'll be finishing it up for maybe around 190 crores.

items.statement: Maintenance capex ~10% of park top line annually for new rides
items.quote: We typically spend 10% of our top line from a particular park as we earmark with and keep it for adding new rides to the park.

items.statement: IT/digital transformation investment ~Rs 4-5 crore in next year
items.quote: In fact, we have a new IT head has joined and so in the next one year, we will be investing I think about 4-5 crores in new tech for our parks.

items.statement: Odisha park soft launch 24 May 2024; full opening next week
items.quote: We are actually soft launching from 24th onwards. I'm taking this call from Bhubaneswar. We just finished the press launch of the park. Tomorrow and day after we having a preview meet for some well-wishers and influencers and all that. And then the next week the park is opening.

items.statement: Chennai park commissioning likely Q3 FY26; targeting late Q2 if no rain delays
items.quote: We will be commissioning most likely in the third quarter. We are trying to finish in second quarter because we would like to be ready before the third quarter. There could be some delays because of unseasonal rains plays havoc in Chennai sometime.

items.statement: Plan to open ~1 new park per year; 5 more locations targeted by FY30
items.quote: We are looking at another five more locations in addition to what we already have. One or two of them will get closed and before the end of this financial year and the rest we will announce as and when they are ready.

items.statement: Bangalore & Kochi parks at capacity in peak season; headroom in Q2/Q4
items.quote: There is a limit, for example, on a summer season, our parks are already running pretty full. So it's hard for us to justify higher footfalls. But there are like for example Q2 and Q4, we do feel that there is some more headroom for us to grow.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 footfall hit by exam prepone & elections (Kochi group -37%); heat wave impacted Bangalore
items.quote: Normally, our Cochin park has a high contribution from group sales in January . That did not happen this year. Now the reason we are told is because of change in exam dates and also preponing of exams because of elections. So these are the two reasons that we were given. The other two parks I've not seen this issue. Only Cochin, I think the group footfalls degrew by 37%.

items.statement: Hyderabad park at 70% of Bangalore/Kochi footfalls; expanding marketing to Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: If you look at footfalls in Hyderabad compared to like for example, Kochi or Bangalore, it's only 70% of the other two parks, whereas we feel that it should be at par with the other parks. So we still feel there is a headroom for us to grow foot falls in Hyderabad.

items.statement: ARPU grew 15% in FY24 driven by non-ticket revenue (F&B, retail)
items.quote: ARPU for the quarter s tood at Rs.1,349, an increase of 14% , and for F Y'24 at Rs.1,430, registering a growth of 15%. Our increase in ARPU was driven by a healthy growth in non-ticket Wonderla Holidays Limited May 17, 2024 revenue along with encouraging response from walk-in groups and all aspects of our customer base

items.statement: Employee cost up 16% YoY in FY24 due to salary revision & headcount increase (+54 for year)
items.quote: There is actually 16% revision in the salary cost as compared to the previous year, and at the same time we had a headcount increase for this quarter as well as for the year, there was about some 16 number has added to the corporate team in the current year and even to the parks as well and then 38 numbers have been added during the full year.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 38.7% (-28pp YoY) due to lower footfall, higher payroll, lower other income

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 49.4% (adj. 49.7%); PAT margin 31.2%

Adjusted EBITDA for FY'24 was at Rs.251 crores as against Rs.235 crores for the same period last year with the margin of 49.7 percentage.

items.statement: Will raise funds (debt/equity combo) for new projects; Chennai capex large
items.quote: We will be looking at some fundraise. Some amount of debt depending on how many projects we sign in the next year or so, we'll take a call on that. We will be definitely doing some fundraise in the form of either debt or equity or most likely a combination of both.

items.statement: Reorganising sales, marketing, IT teams; new IT head hired; beefing up projects team for parallel execution
items.quote: We are reorganizing our sales team and our marketing team is going through a bit of a reorganization. Because of the way we are also going through a digital transformation , our IT team is also going through a substantial change. In fact, we have a new IT head has joined and so in the next one year, we will be investing I think about 4-5 crores in new tech for our parks. So thos e are some of the

items.statement: Government talks on hold due to election code of conduct; will resume after elections
items.quote: Nothing as of now, because this is election season. I think all of those conversations have been put on hold as of now because of code of conduct . We are waiting for normal government functioning to resume, then we will take up.

items.statement: Resort occupancy fell to 55% in FY24 due to loss of long-stay industrial guests
items.quote: In the current year, there were no major long stays. So that's the reason why the occupancy has reduced to 55% in the current FY.

items.statement: Footfall volatile due to exams, elections, heat waves; seasonality limits peak-season growth
items.quote: Every year the story tends to be little different. For us, the best way to mitigate this is to be in more locations and I have always some projects in the pipeline.

items.statement: Depreciation policy: rides & machinery over 10 years; consistent across parks
items.quote: Asset side for the plant and machinery like these rides and things like that we are depreciating over a period of 10 years.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected around Rs 4,000 million, similar to FY24
items.quote: Next year, the figure should be similar to about Rs. 4,000 million, unless there are other new opportunities.

items.statement: Europe FY25 capex budget approx €40 million to complete EV capacity installation
items.quote: Speaking about FY 25, the budget is to implement the total production capacity with an effort of approx. 40 million euro as gross amount.

items.statement: Target four-wheeler share of consolidated business 45% by FY30 from 25% now
items.quote: Increase our four-wheeler share of consolidated business from 25% now to 45% by FY 30.

items.statement: Target aftermarket sales 10% of India sales by FY28
items.quote: Our focus also is to reach 10% of India sales in our aftermarket business in India by FY28.

items.statement: Carbon neutral target >50% by FY30 from 35% in FY24
items.quote: the aspiration is to reach a carbon-neutral percentage of more than 50 % by FY30

items.statement: AURIC non-auto/4W plant capex Rs 4,009 million through March 2028, SOP Q1 FY26
items.quote: The total CAPEX is expected to be Rs. 4,009 million which should be spent in stages from now to March 2028, with the sales expectation of more than Rs. 5,000 million per annum.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated capex Rs 3,833 million, 81% for growth
items.quote: We have done Capex of about Rs. 3,833 million in FY24, which was 81% for growth, which included building, plant machinery and dies.

items.statement: Europe FY24 capex €62 million (VW €8m, Stellantis €33m, Mercedes €10m)
items.quote: In FY24, we booked capex of €62 million of investment in order to install this production capacity.

items.statement: ABS capacity expanded to 640k/yr, target 1.2m single+dual channel by H2 FY26
items.quote: We are further planning to increase this capacity to 1.2 million single and dual channel ABS assemblies per annum in the second half of FY26.

items.statement: Alloy wheel capacity expanded to 5.5m wheels/yr from 4.5m
items.quote: we are now expanding to supply 5.5 million wheels per annum and the SO P has already started for April 24

items.statement: Disc brake assembly run rate 6.2m/yr, brake disc 8.1m/yr
items.quote: With this new plant, we have reached a run rate of 6.2 million numbers per annum of disc brake assembly volumes, and 8.1 million numbers per annum of brake disc volume.

items.statement: EV aluminum castings ramp to 240k sets/yr (Rs 1,000m/yr) peak Q3 FY25
items.quote: For EV Scooters, we are ramping up our sales to 240,000 sets per annum of aluminum castings, which are required for electric vehicle battery packs and motor housings. The total value will be Rs. 1,000 million per annum, which has already started and will reach peak sales value in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Four-wheeler order wins Rs 2,810m in FY24 (23% of total)
items.quote: The total four-wheeler business win in FY24 is Rs. 2,810 million, which is 23% of our total order wins in FY24.

items.statement: Active RFQ pipeline Rs 18,440m from OEMs
items.quote: we are in discussion for Rs. 18,440 million worth of request for quotes from OEMs.

items.statement: Europe FY24 order wins €30.8m (VW Group, Mercedes); 24-month total €115m (€61m BEV, €35m hybrid)
items.quote: In FY 24, we have won €3 0.8 million business , mainly from the V olkswagen Group including Porsche & Audi, and Mercedes Benz. In the last 24 months, out of €115 million orders, €61 million orders are for the growing battery EV business and €35 million are for hybrids.

items.statement: Aluminum alloy prices trending down; driven by scrap availability and sea freight
items.quote: The price trend appears to be downwards.

items.statement: Focus on structural castings (swing arms, subframes, crank cases) and machining for higher value add
items.quote: We are also getting into structural castings like swing arms and subframes and structural fairings which are complex, which need technology and where pricing is better.

items.statement: Aluminum forging expanding beyond backward integration; orders from JLR, Harley-Davidson
items.quote: We have also got orders from Harley-Davidson, and we are talking to other OEMs. We learn from Jaguar Land Rover that aluminum forgings will be a very important part in 4 wheelers.

items.statement: New 4W customers: Tata Punch Powertrain, JLR, Hyundai, Mahindra, Tata Motors
items.quote: These orders are mainly from Tata Punch Powertrain, Tata Motors, Mahindra, Jaguar Land Rover, and Hyundai.

items.statement: ABS market ~3.5m/yr in India; competing with Bosch, Continental; now supplying dual-channel from July 2024
items.quote: the competition is mainly from Bosch and Continental, which controls the major market share in the Indian ABS two-wheeler market of approximately 3.5 million per annum. We are now in the process of supplying our dual channel ABS from July 24, 2024.

items.statement: FAME II subsidy withdrawal impacted 2W EV OEM order flow in India
items.quote: Definitely, the withdrawal of FAME II subsidy in India has affected a lot of 2-wheeler EV OEMs who were market leaders.

items.statement: India standalone exports grew 4.4% to Rs 2,210m FY24; aftermarket exports to 34 countries
items.quote: In FY24, the export sales for India standalone business grew by 4.43% from Rs. 2,116.23 million in FY23 to Rs. 2,210.06 million in FY24.

items.statement: Net debt zero; consolidated cash Rs 5.044 billion
items.quote: There was no net debt and there was a consolidated positive cash available which has crossed the Rs.5 billion mark and it stood at Rs.5.044 billion.

items.statement: Europe considering acquisitions due to supplier bankruptcies in EV transition
items.quote: Unfortunately, there are a lot of companies in bankruptcy due to the fact that the OEM's strategy in the last few years was to focus only on a few suppliers like us for the electric development. We are considering possible acquisition in order to grow.

items.statement: Expect consumer durable division to grow at 20% run rate and sustain by year-end
items.quote: Glad to share that due to high temperatures and good secondary sales in the month of April and May, we are moving with a run rate of 20% growth and expect the same growth by year-end for this division.

items.statement: Target electronics division EBITDA margin of 7.5% to 8% in FY25
items.quote: Now going forward, we are confident to touch EBITDA in the range of 7.5% to 8% for the division in the current year.

items.statement: Target electronics division revenue growth above 35% in FY25
items.quote: We are targeting an EBITDA margin in the range of 7.5% to 8% and expect this division to grow by above 35% in the current Financial Year '25.

items.statement: Expect consolidated EBITDA margin improvement of 50-75 bps and ROCE above 15% in FY25
items.quote: We expect further margin improvement in this current financial year at a consol level by at least 50 basis points to 75 basis points and hence ROCE level to bounce back above 15% in Financial Year '25.

items.statement: Expect railway subsystem and mobility division revenue to double in next two to three financial years
items.period: next two to three financial years
items.quote: With good order book in place, increase in product offering per passenger coach and Sidwal getting a preferred supplier status, we expect railway subsystem and mobility division to double its revenue in the next two to three financial years.

items.statement: Plan capex of Rs.350 to 375 crores for FY25
items.quote: We plan to incur CAPEX of Rs.350 to 375 crores for Financial Year '25.

items.statement: Sidwal total order book approximately Rs.2,000 crores including Rs.515 crores new doors and gangways orders
items.quote: Glad to share that new orders for doors and gangways received from three customers amounting to Rs.515 crores. This makes total order book of Sidwal at approximately Rs.2,000 crores.

items.statement: Consumer durable division operating EBITDA margin increased 100 bps to 7% in FY24
items.quote: Also, our operating EBITDA margins in consumer durable division have increased by 100 basis points, touching to 7% now which is reflective of our component strategy with better margins.

items.statement: Electronics division operating EBITDA margin improved from 3% in 2018 to 5.6% in FY24
items.quote: In this electronic EMS division, we have travelled a journey from 3% EBITDA in 2018 to 5.6% in FY'24.

items.statement: Expect Sidwal blended margins of 18% to 20% with new product categories
items.quote: So we expect on blended basis, I think about 18% to 20% margin for the Sidwal products.

items.statement: Copper price increases will be passed to customers on quarterly lag basis
items.quote: Since there is hardly any movement fluctuations of commodity side, but only the copper is a commodity which is skyrocketing right now, the LMEs shot up which will be passed on to customers definitely on a quarterly lag basis as we have done in past it will be done.

items.statement: Industry may see 20% to 25% growth if Q4 season remains strong
items.quote: I think already in April and May month, we are 20%-plus at run rate of that and if the Q4 also have a good season probably industry will see 20% to 25% range improvement in the whole industry level.

items.statement: RAC contribution decreased from 72% in FY18 to 40% in FY24 due to component strategy shift
items.quote: As a result of this strategic shift, our contribution from room AC has decreased from 72% in FY'18 to just 40% in

items.statement: Two more brand plants to start by next quarter, then business model will stabilize
items.quote: Further, two more customers will begin their plant by next quarter and post that the business model will move towards stability and growth will move in tandem with the industry trend.

items.statement: Received PLI grant of Rs.15 crores for AC components manufacturing
items.quote: I'm also glad to share that Amber received a PLI grant of Rs.15 crores for manufacturing of AC components.

items.statement: Washing machine JV mass production from H2 FY25 targeting 40,000 units in FY25 and 1,25,000 in FY26
items.quote: Mass production from the new plant will commence from H2 second half this year, where we expect around 40,000 washing machines to be produced in this year, which will further take it to 1,25,000 in next financial year.

items.statement: Outlook for Indian capital markets businesses is good over medium to long term due to low penetration, financialization of savings, technology, and evolved regulation
items.quote: Outlook for Indian Capital Markets related businesses is good over the medium to long term. And this is irrespective of any short -term hiccups that we may see. And outlook is strong primarily because of low penetration of financial products, increased financialization of savings, technology development and evolved regulatory regime.

items.statement: Investment banking deal pipeline is very strong with multiple transactions at various stages of execution
items.quote: So the deal pipeline is ve ry strong. And as you know, we have a very strong competitive positioning in banking, given the fact that we have a very strong research franchise and we have a very strong distribution franchise.

items.statement: MTF book at INR1,035 crores can grow easily and company will retain cash for margin requirements
items.quote: But if you look at our MTF book, which is roughly about INR1,035 crores, we think that this book can grow easily. And we make good return on that, so it's better to retain cash for this.

items.statement: Distribution income of INR117 crores in Q4 FY24 up 23% YoY driven by AIF, PMS and insurance sales
items.quote: Distribution income -- financial product distribution income has increased 23%, INR117 crores for this quarter versus INR95 crores for the last year same quarter and primarily because of sale of products like AIF, PMS and insurance.

items.statement: Short-term volatility due to elections in first week of June cannot be ruled out; geopolitical tensions are significant short-term risk
items.quote: Short-term volatility, due to elections to be announced in the 1st week of June, cannot be ruled out.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR3 per share in March taken as final; conservative payout to retain cash for growing brokerage margin requirements
items.quote: So we had announced an interim dividend of INR3 in March and that has been taken as final. The dividend has been kept. We have been conservative in terms of payout simply to retain cash, which is now required for the margin requirements for our growing brokerage business.

items.statement: Board confirmed appointment of Nemkumar as Managing Director from May 15 subject to approvals; separation of Chairman and MD roles for better governance
items.quote: The Board of Directors, based on the recommendation of NRC, has confirmed the appointment of Mr. Nemkumar as the Managing Director starting from May 15 , subject to requisite regulatory and shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Partners contribute 35-40% of retail brokerage income; company will continue acquiring more partners as growth strategy
items.quote: See, roughly, if you look at our brokerage income on the retail side, these people will be contributing about 35%, 40%.

items.statement: Finance costs increased 178% YoY and 26% QoQ due to fund-based requirements for margin and margin trading book funding
items.quote: Finance costs have increased 178% year -over-year, 26% quarter -on-quarter because of fund-based requirement, which is used for funding both margin as well as margin trading book.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 12% to 15% for FY25
items.quote: I think we will continue to maintain the 12% to 15% growth rate in revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of at least 9% for FY25
items.quote: Himanshu, we are always more conservative in our forward-looking estimates. So, at least maybe I will say that 9% for sure is not better.

items.statement: Liquid milk volume growth expected at 6%-7% for FY25
items.quote: So, volume growth, we are taking an aggressive stand, but even if I take it at, 6%-7% of volume growth, our overall margins, I mean, overall revenue will grow to 20% because of added revenue coming from cattle feed and added revenue coming from our commodity sales that we are doing in terms of the inventory that we have and Kenya operations.

items.statement: Kenya plant capacity utilization expected at 35% to 40% in FY25
items.quote: The Kenyan capacity utilization will be around 35% to 40% this year.

items.statement: Orgafeed revenue target of INR 200-207 crores for FY25
items.quote: Actually, in FY24, we have done only INR 83 crores top line. But coming FY25, we have taken a target of INR200 crores, INR207 crores, very aggressive target we have taken.

items.statement: Maharashtra expansion or acquisition decision expected in next couple of months
items.quote: We are evaluating other options in terms of acquisition. So we're trying to phase it out and we'll make definitely a call in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Inventory levels currently at roughly 35 days of sales
items.quote: Roughly now it will be around 35 days or so of sales in terms of value. That is what we will be carrying now currently.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin would have been 12.5% excluding inventory write-down of INR 230 million
items.quote: In the Q4 FY '24, there was a write-down of inventory to the net realisable value amounting to INR 230 million or INR 23 crores. Consequently, the EBITDA for Q4 FY '24 and FY '24 would have been INR 984 million and INR 3,118 million, respectively. The EBITDA margin would have been 12.5% and 10% for Q4 FY '24 and FY '24, respectively.

items.statement: Procurement prices expected to maintain status quo or slight downward trend in FY25
items.quote: I think the way things are going we will not see any procurement price increase as we go Aditya. It might take a little downward trend.

items.statement: Ice cream sales grew 33% in FY24, expecting good growth in FY25
items.quote: Yes, I will answer question number one, ice cream, actually compared to last year to this year, now we have grown by almost 33%. That is as far as ice cream is concerned. FY23 to FY24 comparison, ice cream has grown by 33%. And this year also, even FY25, also we are expecting good growth in ice cream.

items.statement: VAP revenue share grew 143 bps to 28.3% in FY24, VAP sales up 16.3% to INR 7,408 million
items.quote: The revenue share from VAP and Fat and Fat products grew 143 basis points year-on-year to 28.3% of total revenues in the FY '24. Sales of VAP increased by 16.3% year-on-year to over INR 7,408 million in FY '24, driven by deeper market penetration, effective branding activities and a robust distribution network and strong brand recognition.

items.statement: No further inventory write-downs expected as first month sales exceeded NRV provision
items.quote: But I think in the first month of the operation of this current quarter itself we have sold a little higher than the NRV value that we have provided. Therefore, we are confident that the benefit of these results will be seen in the current quarter results itself.

items.statement: Target inventory policy of 20-25 days average for fat and milk powder going forward
items.quote: I think our policy will be that we will maintain the 20 days, 25 days of average inventory for the year. Based on seasonality you might find one quarter to be higher and one quarter to be lower, but I think we will keep around 20 days 25 days of inventory, ma'am.

items.statement: Africa procurement volumes grew to 1.06 lakh litres per day in FY24, volume growth of 8%
items.quote: Africa, procurement last year was 99,000 lakh litres per day. This year, 1,06,000 lakh litres per day.

items.statement: India milk procurement grew 21.2% YoY to 15.73 lakh litres per day in FY24
items.quote: Efforts to enhance the procurement network, including the addition of chilling centres and small collection points in nearby villages, led to 21.2% year-over-year growth in procurement, reaching 16.8 lakh litres per day in the FY '24.

items.statement: Orgafeed capacity expanded fivefold to 480 metric tons per day in FY24
items.quote: The capacity of Orgafeed, that is the company's cattle feed business, was significantly expanded by fivefold to 480 metric tons per day during the FY '24.

items.statement: Company targets at least 1.5x industry growth rate for FY2025 and beyond
items.quote: we are set to continue this trend, growing at, at least 1.5x faster than the underlying industry growth.

items.statement: 80-85% of FY2025 order book visibility already in hand
items.quote: We already have visibility of over 80%, 85% of our FY2025 order book in hand.

items.statement: FY2025 capex guided at Rs.60-70 crores; 2-3 year capex at Rs.160-170 crores
items.quote: we expect that in this current year FY2025, we will do a capex in the range of around Rs.60 crores to Rs.70 crores. But if I talk about for a larger, for the two or three year basis, the capex would be in the range of Rs.160 crores, Rs.170 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target maintained at close to 25%
items.quote: what I've said is, we continue to drive growth, outperforming the market and maintain an EBITDA margin of close to 25%.

items.statement: Exotech EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 15-16% despite recent outperformance
items.quote: Our guidance for this has been that we will be around 15%, 16% margin for Exotech. We outperformed that expectation this quarter. But then the normal expectation from this business should be in the same region of 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Walter Pack EBITDA margins expected at 24-26% going forward with focus on growth over margin expansion
items.quote: 24%, 25%, 26% sort of margins at Walter Pack is what we can expec t moving forward. And the emphasis is of course, would be accelerating growth there

items.statement: Two-wheeler industry growth projected at 8-10%; PV growth at 6-7% due to high base
items.quote: we imag ine that 8% to 10% growth is what is likely moving forward, that's the market growth, we, of course, will grow faster

items.statement: Revenue mix targeted at 36-37% two-wheeler, 35% four-wheeler, 20% consumer
items.quote: we are for 37%, 36% for two-wheelers, 35% for four-wheelers and 20% for consumer. So, I think that's a very good mix and it will continue to be the same.

items.statement: Cover glass business expected to be significant growth driver over next 3-4 years; RFQs received, prototypes given, commercial negotiations underway
items.quote: we expect this to be a very significant growth driver in the next three to four years.

items.statement: Cover glass margins may be low initially due to validation and trial costs before scaling
items.quote: margins could be low initially because ultimately, we will need to prove part s. We will do a lot of trials, parts will not be sold to the

items.statement: FY2024 guidance achieved: 45% revenue growth and 30%+ PAT growth excluding amortization
items.quote: I'm extremely delighted to announce that for the full year FY2024, SJS has achieved its stated guidance of 45% revenue growth and has exceeded its 30% plus PAT growth excluding amortization expenses.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY2024 EBITDA margin 26.2%, up 70 bps Q-o-Q and 147 bps Y-o-Y
items.quote: consolidated EBITDA margin for the quarter improved 70 basis points Q-o-Q and 147 basis points Y-o-Y to 26.2%.

items.statement: Walter Pack Q4 FY2024 EBITDA margin recovered to 25.5% from 20.4% in Q3
items.quote: EBITDA margins reached 25.5%, a significant increase from 20.4% in Q3 of FY2024.

items.statement: Exotech Q4 FY2024 EBITDA margin at 18.1%
items.quote: Exotech recorded EBITDA margin of 18.1%, underscoring our commitment to operational excellence and profitability.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs.163.5 million by end FY2024 after temporary increase for Walter Pack acquisition
items.quote: our net debt level stand at Rs. 163.5 million, reflecting our strong cash flow performance.

items.statement: Expects e-commerce industry growth of 15-20% and plans internal operations for that range
items.quote: See, I think industry growth, at least as far as we've been able to gather from our clients as well and their appetite, remains in that 15% to 20% range.

items.statement: Expects FY25 capex to decline to 6.6-6.9% of revenue from 7.4% in FY24
items.quote: We expect this to decline in fiscal '25 to somewhere between 6.6% and 6.9% of revenue overall.

items.statement: Sufficient capacity to grow through FY25; only major addition is Bangalore mega facility; Tauru gateway capacity expanded 10-15% via process improvements
items.quote: we have sufficient capacity available to grow through fiscal '25. We will need to build our Bangalore mega facility. And there may be some smaller hubs that are planned here and there, but there's nothing major outside of this

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA at 18.4% for FY24, in line with long-term 18-20% target; PTL incremental margins 40-50%; SCS service EBITDA doubled to 6.8%
items.quote: Total service EBITDA from the Express Parcel business has grown from Rs. 636 crores in fiscal '23 to Rs. 934 crores in fiscal '24, which represents 18.4% of revenue and is in line with our long-term targets for this business.

items.statement: Express Parcel volumes grew 12% YoY to 740M in FY24; PTL freight grew 30% YoY to 1.4M metric tons; Truckload grew 40% YoY
items.quote: We delivered 740 million Express Parcels in our Express Parcel business in fiscal '24, which is a growth of nearly 12% year-on-year and 1.4 million metric tons of Part Truckload freight, which is a growth of nearly 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: No significant pricing movements needed or anticipated; will pass cost efficiencies to customers; yields up 6% YoY due to mix, weight increases, and some account repricing
items.quote: We haven't seen any significant sort of pricing movements being necessary in the market so far, and we don't anticipate that there will be significant pricing movements at this point going forward.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved from 38 to 31; receivable days down from 77 to 66; expects further improvement in FY25
items.quote: We are now closing fiscal '24 with a net working capital position of 31 days. Receivable days have declined consistently over the last 5 financial years and especially between '23 and '24 from 77 days to 66 days, and we expect to see further improvements to this financial year.

items.statement: Sandeep Barasia (ED & CBO) leaving after 9 years to pursue personal interests
items.quote: Mr. Sandeep Barasia has announced his decision to move on from Delhivery to pursue personal interests. On behalf of the employees, the Board of Directors and the shareholders of Delhivery, I'd like to place on record our gratitude to Mr. Barasia for his service as an Executive Director and Chief Business Officer of Delhivery for 9 years.

items.statement: Delhivery >100% of Express Parcel profit pool (ex-captives); PTL growth driven by service quality not discounting; pricing comparable to market
items.quote: We are fairly certain that if you take the third-party players put together and our Express business, we are materially over 100% of the profit pool of this industry.

items.statement: PTL truck utilization ~65% on trailer network, 55-60% on secondary line haul; room for improvement
items.quote: Broadly across the trailer network, if I break it in half, I think truck utilization on the trailer network would have been in the range of about 65% or thereabouts. Broadly speaking, on the secondary line haul, we would have been closer to about 55% to 60% utilized.

items.statement: Express Parcel 62% of revenue, PTL 19%, Supply Chain ~10%, Truckload & Cross Border ~9%; PTL share up from 16%
items.quote: Express Parcel continues to be the largest part of our business overall at 62% of revenue. The PTL business has grown significantly between fiscal' 23 and fiscal '24 from 16% of revenue to 19% of revenue.

items.statement: Active multi-service customers increased to 33,278; Meesho volume impact stabilized; new SCS customers ramped in Q3-Q4
items.quote: We have expanded the overall number of active customers who access multiple services of Delhivery with 33,278 customers as of the end of Q4.

items.statement: FY24 revenue Rs 8,142 crores (+12.7% YoY); EBITDA Rs 127 crores (1.6% margin) vs loss of Rs 452 crores; PAT loss narrowed 75% to ~Rs 250 crores
items.quote: We've delivered Rs. 8,142 crores of revenue in fiscal '24, which is a growth of 12.7% compared to fiscal '23 with an EBITDA profit of Rs. 127 crores and an adjusted EBITDA profit of Rs. 76 crores as opposed to an EBITDA loss of Rs. 452 crores.

items.statement: Site 3++ capex Rs 200 crore, expected to come online and stabilize in Q4 FY25
items.quote: To start with, site 3++ is Rs. 200 crores of investment and it is expected to come online and stabilize in Q4 of this financial year 2024-25.

items.statement: Site 5 capex Rs 500 crore, first phase online December 2025, stabilization Q4 FY26, potential unlocking FY27
items.quote: And talking about site 5, we are estimating all getting online in the phase wise manner where the first phase will get online in December of 2025 which will stabilize in the last quarter of 2025-26 and potential will start unlocking in 26-27 for that site. This is expansion of Rs. 500 crores of capital investment.

items.statement: Revenue loss of Rs 150-200 crore over 4 months due to fire accident, pushed to future quarters
items.quote: We lost almost close to Rs. 150 crores to Rs. 200 crores of revenue, which we are assuming in two quarters, I mean 4 months.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from China continues, no price correction expected in Q1-Q2 FY25, hope for improvement from Q2
items.quote: Currently for Q1 and Q2, no, we are not expecting any price to be correcting, but we are seeing a good demand at least to start with, which is a very positive note and with the demand we hope that from Q2 onwards, the pricing will go towards the North.

items.statement: Agro expected at 30-35% of topline in FY25, LSM 59%, CRAMS 14%, contract/exclusive 26% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: We are anticipating 30% to 35% of our total topline to be agro for this financial year.

items.statement: Site 4 commercialized for oil field services, first phase revenue from Q1 FY25, significant contribution expected in coming quarters
items.quote: Production and supply of products from this site 4 to this particular customer will increase in phases with the first phase beginning in this first quarter of fiscal 2025. By the coming quarters, we anticipate very significant revenue contribution from this site 4 in the oil field services domain.

items.statement: Electrolyte additives partial commercialization by end of calendar year 2024, full commercialization in site 3++ by end of FY25 or quarter thereafter
items.quote: So, the commercialization will be partially done by the end of this calendar year and the full commercialization will happen in the site 3++, which will be by the end of this fiscal year or the quarter thereafter.

items.statement: 15 MW solar plant commissioning in 3 phases: Phase 1 end May 2024, Phase 2 July 2024, Phase 3 September 2024
items.quote: Commissioning of the new 15 MW solar power plant will be adding to saving of electricity expenses, which will be done in 3 phases. Phase 1 will come online in the end of May 2024, second phase will start online by July 2024 and the last phase will start in September 2024.

items.statement: Site 2 expected to resume 75% operations soon, full revocation order awaited
items.quote: We're expecting to receive revocation of the closure order of site 2 to resume operations to the extent of 75% of our capacity in the next coming days.

items.statement: CRAMS portfolio grew year-on-year despite accident, significant expansion expected in FY25 with new projects and customers
items.quote: Even with the recent setbacks, our CRAMS portfolio has in fact grown year-on-year and we anticipate the upcoming fiscal year will see a significant expansion of this CRAMS portfolio with new projects and new customers being added across the industry spectrum.

items.statement: Otsuka partnership to contribute substantial revenue for first time in FY25
items.quote: This upcoming fiscal year will see substantial revenue contributions coming up for the first time from our partnership with Otsuka, thus transforming the work done over the last several years and building this partnership into a substantial commercial business.

items.statement: Management expects 30-35% year-on-year revenue growth for the company
items.quote: And for our company, it will be around 30% to 35% year-on-year.

items.statement: Management targets at least 25-30% growth and expects to reach INR1,000 crores revenue in FY25
items.quote: Obviously, we are thinking of at least 25% to 30% growth. Since we have achieved around [3820 31:26], if we add up 30%, it will surely reach INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: New 10,000 sq ft flagship showroom under construction at NSC Bose Road, Chennai, targeting opening by May 2025
items.quote: We have acquired a 3,045 square feet, around 3,304 square meters of land plot on NSC Bose Road and then commence prominent construction stage for the showroom, anticipating to open by May 2025.

items.statement: B2B gross margin 3.5-4%, retail margin 8-9%; overall margin to improve as retail mix increases from 10% to 25% in 2 years
items.quote: If the proportion of retail is going to increase of 20% then the retail is increased, then 8% margin it would be around what they say going to be 1.6% increase. So the retail margin overall margin from B2B, B2C is increased by half a percent, 0.7, 0.8 like that.

items.statement: Diamond sales currently 2% of total; focus on expanding diamond, kundan, jadau, polki segments in new showroom
items.quote: The proportion currently since we are not into B2B distribution of diamonds still now and the current proportion of diamond sales is nearly 2% of the total sales.

items.statement: Volume demand increasing substantially; gold price spikes drive investment demand and higher volumes
items.quote: Volume side also, the demand has been increasing and it will increase substantially.

items.statement: Management sees no major risks due to 50 years experience; all risk segments filtered by experienced management
items.quote: Since we are in the field from the past 50 years our management has a very vast experience. So, all the risk segments has been already filtered by the management with their experience.

items.statement: Inventory turns 4x per year; no hedging policy as gold prices consistently reach new highs
items.quote: Sir, in a year, it rotates around four times.

items.statement: Plan to insource 20% of manufacturing within 2 years; CAD design and automated manufacturing to be implemented
items.quote: Then you can take up, in the coming two years, at least 20% of the production should be of in-house.

items.statement: Geographical expansion planned: 3-4 new showrooms in 2 years after flagship opening
items.quote: And regarding geographical expansion, after opening of this new showroom, we surely have a program of expanding geographically for at least three to four showrooms in coming two to three years, two years, sorry.

items.statement: B2C revenue share target 25% in 2 years from current 10%; EPS impacted by increased share count post-listing
items.quote: Sir, since we have an analysis and we think that in coming years, when the storeroom gate opens, at least the B2C proportion should be at least 25% in the whole wholesale value, whole top line.

items.statement: Online platform finalized, implementation shortly alongside new showroom opening
items.quote: We have finalized the online presentation. Now we are working on it. It will be implemented very shortly along with the new showroom opening.

items.statement: Planning to report quarterly results going forward
items.quote: Yes, we are planning to have and we are working on the plan to give more results on quarterly basis.

items.statement: Volume growth target ~25% YoY; price appreciation additional to value growth
items.quote: So on the volume basis we targeting around 25%, right? Rajesh Mehta: Yes, sir. Raj Sanghvi: And whatever is increased in the price that would be additional

items.statement: B2B margin of 3.5-4% considered sustainable due to product creation capabilities
items.quote: Yes, sir. It is sustainable, because we have been working on the creation of the products and all. So we will see to it that we get that set of margins achieved.

items.statement: Volume aspiration to cross 1 million TEUs in four years from listing, targeting FY27-28
items.quote: When we spoke about that, it was a time in which we were listed and we said our volume aspiration is to cross a million TUs in four years.

items.statement: Expect to return to previous quarter EBITDA margin levels through volume growth and cost savings
items.quote: we believe that we will be coming back to the EBITDA margin levels of the previous last two quarters which w e have seen

items.statement: FY24 capex included INR23 crores for Mundra land; Mundra CFS development, Jhajjar ICD in FY26, and existing facility upgrades are key capex priorities
items.quote: This year's capex budget, apart from, so this in FY '24, we invested in Mundra land close to INR23 crores.

items.statement: Speedy JNPT license valid till December 2025; renewal discussions start Q1 of last year with option to extend 10 years
items.quote: Speedy JNPT, we have the license till 2025 December. We have had a good track record of performance. And as of now, the indication is as per the tender document, you get the renewal in the first quarter of the last year of operation.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 32.4% in Q4 FY24 from 31.6% in Q3 FY24; EBITDA per TEU at INR1,760
items.quote: The gross margin percentage has improved to 32.4% from 31.6% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Every 10% volume increase expected to improve gross margin by 2% due to 30% fixed operating expenses
items.quote: We believe that every 10% increase in our volume would give us incremental EBITDA. Our gross margin percentage would go up by 2% because lot of our, close to 30% of our operation expenses are fixed and they won't go up in case our volume goes up.

items.statement: April volumes showed growth over previous year; exports recovering as seasonal commodity bans lifted; volume uptake already underway
items.quote: April, we have shared the volumes with the stock exchanges and we have had growth over the previous year April numbers which indicates that volumes are starting to bounce back and we expect that trend to continue.

items.statement: Import-export mix stable at 76-77% imports, balance exports
items.quote: No, it has remained similar compared to the previous quarters. I think it is 76 %-77% imports, balance, exports. That has been the average.

items.statement: One-off impacts in Q4 FY24: INR1 crore bad debt provision and INR70 lakhs year-end employee gratuity/leave encashment valuation
items.quote: This is, few of them are like bad debts provision which we have done in the current quarter around close to INR1 crores and one-off adjustments on account of year-end employee gratuity and leave encashment valuation, that is also around INR70 lakhs.

items.statement: ICD Jhajjar land consolidation progressing; targeted launch in 2026
items.quote: ICD Jhajjar, with regard to the land acquisition and related steps, we are progressing as per the plan that we have. And 2026 is the targeted launch of ICD Jhajjar.

items.statement: Gati Shakti Terminal opportunities identified in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana; not yet out for tender
items.quote: In terms of Gati Shakti Terminals, there are a few identified locations that we have. One in Gujarat, one in Maharashtra, and one in Haryana that we have in our list based upon the potential identification that we have done. These are still not coming for tender.

items.statement: Gati Shakti Terminals expected to be exclusive facilities, not common user
items.quote: Our understanding on that is it is an exclusive terminal at this point in time. And that is how some of the existing terminals or the terminals which have been tendered are gone. So we expect the same to continue.

items.statement: Mundra has regulated number of CFSs; company holds two facilities with reasonable market share in growing market
items.quote: Mundra has got a regulated number of CFSs at this point in time. So it is not as widespread number of CFSs compared to JNPT. So that is one point. Second is we have got two facilities in Mundra. And therefore, in our estimate, we have a reasonable market share in a market which is growing.

items.statement: Market share estimated at 10-11% of addressable market in ports where present
items.quote: So, we estimate our market share to be in excess of 10%, maybe 10% to 11% is our estimation of our market share of the addressable market.

items.statement: Historical volume growth 1-2 percentage points above industry; FY24 volume grew 8% vs industry 6.5-7%
items.quote: Even last year when our volumes have grown by about 8%, the industry volume growth was about 7%. So, when I talk about the industry, this is the addressable market which comes into the CFS that we keep track of and this is the addressable market in the ports in which we are present.

items.statement: Revised volume growth target to 1,500 kg and top line target of INR600 crores due to 25% gold price spike
items.value: 1500 kg volume; INR600 crores top line
items.quote: For the target, we have revised to 1500 kg of volume growth due to the spike of around 25% in gold prices. And this would be contributed by, you know, the top line to be around INR600 crores.

items.statement: Akshaya Tritiya demand deferred but not denied; expecting strong recovery in Q1 and Q2
items.quote: The Akshay Trithya which has deferred has not really deferred that -- not really has denied the demand part of it and the demand is there and the quarter one, I think we will be showing you a better picture than the last year quarter one.

items.statement: Normalized profit estimated at INR23-24 crores excluding COGS impact from gold price spike
items.quote: So, the normalized profit would be around INR23-24 crores, you know, in general because, the sales has gone up, the unit quantity of gold sold has gone up.

items.statement: Planning new factory with 5x current capacity; land procurement underway
items.quote: The factory will be coming up, which will be at least having 5x of the capacity which is currently installed.

items.statement: Hedge gold quantity with gold quantity, not rupees; rupee hedging would require INR45 crores margin money
items.quote: On the part of gold hedging, again, I am repeating that it will be we hedge a unit of gold and not a unit of gold with rupee. And if you were to do so, then we would have to pay, let's say, you know, if you had purchased, let's say my balance sheet right now has a gold of let's say 250 kg, 300 kg. So, if I had to hedge that thing, then I had to pay a margin money, which would actually, if you just

items.statement: Service business volume growth projected at 15-20%; retail on track for 600 kg target
items.quote: The service business will again progress by around 15 % to 20% by volumes and the retail part of it is going smooth so in that case whatever the projections we have made for around 600 kg of top line, we are on track of it.

items.statement: GP dip due to weighted average accounting; higher gold procurement costs affected COGS
items.quote: The GP has got hit because we were following the weighted average accounting method in which the procurement of gold, which has been done at a higher rate, has affected the total average cost of goods and thus there is a dip in GP.

items.statement: Expecting strong recovery in Q1 and Q2 FY25; committed to fulfilling business targets
items.quote: Nonetheless, in quarter one and quarter two of this year, we are expecting a strong recovery. And I think we remember quite well our commitments and we are strongly focused on the business operations and on the business to fulfill that.

items.statement: Targets INR 100 crore revenue for FY25, with 80-100 crore range considered exceptionally well
items.quote: Top line our internal target is INR100 crores, but to be very honest we are like I said an internal target is INR100 crores, but anything between 80 to 100 I think, so w e wo uld be doing exceptionally well because 80 would be close to 100% over FY24

items.statement: Targets INR 200 crore revenue for FY26
items.quote: For FY'26, that is correct.

items.statement: Targets $25 million revenue within two years (by FY26)
items.quote: Our immediate goals over the next t wo years is to grab $25 million out of that which on a very logical sense for a company who is approved by Disney, Warner, Paramount , Sony, and all of the majors, to grab $25 million pie out of a $10 billion market is not very difficult

items.statement: Maintains 25% PAT margin guidance for FY25
items.quote: As of now we haven't moved out from there. So as of now we are. It's too early for the full financial year to comment on it.
