items.quote: So it has started coming in, but I would really say the full -fledged effect of the lock, not lockdown, sorry, the strike. Because a lot of productions are in process right now. In our industry, it's the pre-production that takes place first, then the production and we come last in the chain of work, right? So, many productions are on floor and we est imate the VFX boom to really start from late J

items.statement: In talks with productions having total VFX budgets over $50 million; already started work on Star Trek Universe
items.quote: We are right now, I would say very conservatively, very, on a very conservative level. We are in talks with productions which have VFX, total VFX budgets of over $50 million. So productions are already on floor. We've already started getting in quite a bit of work. Like I said, we've already started getting work from Star Trek, which is one of the biggest wins for us this year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved 1127 bps to 32.30% in FY24
items.quote: The EBITDA margin also saw a substantial rise, improving by 1127 bps to 32.30.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 13.92% in FY24
items.quote: This resulted in the EBITDA margin of 13.92.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance 24-26% range due to US/Canada overheads offsetting direct work margin improvement
items.quote: Because the expenses, if we were only India-based with no major overheads in the US and Canada and if my direct work grew from the current, let's say, 25% to 50%, my PAT margins would go up to 30%, 35%, correct? But what is happening is that even though my direct work ratio will go up, but my overheads because of the high salaries in the US have increased. So that will offset the part margins and

items.statement: OTT revenue projected at healthy double-digit crores for FY25 from current INR 2 crore base
items.quote: But the projections for 2024-2025, we've set the base now. And we are looking at very healthy double-digit crores numbers for 2024-2025 from our OTT business.

items.statement: Capital work in progress increased from INR 2 crore to INR 6 crore (INR 4 crore addition) for vpsets.com platform development
items.quote: See, I think you have a lot of capital work in progress now from INR2 crores to it is now INR6 crores. Intangible assets, I can understand you have created this platform. Abhishek More: That's right

items.statement: Hired 4 senior and 7 artist-level people in US and Canada; key hires include Jason Sperling (ex-Head of VFX Netflix), Marina Abramyan (ex-Star Trek VFX Producer), David Crawford (ex-Titanic/Spider-Man)
items.quote: So it's not only Canada. It's U.S. and Canada. So we have a total of 4 senior people and 7 artist level people.

items.statement: Reduced India headcount slightly in Dec-Jan due to post-strike slowdown
items.quote: But we also -- it didn't make sense in January, February for us to, when we saw after the strike. So we did reduce some manpower and that's why you see the effect out there. It's not like dropped from 450 to 100, it's a slight reduction, even in terms of manpower, but that's a good step, right? We were trying to save on cost.

items.statement: Targets 50-60% direct project mix vs current ~25%
items.quote: But this year, that is our target, to have at least 50% to 60% of direct work compared to outsource.

items.statement: Launched beta of vpsets.com with 20 beta users and 300+ potential customers; first SaaS platform for virtual production set rental
items.quote: We have launched, I'm really happy to inform that we have launched the beta version of vpsets.com, i.e. www.vpsets.com. We have, as we speak, we have 20 potential customers as beta users of our website. We are in touch with over 300 potential customers of our website, and this service is the first of its kind in the world.

items.statement: Won Star Trek Universe work as major breakthrough; approved vendor for Disney, Warner, Paramount, Sony, Netflix, Apple
items.quote: and thanks to her efforts, we've already started working on the Star Trek U niverse, which is a huge breakthrough for Digikore and it should lead to substantial revenue for many, many years for

items.statement: Receivables at INR 24-25 crore (over 6 months revenue) due to work influx in Jan-Mar and 60-90 day payment terms now stretching to 120 days
items.quote: Tons and tons of work for the last six months, majority of them has come to us between end January, February, March. So that's why they get in receivables becau se our average payment terms are anywhere between 60 days to 90 days

items.statement: Tippett Studio debtor of INR 50 lakh outstanding 18+ months; filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy; no provision made to preserve recovery case
items.quote: Let me give you an example of Tippet Studio. Tippet Studio is a debtor of more than 18 months to us just now. They have just declared bankruptcy after being taking over by Phantom. So you can't -- we actually have certain debtors which are even older than six months.

items.statement: Increased cash credit limits from bank to manage working capital; no immediate repayment vision but aim to reduce borrowing
items.quote: So, we got an increase from our bank on the CC limits that we enjoyed. So, that is the long-term borrowing that you are talking about.

items.statement: Strategic hiring of senior talent in North America: Jason Sperling (Creative Director/VFX Supervisor, ex-Netflix), Marina Abramyan (Executive Producer, ex-Star Trek), David Crawford (Head of Studio Montreal, 30 years exp)
items.quote: I'm glad to announce that we have onboarded seasoned professionals like Jason Sperling, who joins us as Creative Director and VFX Supervisor, bringing with him a wealth of industry experience and a strong network of connections. For most of you who don't know, Jason's last role was Head of VFX, Netflix, U.S., and Canada. He comes in with over 25 years of experience in the industry, highly respecte

items.statement: Average direct project size $100K-$150K, duration 1-1.5 months; outsource work is bid-based weekly
items.quote: As on today, when we look at direct projects, the average size of the direct project we are experiencing is around $150,000-$200,000 maybe for a direct project. When we do outsource work, let's say a large VFX studio in the US, there, it's not really project. We don't get project-based. One week, they'll send us a bid. We send them back, award it. Next week, they'll send us more bids, award it.

items.statement: H2 historically weaker than H1 due to US/Europe holiday slowdown (Thanksgiving to early January); project-based lumpiness causes quarterly volatility
items.quote: Historically, Digikore has seen H2 weaker than H1, but I'll tell you how it goes now. Let's say in H2, I get a - you see we are project based. Now, let's say in H1 I get a project in July which is like let's say a INR 10 crores project. I can't go and tell the client to give INR 5 crores in H1 and INR5 crores in H2 or else H2 will become weak or vice versa. It's a project. It's not something like

items.statement: AI disruption risk to VFX; company embracing AI and claims to have cracked own version of Sora; announcement expected in couple months
items.quote: We are not against AI. We are not the ones who are scared of AI. We are the ones among the few studios who have embraced AI. There's going to be a very interesting announcement from Digikore on the AI front as well. I don't know if many of you have heard of Sora. We've been able to crack our own version of Sora.

items.statement: Revised operating EBITDA margin guidance to 26-28% for FY25 from previous 25-27%
items.quote: With this outlook, I'm pleased to revise our operating EBITDA margin guidance in the range of 26% to 28% as against our previous guidance of 25% to 27%.

items.statement: Domestic business to outperform IPM by 200 bps; domestic and CDMO to reach 75-80% of revenue in midterm
items.quote: Concluding, I would like to state that the domestic business will continue to outperform the IPM by 200 basis points. The domestic business share in the overall business will continue to increase while CDMO business will continue to gain traction. We expect both domestic and CDMO to cumulate the account for 75% to 80% of overall business in midterm.

items.statement: CDMO business to grow 12-14% in FY25 with high teens growth from Q3 onwards
items.quote: This business should grow between 12% to 14% a nd you should see probably high teens growth happening quarter 3 onwards that is October onwards

items.statement: India, CDMO and emerging markets to grow 12-14%; US, Russia, South Africa to grow 8-9%
items.quote: India, CDMO and our emerging market, which is ROW, should grow between 12% to 14%. US, Russia, South Africa should grow at around high single digit, around 8%, 9%.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA to grow 16-18% in short to midterm; gross margins near 65% for next 2 years
items.quote: Overall business growing at around 12% to 14%; EBITDA growing it around 16% to 18%; and EBITDA margins -- operating EBITDA margins between 26% to 28%. That is where we stand. And both India and CDMO will contribute overall to the growth of the company. And overall generating gross margins closer to 65% for the coming 2 years.

items.statement: CDMO lozenges capacity at 2 billion annually, currently running at 1 billion; only maintenance capex needed
items.quote: we have a capacity of 2 billion lozenges annualized. Currently, we are running at a run rate of 1 billion lozenges. So we have adequate capacity to kind of ramp up our business whatever bottlenecks were there with respect to packaging apart from manufacturing have also been taken care of in the last 12 months

items.statement: Ophthalmology acquisition dilutes gross margin by 150 bps but operating leverage offsets at EBITDA level
items.quote: See the way we have to say this is while the gross margin is close to 150 bps dilutive because of ophthal. We get very strong operating leverage also on ophthal business. And some of the other levers, which we are talking about in terms of improvement of private mix in South Africa, overall portfolio mix in our international business. and the fact that our chronic and the domestic business will co

items.statement: Ophthalmology to cause 50 bps EBITDA margin dip and 100-250 bps gross margin decline in FY25-26
items.quote: No, no, no. So I think that has to be clarified next couple of years FY '25, FY '26, you will see a reverse, probably close 200, again, 50 bps dip in EBITDA margins because of the ophthal revenue. Gross margins -- gross margins, 100, 250 bps decline you may see.

items.statement: Domestic business grew 22% in Q4 and 16% in FY24; chronic portfolio driving growth with 65% from fast-growing therapies
items.quote: domestic business, which grew strong to INR465 crores in quarter 4, registering growth of 22% and INR1,897 crores in FY '24 , recording a healthy growth of 16%. This was driven by strong brand portfolio, meticulous execution on basing on the field productivities and higher share of chronic products

items.statement: Acute business weak due to muted season; expected to recover if season improves in FY25
items.quote: The acute business last year was largely impacting because of muted season. As we see the trends, we believe that the season will be much better this year. But of course, we need to have a guided approach towards that. If the season is better than last year than we see -- certainly see growth coming in from acute as well apart from our chronic growth.

items.statement: CDMO share of international business rose from 21% in FY21 to 27% in FY24; entered European market with consumer players
items.quote: CDMO accounted for 27% of overall international business as compared to 21% in FY '21. Also happy to share the CDMO business has entered. Now we have entered into European market with a couple of strong consumer players in the world of immunity and cough and cold lozenges.

items.statement: Ophthalmology MR count ramped from 75 to 104; further gradual increase planned over 6-8 months
items.quote: Already the ramp -up has happened and we have gone up to close to 104 a nd slowly but gradually in the coming year we will kind of further ramp this up. But this is a steady state number, which we will work with for the next six to eight months

items.statement: MR productivity at INR 7 lakh per month; expected to grow 8-10% without additions
items.quote: So, productivity, what I shared in our -- in my commentary is now close to INR 7 lakh. And you should expect the productivity as is without any addition to grow around 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Net cash positive; gross debt reduced to INR 357 crore from INR 548 crore; ROCE improved to 27%
items.quote: J. B.'s balance sheet further strengthened in the year, and I'm glad to state that we are now net cash positive company. There has been a reduction in gross debt which was INR357 crores as on 31st March 2024 versus INR548 crores as on 31st March 2023. ROCE has also improved to 27% in FY '24 versus 21% in FY'23.

items.statement: Net working capital reduced from 98 days to 87 days over 3 years; operating cash flow conversion 85% in FY24
items.quote: Net working capital has reduced from 98 days 3 years ago to 87 days in FY '24. The objective of sharing this data of the last 3 years in terms of -- is more to share with colleagues on the call is how J. B. as a company, J. B. Pharma as a company has progressed over the last 3 years consistently, not only in terms of top line, but, overall, in EBITDA, in profits and also in net working capital and

items.statement: Open to acquisitions, in-licensing and brand purchases at right value; no specific targets identified
items.quote: It will be mix of all things happening across. First of all, the focus is beyond what we are trying to do with as is the portfolio that we have got. How can we make it big? Equally, we are open to anything which is available in the market and the right value. And if we think that we can grow -- make it grow better as compared to where it stands.

items.statement: US Biosecure Act not expected to impact CDMO as lozenges are herbal and consumer-focused
items.quote: I think that does not have any impact because much of the lozenges – majority of the lozenges that we supply to our partners are more herbal in nature. And it's a business where our partners play that in the consumer world. So limited comment that we can give on this.

items.statement: Trade generics to remain very small proportion; branded generics to stay dominant
items.quote: We have always maintained that it will be a very, very small proportion of our business. Whatever we are doing is to evaluate some markets where the conventional distribution model cannot reach. And that's how it will be for us as well. We primarily believe more in branded generic space where the margins are much more accretive. So it's going to be a very, very small part for us going forward as w

items.statement: ESOP cost expected at INR 40 crore for FY25
items.quote: The ESOP costs for FY'25, we are expecting it to be in the range of around INR40 crores.

items.statement: Azmarda market share stable at 14-15% after competitive pressure; volume growth expected in ARNI segment
items.quote: Overall value wise, if we really look at our share, we are still operating at 14% to 15%. The segment is progressively growing. And we also believe that going forward, we will see a good volume growth in this arni segment. So we are fairly confident about the prospects of Azmarda in the future as well.

items.statement: Russia business profitability improved significantly in FY24 via front-end optimization and favorable CIS mix
items.quote: In fact, a lot of initiators were taken in this financial year, and we have seen significant improvement in the profitability for our Russia business. This includes some front-end optimization as well. And also if we club Russia and CIS together, there has been a favourable product mix for our CIS markets. So we have already seen a significant improvement in terms of operating profitability this y

items.statement: India macro momentum strong with GDP growth above 7.7% in Q1, stable inflation, PMI above 55, high consumer confidence, and improving rural demand.
items.quote: I think the momentum India continues if you look at January to March quarter GDP growth was even above 77%, I think the projection for the for the entire calendar year is in similar magnitude.

items.statement: Automotive industry passenger vehicle growth projected at 4% for the year, construction momentum to continue post-elections, FMCG growth balanced between rural and urban.
items.quote: So we see IHS projection for passenger vehicle growth is 4% for the year which is positive. it's a bit lower than last year but still on the growth side construction you know momentum continues

items.statement: Upstream chemicals face continued margin pressure from Chinese overcapacity and weak demand; downstream businesses more resilient.
items.quote: Expectation now on the chemicals side if you look at the market, I mean there's still a lot of margin pressure here so what we had described in previous analyst conferences I think that situation unfortunately continues

items.quote: I mean we see input cost improving but the pricing pressure is still on yeah so the margins have improved in the material segment which is quite visible but the chemical segment for example which would be intermediates and petrochemicals is still heavily under margin pressure

items.statement: Quarterly sales stabilized around Rs 3,300 crore per quarter, with March quarter achieving similar sales despite being off-season for agro.

items.statement: Full-year profit before tax up 44% despite only 1% sales growth, driven by volume growth and improved input costs.

items.statement: Benzene derivatives greenfield project investment is around INR390 crores (excluding land) with expected turnover of INR400 crores at 85-90% utilization and 5-year payback.
items.value: 390 crores capex; 400 crores turnover at 85-90% utilization
items.quote: So the total investment other than the land and everything, it's less than INR400 crores, so it's around INR390 crores that has been the investment. And the expected turnover at 85%, 90% utilization is around INR400 crores.

items.statement: No new capex planned for next 2 years beyond maintenance; focus on debt reduction.
items.quote: Yes. That is what we are planning at present.

items.statement: Benzene downstream products (MCB, PNCB, ONCB) commercial production started Dec 2023 and Mar 2024; full utilization of 60-70% expected in 1.5-2 months.
items.quote: So, I think for another 1 to 2 months, we'll not be selling much in the market. So, I think after 1.5, 2 months, we will be coming to the market full-fledged with utilization of at least 60%, 70%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 7.7% in Q4 FY24; FY24 EBITDA INR119 crores (down 18% YoY).
items.quote: EBIDTA stood at INR31 crores for Q4 FY '24 with a margin of 7.7%; net profit for the quarter stood at INR2 crores for Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: Chlor Alkali margins historically 16-20%; peak revenue potential INR350-370 crores at full utilization.
items.quote: Chlor Alkali margins vary from say, 16% to 20%. And before 2 years, there was very good time over at that time, even more than 25% margin was also there, but that was normal. We steady case, we can expect about 18% to 20%, 16% to 20% margin.

items.statement: Dye Intermediates and Dyestuffs realization increased slightly 2-3 months ago but has been flat since.
items.quote: Realization increased a little bit 3 months before, 2 to 3 months before. Since then, it has been flat.

items.statement: Demand stability observed over last 2-3 months; destocking ended with gradual recovery at low speed; US/Europe remain slow; China slowdown causing excess volumes.
items.quote: Since last couple of months, we have been experiencing stability in the demand for our industry products. It seems destocking position has come to an end and gradual recovery, but at low speed, is there.

items.statement: Dye Intermediates and Dyestuffs volumes near peak utilization (~80%); no major volume growth expected; focus on diversification.
items.quote: So Dye Intermediates and Dyestuffs, they are a batch type manufacturing process. So there, reaching 90% plus is not possible. Usually, the work -- the peak utilization is about 80%. We are already close to that.

items.statement: Sen-er Boya (Turkey) recorded INR16 crores hyperinflation accounting loss (AS29) in Q4 FY24; volumes gradually recovering post-earthquake but timeline uncertain.
items.quote: During the Q4 FY '24, on implementation of AS29, there is a INR16 crores loss and the sale is already part of declared results.

items.statement: Net debt INR830 crores at March 2024 (peak); targeting INR100-120 crores annual repayment to become debt-free in ~5 years.
items.quote: See, at March balance sheet, our net debt was about INR830 crores. This is something a peak debt of what we are estimating. And every year, about INR100 crores reduction should be there.

items.statement: Permanently stopping production at Vatva Units 1, 3, 4 (built 1989-93); <3% tonnage capacity reduction; fixed overhead reduction to improve efficiency.
items.quote: Furthermore, company will dismantle and sell manufacturing facilities, and it will lead to a reduction of less than 3% in the total tonnage production capacity of the company.

items.statement: Chlor Alkali utilization at 82-83%; targeting 85-87% blended utilization in FY25 with 8-9 months at ~90%.
items.quote: Yes, it is already at 82%, 83%. I think there is still room to go up to 92%, 93% utilization. And things are in place for that. So I think about 8 months of the year, we should do around 90% and the remaining about 80%.

items.statement: Punjab government incentives ~INR20 crores/year expected within 2-3 months post-election approval.
items.quote: There are certain government incentives that we are eligible in Punjab that should be available to the company that are in the range of about INR20 crores per annum. So, because of election process that has deferred, so we are expecting within 2, 3 months that will be approved by the state government.

items.statement: Inventory days elevated due to integration and 100+ dyestuff SKUs requiring stock for quick delivery; no significant improvement expected.
items.quote: See, our integration has been becoming stronger and stronger. And because of that, we are required to have a larger inventory. At the same time, our final product Dyestuff, over there, there are lots of products, more than 100 products. So, to match the required and quick delivery to customers, we are required to give larger stock. So, this is the level that will remain more or less same.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin at 26%-27%, better than long-term industry and company average; FY22-23 was an outlier year.
items.quote: At the 26%-27% EBITDA margin also I would say that this is better than the long-term average EBITDA of the paper industry and our own long-term average.

items.statement: Expects FY25 to be tougher due to competition and dumping from ASEAN countries.
items.quote: The year gone by is over but the coming year is likely to be tougher I would say that the competition and also the dumping of paper from the ASEAN countries will pose a challenge in time to come.

items.statement: Sirpur Paper EBITDA ~30% for FY24 including state incentive on accrual basis; excluding incentive, EBITDA ~22%-23%.
items.quote: So, if I exclude that incentive part then the EBITDA would be close to 22%-23% this is on this part.

items.statement: Corrugation business EBITDA normally 12%-14%, but FY24 was around 10% due to a bad year.
items.quote: In fact the corrugation industry has a very bad time the year '23-24 in the normal course, their EBITDA should be around 12% to 14%, but it was a bad year and it was around 10%.

items.statement: Wood cost increased sharply by 30%-35%; international pulp prices now $700-$750/ton, long-term expected band $550 (+/-$25).
items.quote: The wood cost which is a basic raw material for integrated pulp manufacturer remain very high in fact, it has gone up sharply by close to 30%-35%.

items.statement: April NSR increase only in packaging board segment, not enough to cover wood inflation; further price increases depend on demand-supply.
items.quote: No, see the NSR increase in April this year increase is just in a packaging board one particular segment. There is nothing as a major increase.

items.statement: BCTMP mechanical pulp mill to be commissioned next fiscal year (FY26); will integrate ~70% of mechanical pulp requirement, saving $100-$150/ton vs market price.
items.quote: Yes, next year we will have our own mechanical pulp from our new pulp mill we are setting up.

items.statement: Acquisition hurdle rate: minimum 14%-15% return on investment (4%-5% over ~9%-10% post-tax WACC).
items.quote: So, at this point of time, our cost of capital is something around 9 point odd percent post tax WACC, so 9% or 10% WACC and 4% over that, so in long run we would expect something around minimum 14% to 15% return on investment that is our criteria of any project or any acquisition.

items.statement: Corrugation capacity utilization currently 55%-60% annually; industry best practice is 70%-75% due to seasonal peaks.
items.quote: Right now, our capacity utilization is close to 55%-60% month different month different period, but on an annual basis, our utilization is close to 55%-60%.

items.statement: Imports from Indonesia (ASEAN FTA, forest concessions) and China (surplus capacity, trade diversion) are major concerns; antidumping petition filed against Indonesia, China, Chile.
items.quote: I would say that we are more worried on the import coming from the Indonesia because the Indonesia is a part of ASEAN bloc.

items.statement: Packaging board machine (FY22) at 100% installed capacity; debottlenecking to add 10%-15% more output; further expansion when domestic demand-supply favorable.
items.quote: We are doing debottlenecking of the same machine and hopefully we should be able to increase production by close to 10% to 15% from the same machine this is 1.

items.statement: JK Paper targets double-digit-plus growth, higher than paper industry's single-digit growth.
items.quote: The JK Paper growth has to be a double digit and double digit also plus double digit.

items.statement: No plan to become zero-debt; free cash flow ~Rs 500 cr retained as war chest for projects/acquisitions; buyback/dividend decision not commented.
items.quote: So, whatever the free cash flow will be there in the company that will become a war chest for all our project or acquisition or expansion, no question of converting the company into zero debt company.

items.statement: Corrugated box conversion cost typically Rs 7-10/kg, up to Rs 20/kg for specialized boxes; pricing linked to kraft paper prices.
items.quote: In a normal box it may be Rs. 7 to Rs. 10 conversion cost.

items.statement: Ludhiana corrugation plant commissioned Aug 2023; ramping up, target higher utilization by end of FY25.
items.quote: Ludhiana plant we commissioned last year to be very precise in sometime in August 23 and in this industry it takes time because the customer acquisition is a long process.

items.statement: FTA review with ASEAN is a cumbersome sovereign process; government intent supportive but no action yet; antidumping process may expedite.
items.quote: The Government of India is trying to have the review of the FTA, but this is a very cumbersome process because it has to be mutually acceptable review by both the countries.

items.statement: Management expects to continue the same growth strategy and work towards INR150 crores revenue and INR30 crores EBITDA for FY25 but avoids formal forward-looking statements.
items.quote: We are working towards it. We hope for the best. Definitely don't want to make any forward-looking statements, especially given the question that the previous gentleman asked, on this call. So, we'll work towards it for sure.

items.statement: Management expects all-time high EPS in 2 to 3 years as Project Butterfly investments mature.
items.quote: As I mentioned, we are in the transition phase. We are making all these investments for growth. We expect all time high in 2 to 3 years! time.

items.statement: Company plans to invest INR6-7 crores in US/UK expansion over the year, adding 1-2 people locally and deploying 10 from India, plus partnership support costs.
items.quote: So, it should be around the range of INR6 crores, INR7 crores maybe overall across the year.

items.statement: Government pipeline is very healthy and expected to bear fruit in the next 2 quarters.
items.quote: We also have a very healthy pipe on the government front, which hopefully will bear fruit in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin percentage expected to remain around 20% in transition phase; absolute EBITDA will grow year-on-year.
items.quote: Yes. We're in the transitioning as I mentioned, we are in the transitioning stage because we are investing in growth. We would want to maintain that margin and over a long-term period, improve the margins.

items.statement: Margin percentage will vary quarterly based on revenue composition across segments like government managed services, cloud, data services, and low-code platforms.
items.quote: But from a margin standpoint, that will also depend on the composition of revenue, because each of the segments that we are trying to -- which -- is gaining traction. And it also depends on the opportunities we are trying to materialize.

items.statement: Receivables DSO improved by 20% due to disciplined weekly collection reviews, contributing to cash balance increase to INR64.62 crores.
items.quote: I'm very happy to inform you that our receivables position today, our DSO is down by 20%. It is because of a lot of discipline with which we are looking at and reviewing our collections on a weekly basis.

items.statement: Existing business grew to INR92.98 crores from INR79.08 crores; additional tech-enabled services grew 87% to INR21.5 crores from INR11.5 crores.
items.quote: Our existing business grew to INR92.98 crores from INR79.08 crores. Our additional tech-enabled services business grew to INR21.5 crores from INR11.5 crores, that's almost 87% growth.

items.statement: Core offering expanded from single communication platform to three platforms (communications, data, low-code) plus complementary services: data, transmission, talent, managed services.
items.quote: Now the definition of our core offerings has expanded. So now we're not just doing licenses of our one communication platform alone, we have our communication end-to-end communication governance platform. We have our data platform and a low code platform to deliver managed services.

items.statement: Formed internal risk assessment team; turning down high-risk government deals; partnering to mitigate risk after BSNL experience.
items.quote: We have a risk assessment team internally, which has been formed now, is once bitten, twice shy, there are many deals which we are even turning it down until unless things are there.

items.statement: Headcount reduced from ~600 to 540; savings reinvested into sales (21-22 people) and AI/ML (10-15 people).
items.quote: Last year when we had this conversation, we have almost 600 people. This year, we have 540, that 60 people left. And we've invested all of this money into bringing in more sales personnel and investing in AI/ML.

items.statement: Planning to sell old office property valued around INR6-7 crores; proceeds may fund share buybacks via ESOP trust.
items.quote: We are talking to quite a few property dealers like Frank and Wakefield and all of these people. items.statement: Government tenders require 3-6% performance bank guarantees plus EMD, necessitating healthy cash reserves.
items.quote: I believe it is 5%, 6% of the deal is what they anywhere between 3% to 6% is what they keep it as performance bank guarantee plus there are other things like the EMD for bidding the project for which money is stuck for 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: Added 3 banking logos (including Sri Lanka, Dubai) and ~10 government logos (ULBs in UP, Telangana, Andhra) in FY24.
items.quote: In terms of logo additions, we were we were able to add, I think, about three on the banking side. We added one in Sn Lanka, one in the Middle East from Dubai. And then on the government side, I think we added almost 10 logos last year.

items.statement: Expect total alcohol volumes to rise substantially to approximately 21-21.5 crore litres in FY25
items.quote: For the present fiscal year, we expect our total alcohol volumes to rise quite substantially to approximately 21 - 21.5 crore litres.

items.statement: Executing capex to enhance gears capacity from ₹250 crore to over ₹500 crore, excluding defence
items.quote: The business is currently executing a capex program, which enhances the capacity of our gears business from ₹ 250 crore to over ₹ 500 crore.

items.statement: Power Transmission closing order book at ₹287 crore including ₹90 crore long-duration orders
items.quote: The outstanding order book, as I mentioned, on the 31 st of March stood at ₹ 287 crore, including some loan duration orders of just under ₹ 90 crore.

items.quote: The outstanding order book on the 31st of March stood at ₹ 1,233 crore, which included ₹ 880 crore towards O&M contracts for a longer period of time.

items.quote: The PBIT of the business grew faster than revenues at just over 40% - 40.1% to ₹ 107.1 crore with PBIT margins of 36.7%, up by almost 275 bps, compared on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.quote: The PBIT margins stood at a healthy double -digit at 12.8% for the year, up by almost 600 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Maize procurement prices down 10-15% from previous year due to 20% higher crop
items.quote: The prices that we are seeing now for the first crop, what we're procuring for Bihar is substantially 10-12-15% lower than the prices that we were procuring earlier.

items.statement: Co238 variety reduced from 77% to below 50% of cane area, targeting optimal levels in two years
items.quote: Last year, it was 77%. In the coming year, it will be just below 50%. And we expect that in two years' time, we'll be at absolutely optimal levels.

items.statement: Rani Nangal distillery commissioned at full capacity, running on grain for next few months
items.quote: The Rani Nangal distillery is now functioning at full capacity. It is commissioned at the very onset of this quarter and is running extremely well. We have started these operations on grain and intend to continue with this for the next few months.

items.statement: No fresh capex considered at this point; all previous capex under execution
items.quote: I should mention that there is no fresh capex that has been considered at this particular point. It is all the previous capex that I've spoken about in previous conference calls, which is under execution by the Company.

items.statement: Expect surge in Water business opportunities post-election results with new funding from Central and State Governments
items.quote: We anticipate that post -election results, there will be a surge in business opportunities and new funding is expected to flow both Central and State Governments.

items.statement: Current sugar realisations at ~₹3,950/quintal refined and ₹3,900 sulphitation; expect prices to hold or improve
items.quote: Current sugar reali sations today stand at approximately ₹ 3,950 per quintal, for refined sugar at ₹ 3,900 for sulphitation sugar.

items.statement: Sugar inventories building domestically; ISMA requested 2 MMT export which is under government consideration
items.quote: As a result, as I'm sure you all know, ISMA has written to the Government requesting a n export of 2 million metric tonnes, which we hope is under consideration.

items.statement: Aim to double revenue to $200M and triple PAT to INR160-180 crores by FY26
items.quote: So we are aiming for anywhere between INR160 crores to INR180 crores of PAT by FY'26.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 15-15.5% in FY25, up from 13.7% in FY24
items.quote: So we will look at getting to about 15% or anywhere in the range of 15% to 15.5% on EBITDA this year.

items.statement: Expect better than industry growth in FY25 (industry ~14-15%), back-ended to H2
items.quote: So if the industry growth rate is 14%-15%, we expect to grow better than that. And in certain verticals, yes, the growth will be back-ended specifically when it comes to PES, for example.

items.statement: Confirmed order book increased 27% to INR749 crores, executable in FY25
items.quote: Our confirmed order book across all entities stands at INR749 crores as against INR589 crores at the beginning of the year, an increase of 27%.

items.statement: Executable defence production orders of INR272 crores over 12-18 months
items.quote: It would be generally in the range of 12 months to 18 months.

items.statement: Plan to open marketing office in Dubai in FY25 for energy vertical
items.quote: The company, considering the potential of this vertical has positioned the business unit head in Dubai to enhance current relationships and build new relationships in the Middle East and seeks to open a marketing office in Dubai in FY '25.

items.statement: Defence production EBITDA margin ~30% on INR112 crores revenue in FY24
items.quote: So essentially, for FY '24 the production revenues was INR112 crores on which we made an EBITDA of INR33.18 crores which is about 30%.

items.statement: Digital investments to be EBITDA neutral to positive in FY25 vs negative in FY24
items.quote: As stated earlier with the digital investments was negative to EBITDA in FY' 24, the same as expected to be neutral to positive in FY'25.

items.statement: Heavy engineering growth expected to return in H2 FY25 after US capex slowdown
items.quote: That growth will be muted in this vertical in the first two quarters of FY '25, we expect growth to return to this vertical in the second half of the financial year FY '25.

items.statement: PES production growth expected to return in later part of FY25 as semiconductor inventory clears
items.quote: We expect that growth will return to this vertical during the later part of FY'25 with fleshing out of built-up inventories.

items.statement: Revenue from new customers increased 5x to INR69 crores (7% of revenue) in FY24
items.quote: The outcome of this can be seen from revenue from new customers increasing by 5x from INR14 crores in FY'23 to INR69 crores in FY'24 and contributing to 7% of revenue in FY' 24 versus 2% in FY'23.

items.statement: Anti-drone addressable opportunity INR3,000 crores over 5 years in India, plus exports
items.quote: The addressable opportunity in this area within India is about INR 3,000 crores for the next five years, not to speak of potential for exports.

items.statement: QIP raised INR220 crores; INR120 crores debt retired, additional INR50 crores by Sep 2024
items.value: INR120 crores retired, INR50 crores more by Sep 2024
items.quote: From the QIP proceeds the company has since retired INR120 crores in long-term debt to Investec and bank borrowings and will further retire a minimum amount of INR50 crores in September of 2024.

items.statement: Finance cost to reduce by ~50% in FY25 after debt repayment
items.quote: Upon the retirement of debt in FY '25 we expect that these INR56 crores of finance cost and what is there on the P&L will reduce by at least 50%.

items.statement: Attrition fell from 20% to 16% in FY24; headcount 3,000+ with 500+ net billable adds
items.quote: Our attrition has fallen from 20% in FY' 23 to 16% in FY' 24. There is substantial headroom for growth in each of these verticals we serve.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 12% to 15% with bulk of growth in H2
items.quote: I did talk about the FY '25 outlook, but for completeness, we expect to grow 12% to 15%. Bulk of the growth w ill come in

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA guided at INR 950-1,000 crores
items.quote: We expect EBITDA margins to be about INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 US business revenue guided at $285-300 million
items.quote: We are guiding the US business to be approximately in the range of $285 million to $300 million.

items.statement: FY25 retained business EBITDA guided at INR 750-800 crores
items.quote: Consequently, the retained business will deliver approximately INR750 crores to INR800 crores of EBITDA and we have that run rate already now.

items.statement: FY25 debt-to-EBITDA guided under 2x
items.quote: Consequently, we are now guiding FY '25 for debt to EBITDA under 2x.

items.statement: US business target of $400 million in next 2-3 years
items.quote: We have guided that we'll get to a $400 million size in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: OneSource revenue target of $400 million within 3 years of listing
items.quote: Overall, we have guided $400 million of revenues, three years from the time of listing of OneSource if I'm not mistaken in the last updates.

items.statement: FY25 capex of ~INR 200 crores planned
items.quote: We target to reduce our debt by an additional INR500 crores after spending almost INR200 crores in c apex this

items.statement: Target to reach 21.5% EBITDA margin in next 12-18 months via 200-250 bps cost improvement
items.quote: Like I said, Nitin, we probably have about 200 to 250 basis points of margin expansion through cost improvements and completion of network optimization. And that is why we said our dream goal is to get to our 21.5% peak EBITDA percentage-wise.

items.statement: Institutional business expects significantly higher tender allocation for next two years with uptick in H2
items.quote: I'm now pleased to announce that we see a significantly higher allocation on this program for the next two years and you'll see more upticks in this part of the business in the second half.

items.statement: Endo portfolio has 10-15 viable products meeting criteria but limited to 3-4 launches per year
items.quote: We have a lot of products. I would say 10 to 15 products at least on the endo portfolio that will meet our criteria. But these products in the U.S., we are constrained by the speed in which we can launch these products because we only have the capacity to launch three or four new products a year.

items.statement: Drug-device capacity expanding from 40M to 200M units in FY26
items.quote: Our drug device combinations are about 40 million unit capacity and we will complete an expansion in FY'26 to take it to 200 million units.

items.statement: Red Sea shipping crisis largely behind; premiums dropped dramatically but vigilance maintained
items.quote: The Red Sea crisis is now, I would like to say behind. The shipping premiums have dropped quite dramatically. But yes, this is the nature of the beast. So we have to be vigilant. For now, it's business as usual.

items.statement: OneSource demerger: SEBI approval received; NCLT filing in next couple of weeks; listing expected in 3-4 quarters plus 60 days
items.quote: We expect to file in court, the necessary documentation this quarter. Typically, it can take anywhere from 3 to 4 quarters for the court process to get completed and about 60 days for the stock exchanges to list the stock.

items.statement: Biologics CDMO seeing significant new RFPs due to China-plus-one shift from Biosecurity Act
items.quote: We are seeing significant amount of new RFPs for biologics. And I think the China Plus One on the biologics is playing through. We haven't seen so many RFPs in the last 1 year that we have seen in the last 2 quarters.

items.statement: US pricing strategy: exit products facing irrational price challenges; no price erosion modeled
items.quote: Well, the US business is not a function of price erosion for us is that when we are challenged heavily, we exit the product. So we just get off a product. And if you look at IMS, you'll see us not in products that we were there last year if we are being challenged on pricing.

items.statement: Completed INR 1,500 crore capital raise via INR 900 crore preferential allotment and INR 600 crore QIP in 6 months
items.quote: I'm also pleased to announce that we completed our capital raising program, an ambitious program of INR 1,500 crores in a record 6 months' time. items.statement: Exercised call option on INR 720 crore Tier 2 bonds at 12% coupon between November and February
items.quote: We also had the opportunity to exercise call option on Tier 2 bonds, and we did so during the financial year between November and February, totalling INR 720 crores at a coupon of 12%.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 3.5% to 3.7% for FY25 despite deposit cost pressure
items.quote: So we believe that we'll continue to grow and the NIM would continue to be at the same 3.5% to 3.7% range, Darshan.

items.quote: But our guidance for this financial year, by the end of the financial year, 4 quarters from now, we should see sub-50 or closer to 50, which again, would be due to a lot of rationalization, a lot of digitized processes and ensuring that our cost is under control.

items.statement: ROA guidance maintained at 1.2% to 1.4%
items.quote: The ROA has been maintained about 1.22%. Our guidance has been 1.2% to 1.4%, we are sticking to that guidance.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance: hovering around 0.85% to 1.00% for FY25
items.quote: So, I guess we would be hovering around between 0.85 to 100 bps.

items.statement: Asset quality targets: GNPA to ~3%, NNPA to 1-1.2% going forward
items.quote: I guess that we want to get the GNPA to about 3% and NNPA to closer to 1% to 1.2%. So, this is how it will play out as we go forward.

items.statement: Annual NIM at 3.51%, within guided 3.5-3.7% range; loan yield 9.89%, cost of funds 5.40% for FY24
items.quote: Our NIM, which is a more important metric, stand at about 3.51% annually, which is in line with the guidance that we have given of 3.5% to 3.7%. We are happy to report that our loan yields have continued to be at the same level at 9.89%.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 exit loan yield ~9.75%, cost of funds ~5.55%
items.quote: Quarter will be around 5.55% for the quarter on cost of funds and loan yields around 9.75%.

items.statement: Board recommended 55% dividend for FY24, up from 50% last year
items.quote: Sandeep, we have considered this, and we are also happy to announce that the Board has recommended a dividend of 55% today, and this will be recommended to the shareholders for approval, and this is much more than the 50%, which was declared last year.
