items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 24% vs 20% FY23; FY25 margin expected at least 24-25% if prices sustain
items.quote: We believe that whatever margins we have achieved in the current financial year should be minimum there. Now that depends on the selling price as well. So, if the selling price for some reason or the other goes down, then the margin can go down. Otherwise, we are quite set to achieve the margin of over 24%-25% if the current price is sustained.

items.statement: Pellet realization up 8% to over Rs 10,000/t; other product realizations fell; Q1 FY25 prices ~10% higher than Q4 FY24 across chain
items.quote: For Q1, the market has definitely gone up because there has been a certain demand for finished steel post Holi and people are quite bullish going forward. So, prices are almost 10% up compared to Q4 versus Q1 of FY25 across the chain. Be it iron ore pellet, be it DRI, be it billets, or be it finished steel. So, prices are almost 10% up across the chain post Holi, which is so Q4 versus Q1, you can

items.statement: World Steel Association forecasts India steel demand +8.2% CY24, +8.3% CY25; domestic pellet prices well supported
items.quote: World Steel Association forecasts India's steel demand to increase by 8.2% in calendar 24 and in 25 to 144 million tons and 156 million tons respectively. World Steel Association further predicts that India's steel industry will experience significant expansion propelled by sustained growth across all sectors resilient on steel, particularly driven by robust in infrastructure investment.

items.statement: Pellet sales 50% low grade (56 Fe) / 50% high grade (63 Fe); new pellet plant will shift mix to ~25% low grade, rest high grade
items.quote: So, yes, so the new plant which we are setting up, we will be rather producing higher grade pellets only. So, further, once the capacity is in line, then the ratio will give about 25 of 63, and the remaining will be the high grade. Once the annual capacity goes up and the new plant comes into production in FY26.

items.statement: Environmental approvals delayed by elections; Boria Tibu mine restart at least 3 years away (FY28); no further expansion at Siltara/Urla due to CPA status
items.quote: On the Boria Tibu side, as we mentioned a few months back, we have shut down operations at the moment because of the mines being commercially unviable because the mines have huge quantities of low-grades compared to the Ari Dongri mines. So, we are putting up a beneficial plant as well there for which the designing has already been done. We have started the paperwork to apply for the permissions.

items.statement: Net cash >Rs 1,000 cr; FY25 capex funded internally; integrated steel plant may need up to Rs 1,500 cr debt (<0.3x net worth) after 2 years
items.quote: So, we don't think that we'll be able to require to take more than Rs. 1,500 crore kind of debt in order to complete the new project. So, that's everything should go from the internal accrual. That's what is our expectation is as of now. Now this figure can change somewhere here and there depending on the operating margins etc. So, if we are able to maybe require to take a debt of Rs. 1,500 crore

items.statement: Integrated steel plant (2 mt HR coil via blast furnace) revenue ~Rs 10,000 cr at Rs 50,000/t; target EBITDA ~Rs 10,000/t long-term; commissioning H2 FY28 partial, FY29 full
items.quote: I think second half of FY28 partial and then FY29 will be the full revenue once we are able to operate 100% capacity.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target INR6,000-6,200 crores with 15-18% CAGR and EBITDA margin 10-12%
items.quote: we are solidly on track on this strategy that we presented to all of you in the month of February. The strategy remains exactly the same.

items.statement: FY25 capex plan INR500-550 crores over four years; India INR70-90 crores plus IT capex, Bangladesh 1,000-1,500 machines
items.quote: as a part of our four- year plan we said we'll be investing anywhere between INR500 crores to INR550 crores in next four year s. Coming specific to FY '24-'25, in India, we are looking at a capex between -- commitment to the capex around INR70 crores to INR90

items.statement: Current production capacity 84 million pieces, up from 80 million; targeting 120-140 million by FY28
items.quote: if you go back one year, one and half year, we had the kind of infrastructure that we had, we could maximize it towards 80 million pieces of production. Now as I speak to you today, this is enhanced already to about 84 million pieces approximately.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin improved 100 bps to 9.2% in FY24; target 10-12% by FY28
items.quote: our adjusted EBITDA margins saw a year -on-year improvement of 100 basis points, rising fro m 8.2% in FY23 to 9.2% in FY24

items.statement: Demand healthy post US inventory correction; global growth low single digit; US retailers cautious due to elections
items.quote: I think the demand is at this point of time healthy. I think the biggest factor that we had in 2023 was the over inventory situation that we are facing in the US retailer. So that I think, now we are completely over with

items.statement: ~50% of garments supplied have design input (partial or complete) from Pearl Global
items.quote: So when we are supplying to the customers today where we have some kind of design input maybe a partial one or a complete one so that number today offhand from top of my head I would be say close to about 50% in which we had certain role to play.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 30 in FY24 from 38 in FY23; target 35-40 days steady state; debtor days target ~30
items.quote: Net working capital days decreased from 38 days in FY23 to 30 days in FY24. Debtor increased to 28 days in FY24 from 24 days in FY23. Inventory days decreased to 53 days in FY24 from 59 days in FY23.

items.statement: Gross debt stable at INR445 crores; net debt/EBITDA 0.25x; finance cost INR83 crores includes INR13.6 crores lease interest
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our gross debt is similar to last year level of INR445 crores in FY24 versus INR448 crores in FY23. Net debt to EBITDA stand at 0.25 times for FY24.

items.statement: Dividend INR38.1 crores (22.5% of consolidated PAT) in FY24; policy minimum 20% of PAT
items.quote: We are happy to share that in the fiscal year of FY'24, we distributed a dividend amounting to INR38.1 crores which is 22.5% of our consolidated profit after tax.

items.statement: Bangladesh wage hike impact 12-15% of wage bill (~1-1.5% of revenue); offset by automation, efficiency, Taka devaluation
items.quote: the increase in Bangladesh wages, if you remember, would create an impact between 12% to 15% of our wage bills. Overall, fro m a profit and loss perspective, it changes by approximately 1% to 1.5% when we compare to the top line

items.statement: FY24 PPE capex INR115 crores + INR1.25 crores IT; India INR42 crores (50% growth), Bangladesh INR40 crores (55% automation), Indonesia INR16 crores, Vietnam INR13 crores, Guatemala INR4 crores
items.quote: During the year, we have incurred a property plant and equipment capex of INR115 crores and additional INR1.25 crores approximately towards other IT related capex.

items.statement: Focus on top-tier customers growing wallet share; reducing exposure to financially weak or risky customers
items.quote: We will continue to add and grow with customers who are getting stronger in the world market. We will stay away and decrease our exposure for anyone which is becoming financially weak or we feel they are risky.

items.statement: Bangladesh Bank introduced Crawling Peg exchange rate system (Taka ~117/USD) and market-based interest rates per IMF conditions
items.quote: Bangladesh Bank has unveiled the Crawling Peg Exchange Rate System and an odd bank to buy and sell US dollars freely nearly Taka 117. A Crawling Peg System is a method of exchange rate adjustment that allows a currency with a fixed exchange rate to fluctuate within a band of rates.

items.statement: All shipping on FOB terms; Red Sea crisis adds ~1 week transit but no cost impact; Guatemala transit to US just over a week
items.quote: for us, there is no effect of cost for the Red Sea situation that we are facing since last one year because all our shipping are in FOB terms. As long as we can deliver the goods faster, they need actually one week early

items.statement: India attrition/absenteeism ~double global levels (others <4%); expanding to interior states for local labor to reduce attrition
items.quote: We are able to control below 4%. Whereas India we are still not able to bring down to that level at all. We are almost like double than that number at this point of time.

items.statement: US retailers cautious due to elections, geopolitics, high interest rates; Europe/UK conservative but strong players growing
items.quote: most of the industry captains are still a little conservative and they're very cautious, I would say, they are doing a very cautiously optimistic kind of approach towards the business and that's mainly because of the elections, because of some of the geopolitics that is going on at this point of time and the inflation interest rates still continues to be high

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth 10-15% and EBITDA margin 10-12%
items.quote: We can give guidance, so guidance is that we just said that we will be growing by 10% to 15% in next financial year and we are targeting an EBITDA of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Conservative FY25 revenue Rs 1,800-1,900 crore
items.quote: So, Rs. 1,800 - Rs. 1,900 crores is what we are saying conservatively we should be looking at.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA Rs 180-200 crore
items.quote: Yes, that would be in that region. Yes, correct. 10% to 12% would be a fair estimate.

items.statement: Italy repurpose $2-3 million; China repurpose ~Rs 25 crore ($3 million)
items.quote: So, in Europe, it's probably in the region of between $2 million to $3 million and in China, it would be in the region of about Rs. 25 crores or so, another $3 million.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs 30-40 crore
items.quote: we'll be doing like Rs. 30- Rs. 40 crores of CAPEX only

items.statement: Vanillin FY25 target 2,500 tons at $9-9.5/kg avg price
items.quote: I think average price as we see it going forward in this year should be in the range of between $9 to $9.5.

items.statement: Blends FY25 revenue target Rs 1,000+ crore
items.quote: we closed the blends business at about Rs. 780 crores odd, which this year we expect it to grow to at least about Rs. 1,000 crores plus.

items.statement: Vanillin at $9 price and 45% utilization yields ~10% margin ($7.5-8 cost)
items.quote: the cost should be around $7.5 to $8, so we have a 10% margin there, it's about a dollar there and Rs. 100 negative turns into Rs. 80 positive there.

items.statement: Blends EBITDA margin high teens (18-19%)
items.quote: I think it will be in the high teens like I've mentioned earlier. So, if you are at Rs. 1,100-1,000 crores, it will be Rs. 180 to Rs. 190 crores.

items.statement: Demand improvement expected towards end of FY25; destocking largely done
items.quote: towards the end of this year, I think demand situation also should improve, the destocking that has happened or is happening currently in some of the markets would be done by then

items.statement: Debt reduction minimal; repaying ~Rs 25 crore long-term loans FY25; no fresh loans planned
items.quote: on a year-to-year basis, our long-term borrowing, we will be repaying around Rs. 25 crores of loan. So, if at all the reduction will be that we are not planning any fresh loans at this stage

items.statement: Negolyte: supplied commercial lot to Lockheed Martin; bigger facility discussions to start after Q2 FY25 installation
items.quote: We've supplied them large commercial lot which goes into their first battery that has been done shipped in this quarter and that will get installed in Q2 of this financial year by July, August and thereafter discussions will st art on looking at a bigger

items.statement: Vegetable segment expected to grow at least 20% year-on-year going forward
items.quote: Definitely, we see a good growth in vegetable segment, at least 20% growth going forward year-on-year.

items.statement: Non-cotton segment volume growth expected to be more than 10% in FY25
items.quote: If you see like non-cotton segment, volume growth is more than 10% across.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA expected to be higher than current levels in FY25
items.quote: So definitely, we see good year coming. And in terms of what you say EBITDA, definitely, this will be higher than what it is now.

items.statement: Cotton volumes expected to decline 4-5% in FY25 due to production shortage
items.quote: As of now, we see a slight degrowth in that because we don't have exact inventory. We have done 52 to 53 lakh packets in cotton last year. So we have inventory close to 47 or 49 lakhs. I don't know the exact number, something close to that. So we'll be down by 4% to 5% as compared to previous year.

items.statement: Cotton EBITDA margin expected to be slightly down due to higher production costs
items.quote: Slightly down as compared to previous year because as I said that we might realize more in the market as compared to previous year, a couple of rupees having the increase in the price but the production cost has also gone up. So there's a slight impact on the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Cotton production costs increased by Rs. 60-70 per packet versus previous year
items.quote: But one thing we need to observe this year, the cotton production costs have also gone up. So a significant hike is there in the production costs as compared to previous year, the Rs. 60, Rs. 70 is more than a packet. We incur more than Rs. 60, Rs.70 per packet.

items.statement: Non-cotton segment production cost increases expected to be passed on to farmers
items.quote: Even though the production costs are up in those crops, we'll be able to pass it on to the farmer. So we don't see any pressure on the non-cotton segment.

items.statement: Good demand across all crops except cotton where production is insufficient
items.quote: We see good demand for across all the crops, but the main constraint is in cotton. We don't have enough production for cotton for this year. That's the only crop where we are seeing a bit of difficulty. Whereas other crops, the demand is also good, and we have enough production for that.

items.statement: Maize acreages expected to grow long-term due to ethanol demand and stable prices above MSP
items.quote: Going forward, maize is a very good crop by even government has initiated ethanol plants. So as of now the estimate is like more than 33% of the total production will be utilized by ethanol when it is fully commissioned. So definitely, there will be more pressure to produce maize. And as a crop now with the stable prices and these are not above the MSPs so it is much lucrative for the farmer. So d

items.statement: New product contribution in maize increased from 33.87% to 47.96% of total volumes
items.quote: The contribution of new products was up from 33.87% to 47.96% of the total volumes in maize crop.

items.statement: More than 90% of vegetable seed revenues from own R&D developed seeds
items.quote: More than 90% of the revenues are our own seeds. There are some seeds like cabbage and cauliflower that we import. But otherwise, it's all our own seeds.

items.statement: Rs. 208 crores capex over FY23-24 for new office, plants and cold storage; mostly commissioned and operational
items.quote: So there are a couple of things. One is the new office, which we are constructing, that we will move into next 1 or 2 months. The other thing is all about the plant. We have set up plants and cold storage in the last couple of years. So that the main capex what we have done. All the plants and most of the plants are already commissioned. From this year, we are already using it.

items.statement: Advances from customers at Rs. 160-180 crores as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: I just need to check the exact number, it should be close to like Rs. 160 crores to Rs. 180 crores.

items.statement: Cotton seed production shortage across industry due to pest infestation and difficult conditions
items.quote: Yes, it's across the industry, we see a shortage across the industry. It's not only for Kaveri. We had a very bad year in terms of the production. So entire production got affected, it was India. And there was pests infected and different types of difficulty in producing.

items.statement: Bangladesh subsidiary incorporated; own brand and research expected in 2-3 years
items.quote: So we want to pick up our own brand, develop our own brand and research there. So that's the reason we have set up a subsidiary company. So it may take two to three years to get the entire base and first, we will do marketing, then we will start research there.

items.statement: Cotton market share recovery to 17-18% expected in 2-3 years with new hybrid pipeline
items.quote: Definitely, because we have introduced many hybrids and still there are some more pipeline headwinds. So we are pretty confident going to that market shares in the coming years. They are very promising hybrids, some are already tested and launched in the market that we are going to see the sale in the next coming 2 to 3 years for that.

items.statement: Expect significant improved consolidated financial performance in FY25 due to industry growth, new businesses, JV turning profitable, lithium-ion capacity increase, tool room orders, and aftermarket expansion
items.quote: In FY'25, we expect a significant improved consolidated financial performance due to the industry growth and due to the efforts, that I have already touched upon.

items.statement: Expect capacity utilization more than 80% for full year FY25 based on orders in hand
items.quote: So internally the orders which we have in our hands, so we expect the next year capacity utilization should be more than 80% for the full year basis.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin increased from 8.8% in Q4FY23 to 9.4% in Q4FY24, targeting 10% range for the year
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that our stand-alone EBITDA margin has increased from 8.8% in Q4FY23 to 9.4% in the Q4FY24, which we always said that in this year, we will be somewhere in the 10% range of EBITDA for this year.

items.statement: Working on 28 projects in FY25, with 10 models launching this financial year across Maruti, Tata, Renault, Nissan, Hyundai and Honda
items.quote: For the automotive business, which is the primary business for the company, we are working on 28 projects in this financial year. And most of these vehicles will be -- out of these, 10 models will be launched in this financial year.

items.statement: Aftermarket business currently 3% of total group sales, targeting at least 10% in next 3-4 years
items.quote: Currently, it is about 3% of the total group sal es. See, we started this about three to four years back ago. And right now, it's 3%, but we expect this to become at least 10% of the total revenue in the next three to four years

items.statement: Industry growth officially 8-9% but may not achieve due to elections and other factors; non-auto divisions to play key role in growth strategy
items.quote: The official figures are somewhere in the range of 8% to 9% of growth. But due to elections and due to other factors, there might, the industry may not be able to achieve 8% to 9% growth in this year.

items.statement: Settled inflationary cost compensation with Maruti for certain parts, expecting further corrections by Q2 or Q3
items.quote: For the inflationary cost side, we have settled with the Maruti. So there are certain parts that's also there where we are discussing with Maruti for the price increase side.

items.statement: Capex spending will be aligned with OEMs' capex plans
items.quote: Our Capex spending will be aligned with the OEMs' Capex plans.

items.statement: JV company expected to become profitable in current financial year based on past 50 days trends
items.quote: I am sure that based on the trends which are available in the past 50 days, the JV company will become profitable this year and will start positive contribution to the group.

items.statement: Lithium-ion battery business shifted focus to solar and ESS segments, seeing good traction since April with strong May inquiries
items.quote: So now we have shifted our primary focus to the solar and the ESS side. As you know, the government is focusing on solar power in a very big way by providing rooftop solar and on-grid and off-grid solutions to the customers.

items.statement: Margins almost intact in Q1 for standalone, JV margins improving, tool room has 50% order book of annual targets, aftermarket monthly run rate increasing 10-20%
items.quote: On the JV , on PPAP standalone company, also, margins are almost intact. On the JV company, margins are getting better because we were able to implement the last year's strateg ies starting from 1st of April this

items.statement: Commercial toolroom division renamed Meraki Precision Molds with confirmed orders for 50% of annual targets
items.quote: I'm happy to inform you that we already have confirmed orders to achieve 50% of our annual targets in this division, and we should be doing good business in this as well.

items.statement: Developed parts for 14 models launched in FY24, developing for 10 models in FY25, discussing many more projects
items.quote: In total, we have developed parts for 14 models, which were launched in the FY'24 and are developing parts for 10 models in FY'25 and are discussing on many more projects which are supposed to get decided in FY'25 with all our customers.

items.statement: Content per vehicle increasing: Maruti EV at INR4,600 (vs INR2,500-3,000), Tata at INR6,000, Honda at INR4,500-5,000
items.quote: Maruti side, now the new EV, which we are going to launch this year, we have our contribution of INR4,600 per vehicle, which generally used to be about INR2,500 to INR3,000. And Tata vehicles, which is going to get launched this year, the new vehicle. In fact, the mass production is going to start next month in June. Our per car contribution is roughly INR6,000

items.statement: Net loss of INR4.7 crores due to one-time deferred tax of INR7.9 crores, non-cash item to be reversed in subsequent years
items.quote: Our loss for the year stood at INR4.7 crores due to a one-time deferred tax of INR7.9 crores, which will be reversed and adjusted in the subsequent years.

items.statement: Started working with Mahindra & Mahindra at Tier 2 level, expect to become Tier 1 in current financial year
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have also started working with Mahindra & Mahindra, however, at the Tier 2 level currently, and we expect to become Tier 1 in the current financial year.

items.statement: Capex target for FY25 is INR11,761 Crore on consolidated basis
items.quote: Our capex target for FY'25 is to the tune of INR11,761 Crore and this expenditure does not include any expenditure on pumped storage projects because it will take some time to complete the DPR of our first pump storage project i.e. Indra Sagar Omkareshwar pumped storage project.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 is in the range of INR13,317 Crore
items.quote: For FY '26, our capex is in the range of INR13,317 Crore. So, again, it will be in the same range. There is a plan for INR13,000 Crore plus.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR13,000-15,000 Crore expected for next 7-8 years
items.quote: In the next 7 to 8 years, it is in the same range. We will be incurring capex in the range of INR13,000 to INR15,000 Crore every year.

items.statement: ROE expected at 10-11% for FY25 consolidated
items.quote: At company level, it will be in the range of 10% to 11%.

items.statement: FY25 capex breakup: Parbati-II INR456 Cr, Subansiri INR1,000 Cr, Dibang INR950 Cr, new projects INR950 Cr, solar INR1,623 Cr, Chenab Valley INR3,371 Cr, BSUL solar INR550 Cr, Lanco Teesta-VI INR1,198 Cr, Rangit-IV INR460 Cr, Ratle INR950 Cr
items.quote: We have kept INR456 Crore for the Parbati-II Project. Then, INR1,000 Crore for Subansiri Lower; INR950 Crore for Dibang. Then, we have kept around INR950 Crore for new upcoming projects, which include Sawalkot, Dugar, Dulhasti Stage-II, etc. Then we have kept INR1,623 Crore for solar projects, which include 1000 CPEC Scheme projects and other projects which we have won in bidding process in Gujara

items.statement: PPAs signed for 3,000 MW RE capacity, 1,400 MW in process, total 4,400 MW against 10,000 MW allocated by MNRE
items.quote: We have already signed PPA and PSA for 3,000 megawatt capacity in the REI mode and for 1,400 megawatt, the process is going on. So you can say that we will be able to sign PPA and PSA for 4,400 megawatt against the capacity, which was allocated by the MNRE to the tune of 10,000 megawatt.

items.statement: Subansiri tariff INR5.60/unit, Parbati-II INR6.59/unit; will re-engineer to lower Parbati-II tariff to ~INR6/unit via lower O&M for 5 years and longer depreciation
items.quote: In case of Subansiri, rate is slightly higher, i.e. around INR5.60 per unit. But we will do some reengineering to lower the tariff and to get the power sold and in respect of Parbati-II, the rate is INR6.59 per unit. So, we will do some reengineering to lower the tariff. We will accept lower operation maintenance charges for the first 5 years and we can plan for a longer period of depreciation. So

items.statement: No new capacity addition before March'25, so no top-line growth from new plants in FY25 except few MW solar
items.quote: As we have discussed, there is no new capacity being added prior to March'25. So, there will not be any increase in the top line because capacity is the same. Only few megawatt of the solar can be added.

items.statement: FY24 generation 21,773 MU (-12% YoY) due to Teesta-V flash flood and lower water availability; PAF 77.6% vs 88.75% YoY; Revenue INR8,405 Cr (-10% YoY); PAT INR3,744 Cr (-2% YoY)
items.quote: During FY'24, our power stations have achieved generation of 21,773 million units as against 24,619 million units generated in corresponding period of previous financial year which is lower by about 12% i.e. 2,846 million units. This is mainly due to heavy flash flood in Teesta basin in October '23, which has resulted into complete shutdown of Teesta-V Power Station.

items.statement: FY25 group operating revenue guidance of at least INR4,000 crores (PGEA INR3,400 crores + Goodworth INR1,600 crores), 46% growth over FY24
items.quote: For FY25, our operating revenue guidance starts at least INR3,400 crore s in PGEA, and another INR1,600 crores in our GB company, Good worth Electronics, employing INR4,000 crore s of group operating revenue, which is a growth of 46% over FY24

items.statement: FY25 consolidated net profit guidance of at least INR200 crores for PG Electroplast, 46% growth over FY24
items.quote: We are also guiding for consolidated net profit of at least INR200 crores in PG Electroplast, which is a growth of 46% over FY24 net profit of INR137 crores.

items.statement: FY25 product business revenue guidance of INR2,400 crores, 44% growth from INR1,668 crores in FY24
items.quote: The growth in product business, i.e., washing machines, room air conditioners, and air coolers is expected to be around 44% from INR1,668 crores in FY24 to INR2,400 crores in FY25.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of INR370-380 crores, largely internally funded, including new integrated AC unit in Rajasthan and washing machine expansion to 2 million units in Greater Noida
items.quote: capex guidance for FY25 is in the range of INR370 to INR380 crores, and the company has planned to further expand room AC capacity by setting up a new integrated unit in Rajasthan. The company is also expanding their washing machine capacity from 1.2 million units to 2 million units with a new greenfield facility being planned in Greater Noida.

items.statement: Order book and visibility for product business remains robust, on track to accelerate product business growth significantly in FY25
items.quote: Order book and visibility for product business remains robust, and the company is on track to accelerate product business growth significantly in current financial year also.

items.statement: Operating margins expected to have slight upward bias in FY25 due to TV business exit, despite new facility ramp-up
items.quote: Actually next year in the company PG Electroplast, operating margins, we are having a slight upwards bias for the full year. And one of the main reasons for that is that TV business, which is a low margin business, is no more a part of PG Electroplast.

items.statement: Raw material cost improved 1.35% as percentage of revenue in FY24; copper price increases are pass-through with fixed conversion cost per unit
items.quote: On a full year basis, it is a 1.35% improvement in the cost of raw material as a percentage of revenue versus the same percent last year. But if the copper prices go up, then our sales also goes up. Actually in our business as I have been explaining, it is the fixed amount per unit which I get to make a product. I don't get a percentage. So raw material is a pass-through.

items.statement: TV business (10%+ of FY24 revenue) moving to Goodworth JV; product business to drive growth with plastic molding 10-15% growth and electronics declining
items.quote: Product business will continue to drive the growth. We don't expect the plastic component to have much growth and electronics will actually decline because of the TV business going away and the plastic molding and components is likely to see probably about 10% -15% growth.

items.statement: IT hardware PLI orders delayed as clients await policy/political clarity post-elections; updates expected in 2-3 months
items.quote: will be updating you may be after this election and things are over. Because we are in talk with several clients but none of the clients are making any decision. They are all waiting for the policy and political clarity to happen and hopefully in the nex t 2-3 months we will be updating you more on that

items.statement: Segment margins: plastic molding ~7.5%, electronics ~2%, product business drives remaining margin
items.quote: So this year you can say plastic molding is about 7.5% margin business electronics is about 2% and then rest of the margin whichever way you look is coming from the product business

items.statement: Seasonality shifted forward - AC season now starts late January and continues into late June vs earlier December-April
items.quote: The seasonality still remains very much. It's just that seasonality has shifted forward, earlier business used to start in early December and then it used to end last till April end or mid May. Now this year the business has started late January and is probably continuing into the late June as it looks like.

items.statement: Of FY25 INR380 crore capex, ~INR170-180 crores for land/building (1M sq ft) for future growth optionality; significant completion targeted in FY25
items.quote: Out of the INR380 crores that I talked about, almost INR180 crores will be or INR170 crores will be going in the land and building. And we hope that we should be able to complete significant portion of the building in the next year itself.

items.statement: Aim to double AUM in FY25
items.quote: We are again aiming to double the AUM in current financial year.

items.statement: Plan to raise INR150 crores equity in H1 FY25
items.quote: Now we soon plan to raise another INR150 crores in H1 25 to fund our FY 25 extension plan, and process for the same is initiated.

items.statement: Plan to add 60-75 new branches in FY25
items.quote: Further, we plan to add 60 to 75 new branches in existing and new states this year.

items.statement: AUM grew 112% YoY to INR730 crores in FY24
items.quote: AUM of the company increased 112% year-on-year to INR730 crores including managed book up from INR344 crores in FY23

items.statement: Secured loans share to exceed 40% of AUM by end of FY25
items.quote: We will continue to increase the share of secured loans to over 40% by the end of financial year 25.

items.statement: Expect at least 100 bps reduction in incremental borrowing cost in FY25
items.quote: We expect at least 100% basis point reduction in incremental cost of borrowing this year, driven by rating upgrade and increasing scale.

items.statement: Opex to reach single digits over medium term
items.quote: We still expect this over a medium term to come into single digit number, despite the expansion in branches.

items.statement: Credit gap in INR1-10 lakh segment is INR18 trillion
items.quote: Overall market size is about 22 trillion and out of which only 4 trillion is covered. So as for the crystal study, so that means we are sitting on a 18 trillion sorry, yes, 18 trillion kind of gap in that segment.

items.statement: 3-year AUM target of INR4000 crores with two-thirds secured
items.quote: In terms of next 3 years, we want the AUM to reach around INR4000 crores. And by that time definitely majority. But maybe two-third of our portfolio will look like secured.

items.statement: Tax benefits from carried forward losses to end in FY25
items.quote: So, FY 26, the tax will 100% normalize. This will be the last year where we will have tax benefit because of our activity losses.

items.statement: Post write-off recovery rate ~10% on unsecured loans
items.quote: So, what has been our experience is typically once we completely write off the loan, there is roughly around 10% of that write-off is something which is typically recovered, and which is written back.

items.statement: Branch breakeven at ~INR2-2.5 crores AUM in 6 months
items.quote: So, generally if you calculate the number on a INR2 crores kind of AUM we are able to breakeven to start with. And obviously then opex also increases over a period of time, but if you do the math there it takes approximately 6 months for a branch to breakeven.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 2x to 3x market growth; market expected to grow ~3%
items.quote: Our trajectory, our guidance has been to grow 2-3x the market growth, which we have done in the last years as well, and we continue to aim that.

items.statement: Aiming for double-digit growth if market grows at 4%, high single digits if market at 2-3%
items.quote: If the market, let's say, get some tailwind, and market grows at 4%, we will definitely aim at a double-digit growth. And if the market is at 2% to 3%, then high single digits that's what we are currently aiming at.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 13.5% in Q4 FY24, tracking towards higher end of 12-14% guided band
items.quote: our EBITDA margin sequentially went up 13.5%, tracking towards the higher band, which we talk about 12% to 14%

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~3.5% YoY but dipped 1.6% sequentially due to crude volatility
items.quote: we have improved our gross margins by nearly 3.5% over the year and sequentially, we see a slight dip because the crude was volatile during Q4 and we have seen nearly a 1.6% drop on the gross margin level sequentially

items.statement: Price increase of ~2% taken in retail and B2B segments after 12-15 month gap
items.quote: We have just now announced the price increase in our retail segment and also in certain B2B segments already we are taking the prices up.

items.statement: Price increase varies by category, overall around 2% after 12-15 months gap
items.quote: Overall, in the range of around 2%, but varying between categories.

items.statement: Rural demand picking up; strong domestic demand expected from GDP growth, manufacturing, infrastructure
items.quote: As you have seen in other industries also, rural demand is picking up, and we have seen that also happening in March and then continuing.

items.statement: Industry growing ~3%; Gulf targets 2x-3x market growth with value growth above that
items.quote: the industry is growing at about 3% and – we've been saying all through last many, many years, more than a decade, we have been growing 2x to 3x at the industry.

items.statement: Core lubes volume 37,000 kl in Q4; AdBlue volume 37,000 kl in Q4 (up from 31,000 kl QoQ)
items.quote: we have achieved 37,000 kl in core lubes and we also have the highest in AdBlue this year where we did 37,000 kl in AdBlue

items.statement: Battery business revenue ~INR 80 crore in FY24, EBITDA neutral
items.quote: In the Battery business, we will be at about INR 80 crore and we are looking at toll manufacturing local product and looking to grow that business quite aggressively going forward

items.statement: Core lubricant capex ~INR 20-25 crore annually for filling/storage capacity
items.quote: Our usual capex in the core lubricant business is roughly INR 20 crore, - INR 25 crore, which we have been guiding about.

items.statement: EV investments total ~INR 150 crore so far (Tirex INR 103 crore, ElectreeFi, UK AC charger co.)
items.quote: overall, I think from Gulf India balance sheet, we are putting nearly INR 150 crore in these three investments so far in the EV segment.

items.statement: Base oil prices linked to crude with 1-2 month lag; crude at $83-84 currently, stability expected below $90-92
items.quote: Base oil follows crude. As we have mentioned in earlier questions that it went up to above $90 recently and then now has come back to around $83- $84, which is a good sign.

items.statement: Final dividend INR 20/share (1000%); total FY24 dividend INR 36/share (1800%)
items.quote: the Board has been very happy to announce higher payout and the final dividend of 1,000%, which is INR 20 per share. You will all recall that we have just in February paid an interim dividend of INR 16 per share so with that, the overall dividend for the year is INR 36, which is 1,800% on a face value of INR 2.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR 348 crore in FY24 vs INR 273 crore FY23
items.quote: very robust cash generation from operations, INR 348 crore of cash during the financial year generated out of operations versus INR 273 crore last year

items.statement: Working capital stable at 105-110 days gross working capital
items.quote: Overall, we continue to track in the range of around 105 days of gross working capital, 105 to 110 days, which has been our sort of band in the past trend.

items.statement: Expect recovery in EBITDA starting Q2 and more importantly in H2 of next year
items.quote: So we expect the recovery in EBITDA starting Q2 and more importantly, in H2 of next year.

items.statement: Expect steady 5-10 basis point sequential improvement in EBITDA margins starting Q3 of next year
items.quote: So we are focusing on a steady 5, 10 basis point improvement on a sequential basis starting Q3 of next year.

items.statement: Expect to maintain 18% to 20% head count growth in general staffing going into FY25
items.quote: I think we have -- as we speak, going into H1, we have open positions to kind of reflect that we can still kind of maintain an 18% to 20% head count growth going into this year as well.

items.statement: Specialized staffing Q1 and Q2 will be muted from demand perspective with uptick expected in second half
items.quote: At this point in time we still be lieve that Q1 and Q2 will be muted for the specialized staf fing from a demand perspective and hopefully there will be some uptick as we enter the second half of the

items.statement: EdTech business expected to accelerate profit momentum in FY25 led by improvement in student ARPU and operating leverage
items.quote: EdTech business has reported 30% growth in profits during FY '24 and is expected to accelerate the profit momentum in FY '25 as well, largely led by improvement in student ARPU and operating leverage.

items.statement: RegTech business at INR 40 crores annual revenue with EBITDA potential of 4% to 5% starting H2 FY25
items.quote: RegTech business coupled with complian ce services is currently at INR 40 cr ores of annual revenue with an EBITDA potential of 4% to 5% starting H2 of FY '25

items.statement: Core employee costs will go up by 9.5% effective 1st April 2024 on account of annual appraisal
items.quote: Effective 1st April 2024, core employee costs will go up by 9.5% on account of annual appraisal.

items.statement: General staffing ROCE is upwards of 75% and can be maintained given steady funding mix and EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: So ROCE only within the General Staffing business is upwards of 75%, and that can be maintained given the fact that the funding mix is maintained steadily and the EBITDA margins, as I mentioned earlier, maybe Q3 onwards, we can steadily improve 5 to 10 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: PAPM for general staffing associate was 679 for the quarter
items.quote: So it's 679 for the quarter.

items.statement: Open positions and demand in telecom still visible going into Q1 and Q2 FY25
items.quote: On the Telecom side, first of all, there is an element of consolidation, which is taking place. So I think some of the service providers, who are there are now looking at more larger formal established players, and we are seeing the benefit of that coming through to us. There is also some element of rollout, which is still carrying on to Q1 and Q2 given the open positions that we have.

items.statement: Manufacturing and industrial exposure at 12% to 15% with higher average realizations than BFSI
items.quote: Our current exposure to manufacturing, industrial is about 12% to 15%. And effectively, we believe that ther e is a lot more that we can do on that front from a logo acquisition and number growth perspective. The average realizations are higher than for the BFSI and other

items.statement: 60% of new logo sign-ups in general staffing are on variable markup model
items.quote: One important point that I mentioned earlier on, which is 60% of these new logo sign ups are coming on variable markup which also will help us offset the challenges we are having on PAPM.

items.statement: Variable markup associates constitute about 22% of current general staffing associate base
items.quote: Variable markup will be about 22%.

items.statement: Management anticipates 15% CAGR value growth for India business over next 2-3 years with volume growth higher than value growth
items.quote: We have envisaged and planned for a growth of 15% CAGR, which is a value CAGR that we are talking of. But our estimate is that the volume growth rate is going to be higher as compared to this

items.statement: Targeting 3% incremental EBITDA margin improvement over next 2-3 years from synergies and cost initiatives
items.quote: All this should lead us to a comfortable position gearing we say that we will lead to 3% incremental margin over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Kurlon on track to achieve INR1,000 crores topline and INR100 crores EBITDA as starting point
items.quote: Kurlon is on line to achieve our stated goal of INR1,000 crores topline and INR100 crores EBITDA as a starting point.

items.statement: Kurlon achieved 7%+ EBITDA margin in Q4 FY24, double the margin at acquisition in Q3
items.quote: Kurlon achieved a 7% plus EBITDA margin for the fourth quarter '24, which is double the margin that we acquired in the third quarter.

items.statement: Organized mattress market volumes flattish or marginally down offline; online e-commerce growing at 9-10% of industry
items.quote: Our own assessment of the market from whatever information we have at least of the leading brands, it has either been flattish or the volumes have actually decreased of some of the leading brands who are there in the industry.

items.statement: Sleepwell mattress volume grew 31%, Kurlon mattress volume grew 17% in Q4 FY24; ancillary brands declining
items.quote: Our flagship brand Sleepwell mattress registered a volume growth of 31%, while Kurlon brand mattress registered a volume growth of 17% in Q4 '24.

items.statement: Raw material prices expected to continue fluctuating but without spikes; no system to book for full year
items.quote: Going forward, I do see fluctuations happening or continuing to happen. Though I do not see any kind of spikes happening or a sudden free fall of the raw material

items.statement: Debt breakdown: INR725 crores NCD at 8.45%, INR250-300 crores foreign debt at ~5%, residual ICTCL debt at 5.5-6%; blended rate 7.5-8%
items.quote: So the breakup of this debt is around 800 -- INR725 crores is the NCD that we raised for the acquisition, which is at around 8.45%, there is foreign debt of around INR250 crores to INR300 crores, which would be at a lower cost

items.statement: E-commerce contribution expected to reach 10-15% maximum over next 2-3 years, benchmarked against 17-18% in developed markets
items.quote: Over the next 2 to 3 years, the contribution of e-commerce would probably be in the region of anywhere between, let's say, 10% to 12% or let's say, 10% to 15% maximum.

items.statement: Spain capacity increased from 14,000 to 19,000 tons; revenue drop due to raw material price pass-through, EBITDA% holding up
items.quote: We have already increased our capacities from 14,000 tons to 19,000 tons and slowly ramping that up. What you see as a drop in the top line is primarily on account of the raw material prices falling

items.statement: Australia business expected to normalize in 1 year; working on antidumping duties, furniture segment, bed-in-a-box
items.quote: I would give Australia one year's time where you would see climbing back to normal levels and then even going beyond that.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin would be 12%+ if normalized for 1% increased marketing spend; gross margins expanded
items.quote: Broadly, broadly for a stand-alone level, it would be 12-odd percent margin, if you normalize that.

items.statement: Competition intensity largely in e-commerce space with specific D2C brands; offline dominated by 3 brands
items.quote: The competition intensity, Deepak that you are talking of is largely today in the industry being only seen in one space, which is in the e-commerce space with certain specific brands

items.statement: Kurlon brand refresh launch scheduled for June 9, 2024 with India-Pakistan T20 World Cup match
items.quote: We are on our way to launch a brand refresh for Kurlon on 9th of June with the India-Pakistan match in the T20 World Cup.

items.statement: Management expects 20-30% CAGR for coming years and remains on track for 10,000 crore revenue target in 5 years
items.quote: We should be on track, and we still look at continuing at that CAGR of 20% to 30% for the coming years.

items.statement: Marketplace EBITDA margin guided at 3.5-3.75%, consolidated at 3.3-3.5% for FY25
items.quote: So in the marketplace, we're talking about 3.5% to 3.75%. And on a consolidated, we're looking at 3.3% to 3.5%.

items.statement: Steel business guided at 20-25% CAGR with 2-3% EBITDA margin, non-steel at 30-35% CAGR with 6-6.5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So we're talking about a steel growth of 20% to 25% CAGR with an EBITDA margin of 2-3% and we're looking at non-steel at a growth of 30% to 35% CAGR with an EBITDA margin of 6% to 6.5%.

items.statement: Retail margin sustainable at 6-6.5% going forward driven by non-steel and value-added steel mix
items.quote: We do feel it's sustainable. I think going forward, we should definitely aim for between 6% to 6.5% for the margin profile.

items.statement: Hybrid store conversion capex averages INR2-3 crores per store, targeting 2-3 stores per year
items.quote: The capex per hybrid store, depending on the size, we look at an average of around INR2 crores to INR3 crores, but looking at INR2 crores for a hybrid model.

items.statement: Construction industry expected to remain focus post-elections, company well positioned to capitalize on opportunities
items.quote: For the coming year, we believe the construction industry will continue to be a focus point post-elections. We are well positioned to capitalize on the opportunities in the construction and real estate sector.

items.statement: Non-steel business grew 30% in FY24 at 50% 3-year CAGR, now present in 35 of 91 stores with 6% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Our non-steel offerings are present in 35 out of our 91 stores. Hence, we believe we have a significant runway without a need to aggressively open new stores. Our gross margins in non-steel have been in the range of 10% to 12%. I'm glad to share that as we expand our scale in this segment, our EBITDA margin has also shown improvement, reaching 6% during FY 2024 for non-steel.

items.statement: Demerger scheme awaiting SEBI approval, expected implementation by Q4 FY25 with shared MD but separate management focus
items.quote: Our demerger scheme is currently waiting for approval from SEBI. We believe the entire demerger process should be implemented by Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Post-demerger ROCE targets: marketplace ~28%, manufacturing ~4-5%, consolidated slight improvement from current 18%
items.quote: Post demerger, we are expecting that marketplace business will be around 28%, whereas the existing SBPL will be around 4-5%. On an average, it will improve from 18% little bit on a consol level.

items.statement: No additional capex needed for manufacturing value-added products, focus on capacity utilization from current 50%
items.quote: No, all of our units are well maintained. I think all of our machines are also up to date. So I think with more focus, we could definitely add more of these products.

items.statement: Western and Central India operations grew 46% and 39% YoY respectively, now 14% of total revenue with continued momentum expected
items.quote: Over the past year, we have achieved strong growth from Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh. Our Western and Central India operations have grown by 46% and 39% year-on-year, respectively. Our share from West and Central has been 14% of our total top line in FY '24 and we expect continued growth momentum from these regions.

items.statement: APL Apollo subscribed to warrants, now holds 37% of turnover contribution vs 42% last year, no further shareholding changes expected
items.quote: So this year, overall, Apollo's contributed 37% of our turnover as compared to 42% last year.

items.statement: Fotia Ceramica private label grew 50% to INR116 crores in year 2, expanding to Karnataka, Telangana, Maharashtra with Morbi display center by June 2024
items.quote: Point number three, our private label Fotia Ceramica in the ceramic business has demonstrated a stellar growth of 50% in the second year, achieving INR116 crores top line. We have achieved sizable growth in Kerala and Tamil Nadu markets and now are focusing on Karnataka, Telangana, and Maharashtra in the coming year. We will also be inaugurating our display center in Morbi by June 2024.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA margin guided at 2-2.2% post-demerger, marketplace at 3.5-3.75%
items.quote: We are looking, like you said, an EBITDA margin at the marketplace of 3.5% to 3.75%, and at the manufacturing of 2% to 2.2%.

items.statement: Potential for brownfield expansion at manufacturing units with land bank available, but focus first on turnaround and utilization improvement
items.quote: The land bank is there. I think our first focus is to kind of push and turn around and get a focus on the unit and get it focused on the manufacturing? I think maybe in a year or 2, we'll have a better idea, especially in a year. And then we could look at – we are not opposed to any idea I think we're kind of still in the exploratory phase when it comes to what we can do with the manufacturing.

items.statement: Working capital maintained at ~30 days net (inventory 30 days, debtors 40 days, creditors 40 days) with 55% retail, 45% project/wholesale mix
items.quote: For t he second part for the inventory will be approximately around 30 the days. Debtors approximately 40 days, and creditors will be around 40 days. So net average will be around 30 days

items.statement: Management guides for 18-20% volume growth in FY25
items.quote: Yes, so we are still looking year round, we are still looking at a 20% growth. So, that stays the way it is.

items.statement: Management targets blended EBITDA per ton of Rs 1,550 for FY25
items.quote: So, on a blended basis, we are targeting about 1550.

items.statement: Management expects Q1 FY25 volume growth of 6-7% YoY
items.quote: in April, there was a slight de-growth, in May it seemed like an 8% to 9% kind of growth , in June, we expect that we can get about 10% growth so on a weighted average in Quarter 1, compared to last year Quarter 1, we can expect a growth of about 6% to 7%.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected at Rs 1,000 crore including clinker, Silchar grinding, solar, AAC block, BTAP and fleet
items.quote: So, for FY25, the overall CAPEX is expected to be about Rs.1000 crores. This also includes a lot of operational CAPEX, it includes the group captive solar, it includes AAC Block and the BTAP and it also includes our own fleet that we are expanding now.

items.statement: Silchar 2 MTPA grinding unit capex of Rs 300 crore in FY25, commissioning by Q3 FY26
items.quote: In Silchar grinding unit we have till date only spent Rs.22 crores, in FY25 we plan to spend Rs.300 crores in this Silchar grinding unit. So, most of the CAPEX for the grinding unit will take place in FY25.

items.statement: Jorhat 2 MTPA grinding unit announced with Rs 450 crore capex over 2.5 years, commissioning in 2 years
items.quote: Today in the Board we had also discussed and decided that we want to put a plant in Jorhat which is upper Assam. So, that would be a fresh CAPEX and the CAPEX could be of about Rs.450 crores which will be spent in the next two and half years and we expect to commission Jorhat plant in the next two years.

items.statement: Rajasthan greenfield clinker project of 4.5-5 MTPA planned with Rs 2,500 crore capex over 3 years
items.quote: We would have to spend about Rs.2500 crores to set up 4.5 to 5 million tons capacity during the clicker plant.

items.statement: Weighted average fuel cost target reduced to Rs 1.55/GCV for FY25 from Rs 1.7/GCV in Q4 FY24 via new 10-year FSA
items.quote: So, our target for the coming year is about Rs.1.55 per GCV weighted average.

items.statement: GST incentive benefit of Rs 150-160 crore expected in FY25, rising to Rs 200 crore in FY26
items.quote: In terms of absolute number, it would be about 150 to 160 crores.

items.statement: Coal India FSA lock-in of 3.6 lakh tonnes at Rs 1.5/GCV to save ~Rs 70 crore annually
items.quote: So, it would be about Rs.70 odd crores in a year.

items.statement: Prices outside Northeast (Bengal, Bihar) dropped ~Rs 300/bag vs Q4 FY24 average; Northeast prices stable
items.quote: In terms of price, the price at Northeastern has broadly been stable, whereas the price outside Northeast which is Bengal and Bihar has seen a drop which is common across everyone , every player in the East. So, there is a drop of about Rs.300 in prices outside Northeast.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 demand subdued due to elections and Eid; April saw de-growth, May ~8-9% growth, June expected ~10% growth
items.quote: So, the demand right now a decent Q1 is a bit subdued , that is mainly because of the election and Eid which happened in April. And also, even the election which is now also carrying on in May. So, demand is a bit subdued because of those reasons.

items.statement: Non-trade share to rise from ~15% to 20%; Northeast share to rise from ~25% to 28-29%; trade growth also targeted
items.quote: Our non-trade sale is about 3%, we can expect it to be pushed to 20 %. Northeast sale is about 25% we can expect it to be pushed to 28%, 29%.

items.statement: AAC block plant (800 TPD) to commission in August FY25, expected Rs 35-40 crore revenue and Rs 10 crore profit in FY25
items.quote: It should be about Rs.35 crores or Rs.40 crores and it will just give, and the profitability is decent, it's about 20% margin. So, the profitability will be about Rs.10 crores.

items.statement: WHRS (12 MW) to start Aug-Sep FY25; group captive hybrid solar-wind (26 MW) model being adopted
items.quote: will be starting? Management: No. So, we are now going for a group captive model. So, we will be adopting that in a week's time. And that will be a hybrid model, where we will be setting up 26 megawatts of solar plus wind

items.statement: FY25 capex funded by ~Rs 750 crore internal accruals and ~Rs 200-300 crore additional debt
items.quote: this year we think about 750 crores would be our own cash profit generation that we will have so, that will broadly fund majority of the Rs.1000 crore and then rest would be a bit of debt.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth guidance of 6% to 8%
items.quote: Volume growth of 6% to 8% for FY25 will be the first target and uptick in premium specialties and improvement in the overall mix should further help in strengthening the EBITDA per metric ton.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA per metric ton guidance of Rs 20,500 to Rs 21,500
items.value: Rs 20,500 to Rs 21,500 per metric ton
items.quote: For FY25, the range we are working withstands Rs. 20,500 to Rs. 21,500 per metric ton with H2 gravitating towards the upper range of the band and H1 being closer to the lower range.

items.statement: Target to return to 22% to 23% ROCE in FY25 from 18% in FY24
items.quote: More importantly, we plan to get back to the 22% to 23% ROCE ban from existing 18% clocked in FY24, thus complying with the terminal principles of PAT growth being higher than EBITDA growth and EBITDA growth being higher than the volume growth.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 150-200 crores for FY25
items.quote: No, as we have said, we have a CAPEX of close to Rs. 150-Rs. 200 crores. So, that is also there.

items.statement: AMET market expected to see double-digit volume growth in FY25 barring further escalations
items.quote: Therefore, barring any further escalations, AMET should see double digit volume growth in the coming year.

items.statement: Specialty volumes expected to grow better with mix shifting to premium specialties
items.quote: That essentially means that specialty chemicals should grow better, and more importantly, the mix in the specialty care ingredients should be much better whereas performance surfactants will be majorly driven by what happens in India and Africa and Middle East, Turkey.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA per metric ton at Rs 20,600
items.quote: EBITDA per kg for the quarter, yes, we said it is about Rs 20,600 per metric ton.

items.statement: Red Sea disruption caused ~2,500 metric tons volume loss in Q4 FY24, expected to recoup in coming months
items.quote: So, essentially, you look at that, we are talking about something like something of about 2500 metric tons.

items.statement: Rural recovery, below-average rainfall, slowdown, and premiumization are key risks for India market
items.quote: While the momentum remains strong, rural recovery remains the key going ahead. Below-average rainfall slowdown, and premiumization remain key risks.

items.statement: Specialty capacity can reach 100,000-110,000 tons at 80-85% utilization before new investment
items.quote: See if I can go almost up to 100,000 to 110,000. But then we also need to know that in terms of what capacities we have currently, but we also look at, there are certain super specialties for which we are in the process of even setting up capacities.

items.statement: AMET volumes expected to reach 80,000-85,000 tons in FY25, peak of 94,000 tons in 5 years
items.quote: We will see that this year will see things getting significantly better in terms of the approaching the higher numbers of the previous years of all close to 80,000 to 85,000 tons.

items.statement: New patented molecules expected to commercialize in 1-3 years
items.quote: So, those molecules which are just into the patent process, generally have time to scale it up and go to the market. So, depends on the type of the patent. So, but typically, in a time frame of about one to three years, they will blossom into the market opportunities.

items.statement: 90% of contracts are on CIF or GDP basis, limiting ability to shift freight risk to customers
items.quote: Yes. I think 90% of what we do is all either GDP or CIF.

items.statement: Expect to continue growth momentum similar to last year based on customer schedules, market demand and geopolitical situation
items.quote: We expect to continue this growth momentum over the last year and the current schedules of the customers, the demand in the market and the geopolitical situation at this point shows that we should be very comfortable with achieving what the numbers that we are expecting to on a similar platform that we did in the last year.

items.statement: Target 50 basis points EBITDA margin improvement year-on-year for FY25
items.quote: Like as we have given guidance for last two years that on year-on-year basis, we are seeing margin improvement around 50 basis points. So, last year also for '23-24 we kept that guidance, 50 point basis we will be enforcing, again the same guidance we will be following for current year also.

items.statement: Western India die casting plant capex ~Rs.30 crores, commercialization by August 2024
items.quote: We will be incurring a CAPEX of close to Rs.30 crores on an overall basis for that plant. A large portion has already been released in the market. We are just waiting for the final bills to come up for the payment.

items.statement: EV subsidiary Sandhar Auto Electric Solutions: Rs.10 crores already spent, another Rs.10 crores in FY25, commercial production from July 2024
items.quote: EV front, if you remember our last investor call, last year, we kept a target of crores of investment with a total outlay of Rs.20 crores. So, Rs.10 crores we have already spent, another Rs.10 crores we will be spending this year.

items.statement: Cabins and fabrication margin currently ~8%, expect 50-100 bps improvement in FY25 after new Pune facility starts
items.quote: So, cabins and fabrication, we operate around a margin of 8%, I mean, there's no much change in the margin structure of cabins and fabrication being a heavy equipment as items are very heavy sheet metal base top, and we expect that there can be an improvement of 50 to 100 point basis in the coming year once the new Pune facility starts contributing to it.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through with typical 3-month lag, some companies moved to 1-month platform due to volatility
items.quote: The lag is typically; our costings are done every three months. Because of a lot of volatility that started to happen about three years ago, there are some companies that shifted onto a one-month platform, but more often than not costings are done after a period of every three months. So, the lag is three months.

items.statement: Smart locks for Suzuki and Honda launching October-November 2024, value 8-10x traditional locks, major pivot for locking business
items.quote: I just want to again reiterate the fact that the locking system business is a new platform with smart locks where the value of the smart locks can be anywhere between 8 to 10 times of the locks that we produce. So, for the company, it's a big thing and with two launches now happening in October and November, the landscape of that particular business will change dramatically.

items.statement: Romania plant utilization ~25%, expect continuous month-on-month revenue growth as customers increase sourcing from Eastern Europe
items.quote: We have set up that plant and to that end, the utilization of the existing capacity is within 25%. So, obviously there is a huge upside and now things are changing, things are improving, and our two customers that we have there are growing their businesses in terms of sourcing it more from the Eastern European nations like Romania.

items.statement: Comfortable achieving similar growth as last few years over next 3-5 years, but no specific number given due to uncertainties

items.statement: Maintain FY25 revenue guidance of Rs 4,000 crores assuming commodity prices do not fall further

items.quote: We are expecting to maintain a gross margin of around 49% - 50% in FY25. The EBITDA margins will also sustain at this level as we are also making a lot of development spending in some of the new segments.

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs. 800-900 crore for FY25

items.quote: Yes, it will surely be a 20%-plus kind of level post 3 years development phase.

items.quote: Well, we don't really expect a major impact of this product going off patent in the U.S. in the current fiscal because it will take a few years before another player registers and comes in.

items.quote: Definitely, about INR 270 or INR2 80 crores will be the incremental revenue from this 100 KLPD.

items.quote: EBIDTA margins improved by about 5% to 14.1% in FY24 as compared to 9.09% in FY23.

items.quote: net CAPEX that we have incurred has been Rs. 172 crores, majority of which has been in our upcoming albumin manufacturing facility to the tune of roughly about Rs. 150 crores.

items.quote: another maybe Rs. 50 crores additionally we may have to spend it this is what I can tell you.

items.quote: For our Jadcherla facility, which has undergone a USFDA inspection in November 23, I would like to share that we have submitted all compliance for the 10 observations that were issued.

items.quote: For Aflibercept CDSCO approval for the Phase-3 has been received and manufacturing of CT batches will be done in the Q2.

items.quote: On partnership on alliance front, this year witnessed the onboarding of Deloitte and BDO as a key strategic partner to redefine the payroll landscape and we continue to work with them very closely on getting into the market.

items.quote: One of the significant milestones this quarter earlier was the launch of Ramco Payce.
