And this will be located in the state of Gujarat. We expect to commence construction during this fiscal year after receiving all the necessary permits from the regulatory authorities, and we expect to build more ammonia terminals as t

items.statement: Liquid capacity to reach ~2 million KL by end FY24, targeting 2.3 million KL by end FY25 with 300,000 KL additions.
items.quote: And we expect the capacity to grow next year also by almost 300,000 CBM. So it's more capex growth that is leading to revenue and EBITDA.

items.statement: Liquid division EBITDA margin improved to 46% YoY (INR396 cr vs INR272 cr) on new capacity and acquisitions; realization ~INR3,000/KL.
items.quote: We delivered the highest ever EBITDA at INR396 crores versus INR272 crores in the previous year, which is an increase of 46%.

items.statement: Distribution margin improvement in Q4 FY24 driven by procurement efficiencies; sustainability depends on volume scale-up, with step-up expected when Mangalore/Pipavav cryogenic terminals commission in FY26.
items.quote: It has happened in distribution on account of procurement efficiencies, which we could get in this quarter. So the margins have improved in Q4 as far as distribution volumes are concerned.

items.statement: LPG demand outlook strong: India imports already >20 MT vs 25 MT projected for 2034-35; total demand ~31 MT in FY24, growing for decades; propane cheaper than natural gas by 7-10% in Morbi.
items.quote: If you look at our presentation, the presentation talks about import of 25 million in 2034, 2035. Whereas in the current year, the imports of LPG have already crossed 20 million.

items.statement: Liquid revenue variability driven by product mix (vegetable oil INR125-150/KL/month vs specialty chemicals INR600-1,000), take-or-pay contracts, and evacuation speed; full-year view recommended.
items.quote: For example, vegetable oil could be INR125 or INR150 a month, whereas a specialty chemical or an acid could be INR600, INR700, INR1,000. Could be 10x -- 8x, 10x.

items.statement: KGPL pipeline progress on track, expected to commission with cryogenic terminals by end FY25/Q1 FY26; no government delays reported so far.
items.quote: Again, KGPL is progressing well and is expected to come on line timed with our cryogenic, which is expected by end of FY '25 and Q1 FY '26. So we hope both to commence around the same time.

items.statement: Minority interest expected 15-20% of profit going forward; structure may change.
items.quote: But we expect minority interest to be between 15% to 20%, yes.

items.statement: Final dividend INR2/share recommended; total FY24 dividend INR6.50/share (650% of face value).
items.quote: the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR2 or 200% per share of the face value of INR1. The company has already declared and paid two interim dividends of INR2 in February 2024 and INR2.5 in August of '23 for the financial year ended 31st March. And therefore, the total dividend for the full year amounts to INR6.50 per share or 650% for every share of face value INR1.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin guidance of 10% to 12%
items.quote: Hence, we are cautiously optimistic of the coming quarters and of achieving our target guidance EBITDA of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Mahad and Baroda investments at advanced stages of commercial production
items.quote: We are on track with our investments in Mahad and Baroda, which are at advanced stages of commercial production.

items.statement: Effective contribution from hydrogenation and Mahad facilities expected from Q3 FY25, real contribution from Q1 FY26
items.quote: So, the effective contribution of the hydrogenation facility as well as the Maha d facility would start kicking in from Q3 of financial year '24-'25. Or you can safely say that from Q1 of '25-'26 is when we will have the real contribution of these two plants in our top line

items.statement: Asset turnover for Mahad greenfield around 1.2x, brownfield expansion around 1.5x
items.quote: Asset turnover ratio for actually Mahad is a Greenfield. So, if I compare the cost of the plant with the top line of that plant, it would be around 1.2. And from the other side of business, we are expecting around 1.5.

items.statement: New plants expected to hit 60% to 80% capacity utilization in first year of operations
items.quote: Based on the feedback that we have received from our customers, we are pretty buoyant about capacity utilization hitting anywhere between 60% to 80% in the first year of operations.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin at 9.65%, up from 4.76% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margins stood at 9.65% as compared to around 4.76% in the corresponding period of the previous year.

items.statement: Gross margins recovered to pre-COVID levels of 34-35%, EBITDA still 400-500 bps below
items.quote: I think the gross margin achievement was primarily driven by a lot of business process re-engineering and so the material consumption etc are all kind of adding up to that contribution.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals demand regularized, price realizations improving daily
items.quote: However, I am glad to inform you with cautious optimism , w e have seen that demand is coming back in a regularized way and price realizations for the specialty chemicals is improving by every passing day.

items.statement: Fragrance and flavor division seeing healthy growth from new customer acquisitions globally
items.quote: We have seen healthy and profitable growth in terms of increased sales and improved profitability for this division in the year '23-'24. This growth has been led by way of new customer acquisitions across all geographies that we operate in globally and improved profitability.

items.statement: Camphor and terpene chemicals face continued pricing pressure due to excess capacity and supply exceeding demand
items.quote: We feel that this challenge in camphor powder and terpene chemicals will continue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Chinese camphor production finding its way into India adding to oversupply
items.quote: I think just to add to what Dharmil just said, you also have a third element where there is a lot of camphor that's produced in China which also will have a tendency to kind of find its home in India.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity improved to 0.30x as of March 2024 from 0.34x previous year despite capex
items.quote: Net debt-to-equity ratio improved as on 31 March 2024 is 0.30x, as compared to 0.34x in the previous year. This has improved despite our investment in the CAPEX.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of Rs 142 crores in FY24 vs negative Rs 22 crores in FY23
items.quote: The net operating cash flow was Rs. 142 crores as compared to minus 22 crores in the FY '23.

items.statement: Interest cost expected at Rs 17-18 crores for FY25, depreciation Rs 21-22 crores standalone plus Rs 4-5 crores for new capex consolidated
items.quote: So, interest cost for the next financial year, we are expecting around 17 to 18 crore, and depreciation, we can assume around, for the current side, means for the standalone side, will be around 21 crore, 22 crores, and for the consolidated side, it will go up with the new CAPEX, say 4 to 5 crore more.

items.statement: Product mix remains roughly one-third each across three divisions, minor quarterly variations
items.quote: So, I think, Dhwanil, we will continue to be one -third, one -third, one -third, minor sub-aberrations happening in a few quarters, depending on one of the division having a little bit more or a little bit less, but we are pretty confident that in the few quarters from now, we should stay in the same configuration.

items.statement: TMD order book stands at Rs 3570 Crore for execution plus Rs 300 Crore export order book
items.quote: Currently, we hold an order book to the tune of Rs 3570 Crore, which are lined up for execution and an export order book of around Rs 300 Crore.

items.quote: We have, over the last 3-4 quarters, seen a downtrend in order intake which is reflected in the order book question on hand and this trend continues as of now.

items.statement: Internal planning assumes two quarters of tight capacity utilization before recovery in TMD
items.quote: Our internal planning is that we have to be sitting tight for two quarters and save everything what we have got.

items.statement: Added 5 MW solar capacity in Q4 FY24 taking total renewable capacity to 53 MW serving 90% energy needs
items.quote: During the last quarter, we have put in another 5 MW of solar capacity, taking our total installed capacity to 53 MW of renewable power.

items.quote: In the month of May 2024, we have taken a price revision for machines, which was on a hold for 2 years.

items.quote: The reason we have seen that our margins have come down closer to a single digit margin is that we have invested in capacities but not fully getting utilized.

items.statement: ATC order book upwards of Rs 200 Crore executable over next 18 months
items.quote: The order book for ATC continues to be upwards of Rs 200 Crore, which are executable for the next 18 months.

items.statement: Invested Rs 20 Crore in ATC machines earlier this year
items.quote: We have invested earlier this year, around Rs 20 Crore. into ATC, in terms of machines alone.

items.statement: MTD revenue mix remains 75:25 to 80:20 traditional vs machining centres; new VMC models driving growth
items.quote: It is still hovering between 75:25, or 80:20, depending on whichever quarter we take, depending on the projects we supply to, for that quarter.

items.statement: MTD capacity utilization at 65% with 35% headroom; continues adding capacity ahead of demand
items.quote: Our capacity utilisation is still in the range of 65%. So, we still have about 35% capacity available for utilisation in this particular division.

items.statement: Global economic challenges causing weak export demand expected to persist for couple of quarters
items.quote: The global economic challenges remain, and hence resulting in weak demand. This, we see as a business challenge for the exports market as well, for a couple of quarters.

items.statement: TMD operating 5 days/week in May 2024 due to low capacity utilization; foundry also reducing working days
items.quote: We have also announced a reduction in the number of working days in the month of May 2024 and currently, TMD is working 5 days because of lower capacity utilization.

items.statement: TMD active order book Rs 2300 Crore of total Rs 3520 Crore; order inflow FY24 ~Rs 700 Crore vs ~Rs 1300 Crore prior year
items.quote: The active order book within this is around Rs 2300 Crore. And the order flow during the current year was closer to Rs 700 Crore.

items.quote: In a very limited manner, we have put it on test runs. I should perhaps come back to you in another two quarters, once the commercial launch is announced.

items.statement: India added slightly less than 2 million spindles in FY24
items.quote: I think the spindles added during the current year is little bit less than, in India, it is a little bit less than 2 million spindles.

items.quote: With respect to the manufacturing, yes, we are manufacturing for DMG and we have one machine, which is slowly scaling up to a couple of machines.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected around ₹5,000 Cr ±5%
items.quote: So, next year's turnover should be around ₹5,000 Cr, +-5%.

items.quote: Investment is under consideration proposals have been made, but we are evaluating this proposal and once it is approved by the board, we will be going for some additional investment for the modernization of machines for balancing of the plant.

items.statement: Positive export enquiries but low conversion to bulk orders due to price challenges
items.quote: There is a positive flow of enquiries for export sales. However, at the same time, the conversion rate to bulk is very low due to extreme challenges in terms of prices.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 4.6%, FY24 EBITDA margin 3.2%
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA, which measures our operational efficiency, we saw an impressive rise from ₹22 Cr in Q3FY24 to ₹54 Cr in Q4FY24, with an EBITDA margin of 4.6%.

items.statement: Kaapas project generating ₹6-8/kg premium over peers
items.quote: It is abo ut ₹6/kg to ₹8/kg plus. So, you can expect good amount of profit, but it all depends only this project execution is not sufficient

items.statement: Yarn prices down ~10% YoY in FY24; Mélange down 25%

In the case of PV Dyed it was ₹244/kg in FY23 and FY24 it is ₹207/kg, so the price realization during this FY2023-24 was lower than by around 10%, in case of every type of yarn and in case M elange it is less by 25% from FY23 to FY24

items.statement: PTA and MEG prices expected to decline, aiding production costs
items.quote: Prices for PTA and MEG are expected to decline, which could positively impact production costs.

items.statement: Textile exports grew 7% YoY in first two months of 2024
items.quote: Encouragingly, the positive trend has continued into the first two months of 2024 with exports growing by 7% YoY.

items.quote: The acquisition enlarges RSWM's footprint, cementing its standing in the spinning and fabric industry by incorporating substantial capacity: 80,016 spindles, 720 rotors, 12 tonnes per day of knitted fabric, and its processing.

items.quote: The Company like RSWM is doing for risk management is that we have the Risk Management Committee which includes Directors, CFO and all Stakeholders like Business Head, Business Head - Yarn, Business Head - Denim, Business Head - Mélange, Business Head - Knitting and then Company Secretary and lastly Chief Information Officer. All kinds of risks are discussed and if any new risk is identified, it i

items.quote: However, there is a potential risk of an increase in the dumping of cheap polyester fabric.

items.quote: The RSWM management is pleased to inform the investors about the value creation on its investment in equity shares of Bhilwara Energy Limited, through unrealized mark to market gain of ₹138 crore on fair valuation.

items.statement: Exports expected to reach $200 million in FY25
items.quote: We expect our exports to touch to $200 million.

items.statement: Capex planned at Rs 350-400 crore for FY25
items.quote: So, we would be spending between Rs. 350 crores to Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Wind energy revenue to double from Rs 250 crore to Rs 500 crore+ in 2-3 years

items.quote: Yes. So, we have been talking about Rs. 4,000 crores of order book, the pipeline, and so that's where it is.

items.statement: Aspiration to return to 19-20% EBITDA margin band
items.quote: While getting back to 19.20 is definitely our aspiration.

items.quote: I think notwithstanding the elections, even the commercial vehicles have done well, with government spending happening in Q1 or later part of Q2. items.statement: Export demand recovery sustained; channel destocking over, customer forecasts positive

items.statement: FY24 standalone capex Rs 343 crore; FY25 capex Rs 350-400 crore focused on fastener division for exports and hybrid/PH/EV at SEZ

items.quote: So, the capacity utilization should be around 65% to 70%, yes, across I'm talking about. items.statement: EV revenue currently 6-7%, targeting 10-12% near term, 10-15% eventually
items.quote: At current level, it would be close to about 6%, 7%. And then we are looking to take it up to maybe 10% to 12%. And eventually, we are trying to look at around 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Non-auto revenue 30% currently, aspiration to reach 50%
items.quote: See, with respect to the non-auto portion, while today we are at 30%, the aspiration is to go to 50%.

items.quote: So, purely an apples-to-apples, between a pure ICE to a pure BEV. So, let's say that the delta could be 25%. So, that would be maximum 25% to 30%.

items.statement: UK subsidiary (CPFL) turned around, expected to remain profitable despite UK truck market slowdown; China subsidiary strong despite real estate slowdown
items.quote: We expect the UK subsidiary to have another strong year. Notwithstanding the slowdown in the UK truck market, we expect our operations to be profitable this year in line with last year. And it has turned around completely and lots of operational improvements. The raw metal prices have been managed well and the freight costs have come down. And so there has been a strong operational performance in

items.statement: Raw metal prices stable in FY24; steel prices may rise due to Chinese import licensing restrictions; pass-through arrangements with all customers
items.quote: I think metal prices, especially the steel, have been largely stable last year. We expect that trend to continue. But having said that, the Chinese imports, there are certain licensing requirements now. So, the supply of Chinese steel is going to be limited. And for some market correction, there is a possibility of prices going up in steel.

items.statement: Pass-through arrangements with all customers for metal price changes
items.quote: Yes, sir. We have pass-through arrangements with all our customers.

items.statement: PLI application approved; product testing approval expected in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We have opted for PLI. We are one of the approved companies. Our products are yet to get an approval from the testing agency. And now things have slowed down a bit. We expect some traction in Q2.

items.statement: Atma Nirbhar and QCO orders driving import substitution in PV segment, accelerating local sourcing enquiries
items.quote: Actually, it's a good question. And what is going to be relevant is the extraordinary push from the government side in terms of Atma Nirbhar and the QCO orders, I hope you are familiar. So, it is kind of indirectly nudging and forcing the OEMs to localize whatever they are importing currently.

items.statement: Domestic revenue mix: PV 40%, M&HCV+LCV 25%, Tractors 8-10%
items.quote: With respect to the industry segment, we are at 40% of our domestic revenue with respect to passenger car segment. And between M&HCV and LCV, we should be looking at 25%, tractors in the range of 8% to 10%.

items.statement: PV volume growth budgeted at 8-10% for FY25 vs 7% last year; M&HCV at 12-13% with higher content per vehicle
items.quote: We are looking at around 8% to 10% kind of a growth. Last year, we had 7%. So, we are sure that it will reach maybe close to the double digit, but are 9% to 10%. I think this year should be good.

items.statement: Q4 volume growth 8-10% QoQ across segments except tractors which degrew; industry grew 3-4% QoQ
items.quote: Volume growth, I think barring tractors, all the other segments grew by around 8% to 10%, 7%. Only the tractor segment did not grow much. In fact, there was a degrowth in the tractor segment.

items.statement: Flood-related one-time cost of Rs 3.38 crore recognized in Q4 FY24
items.quote: It is there in our notes and accounts. I will give you the number, that is the net amount, it's Rs. 3.38 crores.

items.statement: FY25 capex guided between Rs. 500-700 crore
items.quote: So, even for FY25, our CAPEX would be between Rs. 500 to Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Mid-teen EBITDA margin target retained; no discounting for market share
items.quote: Our stated objective is to retain this mid-teen EBITDA margin. And that is why I think we're very clear of not really playing a discounting game and growing our market share on the basis of products and our extended network as well.

items.statement: Switch India e-bus order book at 1,500 units including 950 for Delhi and 320 for Bangalore
items.quote: We have 1,500 in hand, we have 950 to deliver in Delhi and another 320 to deliver in Bangalore and then few more.

items.statement: Switch UK Spain plant on track; first vehicles to be delivered in September
items.quote: The first vehicles actually by the way, will be delivered in coming September. I think it is a few numbers, but we want to ensure that we do make that small step in Spain.

items.statement: Current capacity sufficient for 2-3 years; evaluating footprint for expansion beyond that with flexible lines for ICE and EV
items.quote: For next 2-3 years, we see no problem as far as capacity is concerned, but hopefully we have to prepare ourselves for a period beyond that. So, we are looking at it, we will come out with more details and share with you.

items.statement: 6 new product launches planned in 2-3.5 ton SCV segment in FY25; LCV portfolio expansion to cover 70-80% of market
items.quote: We have planned for 6 new product launches in this segment in FY25, which should give us a further boost to our market share. Currently, we address about half of the LCV market in India. We are looking to expanding our LCV product portfolio to cover at least 70% to 80% of the market in the next few years.

items.statement: Export volumes grew despite subdued SAARC and Africa markets; strategy of local presence and focused product development working
items.quote: Despite subdued market conditions in SAARC and in some parts of Africa, Ashok Leyland registered growth in export volume s, this reflects that our strategy of local market presence, focused product development for IO markets and our strong distribution relationships in key markets is working well for us

items.statement: Net debt close to zero at end of FY24 after Rs. 1,500 crore investment in Optare Switch
items.quote: Our net debt at the end of FY24 is close to Zero. This is after Rs. 1,500 crore investment in Optare Switch and owned during the year.

items.statement: KM Balaji appointed CFO effective 1 June 2024; Gopal Mahadevan moves to Director, Strategic Finance and M&A
items.quote: we announced the appointment of Mr. KM Balaji as Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Gopal Mahadevan, currently CF O and Whole-Time Director will continue to be associated with Ashok Leyland as Director, Strategic Finance and M&A. Mr. Balaji, currently Deputy CFO, will take over the role of Chief Financial Officer with effect from 1st June 2024

items.statement: Hinduja Leyland Finance reverse merger back on track; expected to complete in a couple of quarters; exploring third-party investment in Hinduja Housing Finance
items.quote: The reverse merger process is back on track. It had some procedural issues more than anything else. So, otherwise what was envisaged as the original merger strategy continues. So, we expect that this may take a couple of more quarters.

items.statement: OBD-II norms caused pre-buy in Q4 FY23 creating high base; replacement demand from aging BS-IV fleet (avg age 10 years) to drive growth
items.quote: And that was because of OBD-II norms that had forced some prebuy. So, we have to just keep in perspective that if we exclude that period of high base number because of which the industry degrew, industry has been growing before that by 8%-9%.

items.statement: Dedicated Freight Corridor impact not expected in short run; TCO model not working yet, fundamental issues to be resolved over few years
items.quote: The whole TCO of this new model for potential new model around DFC is not working out yet. So, there are some like fundamental issues in the model which have to be sorted out and I really think it will take a long time. It will take a few years at least before it starts taking some shape.

items.statement: Switch India turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY24; expected to remain EBITDA positive in FY25; no major investment needed in H1 FY25
items.quote: Switch in quarter four has been EBITDA positive. Yes, so this is the first quarter where they have turned around into being a p rofitable company. And even in FY 25, we are, as I said, we are still kind of refining the plans. But we hope that S witch would remain EBITDA positive, Switch India would remain EBITDA positive

items.statement: Market share gains to come from product superiority and expanding reach, not discounting; confident of increasing share in trucks and buses
items.quote: We are clear that we are not going to discount our products to win market share. We are confident that our market share wins will come on the back of our products superiority and our expanding reach.

items.statement: Strong interest in eLCV from e-commerce and logistics multinationals for green last-mile; order book building since March launch
items.quote: There is a lot of interest from e-commerce and logistic companies, especially many multinationals who are looking for the last mile to be green as well. So, I would say that it is early days, but a lot of strong interest.

items.statement: Expects FY25 growth similar to FY24 with Q1 slow due to elections, improvement after June
items.quote: The growth of FY '23-'24 is something that we are looking forward to also in the upcoming year. The first quarter could be a little slow because of the election effects.

items.statement: Annual capex expected to continue in INR 400-600 crore range
items.quote: on an average, we've had a capex of between INR 400 crores to INR 600 crores -- INR300 crores to INR 600 crores, if I can be broade r year -on-year. And this is a trend that we will continue

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12.5% in FY24 from 12.1% in FY23
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue improved from 12.1% to 12.5%.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin improved to 13.2% from 12.9% in Q4 FY23
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue improved from 12.9% in Jan to March '23 to 13.2% in Jan to March '24.

items.statement: Two-wheeler division expects sales rise in FY25 due to BS-VI OBD II transition and post-election demand
items.quote: The net sales of the two -wheeler division are anticipated to rise in FY '24 -'25 due to the transition to BS-VI OBD II norms and the projected growth in two-wheeler sales following the general elections.

items.statement: EGT localization SOP expected April 2025 at Bosch plant
items.quote: We expect SOP, the start of production in April '25 because you have to understand that these are quite complex lines. And -- but it's on the way. It's decided. It's ordered SOP April '25.

items.statement: Expects 10-15% of trucks sold by 2030 to use hydrogen ICE technology
items.quote: We expect between 10% to 15% of all trucks sold by 2030 to be with hydrogen ICE technology.

items.statement: Building Technologies outlook positive for FY25 with significant project wins across verticals
items.quote: We anticipate a positive outlook for Building Technologies business in '24-'25.

items.statement: TREM V implementation currently indicated for April 2026, may shift by a quarter
items.quote: The current indication is April '26 for TREM V introduction. We hope that standard does not get pushed. It's possible that it's plus minus one quarter earlier even.

items.statement: Exports at 8.1% of net sales in FY24, working to increase over coming years
items.quote: Exports currently for FY '23-'24 stood at 8.1% overall of our total net sales. And we are working on increasing this over the coming years.

items.statement: CV injector localization ramp-up ongoing at Nashik, main steps completed
items.quote: We have a very good ramp -up of the line of the assembly interesting. Meanwhile, we had last year or in this financial -- in the last financial year, we had a ramp -up of the component business.

items.statement: Portfolio realignment ongoing, may continue for next year, no fixed timeline
items.quote: I would say this is an ongoing portfolio realignment overall. And yes, if I were to give you a broad time line, then maybe it's the next 1 year. We will see some amounts of portfolio readjustments continuing to happen.

items.statement: Building Technologies diversification expected to complete by Q1-Q2 2025
items.quote: We expect this to go through by Q1, Q2 of 2025.

items.statement: OBD 2.2 norms for two-wheelers applicable in 2025, significant technology upgrade for OEMs
items.quote: The OBD 2.2 norms should be applicable in 2025.

items.statement: Other expenses reduced due to hive-off of digital mobility business and sustainable cost measures
items.quote: One topic is that we do have a lower spending related to the new business, which we hived off. On the other side, we also put in place cost measures, which are sustainable.

items.statement: Plan for surplus cash utilization being worked on, will communicate when clear
items.quote: There is certainly a plan that's being worked on. And as soon as we are clear with it, we will let you know.

items.statement: Capex outlay guided at INR 500 crores per year across the company
items.quote: The capex outla y should be in the range of INR 500 crores a year put together across the company

items.statement: Solar power project capex of INR 200 crores, waste management project INR 70 crores, plus spending on 3 mines and hydropower project
items.quote: projects as we told, one is the INR200 crores, we will be spending on the solar power project, then we'll be spending on 3 mines and some spending will be on the hydropower project during the current financial year. Balasubramanian: Okay, sir. So what kind of... Sarda Energy & Padam Jain: Waste management project, we will be spending about INR70 crores. So , total will be about INR500

items.statement: Gare Palma coal mine EC received for capacity increase from 1.44 to 1.68 million tons; CTE and CTO expected soon; further increase to 1.80 million tons proposed in current year
items.quote: We have received environment clearance for increase in the mining Sarda Energy & capacity from 1.44 million tons to 1.68 million tons. The CTE and CTO is expected soon. We propose to increase it further to 1.80 million tons during the current financial year

items.statement: Silico manganese 60% grade price currently around INR 85,000 vs average realization of INR 67,000 in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Current price of silicon manga nese of 60% grade is around INR85,000 against the average realization of INR67,000 in quarter 4 of FY'24

items.statement: Revenue diversification into power and mining to decouple from metal cyclicality; solar power for captive consumption to reduce carbon footprint
items.quote: The company continues to diversify its revenues. Revenue from power and mining will increase over period, decoupling it from cyclicality of metal industry. Journey from here is exciting. We are adding solar power for captive consumption which will help in reducing our carbon footprint in our manufacturing

items.statement: SKS Power acquisition outflow in range of INR 2,000 crores plus minus; major outflow not considered in revenue projections
items.quote: That is already under process. This is in the range of INR2,000 crores plus minus is there. That is a larger acquisition.

items.statement: No material volume improvement expected in current financial year except productivity gains; revenue impact mainly from price effect
items.quote: For the current financial year whatever performance productivity improvements nominal whatever is there that will be there. Otherwise, there won't be any material improvement in the quantum side, but yes the effect of the price increase will definitely be reflected into the revenue.

items.statement: Manganese ore supply disruption from Australian South32 mine expected to normalize by July; company has sufficient inventory
items.quote: Because of that, there has been a supply disruption. Because of supply disruption prices have moved up. But we understand that, that is expected to be restored soon. And maybe I think by July, things should get to normal.

items.statement: 30 MW turbine generator replacement ordered, expected operational in H1 FY27; all 3 turbines will stand replaced
items.quote: The company has placed order for replacement of existing 30-megawatt TG set with new energy-efficient TG set to save energy and reduce carbon footprint. The new TG set is expected to be operational in the first half of FY '27. With this, all the 3 turbines shall stand replaced.

items.statement: Indonesian JV coal mine produced 5.58 lakh tons in FY24; expects to produce about 1 million tons in FY25
items.quote: The Indonesian joint venture coal mine produced 5.58 lakh metric ton coal in FY '24 and 2.24 lakh metric ton coal during the quarter. We expect to produce about 1 million ton coal from this mine in FY '25.

items.statement: Industry outlook for FY25 projected flat or 4-5% lower than FY24, with potential single-digit growth
items.quote: When compared to FY24 to 25, we are projecting flat or about 4% to 5% less.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 2,500-2,600 crore if market returns to FY19 peak volumes
items.quote: So very comfortably we'll be reaching around 2,500 to 2,600 crores with the current presence if the market reaches '18-19.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 50-60 crore per year for next 2 years including automation and new product development
items.quote: the investment the next 2 years kind of about 50 to 60 crores level. But apart from sustenance CAPEX, the specific automation projects, new product development and all this stuff.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 0.4% in FY24 despite 0.5% commodity price settlement impact
items.quote: Though the revenue was lowered by 0.3%-0.4%. And during the year, your company has generated about close to 196 crores of cash and we have no borrowings at this moment of time and all the balance sheet parameters are quite strong.

items.statement: Targeting early-teen margins (13-15%) as market volumes recover with current efficiency initiatives
items.quote: Definitely we are committed to grow in terms of the bottom line and every initiative is taken is towards that only. As you said market it goes up. Definitely margin will go much higher than what we are having it today. But whether it is 13 or 14 depends on the product mix and vario us things. But definitely you will see a significant growth in the margins

items.statement: Four new product launches in FY25: MS 185 axle for 49+ tons, 9-meter bus axle, 325mm and 360mm brakes
items.quote: So, both the bus axle and our largest axle MS 185 and then the brakes, all of them will b e launched this year. And we'll be realizing some revenue out of this new product launches

items.statement: Inventory reduced substantially in Q4 FY24, positive outlook driven by government infrastructure spend and bus orders
items.quote: One good thing is the inventory has come down substantially in the la st quarter. Even though the last quarter production is less things have been the inventory h as come down. I am sure that this year we have a positive outlook, when I say positive outlook, it will be single digit growth would be still there

items.statement: Defence business revenue realization delayed, long-term investment with sporadic government orders
items.quote: Of course, we spend a lot of money on CAPEX on Defence. But the real realization of Defence is still not started. The government is giving orde r little here and there, but it gets a long-term investment

items.statement: Commodity price settlement reduced FY24 revenue by 0.5% with no P&L impact due to pass-through
items.quote: I said the commodit y settlement which has lowered the revenue by 0.5% which is a commodity which you accommodated in the year 2023-24 ISA. There is nothing impacted to the P&L

items.statement: EPS grew from Rs 80 in FY19 to Rs 109 despite 10-12% lower market volumes
items.quote: If you really see our EPS in '18-19, the peak volume is at Rs. 80 and with a 10% to 12% reduction our EPS is about Rs. 109 per share.

items.statement: Zero borrowings and Rs 196 crore cash generated in FY24
items.quote: And during the year, your company has generated about close to 196 crores of cash and we have no borrowings at this moment of time and all the balance sheet parameters are quite strong.

items.statement: Cummins-Meritor acquisition synergy progressing in off-highway and on-highway OEM penetration, no major wins announced yet
items.quote: Good amount of activities have been done in the last one year and we are coming into some stages but we are not in a position to announce anything that yes, we made a big win at this point in time.

items.statement: E-Axle components supplied from existing capacity, remote-mount design preferred by OEMs currently
items.quote: The thing is we still have a capacity to manufactur e some of the key components required for the E Axle. So, at this point of time, E Axle is basically part of Cummins-Meritor. But we supply them the parts wherever it is required and the volumes at this point of time, it is too early for us to tell how this overall E Axle business is going t o develop

items.statement: Domestic product order book increased ~11% to Rs. 348 crores, giving strong revenue visibility for FY25
items.quote: The domestic product business saw growth of around 19% in FY24 to Rs. 261 crores with the order book increasing by about 11% to Rs. 348 crores, giving a strong revenue visibility and a positive outlook for FY25.

items.statement: Domestic project order book stood at Rs. 3,054 crores as on 31st March 2024
items.quote: The order book for the domestic project business stood at Rs. 3,054 crores.

items.statement: International order book stood at Rs. 458 crores as on 31st March 2024
items.quote: In the international business, the order book stood at Rs. 458 crores as on 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook for domestic product business with robust order book and inquiry flows from oil & gas, sewage and drainage segments
items.quote: We see a very strong outlook going ahead because the order book remains strong and the inquiry flows are very strong, so very positive about this, the domestic product business.

items.statement: International core industrial pumps business outlook remains strong driven by MENA region demand and Finder aftermarket revenues
items.quote: The outlook for the core industrial pumps business of Gruppo Aturia remains strong, driven by robust demand in the MENA region and strong aftermarket revenues from Finder.

items.statement: CAPEX not significant, mostly brownfield additions, no major CAPEX planned
items.quote: CAPEX is not significant. These are mostly Brownfield additions, so no major CAPEX.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 15-20% for both project and product segments, currently within range
items.quote: Our aim is around 15% and 20% in the project cycle. So we are very choosy on that. We don't like to do projects with lower margins.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margins for FY24 at 17.92%, Q4 FY24 at 17.31%
items.quote: For the Financial Year ending 2024, the Company's consolidated revenues from operations stood at Rs. 1,664 crores, representing a 4% year-on-year growth. EBITDA was Rs. 298 crores, representing a 12% year-on-year increase with EBITDA margins at 17.92%.

items.statement: One Madhya Pradesh Jal Nigam contract terminated (Rs. 155-160 crores unexecuted), company disputing termination citing land allotment delay
items.quote: However, one of the Madhya Pradesh Jal Nigam contracts was terminated by the client due to slow progress. We have disputed this termination, citing that the land for construction was allotted only in December 2023 causing the delay.

items.statement: Actively pursuing inorganic acquisitions in core industrial pump business, expecting positive outcomes by mid-FY25
items.quote: We are actively pursuing them and in lots of conversations. So we expect to have some results starting from mid-FY25.

items.statement: Targeting domestic revenue mix of 66% project / 34% product (2:1 ratio), currently at 76%/24%
items.quote: So today, if you see that the project segment is 76% and 24% is product and our target was around 66 and 34, 2:1 ratio in India.

items.statement: Expect good revenue growth in FY25 for both project and product segments, execution run rate of Rs. 343 crores in Q4 FY24 gives confidence
items.quote: Based on this strength and the achievement in the last quarter, we expect to see good revenue growth in FY25.

items.statement: Project order book execution timeline 24-30 months, product order book 4-8 months
items.quote: Project order book is normally 24 to 30 months.

items.statement: Most project contracts have price variation clauses to pass on raw material increases
items.quote: Yes, these contracts, most of them have price variation clauses.

items.statement: Navy framework agreement worth Rs. 17-18 crores, type tests completed, supply to continue for 20-30 years
items.quote: The Navy business was a framework agreement for all new types of pumps, which we have introduced in the fleet and after this framework that means the type tests are done, the shipyards can order these for all subsequent ships. So the framework agreement was for about Rs. 17-Rs. 18 crores.

items.statement: R&D spending roughly $2 million equivalent across businesses annually
items.quote: R&D is a constant process for us across all our businesses. Roughly, we would be spending about 2 million across our businesses, $2 million or euros or something.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin of 15-20% with a good Speciality-commodity balance, as envisaged during Dahej CAPEX.
items.quote: we would expect EBITDA of between 15% to 20% and that is what we were envisaging when we made the CAPEX at Dahej.

items.statement: No significant CAPEX planned; only minor debottlenecking for Boron business costing less than Rs. 10-15 crores.
items.quote: Yeah, very little CAPEX. It will be some debottlenecking type of thing, but nothing significant.

items.statement: Good visibility in most segments except agrochemicals; Speciality chemical volumes were very poor in FY23 and FY24.
items.quote: certainly from a volume point of view, financial year 23 and 24 was very poor for the Speciality chemicals.

items.statement: Speciality chemicals target 20%+ margins; commodity margins range from zero to +/-5%. New products target 30% margin.
items.value: 20% and up for specialities; zero plus minus 5% for commodity
items.quote: for the special ities, 20% and up is the number ; while for the commodity it could be anything, it could be zero plus minus 5

items.statement: Topline reduction driven by lower raw material prices; delta between selling price and raw material cost improved marginally.
items.quote: although we reduced our top line, the delta between the selling price and the cost of raw materials has in fact improved a little bit

items.statement: Most sectors showing recovery except agrochemicals where worst is over; Europe remains challenging, US and India better.
items.quote: All sectors, as I mentioned, apart from the agrochemical sector, seem to be doing better. Again, we are not experts on any particular sector.

items.statement: Current revenue split 50:50 Speciality:non-Speciality; long-term target is two-thirds Speciality, one-third commodity.
items.quote: right now it's about 50 :50, b ut if you take the long -term average before we made the investment at Dahej, it was two-thirds Speciality and one-third commodity

items.statement: Agrochemical sector (10-12% of revenue, mostly Speciality) had near-zero demand; Chinese dumping and Red Sea logistics disrupted supply.
items.quote: whatever business we had for the agrochemical sector has been near zero.

items.statement: Repaying Rs. 2 crores monthly; aim to eliminate all fixed term debt in 3 years assuming no further CAPEX.
items.quote: we are paying back about Rs. 2 crores every month and depending on our cash flow, we will be reducing the debt.

items.statement: Dedicated plant expansion requires 3 years from environmental clearance; multipurpose plants quicker but still need permissions.
items.quote: from day zero it would be 3 years before you could actually have commercial output in case of dedicated plants.

items.statement: Boron business can reach Rs. 150 crores from current CAPEX with minor debottlenecking; overall business Rs. 450-500 crores at current raw material prices.
items.quote: we believe that we could do about Rs. 150 crores from our current scale of CAPEX, just from the Boron business.

items.statement: Speciality chemicals capacity utilization at ~50%; bulk chemicals above 90%. Automotive Speciality product successful in commercial trials, ramping up over next few quarters.
items.quote: in the Speciality chemicals while I don't have an exact number and it depends on product to product, but I would say we are at about 50% capacity.

items.statement: Added two directors: Haren Parekh (finance) and Kuldeep Tiwari (operations); Dahej site received Responsible Care Certificate.
items.quote: We also added another person, Mr. Kuldeep Tiwari, as an Executive Director to head our operations and he brings with him a couple of decades of operating experience

items.statement: Installed LPG replacing furnace oil; turbine at Roha using waste heat recovery reduces grid dependence; Dahej >90% energy self-reliant.
items.quote: We've installed LPG for one of our operations replacing furnace oil, that's a much cleaner burning fuel and we continue on our journey towards self-reliance in energy.

items.statement: Ambernath land sale (Rs. 5 crores) delayed due to buyer permissions; not in company's control.
items.quote: this is unfortunately not in our hands, and it depends on permissions that the buyer needs to get and things like that

items.statement: Management avoids forward-looking topline/bottomline projections; will discuss quarterly. FY25 recovery uncertain but visibility good except agrochemicals.
items.quote: It's difficult to predict and I don't like to make forward -looking projections on top line or bottomline. We'll take it, as you know, we'll discuss every quarter

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% plus for FY25 with margins commensurate and order inflow target of INR 8,000-10,000 crores (around INR 9,000 crores)
items.value: 20%+ revenue growth; INR 8,000-10,000 cr order inflow
items.quote: Revenue growth, as we have been maintaining, it will be 20% plus in terms of revenue. Margin also will be commensurate to that. And order inflow, we're expecting the order what we can see in our horizon goes to INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores say INR9,000 crores, our target is to have this year's order inflow.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 10% plus, difficult to improve significantly beyond that in construction industry
items.quote: It's difficult. You see, construction industry has got their own standard margin and revenue. So 10% plus is, I think, okay. If we can do something better, we'll be happy, we'll try that. But I think we have to live with this margin, 10%, a little bit more than 10%.

items.statement: Target 30% of revenue from overseas in 2-3 years; currently pursuing overseas opportunities with 20%+ share expected in near term
items.quote: We aim to do around 30% of revenue from overseas by another 2 years' time or 3 years' time. Now today, the kind of job which we're pursuing, if we get some of them, I think it will be around 20% plus on our overseas business.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected around INR 250 crores, lower than last year's INR 450+ crores due to prior TBM and trench cutter investments
items.quote: Capex will be less than last year because last year or second last year we had to invest for the tunnel boring machines and trench cutters. So it was more than INR450 crores plus I think last year. This year it could be around INR250 crores in that range

items.statement: Order book as of March 2024 is a little under INR 20,000 crores; new orders secured in FY24 were about INR 6,900 crores
items.quote: During the year, we have secured new orders of about INR6,900 crores. And our order book as of March '24 is a little under INR20,000 crores.

items.statement: Strong pipeline of INR 25,000-30,000 crores across domestic and overseas, with 50-50 split in marine segment; submitted bids around INR 20,000 crores
items.quote: I can see around INR25,000 crores to INR30,000 crores jobs in different stage either in tender or we submitted and tender to come they come in 6 months, 7 months' time.

items.statement: Top 8 projects contribute 80% of revenue; focusing on bigger jobs (INR 1,000-3,000 crores) with fewer players and better qualification
items.quote: If you see today, our work in hand, we may have 50 jobs in hand. And out of that, about eight contribute to 80% of our revenue. So the moment you go for the bigger jobs, you have less players.

items.statement: No major legacy project issues remaining; Bangalore Metro completed, only claims/arbitration left which would be upside
items.quote: Yes, as far as the projects are concerned, we had Bangalore Metro as all of you know that is in the last two quarters before it has been behind us. So, what is remaining now only is the claim and arbitration.

items.statement: Overseas contracts typically fixed price with escalation built into bid price; mobilization advances of 10-15% received on recent overseas jobs
items.quote: See, basically in foreign contract, escalation normally you have to cover in your price. That is what we see in foreign contract.

items.statement: TBMs depreciated over 5-6 years; working capital cycle sustainable at current levels with payments received on time per contract terms
items.quote: The TBMs are depreciated. The current ones that we have in use are being depreciated over a period of five to six years.

items.statement: Management expects ~10% topline growth in FY25, targeting around Rs. 4,800 crores revenue, with potential to reach Rs. 5,000 crores if CV and car industries grow.
items.quote: More or less we are saying that we will go by 10% this year on the topline. So, that would come out to a number of Rs. 4,800 crores, around that number.

items.statement: Overall volume target of 20 million wheels in FY25 versus 19 million in FY24.
items.quote: On numbers, we are looking at 20 million wheels this year versus 19 million last year.

items.statement: Domestic CV industry expected flat to tepid growth in FY25 due to election year and monsoons.
items.quote: we all know that this is an election year and so there is, we have seen a slight slowdown in the CV industry so far and this is going to be followed by monsoons. last year we did the highest CV volume. This year our forecast is ranging from a flat year to somewhat tepid growth

items.statement: Domestic aluminum wheel business projected to grow ~10% in FY25 based on past nominations.
items.quote: On the domestic aluminum wheel side, we expect about a 10% growth. This is based on our past performance, past projects that we have been nominated for.

items.statement: Two-wheeler EV wheel business targeted to grow ~16% in FY25.
items.quote: And there we are leaders now for wheels and they are in much better value addition on these wheels and this business should grow about 16%.

items.statement: Passenger car steel wheel business projected to grow 10.6% in FY25 after regaining projects.
items.quote: So, but this year I am glad to tell you that we are projecting a 10.6% growth in the steel wheel for passenger cars.

items.statement: Tractor business expected to grow ~12% in FY25 driven by market share gains from new LTAs.
items.quote: So, here I can say with prominence that our tractor share of business is going to go up this year and this means about 12% growth in revenue in terms of volume and obviously value also will follow suit.

items.statement: Export business expected to grow ~10% in FY25 with new OTR product lines gaining traction in Europe and America.
items.quote: We expect this to grow by another 10% this year and in the export business we're adding new product lines like off-road vehicle wheels.

items.statement: Aluminum knuckles revenue to start from September, targeting ~Rs. 35 crores in FY25, then more than double and 4x thereafter.
items.quote: We should start our revenue growth from September onwards. Revenue is coming in from knuckles perhaps a little bit earlier and this year we should be doing close to about if I am not mistaken, about Rs. 35 crores in revenue and then going forward, we expect this revenue to go more than double and then after that, this revenue to go more than 4x.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at ~Rs. 225 crores, to be funded entirely from internal accruals with no fresh borrowing.
items.quote: In terms of overall CAPEX, which was there on the table, I think for next year was in the range of Rs. 225 odd crores which can be funded entirely from the accruals, and nothing needs to be borrowed from the outside market.

items.statement: New alloy wheel capacity expansion planned near Maruti in Punjab/Haryana, timing FY26-FY27.
items.quote: So, FY26, FY27, yes, but we would definitely need to come closer to Maruti. So, I am just giving you a heads up and all to the investor community that we may be coming up with a new factory in Punjab, very close to Maruti.

items.statement: EBITDA per wheel expected to improve above FY24's Rs. 253 due to favorable mix (alloy, export, tractor) and price correction in passenger car steel wheels.
items.quote: 253 was the number last year, so definitely you will see a much better number than 253.

items.statement: Price correction agreed with major OEMs on passenger car steel wheels (70-80% of business), effective from April 1, impact visible in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Once that happens, you will see the impact of that itself in the first quarter. So, because that will be backdated from 1st of April.

items.statement: Debt peaked at Rs. 1,048 crores as of March 2024; scheduled repayments of ~Rs. 105 crores annually for next 3 years plus potential prepayments from accruals.
items.quote: So, as we guided last time that the debt that you are seeing as on March 24 is the peak debt in our books and subsequently it should taper down.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis impact largely absorbed; customers adjusted inventories and freight advantage vs Asian competitors persists.
items.quote: Customers have adjusted their inventories. So, there will be other dynamics rather than the Red Sea issue that will come into play.

items.statement: Alloy wheel order book visibility extends to 2027; Maruti nomination secured with potential 20-25% market share over 2-3 years.
items.quote: I have an order book in front of me that is extending up till 2027. I see the numbers. I see the possibility of expanding my market beyond India.

items.statement: AMW acquisition completed; equipment being relocated to Jamshedpur for CV capacity expansion of ~400,000 wheels operational by June.
items.quote: We are adding a new CV capacity of almost 400,000 wheels that is coming from equipment that was lying in AMW. We're not letting the equipment idle. We're just moving that equipment to other parts of our locations where they're already producing in mass.

items.statement: Target INR 1,000 crores revenue from India over next 5 years
items.quote: We remain optimistic on building our India presence with 2 brands, both Himeya and Atmosphere, and we continue to want to achieve revenues of approximately INR1,000 crores from India over the next 5 years.

items.statement: Aim to reach full capacity utilization in 18-24 months
items.quote: We would like to head in that direction and be running at full capacity over the next 18 months or so, 18 months, 2 years kind of time frame, if not earlier.

items.statement: Current capacity can support revenue of just over INR 4,000 crores
items.quote: Approximately INR4,000 crores, just over INR4,000 crores, is our estimate.

items.statement: EBITDA margin typically operates in 18-22% band in stable conditions
items.quote: And the band of EBITDA that I've shared with investors and other stakeholders, we typically operate in the 18% to 22% band depending on product mix and timing and market conditions.

items.statement: Demand environment stable with slight negative bias in major markets
items.quote: So the absolute demand remains stable. I would say, there is an overhang of caution in major markets. So I'm using the word stable with a slight negative bias, if you will, at least in major markets.

items.statement: Growth to be driven by broader product mix, larger client mix, and more markets served
items.quote: And therefore, we will endeavor to continue to enhance -- to continue to grow, will be driven by a broader product mix, larger client mix, and more markets that we serve.

items.statement: Lost revenue from Bed Bath & Beyond wind-down and exited non-core product categories losing INR 200 crores
items.quote: We've also pulled out of some categories of products, which I've shared with stakeholders earlier, we lost INR200 crores on that front because we don't see that as core going forward.

items.statement: No major capex planned beyond annual maintenance and organic requirements
items.quote: We don't have any plans for any additional capex of any consequence other than our annual maintenance and organic capex requirements and something we've shared very openly and clearly with stakeholders.

items.statement: Plan to raise equity sometime this fiscal to strengthen balance sheet
items.quote: So keeping all of these things in line, we would like to strengthen and raise equity sometime this fiscal, that's what we're running for.

items.statement: Target net debt to EBITDA below 3.5x and DSCR in 1.8x-2.2x range
items.quote: So we would like to bring our net debt to EBITDA levels to below 3.5x, which is where we used to be. And so we would like to head there. And we would like to make sure that our DSCRs are in the region of 1.8x to 2.2x.

items.statement: Focus on growth, deleveraging, and strengthening equity over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes, focusing on growth, focusing on deleveraging, and focusing on strengthening equity. These are the 3 things I would like to focus on, and that's what we've shared with stakeholders.

items.statement: Brand demand similar to private label, no higher demand for brands
items.quote: I don't see much movement. I think that the same logic that applies to private label in terms of demand would apply to the world of brands.

items.statement: Working on reducing working capital cycle time but no specific target disclosed
items.quote: Well, see, that's something I wouldn't want to specifically spell out. But I would say that we are working to be better our current cycle time.

items.statement: Peak revenue was INR 3,200+ crores in FY22, aim to return to that level and grow beyond
items.quote: Our peak revenues were about INR 3,200 plus crores in FY '22, and then we lost some steam post some of the macro issues that the market faced. And so we want to head back in that direction and then onwards from there.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 sales turnover guidance of INR1,500-1,600 crores with blended EBITDA margin of 16%
items.quote: we are looking for a sales turnover of over INR1500 to INR1600 crores on consolidated basis and margins should be now to 16% on blended basis

items.statement: Full capacity consolidated revenue target of INR1,700-1,800 crores when all plants fully operational
items.quote: From our subsidiaries and it can be on a console basis we are looking for a sales of about INR1,700 crores to INR1,800 crores when all the plants will be fully operational

items.statement: FY25 capex plan of INR70-80 crores including solar installation and maintenance, expansion capex to be finalized soon
items.quote: roughly, as of now, we are having the capex plan about INR70 to INR80 crores, but for capacity expenses we will come out with the plans very soon

items.statement: Warangal unit capex of INR600 crores spent out of envisaged INR650 crores, third rPET line operational by June 2024
items.quote: we have spent over about INR600 crores on our Warangal unit and almost all the plants have been operating, except this rPET granule line, which is expected to be operational by end of next month

items.statement: Legacy business order book visibility only 1-2 months, textile sector recovery expected from August onwards
items.quote: in our legacy business order book is not of 3 months and 4 months. It is hardly 1 to 2 months only, but we are seeing the improvement in the sector from August onwards

items.quote: We earned EBITDA of INR. 27.79 crores during Q4 FY24, dropped to 11.72% by 101 basis points over Q3 FY24 EBITDA margins of 12.73%

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 15.40%, up 137 bps QoQ with subsidiaries contributing INR19.27 crores EBITDA
items.quote: EBITDA margins at 15.40% have improved by 137 basis points. In absolute terms, we achieved revenue of INR 305.53 crores and earned EBITDA of INR47.06 crores

items.statement: Warangal unit achieved operating profits over 22% in Q4 FY24 with improved capacity utilization
items.quote: We achieved a very good set of numbers from our Warangal plant where we achieved operating profits of more than 22% during the quarter

items.statement: Textile sector recovery expected around July-August 2024, legacy business maintaining 11%+ EBITDA margins
items.quote: we are looking for the recovery in the textile sector which seems to be happening around July and August month

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting from 65% textile to 50% packaging and 50% textile/technical textile in next 1-2 years
items.quote: going forward, say, in the next one or two years, we are seeing almost 50% contribution in sales will be from the packaging sector, 50% from the textile and technical textile sector

items.statement: HDPE/PP recycling delayed due to pending FSSAI/EFSA food-grade regulations and unorganized sector competition
items.quote: the regulation for approval from FSSAI for food safety of HDPE, PP is still pending. The FSSAI and EFSA both are not very much clear

items.statement: QIP and preferential warrants proceeds used to repay all working capital borrowings and term debt, achieving near zero debt status
items.quote: On the back of funds raised at the recent QIP as well as preferential warrants issue, we have set off entire working capital borrowings as well as repaid term debt of the holding company achieving almost zero debt status currently

items.statement: Third rPET granule line (14,000 tons) expected operational by June 2024, taking total rPET capacity to 42,000 tons
items.quote: 3rd line is also expected to be operational by June end

items.statement: New capacity commissioning timeline 15-18 months from approval, expansion plans to be finalized soon
items.quote: it takes about 15 months to 18 months' time to commission the new facility fully operational

items.statement: Warrant conversion period up to September 2025, no conversion planned in FY25
items.quote: the warrant currency is for 18 months and we have allotted the warrants in January itself. So, the 18-month period is up to September 25. So, based on the requirement of the funds, we will convert the warrants in trenches also we can, but as of now there is no plan to convert in this financial year

items.statement: Next two years focus on consolidating North, East, Central corridors; next three years entering South and West
items.quote: The next two years are going to be more consolidating in the North, East, Central corridor, and the next three years also entering South and West.

items.statement: Customer GTV grew 7% YoY to Rs 1.08 lakh crore in FY24, second consecutive year above Rs 1 lakh crore
items.quote: It's been a relatively flat year because of headwinds in the AePS business. So only a 7% growth , 107,000 crores compared to 100,000 crores in the previous year .

items.statement: Service fee gross margin grew 10% YoY to Rs 169 crore in FY24 from Rs 154 crore in FY23
items.quote: Service fees, the main number that we track,which has grown from Rs. 154 crores the previous year to Rs. 169 crores in the last financial year .

items.statement: EBITDA of Rs 14.2 crore and PAT of Rs 12.1 crore achieved at consolidated level for continued and Spice Money business in FY24
items.quote: We have achieved an EBITDA of Rs. 14.2 crores for the financial year and a PAT level of Rs. 12.1 crores at consolidated level .

items.statement: Cash and Cash-out GM contribution declined from 77% to 68%; Collections grew from 8% to 14%; Subscription packs now 6%; Banking 2%
items.quote: If you look at our core business of Cash and Cash out, it's declined from a GM contribution point of view from 77% to 68%. And we have seen new product lines, especially if you look at collections, our contribution of collections to gross margin has grown from 8% to 14%.

items.statement: Cash Management Services GTV grew 54% YoY to Rs 27,682 crore in FY24; large CMS Adhikaris up 23% to 7,300 contributing 90% of GTV
items.quote: So, we are close to Rs. 27,000 crores in FY'24. This is the gross transaction value of the collections made from the branches compared to Rs. 18,000 crores in the past year .

items.statement: Bharat Bill Payment System GTV grew 90% YoY to Rs 4,190 crore; EMI loan repayments grew 2.4x to Rs 3,160 crore; repeat customer base nearly 50%
items.quote: year-on-year overall while we have grown 90% in customer GTV Rs. 4,190 crores compared to Rs. 2,210 cr ores which is about 1.9x growth. Within this EMI , loan repayments have grown 2.4x year-on-year, Rs. 3,160 crores from Rs. 1,325 crores

items.statement: AePS industry declined 6% due to 2FA implementation and issuer bank transaction limits; Spice Money GTV declined only 5%, gaining market share to 17.53% in Q4
items.quote: In FY'23, if you look at the industry, it did about the Off-Us part of the industry, FY'23 was about Rs. 3,33,000 crores and in FY'24 that's dropped 6% to Rs. 3,14,000 crores.

items.statement: Lifetime merchant base reached 1.4 million (14 lakh) with 4 lakh monthly transacting; 55% CAGR over 5 years from 240,000 in FY20
items.quote: to -date lifetime we have onboarded about 14 lakh small merchants, who we refer to as Spice Money Adhikaris on our web and app platform, majority of them use our mobile app to deliver ATM and other financial services to c onsumers in rural India

items.statement: Planning to enter lending business via strategic NBFC acquisition to create credit products for merchants and small businesses in Emerging India
items.quote: In our board meeting recently where we adopted the financial results for last year , we have also passed a resolution and made the necessary announcements where we are looking to enter the lending business through a strategic NBFC acquisition within the company.

items.statement: Lifetime CASA accounts opened crossed 3.5 lakh; Q4 saw 16,000 Adhikaris each opening 5+ accounts; focus on float and cross-sell
items.quote: Lifetime now we have opened over 3 lakh accounts in semi -urban and rural and what we are tracking here is growth in float in terms of people using these accounts.

items.statement: Third-party lending facilitated nearly 100,000 loans lifetime; key learnings: inherent credit demand, need for customized products with friendly repayment, erratic supply from partners
items.quote: We have seen significant learning. So more than the number s, I would encourage you to look at the box where we're talking about our three key learnings, right.

items.statement: Credit business is long-term (10-20 years); will build brick-by-brick with no short-term number commitments; focus on product innovation, physical proximity, enhanced risk management
items.quote: This is a business over the next 10 to 15 to 20 years that we want to build, and we will build it like brick-by-brick, block-by-block.

items.statement: Changed device capitalization policy in FY24; previously capitalized devices and provided right-to-use to Adhikaris, now expensed
items.quote: This is basically a change in capitalization policy because till FY'23, we were capitalizing the devices and providing a right -to-use to the Ad hikaris. This is something that we changed as a policy in FY '24

items.statement: No short-term numbers committed; building long-term business over 10-20 years brick-by-brick
items.quote: I will not commit to any short-term numbers here. This is a business over the next 10 to 15 to 20 years that we want to build, and we will build it like brick-by-brick, block-by-block.

items.statement: FY25 AePS business muted; focus on counter share; collections growing steadily
items.quote: I think that effectively this year is going to be little mute in terms of the impact on the A ePS business, but our growth is going to be to grow counter share and that's what we're going to focus on

items.statement: No AUM target for FY25; focus on completing NBFC acquisition and testing products in Q4
items.quote: So, I don't think we put any AUM target for this financial year. I think our focus is going to be first to complete the process of acquisition and once that's done, we're going to start by a few products which we know have worked on the marketplace that we can work with our own capital and we're going to test out those products with the NBFC.

items.statement: UPI wallet pilots planned for Q2 FY25
items.quote: So UPI wallet in the Q2 is where we see us being ready to run some pilots around the wallet.

items.statement: Significant tech and innovation budget allocated for FY25 and FY26, mainly hiring tech talent
items.quote: I think in this coming year and the next year, we have actually allocated a good number for tech and innovation and it's mainly in the form of hiring tech talent.

items.statement: EBITDA doubled from Rs 10.2 cr to Rs 21.7 cr in FY24 due to gross margin improvement and lower indirect costs
items.quote: So that has improved EBITDA almost by 100% from Rs. 10.2 crores to Rs. 21.7 crores

items.statement: Collections business growing steadily, not hockey-stick; aiming to add large enterprises
items.quote: Collections is a key business for us, but it is a B2B business. So, it's heavy lifting on the ground in terms of working with the enterprise agents to map them to collection centers that we have. So , it's a business that's growing steadily, not a hockey sti ck, but st eadily business growth and we are hoping that we'll continue to grow it

items.statement: CMS business drives higher GTV but lower margin vs other products
items.quote: it's a nature for the product mix due to which because we are doing a CMS business which have kind of a more in terms of G TV standpoint of view but having a lesser margin in comparison to other

items.statement: Legacy business closure cash burn to continue this year and possibly next year; indirect costs to halve from Rs 4.2 cr/quarter
items.quote: We're trying to find solutions where we can, keep the cash burn as minimal as possible, as Sunil mentioned, some numbers, but there is cost to closure.

items.statement: No rush to fundraise; may consider for credit business after model stabilizes and proof-of-concept demonstrated
items.quote: Directionally, there might be need to think about fundraising for the credit business, but something that we are going to come back on. I think right now our focus is to make sure that we drive operating leverage and make sure that many things especially on the credit side, we're able to build products that wor th using our own c apital, maybe work in a some sort of a co-lending model, but initial

items.statement: Debt-free company; borrowings only for treasury operations (OD/FD) to open collection accounts
items.quote: effectively we don't have any debt, only debt or the borrowings, which is coming under the financ ials i s against our OD and FD just for the treasury management, effectively we don't have any debt , we are kind of a debt -free company

items.statement: Holding in Digi Asia Bios Pte Ltd is a little over 3% after rights issue
items.quote: Lalit, it's a little over 3%.

items.statement: Projecting conservative revenue growth of 15% for FY25
items.quote: We are projecting a conservative revenue growth of 15%.

items.statement: Expecting FY25 revenue of INR 2,470-2,480 crores excluding defence
items.quote: The total figure that we are getting it's close to INR 25-30 crores and for defence we have taken only INR 60 crores in that. So it comes to about INR 2,470-2,480 crores.

items.statement: Targeting FY25 EBITDA margin of 11.5% with potential to reach 12%+ by year-end
items.quote: And our internal EBITDA margin is plus 12%, but here we'll like to come in at 11.5%.

items.statement: Repaying INR 90 crores debt in FY25 and INR 80 crores in FY26
items.quote: During this current year, we'll be repaying around INR 90 crores.

items.statement: Improved EBITDA by 50-60 bps in FY24 despite INR 140 crore revenue loss
items.quote: However, in spite of that, we have been able to maintain our EBITDA levels and improved a bit. So it is around 50 bps-60 bps, we have been able to improve upon the EBITDA level.

items.statement: Expecting rural market recovery to boost 2-wheeler and low-end vehicle demand
items.quote: There is a lot of excitement in the rural market and it is being predicted that bulk of the increase will actually come from the rural market and we are expecting a good monsoon also this year.

items.statement: Maruti Suzuki share increasing from 5% to 10-12% of turnover
items.quote: Earlier our supplies to Maruti was just about 5% of our turnover. We'll be touching around 10%-12% of our turnover

items.statement: Defence revenue uncertain due to approval delays; guiding INR 60 crores vs internal target of INR 100+ crores
items.quote: We are guiding you to INR 50-60 crores. I'll let my colleague Ish also talk on this, he's looking after the defence.

items.statement: Defence revenue expected to double/triple annually; FY26 target much above INR 200-300 crores
items.quote: It should be much above INR 200-300 crores.

items.statement: Hosur land acquired for Toyota proximity; investment mainly in building, equipment transferred from Toyota
items.quote: We are working on the details of Hosur plant. And there would be a lot of equipment that would be transferred from the Toyota plant itself.

items.statement: White-collar headcount reduced by 400+ for permanent savings
items.quote: Although we have been able to reduce our white-collar numbers by around m ore than 400 person, the headcounts have been reduced and that is going to give us permanent savings

items.statement: Solar power implemented at main plants for power cost savings
items.quote: Solar has also been introduced. The main plants already have solar so there'll be a lot of power saving there also.

items.statement: Renault Nissan India sales disappointed; equipment removed and redirected to other programs
items.quote: Renault Nissan was the other disappointment that we had in India. Their sales in India did not pick up at all and they kept on telling us to retain the capacity and that they wil l be able to achieve the targets, but that was a total failure

items.statement: GKN export programs restarting June-July; Aisin delayed programs starting this year; BMW programs starting by year-end
items.quote: GKN would start by June-July this year. And we are also expanding capacity for Toyota and Maruti Suzuki. In particular, Maruti Suzuki, we've won more businesses and also got a larger sha re of the current businesses that we are supplying

items.statement: Internal target to build INR 150+ crores new business this year; budgeted INR 50-60 crores
items.quote: And it depends, last year, we could build about INR 4.5-5 crores only. And this year, the orders are much higher, but we are t aking a conservative look. We think we will build around INR 50 crores to INR 70 crores this year. And our internal target is, of course, over INR 150 crores

items.statement: Targeting consolidated revenue of ₹500 crores plus with EBITDA of 20% for FY25
items.quote: For the financial year '24-'25, we are targeting a consolidated revenue of ₹ 500 crores plus with an EBITDA of 20%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance in the range of 20% for FY25
items.quote: It would be in the range of 20%.

items.statement: Group order book backlog at ₹284 crores as of 31st March
items.quote: Our order book backlog as of 31st March at group level, that is both the companies together stand at ₹284 crores.

items.statement: Received orders of ₹65 crores year-to-date in current financial year
items.quote: In the current financial year, we have received orders of ₹65 crores till date.

items.statement: Targeting order intake of ₹500 crores plus at group level for FY25
items.quote: At the group level, we are targeting order intake of ₹500 crores plus.

items.quote: Presently, it is I know the CapEx is in the range of 10 to 15.

items.quote: We are doing approximately ₹10 crores to ₹12 crores kind of CapEx, annually.

items.quote: Our current enquiry pipeline is in the range of ₹2,000 plus crores for both the companies together.

items.statement: M.E. Energy revenue expected to cross ₹100 crores in FY25
items.quote: For M.E. Energy, revenue definitely would be more than ₹100 crores this year. It should cross that.

items.quote: For the past one or two years, their EBITDA margins have been around 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Expecting major orders from petrochemical and oil & gas in next 12-18 months
items.quote: We are expecting major orders from the petrochemical and oil and gas in the current year or maybe, let me say next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Export orders increased to ₹40 crores this year from ₹30 crores last year
items.quote: We've received around ₹40 crores of orders this year compared to around ₹30 crores last year from the exports.

items.statement: Execution timeline 4-5 months up to 11-12 months depending on equipment type
items.quote: Well, it depends on the type of equipment, but we look anything from 4 to 5 months right up to 11 to 12 months.

items.statement: 25% to 30% of work outsourced; subcontract cost 7% to 8% of sales
items.quote: Maybe 25% to 30% of our work is outsourced. But as a percentage of sales, our subcontract cost is only around 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Targeting retail mortgage AUM over INR 6,000 crores by FY27
items.quote: The affordable housing focused retail mortgage business continues to be an integral part of the group and has demonstrated strong performance over the last few years. And we are targeting an AUM of over INR 6,000 crores in our retail mortgage business by FY27.

items.statement: Expect incremental cash release of approximately INR 2,000 crores over next three to four years from pivot
items.quote: As the gradual pivot from on-balance sheet lending to a distribution and alternative structure takes place over the next three to four years, we expect an incremental cash release of approximately INR 2,000 crores.

items.statement: Expect net debt-to-equity to be zero in both NBFCs in next three years
items.quote: If you fast forward, say, three years from now, we will be extremely balance sheet light in terms of literally our net debt-to-equity will be zero in the next three years in both our NBFCs.

items.statement: Mutual fund equity AUM breakeven expected at INR 15,000 crores in next two years
items.quote: To a pointed question on where do we think we will break even, I think we should be able to break even once we achieve close to a INR 15,000 crores equity AUM.
