items.statement: PMS business expected to make money this year if markets remain strong
items.quote: Then I am hoping, fingers crossed, that the PMS business actually makes money this year. So, I think we are seeing good outcomes.

items.statement: Will continue investments in digital and asset management businesses over next two to three years
items.quote: We have made further investments in digital as well as our asset management businesses and we will continue to do so over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Investment banking transaction pipeline is extremely robust
items.quote: The pipeline of transactions is extremely robust.

items.statement: Wholesale mortgage cost of liabilities almost 150 basis points above retail mortgages
items.quote: The cost of liabilities for wholesale mortgages is almost 150 basis points above retail mortgages and as we pivot from on-balance sheet to off-balance sheet, it will bring down our cost of funds even further for our home finance business.

items.statement: Draft regulatory papers propose standard asset provisioning increase from 40 bps to 500 bps for real estate
items.quote: Fourth, some interesting new draft sort of regulatory papers which substantially increase provisioning requirements on real estate and infrastructure sectors and if you specifically see real estate, the paper talks about 40 basis points provisioning cover expanding to almost 500 basis points, which is an increase of 12.5 times.

items.statement: Seeing lot of opportunities in syndication and distribution space in private credit over next two to three years

items.statement: Pivoting wholesale credit businesses from on-balance sheet to distribution-led syndication model
items.quote: In light of the same, it is thought prudent to refocus our expertise in the wholesale credit businesses by pivoting them from its on balance sheet-business model to more of a distribution-led syndication driven business model.

items.statement: Will create strategic AIF for land and approval financing and pivot distressed credit turnarounds to AIF model

items.statement: Retail mortgage AUM will double in the next 3 years

items.quote: We expect GDP growth to print below 6.5% in the first half of this financial year, before improving to 7.2% in the second half, aided by back-ended government capex, likely pick-up in private capex, improved rural demand if the monsoon turns out to be favorable and some pick-up in export growth. Overall, ICRA expects the GDP growth to land at 6.5% in this financial year.

items.statement: Technology investments will continue for the next few years until a normalized level is reached, with a roadmap already underway for about 1.5-2 years.
items.quote: Where we will continue to see spends over the next two to three years essentially will be in the technology area. This is an area where we have to naturally invest in infrastructure as well as enhancing the quality or efficiency of our applications to improve user experience both internally and with respect to our external users.

items.statement: Management is focused on continuous margin improvement through cost rationalization, technology efficiencies, repricing, and organizational restructuring.
items.quote: It will continue to improve. As we said before, this is something that will be part of our agenda perpetually. We will continue to use multiple levers to deliver on this, either in terms of cost rationalization or bringing in efficiencies through technology interface or repricing some of our offerings, rationalizing some of our offerings, etc.

items.statement: ESG rating pricing will be market-driven, not regulated, as SEBI framework does not regulate pricing for credit or ESG ratings.
items.quote: So, see, it is not regulated the pricing is not regulated neither on credit rating nor on ESG ratings. There is a regulatory framework which SEBI has put in place under which many entities including ours has got a license. So, pricing is -- will be market driven. So, we will see how it evolves.

items.statement: Bank credit growth may face headwinds from higher risk weights on NBFC/HFC lending and elevated credit-to-deposit ratios; bond issuances to benefit from competitive domestic funding costs and possible RBI rate cut.
items.quote: Bank credit growth may face some headwinds with higher risk weights for certain high growth consumption segments as well as their elevated credit to deposit ratio for which the regulator has expressed some concern. Bond issuances are likely to benefit from competitive funding cost domestically which may additionally be supported by a possible rate cut by RBI sometimes later in FY '25.

items.statement: D2K acquisition completes end-to-end risk product suite (IRS, ECL, EWS, asset classification); developing lighter SaaS versions for AMCs and non-bank segments.

items.statement: Knowledge services faces structural headwinds from client automation and captive competition; project revenue declined while FTE revenue remained steady.
items.quote: There has been headwinds that we have seen in certain parts of the services that we offer to them. These are largely driven by the drive for automation that we are seeing globally. And that impacts all our clients. And obviously, they would like to automate the solution.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 100 per share (including special dividend of INR 60) for FY24, continuing consistent shareholder rewards.
items.quote: I am pleased to advise that the board has recommended, subject to shareholder's approval a dividend of INR100 per share, which includes a special dividend of INR60 a share.

items.statement: Pragati Development Consulting Services received SEBI approval as Category 1 ESG Rating Provider; teams and structure in place, actively engaging with corporates and PE-led entities.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue growth expected at 18-20% year-on-year

items.statement: Rural demand was soft in recent quarters; expecting improvement in coming quarters

items.statement: Premium segment volume grew 25% in FY24; new Signature collection with Rohit Bal launched
items.quote: Notably, we achieved a healthy 17% annual growth in volume, driven by a 16% growth in economy segment, 17% in mid-premium segment and 25% growth in premium segment.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility remains key risk; yarn prices stabilized at 285-290 for 40s count vs 350 in FY23

items.statement: Discontinuing licensed brands FOTL and FCUK; wrote off INR 3.82 crores for FCUK business rights
items.quote: There is an exceptional item in the profit and loss accou nt for INR3.82 crores which is a write- off for unamortised balance of business rights for our licensed brand FCUK which we are not going to continue in near future

items.statement: Pragati loyalty scheme launched in two states (one new, one old) to map secondary sales and improve retailer stickiness

items.quote: Our net debt has reduced significantly as on March 24 and stands at INR6 crores versus INR134 crores last year.

items.quote: Ma'am, for both these subsidiaries, operations have not yet started. And means the performance is basically, we have very negligible negative EBITDA for these two subsidiaries.

items.statement: Capex plan for FY25 similar to FY24 average plus a new Pune facility with INR50 crore investment
items.quote: The capex plan for this year is similar to be average of last year, plus we'll be adding a new facility. For that, we made an announcement that we'll be doing INR50 crores on that facility in Pune. INR50 crores.

items.statement: Value-added sales growth to outperform industry by 10-15% due to RDE content increase
items.quote: We had guided last year that our value-added sales will increase, and it will outperform industry between 10% to 15% because of the content increase that would come from RDE.

items.quote: We have a very good RFQ pipeline. We do expect some new additions. To time it is very difficult. Also, as Puru sir mentioned that globally, the off-highway segment is in a slowdown, which has more to do with the U.S. and Europe market.

items.statement: TREM V implementation risk low as government notified and OEMs nominated suppliers; 3-player market for advanced emissions
items.quote: So, now it's notified by the government. It's a formal notification and almost all OEMs have nominated and started development also, right? So maybe there's just one or two OEMs left. items.quote: This year we won't see some big parts. We could. As of now it looks like there's not going to be some big addition in the 3-4-liter segment.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin improved 796 bps to 16.5% from 8.5% in FY23
items.quote: The EBITDA Margin improved by 796 bps from 8.5% in FY23 to 16.5% in FY24.

items.quote: On a full-year basis, we handled 2,117 films, up from 1,762 in FY20.

items.statement: Incremental ad revenue yields 65-70% operating margin; incremental CDC revenue fetches nearly 90% margin
items.quote: Incremental advertisement revenue typically yields a 65 -70% operating margin, while incremental CDC revenue fetches nearly a 90% margin.

items.statement: Multiplex screens now 55% of network (2,117) vs 45% single screens (1,742) in FY24
items.quote: Consequently, the proportion of multiplex screens now around 55%.

items.statement: NOVA Cinemaz: 16 screens across 8 properties in pipeline; first two near Meerut expected to open in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Currently, we have around 16 screens, spread across 8 properties, in the pipel ine. We expect to open a couple of these properties in Q1 of this

items.quote: Our ad revenue decreased from INR 38 crores in Q3 to around INR 31 crores in Q4. While this still represents a 24% year-over-year growth from INR 25 crores, it's a quarter-over-quarter decline.

items.quote: We have been working on a programmatic solution for advertisers that will offer better value for money and enable sustained and regular advertising, not just during big blockbuster films.

items.quote: Target for this is already stated. So, we expect 15% minimum growth for next year and let us see that we achieve this target of 1000 crore by FY28.

items.quote: The total CAPEX outlay for FY24 was INR 26 crore, and the company plans to invest an additional INR 60 crores in FY25 funded through internal accruals.

items.quote: So, whatever price movement is whether it is in the case of currency or in case of raw material cost. So we are always hedged. So we take care of our margins and we are able to negotiate with our customers at all times.

items.quote: So, Q1 is looking much brighter as compared to last year and also as compared to last quarter for us. items.statement: Export market seeing bullish trends with Europe coming back, North America responsive, South America decent
items.quote: Going ahead, the export market is seeing, bullish as compared to previous years, because Europe is coming back and North America has been like I said more responsive and also the South American market has been decently responsive.

items.statement: FY26 expected to return to 15%-20% CAGR trajectory
items.quote: I feel, I mean the conclusion that, it's not a feeling it's a conclusion of our analysis that we will pretty much, get back on the track, of 15% CAGR.

items.statement: Export order book annualized value INR75-80 crores with eight part numbers across Mexico, US, Portugal

items.statement: New business order wins have lifecycle revenue of INR900+ crores, including INR390-400 crores export with North American Tier 1s
items.quote: The orders we have won have a lifecycle revenue of INR 900 plus crores. Of this, we have export business with marquee Tier 1 North American. So not just one BorgWarner, but their peers as well.

items.statement: Commitment to maintain EBITDA above 20% range and target minimum ROIC of 18%

items.statement: IPO capex of INR170 crores, INR45 crores deployed to date, FY24 capex spend INR78 crores
items.quote: Out of the IPO process of capex of INR170 crores, till date we have deployed INR45 crores and capex spent for FY '24 was INR78 crores.

items.statement: Headwinds from four major OEMs (Mahindra, Tata EV, MG Motors, Mahindra Defense) to continue for first two quarters of FY25
items.quote: The headwinds that caused this dent in the last two quarters of FY24 we expect that to continue for the first two quarters of FY25.

items.statement: Asymmetric dependence on Mahindra transfer case business; lost INR35 crores top line in transfer case segment
items.quote: It is interesting to note that we lost about INR35 crores top line in the transfer case. So it's not as if we had not anticipated uncertainty with our major customer, Mahindra.

items.statement: Export business brings decidedly better margins than domestic business at component level
items.quote: Now when it comes to actually delivering a proprietary product the margins are of course the best, but even otherwise at the component level compared to the domestic business there is no doubt that overseas business brings decidedly a better margin.

items.statement: Strategic alliance with Toyota Group parts distribution company for opportunities in India and Southeast Asia with Japanese OEMs
items.quote: The visit was hosted by the parts distribution company of the Toyota Group, with whom we have a long -term strategic alliance. And working with them, we are looking at opportunities both in India and Southeast Asia with Japanese OEMs.

items.statement: Three-wheeler EV transmission development underway with significant OEM and startup ecosystem; not yet in budget/long-term plan
items.quote: So, I can tell you that, in the three wheeler segment, we are, working with all the stakeholders there, we are in touch with the vehicle engineers, who are advising, these companies.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR2.60 per equity share (face value INR5) for FY24
items.quote: Finally, to conclude, the Board of Directors at its meeting has recommended final dividend of INR2.60 per equity share of face value of INR5 each for FY'23-'24.

items.statement: Management targets 18-20% top-line growth and 15-20% bottom-line growth for FY25, with a conservative estimate of 15% and optimistic of 20%.
items.quote: we will want to continue to grow at about 18 % to 20% in terms of top line. And in the same way with our mix of gold versus diamonds stud ratio and the other products, we will also want to ensure that our bottom line also grows approximately between 15 % to 20%.

items.statement: Management aims to improve EBITDA margin towards 8% from current 7.3% by increasing stud ratio 100-150 bps annually.
items.quote: our EBITDA margin is at 7.3% that we have seen, and we will work on increasing it towards 8%, that's what we are saying, that is going to be our endeavor.

items.statement: Average capex per store is Rs 6,000-7,000 per sq ft, averaging Rs 2.5 crore per store; most stores are leased, not owned.
items.quote: on an average around Rs. 2.5 crore is our CAPEX per store, there are stores w here we have incurred Rs. 1.6 crore also, there are stores which have got Rs. 1.6 crore and Rs. 1.2 crore and Rs. 2.5 crore, there are multiple ranges, but average is around Rs. 6,000 per store, per square feet

items.statement: Export revenue grew from Rs 70 crore to Rs 187-188 crore in FY24; export gross margins are 6-7%.
items.quote: export last year was Rs. 70 crore to be precise and this year we have done exports around Rs. 187 crore to Rs. 188 crore. So, as you are aware export business gross margins are usually lower, let's say 6% to 7% range.

items.statement: Gold prices rose from ~Rs 57,000 to ~Rs 67,000 in FY24, impacting consumer behavior and shifting demand to lighter diamond-studded jewellery.
items.quote: the way it has worked out in the previous financial year, which has moved from ~Rs. 57,000 in the beginning of the year to about Rs. 67,000 by the end of the year

items.statement: Volume growth flat in recent period due to high gold prices; value growth driven by price increase. Wedding jewellery demand remains inelastic.
items.quote: in terms of value till Akshaya Tritiya, the value growth we can talk about 15% odd, but in terms of volume, we have not seen much of growth happening. So, people are taking a little bit of time to get used to the new gold prices.

items.statement: Stud ratio increased 100 bps to 11.4% in FY24; target 100-130 bps annual increase to offset gold margin pressure.
items.quote: our stud ratio is 11.4% as on date. And you are all aware that our fellow friends have had a bigger share in terms of their stud ratio and the diamond jewellery sales. So, even if we do a 100 to 150 basis point jump in the stud ratio that will create an upward pressure on the margins and the EBITDA.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increasing with more discounts and aggressive campaigns from peers, pressuring margins; expected to stabilize in 4-5 years.
items.quote: the competitive scenario is increasing, we have our fellow jewelers who are also working towards , trying to acquire new customers. And in that competitive scenario, there are more offers and discounts and aggressive campaigns that are happening and that is what is leading to this whole, downward pressure on the margins.

items.statement: Gold metal loan share increased from 55% to 61% of borrowing; target 75% to reduce finance cost.
items.quote: last year it was around 55% and has improved to 61% as of March 24, we propose to take it to around 75%.

items.statement: Plan to add 15-20 stores in FY25 (8-10 COCO, 8-10 franchise); 70-80% in East and North India.
items.quote: we are looking at about 8 to 10 Company owned, Company operated stores and 8 to 10 franchisees these are the thought process with which we are working for the new financial year. so about adding between 15 to 20 odd stores in the coming year.

items.statement: Old gold exchange share rose from 25% to 32% of business, indicating shift from unorganized to organized sector.
items.quote: our old gold exchange with our customers has grown substantially, two years back it was about 25% of the overall business,, but today we see 32% of the overall business is happening through the exchange of old gold.

items.statement: New customer acquisition ~45-50% of transacting customers; repeat buyers ~55%. New customer growth rate 5-10% YoY.
items.quote: we had a total number of customers that transacted was 5,54,000 and out of that new customer was 2,72,000. So, approximately 45% to 50%, that's how one has to look at it. And the repeat buyers were the remaining 2,80,000 odd, so around 55%.

items.statement: Launched Marygold savings scheme (6-9 month tenure) with fixed and flexible options to help consumers manage high gold price volatility.
items.quote: we have launched the Marygold scheme, in which a consumer can keep accumulating their money, save it with us over a period of six months or nine months and then they can buy it at the end of the tenure and there is a flexible option and a fixed option.

items.statement: Dubai store inaugurated on Akshaya Tritiya; global expansion is long-term (5-6 years) after East/North and West/South focus.
items.quote: the store in Dubai we did the puja and the auspicious beginning on the Day of Akshaya Tritiya, store in Dubai is under I wouldn't say the initiatives, the plan, the consumer connect, all those things are under process and right now there is nothing substantial to talk about

name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

items.statement: Confident of sustaining 29% revenue growth and 35% EBITDA growth in years ahead

items.statement: Acquisition CAPEX estimated at Rs 60-70 lakh per bed for existing facilities

items.quote: So, I think roughly I would say around 6%-7% can make an impact on the cash patient, 6% to 8% kind of.

items.quote: We feel that in the years to come international patients should be contributing close to a double-digit contribution in our overall revenue and we are confident at this time.

items.quote: I am quite confident that in the coming quarters this ARPOB in Noida Extension will even touch Rs. 40,000.

items.quote: We can expect a range of about 3 odd percent in FY'25. That's what we are targeting. But if not '25, '26, definitely.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA fell from ₹23.6 cr to ₹9.4 cr in FY24
items.quote: The revenue overall was ₹1,018 crores as compared to ₹768 crores in the previous year, where the EBITDA was ₹23.6 crores to ₹9.4 crores for FY'24.

items.statement: Seeing pickup in IT recruitment mandates from IT services companies and US clients; RFPs and vendor renewals increasing
items.quote: We started getting demand, Jatin. The science for us is the number of open mandates that we are receiving from our customers. And this usually starts with IT services company.

items.quote: The contracts that we have bagged will not help us reach a 30% mark, but they will contribute around a 12% to 13 % odd growth in the top line of the organisation.

items.quote: There was a lot of turnaround and quick turnaround that happened in the shipments in this H2, where usually, we used to be able to rotate capital twice in the month. However, a number of times, we were able to do it thrice in the last H2.

items.statement: Candidate salary hike expectations dropped from 30-40% to 20-25%, causing offer shopping and lower joining ratios
items.quote: At the moment, the industry is offering more in the range of about 20%, 22%, 25%, which is resulting in a fair amount of retention as well. And a lot of offer shopping, which is why it's not yet corresponding into performance from an organisational standpoint, it will come.

items.quote: So, trading has some bit of it, Rahi l. I believe it is to the tune of ₹10 odd crores roughly

items.quote: Annual number, just a second. So, our salary cost has gone up from a ₹14 odd crores to a ₹22.2 odd crores.

items.statement: Added 70 new logos in H2; client attrition routine, no significant losses

items.quote: So, Jatin, what has happened is we have been able to bag a contract, which is not a contract staffing assignment, but it is a professional staffing assignment. So, the fee to those professionals has been put in the other operating expenses.
